title: §3.5.1 ObjectId Content-Addressed Identity
description:
Implement ObjectId type and canonical encoding rules for ECS (§3.5.1, spec lines 2702-2723).

WHAT: ObjectId is the content-addressed identifier for every ECS object. It is the foundational type for the entire ECS substrate. Every object stored, replicated, or referenced in FrankenSQLite is identified by its ObjectId.

OBJECTID CONSTRUCTION (verbatim from spec):

  ObjectId = Trunc128( BLAKE3( "fsqlite:ecs:v1" || canonical_object_header || payload_hash ) )

We use BLAKE3 for speed and security, truncated to 128 bits (16 bytes) for storage efficiency. The prefix "fsqlite:ecs:v1" prevents cross-protocol collisions (domain separation).

CANONICAL ENCODING RULES (Deterministic Bytes, Not "Serde Vibes"):

These rules ensure deterministic addressing across all replicas:

1. EXPLICIT VERSIONED WIRE FORMAT: The byte stream must be fully defined, not dependent on compiler layout or serialization library defaults. No #[repr(C)] or mem::size_of reliance for on-disk formats.

2. LITTLE-ENDIAN INTEGERS: All fixed-width integers use little-endian byte order (matches native x86/ARM/WASM). This is a project-wide convention (§1.5).

3. SORTED MAP KEYS: If map-like structures are encoded, keys must be sorted lexicographically by byte representation. This ensures canonical form regardless of insertion order.

4. NO FLOATING-POINT IN HEADERS: Canonical headers must use fixed-point or integers to avoid NaN/rounding non-determinism. IEEE 754 has multiple NaN representations and platform-dependent rounding modes that would break content addressing.

OBJECTID PROPERTIES (normative):
- IMMUTABLE: Once created, an ObjectId never changes. Objects are write-once-read-many (WORM).
- CONTENT-ADDRESSED: Identical objects have identical ObjectIds. Deduplication is automatic across replicas.
- COLLISION-RESISTANT: 128-bit BLAKE3 is sufficient for all non-adversarial collisions and most adversarial ones in this context. Birthday bound at 2^64 objects.

DATA STRUCTURE:

  struct ObjectId([u8; 16]);

Required trait implementations:
  Display (32-char lowercase hex), Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Copy, Clone, Ord, PartialOrd

Required methods:
  fn from_canonical(header: &[u8], payload_hash: &[u8; 32]) -> ObjectId
  fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; 16]
  fn is_zero(&self) -> bool  // check for null/unset ObjectId

CANONICAL ENCODING TRAIT:

  trait CanonicalEncode {
      fn canonical_encode(&self, buf: &mut Vec<u8>);
      fn canonical_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
          let mut buf = Vec::new();
          self.canonical_encode(&mut buf);
          blake3::hash(&buf).into()
      }
  }

DOMAIN PREFIX ISOLATION: The "fsqlite:ecs:v1" prefix ensures that ObjectIds computed for FrankenSQLite ECS objects will never collide with:
  - ChangesetIds (prefix "fsqlite:replication:changeset:v1", §3.4.2)
  - MarkerIds (prefix "fsqlite:marker:v1", §3.5.4.1)
  - DbFecGroupMeta ObjectIds (prefix "fsqlite:compat:db-fec-group:v1", §3.4.6)
  - Root auth tags (prefix "fsqlite:ecs-root-auth:v1", §3.5.5)
  - Symbol auth tags (prefix "fsqlite:symbol-auth:v1", §3.5.2)

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_object_id_deterministic_construction:
   Given identical header+payload_hash, ObjectId MUST be identical across calls.

2. test_object_id_different_content:
   Different header bytes MUST produce different ObjectIds.

3. test_object_id_domain_separation:
   Same bytes with different domain prefix ("fsqlite:ecs:v1" vs "fsqlite:marker:v1") MUST produce different hashes.

4. test_object_id_display_format:
   ObjectId([0x01, 0x23, ...]).to_string() == "0123..." (32-char lowercase hex).

5. test_object_id_ord_is_lexicographic:
   Ord impl MUST match lexicographic comparison of underlying bytes.

6. test_canonical_encode_little_endian:
   u32 value 0x12345678 encodes as bytes [0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12].

7. test_canonical_encode_sorted_map_keys:
   Map with keys ["b", "a", "c"] encodes in order ["a", "b", "c"].

8. test_canonical_encode_no_padding:
   Canonical encoding MUST NOT include alignment padding bytes.

PROPERTY TESTS:

9. prop_object_id_collision_resistance:
   For 10,000 random payloads, all ObjectIds are unique (probabilistic; BLAKE3 128-bit).

10. prop_canonical_encode_roundtrip:
    For any CanonicalEncode value, canonical_encode produces stable output across calls.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ObjectId type compiles with all required traits
- blake3 crate used for hashing
- Domain prefix "fsqlite:ecs:v1" hardcoded and tested
- All canonical encoding rules enforced and tested
- Zero-cost in release builds (no allocation for ObjectId operations)

title: §3.5.2 SymbolRecord Envelope and Auth Tags
description:
Implement SymbolRecord — the atomic unit of physical storage for ECS (§3.5.2, spec lines 2725-2831).

OVERVIEW: Every ECS object is stored as one or more symbol records. A symbol record is the atomic unit of physical storage — the smallest thing that can be read, written, verified, and transmitted. It is self-describing: a decoder collecting K' symbols with the same ObjectId can reconstruct the original object without any external metadata.

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

SymbolRecord := {
    magic       : [u8; 4],      -- 0x46 0x53 0x45 0x43 ("FSEC")
    version     : u8,           -- envelope version (1)
    object_id   : [u8; 16],     -- ObjectId (128-bit)
    oti         : OTI,          -- RaptorQ Object Transmission Information
    esi         : u32,          -- Encoding Symbol Identifier (which symbol this is)
    symbol_size : u32,          -- T: symbol size in bytes
    symbol_data : [u8; T],      -- the actual RaptorQ encoding symbol
    flags       : u8,           -- bitflags (see below)
    frame_xxh3  : u64,          -- xxhash3 of all preceding fields (fast integrity)
    auth_tag    : [u8; 16],     -- Optional: HMAC/Poly1305 for authenticated transport
}

OTI := {
    F  : u64,       -- transfer length (original object size in bytes)
    Al : u16,       -- symbol alignment (always 4 for FrankenSQLite)
    T  : u32,       -- symbol size in bytes (see RFC 6330 OTI divergence note)
    Z  : u32,       -- number of source blocks
    N  : u32,       -- number of sub-blocks per source block
}

RFC 6330 OTI DIVERGENCE (normative): The FrankenSQLite OTI is an internal encoding, not the RFC 6330 Common FEC OTI wire format. Field widths are widened for implementation convenience:
  - F is u64 (RFC: 40-bit)
  - T is u32 (RFC: 16-bit) — CRITICAL: RFC 6330 limits symbol size to 65,535 bytes, but SQLite allows page_size = 65,536 (encoded as 1 in the file header because 65,536 overflows u16). Since PageHistory objects use T = page_size, OTI.T MUST be u32 to represent all valid SQLite page sizes.
  - Z is u32 (RFC: 12-bit)
  - N is u32 (RFC: 8-bit)

KEY INVARIANT (normative): For a well-formed SymbolRecord, symbol_size == OTI.T. On mismatch, the record MUST be treated as corrupt (reject for decode, count as a corruption observation for §3.5.12).

FLAGS (normative):
  0x01 = SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START: This record is the first source symbol (esi = 0) and the writer attempted to place the entire systematic run (esi = 0..K_source-1) contiguously in the local symbol log.
  Additional local flags MAY be defined but MUST be treated as advisory optimization hints. Correctness never depends on them.

AUTHENTICATED SYMBOLS (normative when enabled):

  Enable via: PRAGMA fsqlite.symbol_auth = on (default: off for local-only durability)
  If PRAGMA durability = quorum(M) and transport is not already authenticated, symbol_auth MUST be enabled.

  Tag construction (normative):
  Let epoch_id be the SymbolSegmentHeader.epoch_id of the segment containing this SymbolRecord (§3.5.4.2).
  Derive the epoch key K_epoch as in §4.18.2.

  auth_tag = Trunc128( BLAKE3_KEYED( K_epoch, "fsqlite:symbol-auth:v1" || bytes(magic..frame_xxh3) ) )

  Failure behavior (normative):
  - If symbol_auth = on and auth_tag verification fails: symbol MUST be rejected (MAY still count as corruption observation for §3.5.12).
  - If symbol_auth = off: auth_tag MUST be all-zero and MUST be ignored.

SYSTEMATIC READ FAST PATH (hybrid decode):

  RaptorQ is systematic: the first K_source symbols are (a padded form of) the original bytes. Therefore, for local reads:

  1. Locate SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START for the object (via object locator / index).
  2. Read K_source = ceil(F / T) symbol records sequentially.
  3. Verify per-record frame_xxh3 (and auth_tag if enabled).
  4. Concatenate symbol_data payloads and truncate to F bytes.

  If all checks pass: decoding complete WITHOUT invoking GF(256) matrix solve.
  If any record missing/corrupt: fall back to general fountain-code decoder (collect any K' symbols including repairs; decode; optionally produce DecodeProof).

  This ensures:
  - Happy-path reads are "read + checksum" (low latency).
  - Repair-path reads are "decode + proof" (self-healing, auditable).

SYMBOL RECORD SIZING: The symbol size T is object-type-aware and is encoded in the object's OTI (self-describing). The default policy is specified in §3.5.10 and is versioned in RootManifest so replicas decode correctly. Examples:
  - PageHistory and full page images: T = page_size (one source symbol per page)
  - CommitCapsule: T = min(page_size, 4096)

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_symbol_record_serialize_deserialize:
   Round-trip SymbolRecord through canonical bytes. All fields preserved exactly.

2. test_symbol_record_magic_validation:
   Records with magic \!= "FSEC" MUST be rejected.

3. test_symbol_record_frame_xxh3_integrity:
   Compute frame_xxh3 over magic..symbol_data+flags. Flip one bit in symbol_data — frame_xxh3 MUST fail.

4. test_symbol_record_invariant_symbol_size_eq_oti_t:
   Create record with symbol_size \!= OTI.T. Validation MUST reject as corrupt.

5. test_symbol_record_auth_tag_verification:
   With symbol_auth=on, create record with valid auth_tag. Verify passes. Tamper with one byte — verify MUST fail.

6. test_symbol_record_auth_tag_ignored_when_off:
   With symbol_auth=off, auth_tag MUST be all-zero. Non-zero auth_tag with auth off: accept record but ignore tag.

7. test_symbol_record_systematic_flag:
   Record with flags 0x01 MUST have esi=0. If SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START set with esi\!=0, treat as malformed hint (advisory).

8. test_oti_field_widths:
   OTI.T = 65536 (u32, not u16). Verify this encodes and decodes correctly.

9. test_systematic_fast_path_happy:
   Create object with K_source=4 symbols. Place all 4 contiguously with SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START on first. Read back via fast path — no GF(256) needed.

10. test_systematic_fast_path_fallback:
    Same setup but corrupt symbol 2. Fast path fails → fall back to fountain decoder with repair symbols.

PROPERTY TESTS:

11. prop_symbol_record_roundtrip:
    For random OTI/ESI/symbol_data, serialize + deserialize produces identical record.

12. prop_frame_xxh3_collision_resistance:
    For random symbol data, no frame_xxh3 collisions in 100,000 trials.

E2E TESTS:

13. test_e2e_systematic_read_full_object:
    Store a complete ECS object as K_source SymbolRecords. Read back via systematic fast path. Verify byte-identical to original.

14. test_e2e_repair_path_with_decode_proof:
    Store object, corrupt 2 source symbols, add repair symbols. Decode succeeds. DecodeProof emitted.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- SymbolRecord serialization is byte-exact (no padding, no alignment assumptions)
- OTI.T is u32 (not u16), supporting page_size=65536
- frame_xxh3 integrity check detects single-bit corruption
- auth_tag verification works with epoch-scoped keys
- Systematic fast path avoids GF(256) on happy path
- All invariants enforced at deserialization time

title: §3.5.3 Deterministic Repair Symbol Generation
description:
Implement deterministic repair symbol generation for ECS objects (§3.5.3, spec lines 2832-2894).

OVERVIEW: Given an ECS object and a repair symbol count R, the set of repair symbols is deterministic: the same object and same R always produce the same repair symbols. This is a fundamental enabler for the ECS architecture.

DETERMINISM ENABLES:
1. VERIFICATION WITHOUT ORIGINAL: Given the ObjectId and repair symbols, any node can verify that the repair symbols are valid by re-encoding from the source symbols.
2. INCREMENTAL REPAIR: If a storage node discovers corruption, it can request specific ESIs from peers and verify them independently.
3. IDEMPOTENT WRITES: Writing the same repair symbols twice has no effect.
4. APPENDABLE REDUNDANCY: Additional repair symbols can be published for an existing object later without changing its ObjectId or rewriting the object bytes (§3.5.12).

REPAIR SYMBOL BUDGET (normative):

  PRAGMA raptorq_overhead = <percent>    -- default: 20%

For K_source source symbols, budget deterministic repair symbols:

  slack_decode = 2  // V1 default: target K_source+2 decode slack (RFC 6330 Annex B)
  R = max(slack_decode, ceil(K_source * overhead_percent / 100))

TWO DISTINCT OVERHEADS (critical understanding):

1. DECODE SLACK (additive): The number of extra symbols beyond K_source needed to make decode failure probability negligible. V1 targets K_source+2 per RFC 6330 Annex B (see §3.1.1). This is NOT "extra safety for erasures"; it is there to drive RaptorQ's exactly-K decode failure probability into the floor.

2. LOSS BUDGET (multiplicative): How many symbols we can afford to lose to erasures/corruption and still collect K_source + slack_decode survivors.

TOLERATED ERASURE FRACTION (without coordination):

  loss_fraction_max = max(0, (R - slack_decode) / (K_source + R))

For large K_source, this approaches R/(K_source+R) = overhead/(100+overhead).

SMALL OBJECT WARNING: Small objects (small K_source) are dominated by the additive slack. The implementation MUST clamp policies to avoid under-provisioning. Example: K_source=3, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, ceil(0.6)) = 2. loss_fraction_max = max(0, (2-2)/(3+2)) = 0. This means NO erasure tolerance beyond the decode slack! The implementation MUST detect this and warn or increase R.

ADAPTIVE OVERHEAD (alien-artifact, optional but recommended):

The engine MAY auto-tune PRAGMA raptorq_overhead using anytime-valid evidence:

- Maintain an e-process monitor on symbol survival/corruption (§4.3).
- If evidence suggests the symbol erasure rate exceeds the assumed budget, increase overhead_percent (and thus R) until the derived loss_fraction_max clears the new budget with margin.
- If evidence suggests the erasure rate is far below budget for a sustained period, the engine MAY decrease overhead_percent to reduce space/write amplification, but ONLY under a conservative loss matrix where the cost of a false decrease (future data loss risk) dwarfs the benefit of saved bytes.

NORMATIVE: Every automatic retune MUST emit an evidence ledger entry containing: the prior/assumed budget, the observed e-value trajectory, the chosen new overhead, and the implied loss_fraction_max bound.

SEED DERIVATION (from §3.5.9, required for determinism):

  seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes)

This seed MUST be wired through RaptorQConfig or sender construction. It ensures repair symbol generation is deterministic for a given ObjectId. This makes "the object" a platonic mathematical entity: any replica can regenerate missing repair symbols (within policy) without coordination.

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_repair_symbol_count_formula:
   K_source=100, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 20) = 20.
   K_source=3, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 1) = 2.
   K_source=1, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 1) = 2.
   K_source=56403, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 11281) = 11281.

2. test_repair_deterministic_same_object:
   Generate repair symbols for object X with R=10. Generate again. Symbols MUST be byte-identical.

3. test_repair_deterministic_different_object:
   Different ObjectId -> different repair symbols (different seed).

4. test_repair_seed_derivation:
   seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes). Verify deterministic for given ObjectId.

5. test_loss_fraction_max_computation:
   K_source=100, R=20: loss_fraction_max = (20-2)/(100+20) = 0.15 (15%).
   K_source=3, R=2: loss_fraction_max = 0 (no loss tolerance beyond slack).

6. test_small_k_underprovisioning_warning:
   K_source=3, overhead=20% -> R=2. System MUST log warning that loss_fraction_max=0.

7. test_repair_symbol_esi_range:
   Repair symbols have ESI in range [K_source, K_source+R). All ESIs present and unique.

8. test_repair_symbols_decode_compatible:
   Generate K_source source + R repair symbols. Drop any 2 source symbols. Decode from remaining K_source-2 source + 2 repair. MUST succeed.

9. test_pragma_raptorq_overhead:
   Set overhead=50%. K_source=100 -> R = max(2, 50) = 50.

10. test_adaptive_overhead_evidence_ledger:
    Simulate retune (increase overhead from 20% to 40%). Evidence ledger entry MUST contain: old budget, new budget, e-value, loss_fraction_max.

PROPERTY TESTS:

11. prop_repair_deterministic:
    For random payloads, repair symbols are identical across multiple generations with same seed.

12. prop_loss_fraction_monotonic:
    Increasing R always increases or maintains loss_fraction_max.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- R formula correctly computed for all K_source values (including edge cases K_source=1,2,3)
- Seed derivation via xxh3_64(object_id_bytes) is deterministic
- Same object + same config = identical repair symbols (byte-exact)
- Adaptive overhead emits evidence ledger on every retune
- Small-K underprovisioning detected and warned

title: §3.5.4 Commit Marker Stream Format
description:
Implement the CommitMarker stream — the total order of commits in Native mode (§3.5.4 + §3.5.4.1, spec lines 2895-3126).

OVERVIEW: The CommitMarker stream under ecs/markers/ is the total order of commits. It is the authoritative, tamper-evident, seekable commit log for Native mode.

DIRECTORY LAYOUT (Native mode, §3.5.4):

  foo.db.fsqlite/
  +-- ecs/
  |   +-- root              -- tiny mutable pointer file (atomic update)
  |   +-- symbols/          -- append-only symbol record logs
  |   |   +-- segment-000000.log
  |   |   +-- segment-000001.log
  |   +-- markers/          -- append-only commit marker stream
  |       +-- segment-000000.log
  +-- cache/                -- rebuildable derived state (NOT source of truth)
  |   +-- object_locator.cache
  |   +-- btree.cache
  |   +-- index.cache
  |   +-- schema.cache
  +-- compat/               -- optional compatibility export
      +-- foo.db
      +-- foo.db-wal

KEY INVARIANTS (normative):
- ecs/ is the source of truth. Everything in cache/ is rebuildable from ecs/. Deleting cache/ is always safe (costs a rebuild).
- ecs/symbols/*.log are immutable once rotated.
- ecs/root is the ONLY mutable file in the ECS directory.

CRASH-SAFE ROOT UPDATE SEQUENCE (normative):
  1. Write new contents to temp file in ecs/ (e.g., ecs/.root.tmp)
  2. fsync the temp file (ensures data durable before rename)
  3. rename(temp, ecs/root) (atomic within a filesystem)
  4. fsync the ecs/ directory (ensures rename is durable)
  Omitting step 2 risks garbage after crash. Omitting step 4 risks rename loss after crash.

MARKER STREAM REQUIREMENTS (§3.5.4.1, normative):
- Append-only
- Record-aligned (fixed-size records)
- Seekable by commit_seq in O(1)
- Auditable (tamper-evident hash chain)

ON-DISK ENCODING (normative):
- All fixed-width integers encoded little-endian (§3.5.1)
- All sizes are BYTE-EXACT. Implementations MUST NOT use sizeof(struct) / mem::size_of::<T>() for on-disk offset math (padding would silently corrupt indexing)

V1 CONSTANTS (normative):
  MARKER_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES := 36
  COMMIT_MARKER_RECORD_BYTES  := 88

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

MarkerSegmentHeader := {
    magic           : [u8; 4],    -- "FSMK"
    version         : u32,        -- 1
    segment_id      : u64,        -- monotonic identifier (matches filename)
    start_commit_seq: u64,        -- first commit_seq stored in this segment
    record_size     : u32,        -- bytes per CommitMarkerRecord (MUST be 88 in V1)
    header_xxh3     : u64,        -- xxhash3 of all preceding header fields
}

CommitMarkerRecord := {
    commit_seq         : u64,
    commit_time_unix_ns: u64,
    capsule_object_id  : [u8; 16],
    proof_object_id    : [u8; 16],
    prev_marker_id     : [u8; 16],  -- 0 for genesis
    marker_id          : [u8; 16],  -- domain-separated BLAKE3-128
    record_xxh3        : u64,       -- xxhash3 of all preceding fields
}

MARKER_ID DEFINITION (normative):

  marker_id = Trunc128( BLAKE3( "fsqlite:marker:v1" || record_prefix_bytes ) )

where record_prefix_bytes is the canonical byte encoding of:
  (commit_seq, commit_time_unix_ns, capsule_object_id, proof_object_id, prev_marker_id)

marker_id is both:
- The marker's integrity hash (tamper-evident)
- An ObjectId-compatible identifier (128-bit BLAKE3) suitable for RootManifest.current_commit and CommitMarker.prev_marker

DENSITY INVARIANT (normative, required for O(1) seeks):
- Within any marker segment, the record at slot index i (0-based) MUST be the marker for commit_seq = start_commit_seq + i.
- The marker stream MUST NOT have gaps in commit_seq for committed markers.
- If record commit_seq = N exists, then every commit_seq < N MUST also have a record.

COMMIT_SEQ ALLOCATION (gap-free, crash-safe):
commit_seq MUST be derived from the physical marker stream tip inside the same cross-process serialized section used to append the marker record. MUST NOT use in-memory AtomicU64::fetch_add (crash gap risk).

Allocator pseudocode:
  // Inside the marker-append lock / commit section.
  let n_records = floor((segment_file_len_bytes - MARKER_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES) / record_size);
  next_commit_seq = start_commit_seq + n_records;

TORN TAIL HANDLING (normative):
- Partial record at end: ignore, recovery MAY truncate.
- Last complete record fails record_xxh3: treat it and subsequent records as corrupt/torn. Scan forward from segment start; valid prefix is authoritative.

O(1) SEEK BY COMMIT_SEQ (normative):

Fixed rotation policy (recommended):
  markers_per_segment = 1,000,000 (constant)
  segment_id := commit_seq / markers_per_segment
  start_commit_seq := segment_id * markers_per_segment

Offset computation:
  offset = MARKER_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES + (commit_seq - start_commit_seq) * record_size

Read one CommitMarkerRecord, verify record_xxh3, verify record.commit_seq == commit_seq.

BINARY SEARCH BY TIME (enables time travel):
commit_time_unix_ns is monotonic non-decreasing in commit_seq (enforced by §7.11.2 step 2: commit_time_unix_ns := max(now_unix_ns(), last_commit_time_unix_ns + 1)). Binary search over [0, latest_commit_seq] with random-access record reads. Complexity: O(log N).

FORK/DIVERGENCE DETECTION (replication correctness):
  1. Compare (latest_commit_seq, latest_marker_id)
  2. If commit_seq differs, use smaller as comparison bound
  3. If marker_ids mismatch, binary search in commit_seq space for greatest k such that marker_id(seq=k) matches on both replicas → greatest-common-prefix commit in O(log N)

OPTIONAL MMR (Merkle Mountain Range):
For replication and audit, supports O(log N) inclusion proofs and prefix proofs.

Leaf hash: BLAKE3_256( "fsqlite:mmr:leaf:v1" || le_u64(commit_seq) || marker_id )
Node hash: BLAKE3_256( "fsqlite:mmr:node:v1" || left || right )

MMR state: peaks for current tip. Periodic MMRCheckpoint objects (e.g., every 1,048,576 markers) store n_leaves, peaks[], bagged_root.

Replication use: exchange (latest_commit_seq, latest_marker_id, bagged_root). Match → identical histories. Mismatch → request inclusion/prefix proofs.

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_marker_segment_header_encode_decode:
   Round-trip MarkerSegmentHeader. Verify 36 bytes exactly. header_xxh3 validates.

2. test_commit_marker_record_encode_decode:
   Round-trip CommitMarkerRecord. Verify 88 bytes exactly. record_xxh3 validates.

3. test_marker_id_computation:
   Compute marker_id from known fields. Verify = Trunc128(BLAKE3("fsqlite:marker:v1" || prefix_bytes)).

4. test_density_invariant:
   Append 5 markers. Record at slot i has commit_seq = start + i.

5. test_o1_seek_by_commit_seq:
   Write 1000 markers. Seek to commit_seq=500 via offset formula. Verify correct record.

6. test_commit_seq_allocation_from_file_length:
   Write 10 records. File length = 36 + 10*88 = 916. next_commit_seq = start + floor((916-36)/88) = start + 10.

7. test_torn_tail_handling:
   Write 5 complete records + 44 partial bytes. Recovery sees 5 records, ignores tail.

8. test_torn_tail_corrupt_last_record:
   Write 5 records, corrupt record_xxh3 of record 4. Valid prefix is records 0-3.

9. test_binary_search_by_time:
   Write markers with monotonic timestamps. Search for timestamp T. Verify returns correct commit_seq.

10. test_fork_detection:
    Two streams sharing prefix. Detect divergence point via binary search.

11. test_hash_chain_integrity:
    Verify prev_marker_id links form tamper-evident chain. Tampering with any record detected.

12. test_marker_no_mem_size_of:
    Verify on-disk sizes are constants (36, 88), not derived from mem::size_of.

PROPERTY TESTS:

13. prop_marker_id_unique:
    For random commit data, marker_ids are unique.

14. prop_density_invariant_holds:
    After N appends, record at slot i always has commit_seq = start + i.

E2E TESTS:

15. test_e2e_marker_stream_recovery:
    Write 10000 markers, simulate crash (truncate mid-record), reopen. All complete markers preserved.

16. test_e2e_time_travel_query:
    Write markers over simulated time span. Query "AS OF timestamp T" resolves to correct commit_seq.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- MarkerSegmentHeader = 36 bytes, CommitMarkerRecord = 88 bytes (exact, no padding)
- O(1) seek works for any valid commit_seq
- Density invariant enforced (no gaps)
- commit_seq allocated from file length (crash-safe)
- Torn tail handled gracefully
- Hash chain is tamper-evident
- Binary search by time works with O(log N) reads

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

title: §3.5.4.2 Symbol Record Logs (Append-Only)
description:
Implement Symbol Record Logs — the persistence substrate for ECS objects (§3.5.4.2, spec lines 3127-3195).

OVERVIEW: Symbol record logs under ecs/symbols/ are the persistence substrate for ECS objects. Unlike the marker stream (fixed-size records), symbol logs store variable-sized SymbolRecords (because T = symbol_size is object-type-aware). The format is optimized for sequential append writes, sequential scans (for rebuild), and random access via locator offsets (for decode).

DIRECT I/O CONSTRAINT (normative): Because SymbolRecord entries are variable-sized, ecs/symbols/*.log does not, in general, preserve sector alignment at record boundaries. Implementations therefore MUST NOT require O_DIRECT for symbol logs (§1.5). Buffered I/O is permitted and expected.

OPTIONAL ALIGNED VARIANT: Implementations MAY provide an aligned symbol log variant for O_DIRECT experiments: pad each on-disk SymbolRecord to align_up(record_len, sector_size) and record the padded length in a per-segment index. This is optional and MUST NOT change the logical SymbolRecord bytes used for frame_xxh3/auth_tag verification.

V1 CONSTANTS (normative):
  SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES := 40

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

SymbolSegmentHeader := {
    magic      : [u8; 4],   -- "FSSY"
    version    : u32,       -- 1
    segment_id : u64,       -- monotonic identifier (matches filename)
    epoch_id   : u64,       -- ECS coordination epoch (RootManifest.ecs_epoch at segment creation)
    created_at : u64,       -- unix_ns (monotonic in lab via virtual time)
    header_xxh3: u64,       -- xxhash3 of all preceding header fields
}

EPOCH MEANING (normative):
epoch_id is NOT needed for RaptorQ decoding (OTI+ESI are sufficient). It exists to make distributed operation and security policy explicit:
- Symbol auth key derivation is epoch-scoped (§4.18.2)
- Remote durability/quorum configuration is epoch-scoped (§4.18.3)
- Epoch transitions are explicit and quiescent (§4.18.4)

TORN TAIL HANDLING (normative):
If a symbol segment ends with a partial SymbolRecord (incomplete bytes), rebuild/recovery MUST ignore the torn tail. The variable-size nature of records means partial writes are detected by:
  1. Reading the record header to determine expected size
  2. If remaining bytes < expected size, treat as torn tail

LOCATOR OFFSETS (normative):

SymbolLogOffset := {
    segment_id   : u64,
    offset_bytes : u64,  -- byte offset AFTER SymbolSegmentHeader
}

cache/object_locator.cache stores (at minimum): ObjectId -> Vec<SymbolLogOffset>

This is an accelerator only and MUST be rebuildable by scanning ecs/symbols/ and parsing symbol records. If the cache is missing or corrupt, the system MUST be able to reconstruct it by a sequential scan.

SEGMENT FILE FORMAT:

ecs/symbols/segment-XXXXXX.log:
  [SymbolSegmentHeader: 40 bytes]
  [SymbolRecord_0: variable size]
  [SymbolRecord_1: variable size]
  ...
  [SymbolRecord_N: variable size]
  [possible torn tail: ignored]

Symbol records are concatenated with NO padding between them (unless the optional aligned variant is used). Each SymbolRecord is self-describing (magic, version, OTI tells the reader the total record size).

SEGMENT ROTATION POLICY:
- Segments are rotated (closed and a new segment opened) based on size threshold or time/commit count.
- Once rotated, a segment is IMMUTABLE. No existing bytes are modified.
- New symbols are always appended to the active (current) segment.

LOCATOR CACHE REBUILD ALGORITHM:

  rebuild_object_locator(symbols_dir: Path) -> HashMap<ObjectId, Vec<SymbolLogOffset>>:
      locator = HashMap::new()
      for segment_file in sorted(symbols_dir.list()):
          header = read_and_verify(segment_file, SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES)
          offset = SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES
          while offset < file_len:
              record = try_read_symbol_record(segment_file, offset)
              if record is None:
                  break  // torn tail
              locator.entry(record.object_id)
                     .or_default()
                     .push(SymbolLogOffset { segment_id: header.segment_id, offset_bytes: offset - SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES })
              offset += record.total_wire_size()
      return locator

- test_bd_1hi_24_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_24_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

4. test_symbol_log_torn_tail_recovery:

5. test_locator_offset_computation:

6. test_locator_cache_rebuild:
   Write records for 3 different ObjectIds across 2 segments. Rebuild locator from scan. Verify all records found.

   Delete cache. System rebuilds from sequential scan. All objects still accessible.

9. test_immutable_rotated_segments:
   After rotation, attempting to append to rotated segment MUST fail/error.

10. test_variable_size_records:
    Append records with T=1024, T=4096, T=65536 in same segment. All read back correctly.

11. test_no_o_direct_requirement:
    Symbol log works with standard buffered I/O. No alignment requirements for correctness.

12. test_aligned_variant_optional:
    If aligned variant enabled, padded records still verify frame_xxh3 on logical (unpadded) bytes.

PROPERTY TESTS:

    For random sequences of record appends across multiple segments, locator rebuild always produces correct index.

- test_e2e_bd_1hi_24_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

    Create segments, append records, rotate segments, rebuild locator, read all objects. Full lifecycle.

    Simulate crash during append (partial write). Recovery ignores torn tail. All prior records intact.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- SymbolSegmentHeader = 40 bytes exact
- Variable-sized records stored without padding (default)
- Torn tail handling correct
- Locator cache rebuildable from sequential scan
- epoch_id stored but not required for decoding
- O_DIRECT not required
- Immutability of rotated segments enforced

title: §3.5.5 RootManifest Bootstrap Sequence
description:
E2E Test:
- test_e2e_bd_1hi_25_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement RootManifest and the full bootstrap sequence for Native mode (§3.5.5, spec lines 3197-3277).

OVERVIEW: The RootManifest is the bootstrap entry point for the ECS substrate, stored as a standard ECS object. The ecs/root file points to it. This is how a FrankenSQLite Native mode database opens: read root pointer -> fetch manifest -> verify marker chain -> reconstruct schema -> open for queries.

ECS ROOT POINTER (ecs/root file, required):

ecs/root is the mutable anchor file. It is tiny, atomically updated (§3.5.4 crash-safe sequence), and is the only place the engine reads before it knows which ECS objects are the current tip.

EcsRootPointer := {
    magic            : [u8; 4],   -- "FSRT"
    version          : u32,       -- 1
    manifest_object_id: [u8; 16], -- ObjectId of the RootManifest ECS object
    ecs_epoch        : u64,       -- current ECS coordination epoch (must match RootManifest.ecs_epoch)
    checksum         : u64,       -- xxh3_64 of all preceding fields (torn-write detection)
    root_auth_tag    : [u8; 16],  -- Optional: keyed authenticity tag (see below)
}

ROOT POINTER AUTHENTICITY (normative when symbol_auth enabled):

When PRAGMA fsqlite.symbol_auth = on (§3.5.2), the engine MUST treat ecs/root as part of the authenticated bootstrap chain:
- root_auth_tag MUST be present and MUST be verified before using manifest_object_id or ecs_epoch.
- root_auth_tag is derived from the epoch-independent master_key (§4.18.2) so bootstrap does not require knowing the epoch a priori.

  root_auth_tag = Trunc128( BLAKE3_KEYED(master_key, "fsqlite:ecs-root-auth:v1" || bytes(magic..checksum) ) )

If symbol_auth = off: root_auth_tag MUST be all-zero and MUST be ignored.

ROOT MANIFEST ECS OBJECT:

RootManifest := {
    magic           : [u8; 8],     -- "FSQLROOT"
    version         : u32,         -- manifest version
    database_name   : String,      -- human-readable name
    current_commit  : ObjectId,    -- ObjectId of the latest CommitMarker
    commit_seq      : u64,         -- latest commit sequence number
    schema_snapshot : ObjectId,    -- ObjectId of current schema ECS object
    schema_epoch    : u64,         -- monotonic schema epoch (bumps on DDL/VACUUM)
    ecs_epoch       : u64,         -- monotonic ECS coordination epoch
    checkpoint_base : ObjectId,    -- ObjectId of last full checkpoint
    gc_horizon      : u64,         -- safe GC horizon commit sequence
    created_at      : u64,         -- Unix timestamp
    updated_at      : u64,         -- Unix timestamp
    checksum        : u64,         -- xxhash3 of all preceding fields
}

BOOTSTRAP SEQUENCE (9 steps, normative):

1. READ ecs/root. Verify checksum. If checksum fails -> root is corrupted (see recovery below).

2. IF symbol_auth = on: verify root_auth_tag using master_key (epoch-independent). Reject on failure.

3. RECORD root_epoch = EcsRootPointer.ecs_epoch and manifest_object_id.

4. FETCH RootManifest object from symbol logs (using object_locator.cache or sequential scan).
   FAIL-CLOSED EPOCH CHECK (bootstrap): While loading the manifest, the engine MUST reject symbol segments with SymbolSegmentHeader.epoch_id > root_epoch (future-epoch misconfiguration/replay guard; §4.18.1).

5. DECODE RootManifest.
   INVARIANT (required): RootManifest.ecs_epoch MUST equal root_epoch. On mismatch, treat as corruption (do not silently pick one).

6. FETCH AND VERIFY latest CommitMarkerRecord:
   - Locate record by RootManifest.commit_seq via §3.5.4.1.
   - Verify marker_id == RootManifest.current_commit.
   - (Optional, bounded): verify marker hash chain back to latest checkpoint tip (detects marker-stream corruption early without O(N) open).

7. FETCH schema_snapshot -> reconstruct schema cache.

8. FETCH checkpoint_base -> populate B-tree page cache for hot pages.

9. Database is open and ready for queries.

RECOVERY FROM CORRUPTED ROOT:
If ecs/root is corrupted (missing or invalid checksum), the database can be recovered by:
- Scanning ecs/markers/*.log to find the latest valid CommitMarker, or
- Scanning ecs/symbols/*.log to find the latest RootManifest symbol.

- test_bd_1hi_25_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_25_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

1. test_ecs_root_pointer_encode_decode:
   Round-trip EcsRootPointer. Verify checksum. All fields preserved.

2. test_ecs_root_pointer_magic:
   Magic MUST be "FSRT". Wrong magic rejected.

3. test_ecs_root_pointer_checksum_tamper:
   Modify one byte of manifest_object_id. checksum MUST fail.

4. test_root_auth_tag_verification:
   With symbol_auth=on, create root with valid auth_tag. Verify passes. Tamper -> fails.

5. test_root_auth_tag_zero_when_off:
   With symbol_auth=off, root_auth_tag MUST be all-zero.

6. test_root_manifest_encode_decode:
   Round-trip RootManifest. Verify checksum. All fields preserved including String database_name.

7. test_root_manifest_magic:
   Magic MUST be "FSQLROOT".

8. test_bootstrap_step_4_epoch_guard:
   Symbol segment with epoch_id > root_epoch MUST be rejected during bootstrap.

9. test_bootstrap_step_5_epoch_invariant:
   RootManifest.ecs_epoch \!= root_epoch -> treated as corruption.

10. test_bootstrap_step_6_marker_verification:
    RootManifest.current_commit must match marker_id at commit_seq. Mismatch -> error.

11. test_bootstrap_full_sequence:
    Create valid root + manifest + markers + schema. Bootstrap all 9 steps successfully.

12. test_bootstrap_corrupted_root_recovery:
    Corrupt ecs/root. Recovery scans markers to find latest valid state.

13. test_crash_safe_root_update:
    Write temp -> fsync temp -> rename -> fsync dir. Verify atomicity.

PROPERTY TESTS:

    For random ObjectIds and epochs, EcsRootPointer round-trips perfectly.

- test_e2e_bd_1hi_25_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

    Create database from scratch, write commits, close, reopen via bootstrap. All data accessible.

16. test_e2e_bootstrap_after_crash:
    Simulate crash after commit but before root update. Bootstrap recovers to last consistent state.

17. test_e2e_bootstrap_schema_migration:
    DDL changes bump schema_epoch. Bootstrap loads correct schema version.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- EcsRootPointer is tiny and atomically updated (crash-safe 4-step)
- RootManifest contains all bootstrap state
- 9-step bootstrap sequence implemented and tested
- Future-epoch guard prevents loading segments from wrong epoch
- Epoch invariant (root vs manifest) enforced
- Recovery from corrupted root possible via marker/symbol scan
- Auth tag verified when symbol_auth enabled

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

title: §3.5.6 Inter-Object Coding for Replication
description:
Implement inter-object RaptorQ coding for replication optimization (§3.5.6, spec lines 3278-3298).

OVERVIEW: ECS objects can be coded across objects using inter-object RaptorQ encoding. This allows a replica to reconstruct missing objects from a subset of symbols spanning multiple objects. This is a replication optimization, not a correctness requirement.

MECHANISM (verbatim from spec):

  Inter-object coding group:
      Objects O1, O2, ..., Ok share a coding group
      RaptorQ-encode the concatenation of their canonical encodings
      Transmit encoding symbols with group metadata

  Receiver:
      Collect symbols from any subset of the group
      Decode to recover all objects in the group

USE CASE: Replication catch-up. A lagging replica requests "all commits since sequence N" as a single coded group. It can recover even if some symbols are lost in transit (UDP multicast). This is particularly effective because:
  1. Multiple small objects (capsules, proofs, markers) can be grouped for batch recovery
  2. Symbol loss across objects is shared — losing some symbols from object O1 can be compensated by extra symbols from O2
  3. Reduces the number of individual decode operations

CODING GROUP CONSTRUCTION:

  CodingGroup := {
      group_id     : ObjectId,      -- content-addressed from group metadata
      member_ids   : Vec<ObjectId>, -- ObjectIds of member objects
      total_len    : u64,           -- total bytes of concatenated canonical encodings
      member_lens  : Vec<u64>,      -- individual object lengths for demultiplexing after decode
      k_source     : u32,           -- total source symbols for the group
      symbol_size  : u32,           -- T for this group (must accommodate all members)
  }

ENCODING PROCESS:

  encode_coding_group(objects: &[EcsObject], T: u32) -> (CodingGroup, Vec<SymbolRecord>):
      // 1. Concatenate canonical encodings
      let concat = objects.iter().map(|o| o.canonical_encode()).collect::<Vec<u8>>().concat()
      let total_len = concat.len()
      let member_lens = objects.iter().map(|o| o.canonical_encode().len() as u64).collect()

      // 2. Compute group identity
      let member_ids = objects.iter().map(|o| o.object_id()).collect()
      let group_meta = canonical_encode(member_ids, member_lens)
      let group_id = ObjectId::from_canonical(&group_meta, &blake3::hash(&concat))

      // 3. RaptorQ-encode the concatenation
      let k_source = ceil(total_len / T)
      let encoder = RaptorQEncoder::new(concat, T, seed=xxh3_64(group_id.as_bytes()))
      let symbols = encoder.encode_all(k_source + R)

      return (CodingGroup { group_id, member_ids, total_len, member_lens, k_source, symbol_size: T }, symbols)

DECODING PROCESS:

  decode_coding_group(group: &CodingGroup, symbols: &[SymbolRecord]) -> Vec<EcsObject>:
      // 1. RaptorQ-decode the concatenation
      let decoder = RaptorQDecoder::new(group.k_source, group.symbol_size, seed=xxh3_64(group.group_id.as_bytes()))
      for sym in symbols:
          decoder.add_symbol(sym.esi, sym.symbol_data)
      let concat = decoder.decode()?  // K' >= K_source symbols needed
      let concat = &concat[..group.total_len]  // truncate padding

      // 2. Demultiplex into individual objects
      let mut offset = 0
      let objects = group.member_lens.iter().map(|&len| {
          let obj = EcsObject::from_canonical(&concat[offset..offset+len as usize])
          offset += len as usize
          obj
      }).collect()

      // 3. Verify each object's ObjectId matches
      for (obj, expected_id) in objects.iter().zip(group.member_ids.iter()):
          assert_eq\!(obj.object_id(), *expected_id)

      return objects

INTEGRATION WITH REPLICATION:
- The replication sender (§3.4.7, anti-entropy loop step 3) MAY group missing objects into coding groups before transmitting symbols.
- The replication receiver collects symbols per group_id and decodes when sufficient symbols arrive.
- Grouping policy: group objects by commit_seq range or by object type for efficiency.

- test_bd_1hi_26_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_26_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

1. test_coding_group_encode_decode:
   Create 5 small ECS objects. Encode as coding group. Decode from K_source symbols. Verify all 5 objects recovered byte-identical.

2. test_coding_group_with_loss:
   Encode group. Drop 20% of symbols. Add repair symbols. Decode succeeds.

3. test_coding_group_member_verification:
   After decode, each recovered object's ObjectId matches the original.

4. test_coding_group_demultiplexing:
   Objects of different sizes in one group. After decode, member_lens correctly splits concatenation.

5. test_coding_group_deterministic:
   Same objects in same order -> same group_id and same symbols.

6. test_coding_group_single_object:
   Group with one object behaves identically to direct object encoding.

PROPERTY TESTS:

7. prop_coding_group_roundtrip:
   For random sets of objects, encode+decode always recovers all objects.

- test_e2e_bd_1hi_26_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

8. test_e2e_replication_catchup_with_coding_group:
   Lagging replica catches up via inter-object coded batch. All missing objects recovered.

9. test_e2e_multicast_coding_group:
   3 replicas receive same coded stream. Each with different loss pattern. All decode successfully.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Coding groups correctly concatenate and demultiplex objects
- RaptorQ encoding/decoding of concatenated payloads works
- group_id is deterministic and content-addressed
- Loss tolerance works across the group (symbol sharing benefit)
- Integration with replication anti-entropy loop

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

title: §3.5.7 RaptorQ Permeation Map Audit
description:
Implement and enforce the RaptorQ Permeation Map — every subsystem that persists/ships bytes MUST declare its ECS object type, symbol policy, and repair story (§3.5.7, spec lines 3299-3367).

OVERVIEW: This is the "no excuses" mapping from subsystem to ECS/RaptorQ role. If a subsystem persists or ships bytes, it MUST declare its ECS object type, symbol policy (K/R), and repair story. This is an audit checklist and enforcement mechanism.

DURABILITY PLANE (disk) — verbatim from spec:

| Subsystem     | ECS Object Type | Symbol Policy | Repair Story |
|---------------|-----------------|---------------|--------------|
| Commits       | CommitCapsule + CommitProof (coded) + CommitMarkerRecord (marker stream) | Capsule/Proof: T = min(page_size, 4096), R = 20% default; Marker: 88B fixed records | Capsule/Proof: decode from surviving symbols; Marker: torn-tail ignore + record_xxh3 + hash-chain audit |
| Checkpoints   | CheckpointChunk | T = 1024-4096B, R = policy-driven | Chunked snapshot objects; rebuild from marker stream if lost |
| Indices       | IndexSegment (Page, Object, Manifest) | T = 1280-4096B, R = 20% default | Decode or rebuild-from-marker-scan |
| Page storage  | PageHistory | T = page_size, R = per-group | Decode from group symbols; on-the-fly repair on read |

CONCURRENCY PLANE (memory) — verbatim from spec:

| Subsystem          | ECS Role | Notes |
|--------------------|----------|-------|
| MVCC page history  | PageHistory objects (patch chains) | Bounded by GC horizon; compressed via intent log + structured patches |
| Conflict reduction | Intent logs as small ECS objects | Replayed deterministically for rebase merge |
| SSI witness plane  | ReadWitness / WriteWitness / WitnessIndexSegment / DependencyEdge / CommitProof | The serialization graph is itself a fountain-coded stream (§5.6.4, §5.7) |

REPLICATION PLANE (network) — verbatim from spec:

| Subsystem        | Transport Primitive | Notes |
|------------------|-------------------|-------|
| Symbol streaming | SymbolSink/SymbolStream | Symbol-native, not file-native |
| Anti-entropy     | ObjectId set reconciliation (IBLT) | O(delta) reconciliation; fallback to segment hash scan |
| Bootstrap        | CheckpointChunk symbol streaming | Late-join = collect K symbols |
| Multipath        | MultipathAggregator | Any K symbols from any path suffice |

ANTI-ENTROPY VIA IBLT (recommended):

Naive set reconciliation ("send me your ObjectIds") is O(|A|) bandwidth. Use an Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) to reconcile the symmetric difference in O(delta) where delta = |A symmetric_diff B|.

Protocol sketch:
1. Replica A builds IBLT over its ObjectId set in reconciliation scope
2. A sends IBLT to replica B
3. B subtracts its own ObjectIds from received IBLT and attempts to peel (decode)
4. On success: B obtains missing ObjectIds and requests needed symbols
5. If peeling fails (delta too large): B requests larger IBLT or falls back to segment-hash scan

Correctness-preserving: failure to peel is not silent; it degrades to slower fallback.

OBSERVABILITY PLANE (alien-artifact explainability):

| Subsystem             | Mechanism | Notes |
|-----------------------|-----------|-------|
| Repair auditing       | DecodeProof artifacts | Attached to lab traces when repair occurs |
| Schedule exploration  | LabRuntime deterministic trace | Reproducible concurrency bugs from a single seed |
| Invariant monitoring  | e-process monitors | MVCC invariants, memory bounds, replication divergence |
| Model checking        | TLA+ export of traces | Bounded model checking of commit/replication/recovery |

WILD BUT ALIGNED EXPERIMENTS (encouraged, feature-gated):
- Symbol-level RAID on single machine: Distribute symbols across multiple local devices/paths; any K reconstructs. RAID-like redundancy without strict striping constraints.
- Integrity sweeps as information theory: Periodically sample symbols and attempt partial decodes; use e-process monitors to detect elevated corruption rates early.

ENFORCEMENT RULE (normative): If a new feature persists bytes or ships bytes, it MUST declare its ECS object type, symbol policy, and repair story BEFORE implementation begins. This rule applies to all development, not just V1.

AUDIT CHECKLIST IMPLEMENTATION:

  struct PermeationEntry {
      subsystem: &'static str,
      object_type: &'static str,
      symbol_size_policy: &'static str,  // formula or range
      repair_story: &'static str,
      plane: Plane,  // Durability | Concurrency | Replication | Observability
  }

  enum Plane { Durability, Concurrency, Replication, Observability }

  static PERMEATION_MAP: &[PermeationEntry] = &[
      PermeationEntry { subsystem: "Commits", object_type: "CommitCapsule", symbol_size_policy: "T=min(page_size,4096), R=20%", repair_story: "decode from surviving symbols", plane: Durability },
      // ... all entries from tables above
  ];

  fn audit_permeation_map() -> Vec<AuditFailure> {
      // Verify every registered subsystem has a valid entry
      // Verify no subsystem is missing from the map
      // Return any gaps or inconsistencies
  }

title: §3.5.8-3.5.10 Decode Proofs + Deterministic Encoding + Symbol Size Policy
description:
Implement DecodeProofs, deterministic encoding seed derivation, and symbol size policy (§3.5.8-3.5.10, spec lines 3368-3422).

NOTE: This bead covers THREE distinct spec subsections (§3.5.8, §3.5.9, §3.5.10). Each is relatively small and closely related, so they are tracked together. If any subsection grows in scope during implementation, consider splitting into separate beads.

=== §3.5.8 DECODE PROOFS (Auditable Repair) ===

Asupersync includes a DecodeProof facility (asupersync::raptorq::proof). We exploit this in two critical ways:

1. IN LAB RUNTIME: Every decode that repairs corruption MUST produce a proof artifact attached to the test trace. This makes repair operations auditable and reproducible.

2. IN REPLICATION: A replica MAY demand proof artifacts for suspicious objects (e.g., repeated decode failures), enabling explainable "why did we reject this commit?" answers.

DecodeProof records:
- The set of symbol ESIs received
- Which symbols were repair vs source
- The intermediate decoder state at success/failure
- Timing metadata under LabRuntime (deterministic virtual time)

This is the "alien artifact" stance on repair: we do not merely fix things; we produce a mathematical witness that the fix is correct.

DecodeProof STRUCT:

  DecodeProof := {
      object_id       : ObjectId,
      k_source        : u32,
      symbols_received: Vec<u32>,    // ESIs of all symbols fed to decoder
      source_esis     : Vec<u32>,    // subset that were source symbols
      repair_esis     : Vec<u32>,    // subset that were repair symbols
      decode_success  : bool,
      intermediate_rank: Option<u32>, // decoder matrix rank at success/failure
      timing_ns       : u64,         // wall-clock or virtual time (LabRuntime)
      seed            : u64,         // RaptorQ seed used
  }

=== §3.5.9 DETERMINISTIC ENCODING (Seed Derivation from ObjectId) ===

If ObjectId is content-derived, symbol generation MUST be deterministic:
- The set of source symbols is deterministic by definition (payload chunking).
- Repair symbol generation MUST be deterministic for a given ObjectId and config.

PRACTICAL RULE (normative):
  - Derive any internal "repair schedule seed" from ObjectId:
    seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes)
  - Wire it through RaptorQConfig or sender construction as needed.

This makes "the object" a platonic mathematical entity: any replica can regenerate missing repair symbols (within policy) without coordination.

IMPLICATIONS:
1. Two replicas encoding the same object independently produce identical repair symbols.
2. A replica can verify repair symbols received from peers by regenerating them locally.
3. Repair symbols are content-addressed by (ObjectId, ESI) — dedup is automatic.
4. Symbol generation order does not matter; only (ObjectId, config) determines output.

SEED DERIVATION USES (cross-reference):
- ECS objects: seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes) (this section)
- Replication changesets: seed = xxh3_64(changeset_id_bytes) (§3.4.2)
- Both use the same pattern: xxh3_64 of the content-addressed identifier bytes.

=== §3.5.10 SYMBOL SIZE POLICY (Object-Type-Aware, Measured) ===

Symbol size is a major performance lever:
- Too small: too many symbols, higher metadata overhead, more routing work.
- Too large: worse cache behavior, higher per-symbol loss impact, more wasted decode work.

POLICY TABLE (verbatim from spec):

| Object Type       | Default Symbol Size      | Rationale |
|-------------------|--------------------------|-----------|
| CommitCapsule     | min(page_size, 4096)     | Aligns encoding with page boundaries; u16-bounded |
| IndexSegment      | 1280-4096 bytes          | Metadata-heavy; smaller symbols reduce tail loss impact |
| CheckpointChunk   | 1024-4096 bytes          | MTU-aware (prefer <=1366 on UDP); large objects use larger K/more blocks rather than huge T |
| PageHistory       | page_size (4096)         | Natural alignment with page boundaries |

NORMATIVE RULES:
1. All sizing is versioned in RootManifest so replicas decode correctly.
2. Benchmarks MUST drive tuning decisions; these defaults are starting points.
3. Symbol size for an object type MUST be consistent across all replicas for a given RootManifest version.
4. Changing symbol size policy requires a RootManifest version bump.

SYMBOL SIZE CONFIGURATION:

  struct SymbolSizePolicy {
      commit_capsule:     fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: min(page_size, 4096)
      index_segment:      fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: range 1280-4096
      checkpoint_chunk:   fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: range 1024-4096
      page_history:       fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: page_size
  }

  impl Default for SymbolSizePolicy {
      fn default() -> Self {
          Self {
              commit_capsule:   |ps| ps.min(4096),
              index_segment:    |_| 4096,
              checkpoint_chunk: |_| 4096,
              page_history:     |ps| ps,
          }
      }
  }

UNIT TESTS:

§3.5.8 Tests:
1. test_decode_proof_creation:
   Decode an object. DecodeProof MUST contain correct source/repair ESI sets.

2. test_decode_proof_lab_mode:
   Under LabRuntime, timing_ns uses deterministic virtual time.

3. test_decode_proof_failure_case:
   Attempt decode with insufficient symbols. DecodeProof records failure with intermediate_rank.

4. test_decode_proof_auditable:
   Given DecodeProof, verify the decode can be reproduced (same seed, same ESIs -> same result).

5. test_decode_proof_attached_to_trace:
   In lab runtime, every repair decode produces proof attached to test trace.

§3.5.9 Tests:
6. test_seed_derivation_deterministic:
   seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes). Same ObjectId -> same seed across calls.

7. test_seed_derivation_different_objects:
   Different ObjectIds -> different seeds (with overwhelming probability).

8. test_deterministic_repair_generation:
   Same ObjectId + same config -> identical repair symbols. Different ObjectId -> different symbols.

9. test_cross_replica_determinism:
   Two independent encoders with same ObjectId produce byte-identical repair symbols.

§3.5.10 Tests:
10. test_symbol_size_commit_capsule:
    page_size=4096: T = min(4096, 4096) = 4096.
    page_size=65536: T = min(65536, 4096) = 4096.

11. test_symbol_size_page_history:
    page_size=4096: T = 4096.
    page_size=65536: T = 65536.

12. test_symbol_size_versioned_in_manifest:
    RootManifest contains symbol size policy version. Replicas use same version.

13. test_symbol_size_consistency:
    All SymbolRecords for an object MUST have same T (OTI.T == symbol_size).

PROPERTY TESTS:

14. prop_seed_no_collision:
    For 100,000 random ObjectIds, all seeds are distinct (probabilistic).

15. prop_symbol_size_within_bounds:
    For all object types and valid page_sizes (512..65536), symbol size is within expected range.

E2E TESTS:

16. test_e2e_decode_proof_on_repair:
    Store object with repair symbols. Corrupt 2 source symbols. Decode succeeds. DecodeProof emitted with correct metadata.

17. test_e2e_deterministic_cross_node:
    Two nodes independently encode same object. Symbols are byte-identical.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- DecodeProof type implemented with all required fields
- Lab runtime always produces proofs on repair decodes
- Seed derivation via xxh3_64(object_id_bytes) is deterministic and wired through
- Symbol size policy per object type implemented with defaults
- Policy versioned in RootManifest
- Cross-replica determinism verified

title: §3.5.11 Tiered Storage (Bottomless, Native Mode)
description:
Implement tiered storage for Native mode — effectively bottomless history via remote object offload (§3.5.11, spec lines 3424-3498).

THREE TIERS:
- L1 (hot): In-memory caches (ARC for decoded objects + hot pages)
- L2 (warm): Local append-only symbol logs (ecs/symbols/ and ecs/markers/) — default source of truth
- L3 (cold): Remote object storage (S3/R2/Blob) keyed by ObjectId (optionally by (ObjectId, ESI) for symbol-addressable fetch)

REMOTE DURABILITY MODES:
- PRAGMA durability = local: L2 sufficient, L3 optional (archival/time-travel)
- PRAGMA durability = quorum(M): L3/peers participate in durability contract, commit not successful until quorum acknowledges enough symbols

REMOTE TIER INTEGRATION (asupersync normative):
- L3 fetch/upload MUST require RemoteCap in Cx. Without it, fail with explicit error, no network I/O
- Remote operations as named computations (ComputationName, no closure shipping)
- Remote fetch/upload MUST be idempotent (IdempotencyKey derived from request bytes + ecs_epoch)
- Multi-step workflows use Saga discipline: complete or compensations leave system in 'never happened' state

EVICTION POLICY:
- Operates at granularity of rotated log segments (not individual objects)
- MAY evict from L2 only if: every reachable object retrievable from L3 with enough symbols for decode AND segment not needed for in-flight read/repair
- MUST be cancel-safe: keep locally OR prove fully retrievable remotely before deleting

FETCH-ON-DEMAND READ PATH:
1. Try local systematic fast path (§3.5.2)
2. Request missing symbols from L3/peers under Cx budget (source symbols first, then repairs)
3. Decode (emit DecodeProof in lab/debug)
4. Populate L1, optionally write-back repaired symbols to L2 (self-healing cache fill)

RETENTION: Orthogonal to GC horizons. GC horizons = correctness for current ops. Retention = how much history kept for time travel/audit. Default: retain full commit history, cold eligible for L3-only.

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_l3_fetch_requires_remote_cap: Attempt L3 fetch without RemoteCap in Cx; verify it fails with explicit error and no network I/O occurs
- test_l3_upload_idempotency_key: Upload same object twice with same IdempotencyKey; verify deduplication (second upload returns recorded outcome, not double-write)
- test_eviction_cancel_safety: Start segment eviction (upload to L3), cancel mid-upload; verify local segment is retained and not deleted
- test_eviction_precondition_check: Attempt to evict L2 segment when L3 does not have enough symbols for decode; verify eviction is rejected
- test_fetch_on_demand_systematic_fast_path: Store object with systematic symbols in L2; verify fetch uses fast path (no RaptorQ decode needed for systematic ESIs)
- test_fetch_on_demand_repair_fallback: Store object with missing systematic symbols; verify fetch requests repair symbols from L3 and successfully decodes
- test_durability_mode_local_no_remote: Set PRAGMA durability=local; verify commits succeed without any L3 interaction
- test_durability_mode_quorum_requires_ack: Set PRAGMA durability=quorum(2); verify commit blocks until quorum of peers acknowledge sufficient symbols

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_tiered_storage_evict_and_fetch.rs: Write 500 commits to database, evict cold segments from L2 to a mock L3 store, then read historical data (time-travel query) that requires fetching from L3; verify all pages materialize correctly via fetch-on-demand path with self-healing cache fill back to L2.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] L3 operations are impossible without RemoteCap in Cx (compile-time or runtime enforcement)
- [ ] Eviction is cancel-safe: interrupted eviction never deletes local data before proving remote retrievability
- [ ] Fetch-on-demand correctly falls back from systematic fast path to RaptorQ decode when symbols are missing
- [ ] PRAGMA durability=local commits succeed with zero remote I/O
- [ ] Multi-step eviction workflows follow Saga discipline (complete or compensate to clean state)

title: Understand and Verify RaptorQ Encoding Pipeline (§3.2.3)
description:
Ensure deep understanding and verification of the 5-step RaptorQ encoding process. While FrankenSQLite uses asupersync implementation (not re-implementing RFC 6330), correct integration requires understanding every step.

SPEC REFERENCE: §3.2.3 (Encoding Step by Step)

THE 5 ENCODING STEPS:

STEP 1: DETERMINE CODING PARAMETERS
Given K source symbols C_prime[0], C_prime[1], ..., C_prime[K-1]:

1. Look up K_prime in the systematic index table (RFC 6330 Table 2). K_prime is the smallest value in the table >= K. Examples:
   - K = 5 -> K_prime = 6
   - K = 10 -> K_prime = 10
   - K = 100 -> K_prime = 101

2. Pad source block with (K_prime - K) zero symbols to get exactly K_prime source symbols: C_prime[0], ..., C_prime[K-1], 0, 0, ..., 0.

3. For K_prime, the systematic index table also defines:
   - J(K_prime): the systematic index (used in the Tuple generator)
   - S(K_prime): the number of LDPC symbols
   - H(K_prime): the number of HDPC symbols
   - W(K_prime): the LT generator modulus parameter

4. L = K_prime + S + H: the total number of intermediate symbols.

FrankenSQLite relies on asupersync RFC 6330 implementation for these derivations; do NOT substitute ad-hoc formulas.

STEP 2: CONSTRUCT THE CONSTRAINT MATRIX A (L x L)
The constraint matrix A encodes the relationship between intermediate symbols C[0], ..., C[L-1] and the source/constraint data. A is divided into three regions:

```
A (L x L matrix):
    Rows 0 to S-1:          LDPC constraints (sparse, over GF(2))
    Rows S to S+H-1:        HDPC constraints (dense, over GF(256))
    Rows S+H to L-1:        LT constraints for source symbols (sparse, over GF(2))

         |<--- K_prime cols --->|<- S cols ->|<- H cols ->|
    LDPC |   LDPC_LEFT         | I_S(SxS)   |   0        |  S rows
    HDPC |   MT * GAMMA        |   0         | I_H(HxH)  |  H rows
    LT   |   LT_MATRIX         |   0         |   0        |  K_prime rows
```

LDPC ROWS (0..S-1):
Each LDPC row has approximately 3 * ceil(K_prime/S) non-zero entries in the leftmost K_prime columns, plus a 1 on the diagonal of the S x S identity block. Sparse and binary (GF(2)).

LDPC constraint generation (RFC 6330 §5.3.3.3):
```
For j = 0 to K_prime-1:
    a = 1 + floor(j / S)
    b = j % S
    A[b][j] = 1
    b = (b + a) % S
    A[b][j] = 1
    b = (b + a) % S
    A[b][j] = 1
```
Additionally, column K_prime + i is set to 1 for row i (the S x S identity block).
Each source column contributes exactly 3 nonzeros, total LDPC nonzeros = 3*K_prime.

HDPC ROWS (S..S+H-1):
Dense over GF(256). Generated using:
1. The MT matrix (H x (K_prime+S)), computed from a random walk using the Rand function
2. The GAMMA matrix ((K_prime+S) x (K_prime+S)), structured matrix over GF(256) defined by alpha (primitive element)
These rows provide the algebraic strength that makes RaptorQ achieve near-optimal failure probability. They are the reason GF(256) is used.

LT ROWS (S+H..L-1):
Row S+H+i corresponds to source symbol C_prime[i]. Generated by the Tuple function:
```
(d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) = Tuple(K_prime, i)

Row S+H+i has 1s at positions:
    b                          (always)
    (b + a) mod W              (if d >= 2)
    (b + 2*a) mod W            (if d >= 3)
    ...
    (b + (d-1)*a) mod W        (if degree is d)
Plus "permanent inactivation" entries from d1, a1, b1 in columns W..K_prime-1
```

STEP 3: BUILD THE SOURCE VECTOR D (L entries)
```
D[0..S-1]      = zero symbols (LDPC constraints have zero right-hand side)
D[S..S+H-1]    = zero symbols (HDPC constraints have zero right-hand side)
D[S+H..L-1]    = C_prime[0], C_prime[1], ..., C_prime[K_prime-1] (padded source symbols)
```

STEP 4: SOLVE A * C = D FOR INTERMEDIATE SYMBOLS
Find intermediate symbols C[0], ..., C[L-1] such that A * C = D.
- A is L x L and invertible (by construction for valid K_prime)
- Standard linear system solve over GF(256)
- Gaussian elimination with nonzero pivot selection
- Matrix A structure (sparse LDPC + dense HDPC + sparse LT) is amenable to efficient elimination via inactivation decoding (§3.2.4)

STEP 5: GENERATE ENCODING SYMBOLS
Given intermediate symbols, any encoding symbol with Internal Symbol ID (ISI) X can be generated:

```
generate_symbol(X, K_prime, C[0..L-1]):
    if X < K_prime:
        return C_prime[X]    // systematic: return source symbol itself
    else:
        return LTEnc(K_prime, C[0..L-1], X)
```

LTEnc function for ISI X >= K_prime:
```
LTEnc(K_prime, C[0..L-1], X):
    (d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) = Tuple(K_prime, X)
    result = C[b]
    for j in 1..d:
        b = (b + a) mod W
        result = result XOR C[b]
    // Permanent inactivation component
    while b1 >= L:
        b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
    result = result XOR C[b1]
    for j in 1..d1:
        b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
        while b1 >= L:
            b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
        result = result XOR C[b1]
    return result
```

KEY INSIGHT -- SYSTEMATIC PROPERTY:
For ISI X < K_prime, the encoding symbol is EXACTLY the source symbol C_prime[X]. This means in the no-loss case, the receiver already has all K source symbols and no decoding is needed. Repair symbols (ISI >= K_prime) are generated ONLY as redundancy.

VERIFICATION TEST CASES:
1. For K=5: encode, verify first 5 encoding symbols are identity (systematic property)
2. For K=100: encode, verify first 100 symbols are identity, generate 10 repair symbols
3. Constraint matrix A: verify dimensions are L x L, verify LDPC rows are sparse/binary, verify HDPC rows are dense/GF(256), verify LT rows match Tuple output
4. Intermediate symbol solve: verify A * C = D after solving
5. Round-trip: encode K symbols, generate K+2 repair symbols, verify decode recovers original
6. Zero-padding: K=5, K_prime=6, verify the 6th source symbol is zero
7. LTEnc: spot-check specific ISIs against known-good asupersync output

E2E TEST:
- Encode database pages (K=64, page_size=4096), generate 4 repair symbols (ISIs 64..67)
- Verify source symbols 0..63 are identity (page data unchanged)
- Drop 2 random source symbols, replace with repair symbols, decode, verify all 64 pages recovered
- Encode with K=56403 (max), verify no panics/overflows

CRATE: Integration tests in fsqlite-harness against asupersync::raptorq
ACCEPTANCE: End-to-end encoding test passes. Systematic property verified. Repair symbols decode correctly. Constraint matrix structure verified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Encoding pipeline structure matches the spec and is verified against `asupersync::raptorq` (stage sequence + constraint-matrix structure assertions).
- [ ] Unit tests listed in the §3.2.3 normalization comment for **bd-1hi.3** are implemented and pass (stages, correctness, systematic property, determinism).
- [ ] E2E test `test_e2e_encode_decode_pipeline` passes on a realistic page set (e.g., 1000 pages, T=4096) with deterministic output.
- [ ] Logging requirements implemented: `tracing` span per stage with required fields; failures emit one structured ERROR with ISI + small digests (no full buffers).

title: §3.5.12 Adaptive Redundancy (Anytime-Valid Durability Autopilot)
description:
Unit Test Requirements:
- test_bd_1hi_30_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_30_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement adaptive redundancy control loop with formal guarantees (§3.5.12, spec lines 3499-3627).

CORE THESIS: Static redundancy assumptions are a correctness risk. RaptorQ redundancy is a control loop with formal guarantees: monitor symbol health with anytime-valid tests, raise redundancy when evidence indicates durability budget violated.

KEY ENABLING FACT: Repair symbol generation is deterministic → redundancy is appendable (add repair symbols later without changing ObjectId or rewriting).

DURABILITY BUDGETS (§3.5.12.1, per object type):
- p_symbol_budget: max acceptable symbol corruption probability per record
- epsilon_loss_budget: max acceptable probability object becomes undecodable
- slack_symbols: additive decode slack per source block (V1 default +2)
- CommitMarker/CommitProof MUST use conservative budgets (small objects clamp)

E-PROCESS MONITORING (§3.5.12.2):
- Bernoulli observation each symbol verify: X=1 if corrupt, X=0 otherwise
- Monitor H0: p <= p0 (p0 = p_symbol_budget). E-value > 1/alpha → reject (Ville's inequality)
- Monitoring MUST be separated from hot path: batch observations in decode/verification bookkeeping

LIVING CORRUPTION-RATE ESTIMATES (§3.5.12.2.1):
- Bayesian posterior: Beta(alpha0 + n_bad, beta0 + n_ok). Surface posterior mean and 99.9% credible bound
- IMPORTANT: Bayesian bounds NOT anytime-valid under optional stopping — diagnostics ONLY
- Safety-critical decisions MUST use anytime-valid bound p_upper (e-process inversion/martingale)
- PolicyController MAY use Bayesian for expected-loss ranking, MUST treat e-process as hard guardrail

AUTOPILOT POLICY (§3.5.12.3, when INV-SYMBOL-CORRUPTION rejects):
1. Raise redundancy for new objects: overhead := min(overhead_max, max(overhead_min, overhead * 2))
2. Retroactive hardening (background): generate+persist additional repair symbols for reachable objects. Union-only: can't invalidate prior decodes
3. Escalate integrity sweeps: increase frequency+sampling
4. Emit explainable evidence: evidence ledger with rejection, policy change, hardened objects

GRACEFUL DEGRADATION: If retroactive hardening can't decode (insufficient survivors) → surface 'durability contract violated' with decode proofs, halt operations claiming durable commit for unverifiable objects.

ALIEN-ARTIFACT QUALITY: Formal safety guarantees (optional stopping safe), explainability (evidence ledgers), self-healing (append-only deterministic), graceful degradation (repair or prove).

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Adaptive redundancy adjusts RaptorQ symbol overhead based on observed channel loss rate
- [ ] Anytime-valid durability guarantees hold under optional stopping (no matter when observation ceases)
- [ ] Evidence ledger entries for redundancy decisions are append-only and deterministically reproducible
- [ ] Self-healing repairs are triggered automatically when symbol loss exceeds configured threshold
- [ ] Graceful degradation: when repair is impossible, system produces a proof of insufficiency rather than silent corruption
close_reason: Implemented adaptive redundancy autopilot with p_upper hard guardrail, evidence-context retunes, and bd-1hi.30 unit/property/e2e compliance tests

title: §3.6.1-3.6.3 Native Index Types: VersionPointer + IndexSegments
description:
Implement VersionPointer and IndexSegment types for Native Mode coded indexing (§3.6.1-3.6.3, spec lines 3628-3658).

THE INDEX MUST ANSWER: Given (pgno, snapshot), find newest committed version V where V.commit_seq <= snapshot.high, plus pointer to bytes/intent recipe to materialize V.

VERSION POINTER (atom of lookup):
  VersionPointer { commit_seq: u64, patch_object: ObjectId, patch_kind: PatchKind (FullImage|IntentLog|SparseXor), base_hint: Option<ObjectId> }
Stable and replicable: references content-addressed objects, not physical offsets.

INDEX SEGMENT TYPES (all ECS objects):
1. PageVersionIndexSegment: Maps Pgno → VersionPointer for specific commit range. Includes bloom filters for fast 'not present' checks
2. ObjectLocatorSegment: Maps ObjectId → Vec<SymbolLogOffset>. Accelerator for finding symbols on disk. Rebuildable by scanning symbol logs
3. ManifestSegment: Maps commit_seq ranges to IndexSegment ObjectIds. Used for bootstrapping

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_version_pointer_serialization_roundtrip: Serialize and deserialize VersionPointer with all PatchKind variants (FullImage, IntentLog, SparseXor) and with/without base_hint; verify field-level equality
- test_page_version_index_segment_lookup: Insert 50 (pgno, VersionPointer) entries covering commit range [10,60], verify lookup returns correct newest version for a given (pgno, snapshot.high)
- test_page_version_index_segment_bloom_filter: Verify bloom filter returns false for pages not in segment (zero false negatives) and measure false positive rate stays below configured threshold
- test_object_locator_segment_rebuild: Build ObjectLocatorSegment, then rebuild from scanning symbol logs; verify rebuilt segment produces identical lookups
- test_manifest_segment_bootstrap: Create ManifestSegment mapping commit_seq ranges to IndexSegment ObjectIds, verify bootstrap can locate correct segment for any commit_seq
- test_version_pointer_references_content_addressed: Verify VersionPointer.patch_object is a valid ObjectId (BLAKE3 content hash), not a physical offset
- test_index_segment_is_ecs_object: Verify each segment type can be encoded as an ECS object with valid ObjectId, symbol records, and repair symbols

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_native_index_lookup_path.rs: Commit 200 transactions modifying overlapping pages, build PageVersionIndexSegments covering the full commit range, then read each page under 10 different snapshot values and verify the lookup algorithm (§3.6.4) returns the correct newest visible version for each snapshot.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] VersionPointer correctly encodes all three PatchKind variants and round-trips through serialization
- [ ] PageVersionIndexSegment bloom filter has zero false negatives for contained pages
- [ ] ObjectLocatorSegment is rebuildable from symbol log scan with identical results
- [ ] ManifestSegment correctly maps arbitrary commit_seq to the covering IndexSegment
- [ ] All index segments are valid ECS objects (content-addressed, repairable via RaptorQ)
close_reason: Implemented PatchKind, VersionPointer, SymbolLogOffset, BloomFilter, PageVersionIndexSegment, ObjectLocatorSegment, ManifestSegment in fsqlite-types/src/ecs.rs. 30 total ECS tests pass (8 new for index types). Bloom filter with zero false negatives verified. All types support binary-search lookup, deterministic ordering, and rebuild-from-scan. Clippy clean.

title: §3.6.4-3.6.5 Native Index Lookup Algorithm + Segment Construction
description:
Unit Test Requirements:
- test_bd_1hi_32_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_32_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement the read-path lookup algorithm and background segment construction for coded indexes (§3.6.4-3.6.5, spec lines 3659-3677).

LOOKUP ALGORITHM (read page P under snapshot S):
1. Check Cache: Consult ARC cache for visible committed version
2. Check Filter: Version Presence Filter (Bloom/Quotient). If 'no versions', read base page
3. Index Scan: Scan PageVersionIndexSegments backwards from S.high until visible version found
4. Fetch and Materialize: Fetch patch_object (repair via RaptorQ if needed). If full image → return. If patch/intent → apply to base page (recursively if needed)

SEGMENT CONSTRUCTION (background, deterministic):
- Segment Builder consumes commit marker stream
- Accumulates Pgno → VersionPointer updates in memory
- Periodically flushes new PageVersionIndexSegment covering [start_seq, end_seq]
- Construction is DETERMINISTIC: stable map iteration order, stable encoding → all replicas build identical index segments

TESTS: lookup with cache hit, lookup with bloom filter negative, lookup through index scan, patch materialization (full image + intent log + sparse XOR), segment builder round-trip, determinism verification (same input → same segment ObjectId).

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Native index lookup returns correct results for point queries and range scans across all stored key types
- [ ] Segment construction round-trips correctly: build segment from data, read back, verify identical content
- [ ] Patch materialization correctly combines full image + intent log + sparse XOR to produce final page state
- [ ] Determinism verification passes: same input always produces the same segment ObjectId

title: §3.6.6-3.6.7 Native Index Repair/Rebuild + Boldness Constraint
description:
Unit Test Requirements:
- test_bd_1hi_33_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_33_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement index repair, rebuild, and enforce the boldness constraint (§3.6.6-3.6.7, spec lines 3678-3692).

REPAIR AND REBUILD (because IndexSegments are ECS objects):
- Repair: Missing/corrupt segments repaired by decoding from surviving symbols (local or remote)
- Rebuild: If segment irretrievably lost, rebuild by re-scanning commit marker stream and capsules
- Diagnostics: 'Index unrebuildable but commit markers exist' = critical integrity failure

BOLDNESS CONSTRAINT: Coded index segments ship in V1. NOT a 'Phase 9 nice-to-have'. The index is part of the fundamental ECS thesis: if durability, storage, and transport are all object-based and symbol-native, then the index MUST be too. Fallbacks (linear marker-stream scan) exist ONLY as emergency escape hatches, activated only after conformance/performance data proves a need.

TESTS: repair from surviving symbols, full rebuild from marker stream scan, critical integrity failure detection, fallback linear scan (emergency only).

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Native index repair reconstructs a valid index from surviving RaptorQ symbols without full rebuild
- [ ] Full rebuild from marker stream scan produces an index identical to the original (deterministic)
- [ ] Critical integrity failures are detected and reported with specific error codes before any repair attempt
- [ ] Fallback linear scan (emergency mode) correctly locates all entries when index is completely destroyed
- [ ] Boldness constraint limits repair aggressiveness to prevent cascading corruption
