Implement observability/diagnostics and the PolicyController service (§4.16-4.17, spec lines 5112-5330).

OBSERVABILITY (§4.16):
- Task inspector: live visibility into blocked reasons, budget usage, mask depth, held obligations, cancellation status
- Diagnostics: structured explanations for cancellation propagation and blocked tasks
- Deterministic repro bundles: when ASUPERSYNC_TEST_ARTIFACTS_DIR set, failures emit repro manifest + trace artifacts

EVIDENCE LEDGER (§4.16.1):
- Bounded, deterministic record of WHY decisions occurred (trace-backed, replay-stable)
- Covers: cancellation propagation, race/timeout/hedge winners, scheduler choices, commit/abort decisions
- Commit-ledger rule: if decision influenced by contention telemetry, include regime_id, writers_active, M2_hat/P_eff_hat, f_merge, expected losses
- EvidenceEntry schema: decision_id, kind, context, candidates, constraints, chosen, rationale, witnesses
- Determinism: stable field ordering, candidate ordering, witness references
- Emission: Lab=always for failures/SSI aborts. Production=sampleable, no unbounded overhead

POLICY CONTROLLER (§4.17):
- Tunes non-correctness knobs using principled math. MUST NOT change correctness semantics
- Inputs: e-processes, conformal budgets, BOCPD regime detection, local telemetry
- Decision rule: expected loss minimization: a* = argmin E[L(a, state) | evidence]
- Guardrails: MUST NOT violate active e-process budget. BOCPD shift → MAY retune but MUST emit evidence ledger
- Explainability: every auto policy change emits evidence ledger entry
- Determinism in lab: no wall-clock, no hash randomization
- VOI budgeting: schedule optional monitors by Value of Information under CPU/I/O budgets

AUTO-TUNING (§4.17.1):
- PRAGMA fsqlite.auto_tune = ON|OFF (default ON)
- PRAGMA fsqlite.profile = balanced|latency|throughput
- PRAGMA fsqlite.bg_cpu_max, remote_max_in_flight, commit_encode_max (0=auto, positive=hard cap)
- Derived defaults: clamp(P/8, 1, 16) for balanced, sublinear scaling
- Hysteresis required, BOCPD shifts reset calibration windows
- Graceful fallback: auto_tune OFF → use derived defaults, safe but potentially slower

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Observability layer emits structured tracing events with correct span hierarchy and field types
- [ ] Evidence ledger records all policy decisions with timestamps, inputs, and outcomes for auditability
- [ ] Policy controller applies hysteresis to prevent oscillation, with BOCPD shifts resetting calibration windows
- [ ] Graceful fallback engages correctly: auto_tune OFF uses derived defaults without performance cliff
- [ ] Observability overhead scales sublinearly with transaction throughput

title: §4.18 Epochs (Validity Windows + Coordination)
description:
Implement EpochClock and epoch coordination (§4.18). Includes SymbolValidityWindow, epoch-scoped symbol auth key derivation (§4.18.2), and the Epoch Transition Barrier (§4.18.4) for quiescent configuration changes.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_epoch_id_monotone: Increment ecs_epoch 100 times; verify it is strictly monotonically increasing and never reused
- test_symbol_validity_window_rejects_future: Create symbol with epoch_id > RootManifest.ecs_epoch; verify it is rejected by SymbolValidityWindow check
- test_symbol_validity_window_accepts_past: Create symbol with epoch_id < RootManifest.ecs_epoch; verify it is accepted (time travel + full history retention)
- test_epoch_scoped_key_derivation: Derive symbol auth key for epoch 5 and epoch 6 from same master_key; verify keys are different; re-derive for epoch 5; verify deterministic (same result)
- test_epoch_key_derivation_domain_separation: Verify auth key derived from encryption DEK uses domain separation ("fsqlite:symbol-auth-master:v1"); key != DEK
- test_epoch_transition_barrier_all_arrive: Create EpochBarrier with 4 participants; have all 4 arrive; verify barrier completes with AllArrived and epoch increments
- test_epoch_transition_barrier_timeout: Create EpochBarrier with 4 participants and timeout; have only 3 arrive; verify barrier aborts on Timeout and epoch does NOT increment
- test_epoch_bootstrap_from_ecs_root: Before RootManifest is decoded, verify engine uses EcsRootPointer.ecs_epoch as provisional upper bound and rejects symbols with higher epoch

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_epoch_transition_quiescence.rs: Start database with active WriteCoordinator, SymbolStore, Replicator, and CheckpointerGc; trigger an epoch transition (e.g., quorum membership change); verify all participants drain in-flight work, arrive at the barrier, epoch increments durably in RootManifest, SharedMemoryLayout.ecs_epoch is updated with Release ordering, and new symbols use the new epoch.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] ecs_epoch is strictly monotone and durably stored in RootManifest
- [ ] SymbolValidityWindow rejects symbols from future epochs (fail-closed)
- [ ] Symbol auth keys are deterministically derived from (master_key, ecs_epoch) with BLAKE3 domain separation
- [ ] Epoch transition barrier is all-or-nothing: either all participants arrive or epoch does not advance
- [ ] Auth tag failures cause symbol rejection (fail-closed, no silent acceptance)

## Testing Requirements for §4.18-4.19 Epochs + Remote Effects (Integration Level)

### Epoch Integration Tests (§4.18, fsqlite-harness crate)

15. **test_epoch_barrier_participants_drain_before_arriving**: WriteCoordinator has in-flight commits. Verify it drains them before arriving at barrier (no straddle).
16. **test_epoch_barrier_cancelled_aborts**: Create barrier. Cancel during wait. Verify abort (remain in old epoch).

### Remote Effects Integration Tests (§4.19)

**Global remote bulkhead:**
17. **test_remote_bulkhead_caps_concurrency**: Set remote_max_in_flight=4. Submit 10 remote ops. Verify at most 4 run concurrently.
18. **test_remote_bulkhead_prevents_retry_storms**: Remote tier fails, causing retries. Verify bulkhead prevents unbounded concurrent retries.

19. **test_no_remote_cap_no_network_io**: Create Cx without RemoteCap. Attempt remote operation. Verify refusal (compile-time or runtime).
20. **test_native_mode_works_without_remote**: Open database in native mode with durability=local. Verify full functionality without RemoteCap.

**Cross-subsection integration:**
21. **test_epoch_transition_with_remote_durability**: Configure durability=quorum(2). Perform epoch transition. Verify remote requests carry ecs_epoch. Verify peers reject requests outside SymbolValidityWindow.
22. **test_saga_eviction_with_epoch_scoped_auth**: Evict segment to L3 (saga). Verify symbols are auth-tagged with current epoch's K_epoch. Verify remote accepts within validity window.
23. **test_full_remote_lifecycle_in_lab**: In lab with VirtualTcp, perform: symbol_put_batch -> symbol_get_range -> verify correctness. All under epoch-scoped auth. All with idempotency keys.

**Lease-backed liveness (§4.19.3):**
24. **test_lease_expiry_escalates**: Acquire remote handle with lease. Let lease expire (simulate slow remote). Verify escalation (cancel/retry/fail). Verify trace-visible.

### End-to-End Scenario

25. **test_epoch_transition_full_ceremony**: Full sequence: (1) create barrier, (2) drain all participants, (3) all arrive, (4) increment epoch, (5) update RootManifest, (6) update SharedMemoryLayout, (7) derive new K_epoch, (8) update SymbolValidityWindow. Verify each step via trace.

### Logging Requirements
- INFO: Epoch transition (old_epoch -> new_epoch, reason, participants)
- DEBUG: Barrier participant arrival (service name, drain time)
- WARN: Epoch barrier timeout (participants arrived vs expected)
- INFO: Remote operation submission (computation name, ecs_epoch, idempotency key)
- WARN: Symbol rejected for future epoch (epoch_id, current_epoch)
- DEBUG: Key derivation (epoch, domain separation context — NOT the key itself)
- ERROR: Auth failure on symbol (object_id, epoch_id, expected vs actual tag hash prefix)

**Spec reference:** COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md, lines ~5331–5429

## Definition (Normative)
- `ecs_epoch: EpochId` is a monotone `u64` stored durably in `RootManifest.ecs_epoch` (§3.5.5) and mirrored in `SharedMemoryLayout.ecs_epoch` (§5.6.1).
- `ecs_epoch` increments only under a serialized coordinator decision.
- Epochs MUST NOT be reused.

## §4.18.1 SymbolValidityWindow (Normative Default)

```
SymbolValidityWindow := [0, RootManifest.ecs_epoch]
```

Bootstrap rule (required): before `RootManifest` is decoded, use `EcsRootPointer.ecs_epoch` from `ecs/root` as provisional upper bound; reject any symbol segments with `epoch_id > root_epoch` while loading; after decoding, enforce `RootManifest.ecs_epoch == root_epoch`.

Fail-closed rule: symbols tagged with `epoch_id > RootManifest.ecs_epoch` MUST be rejected as misconfiguration or replay from an incompatible future configuration.

## §4.18.2 Epoch-Scoped Symbol Authentication Key Derivation (Required)
When symbol auth is enabled (§3.5.2), verification key MUST be derived deterministically from `(master_key, ecs_epoch)`:

```
K_epoch = BLAKE3_KEYED(master_key, "fsqlite:symbol-auth:epoch:v1" || le_u64(ecs_epoch))
```

Master key source (normative):
- production with page encryption: derive `master_key` from DEK with domain separation:
  `master_key = BLAKE3_KEYED(DEK, "fsqlite:symbol-auth-master:v1")`
- production without encryption: enabling `symbol_auth=on` MUST require explicit `SymbolAuthMasterKeyCap` via `Cx` (no ambient keys)
- lab: derive deterministically from seed for replay stability

Auth failures MUST fail closed (invalid/missing auth_tag rejects symbol for decoding).

## §4.18.3 Epoch-Scoped Remote Durability Configuration (Required)
If durability depends on remote acknowledgements (`PRAGMA durability = quorum(M)`):
- requests MUST carry `ecs_epoch`
- peers MUST reject requests outside their SymbolValidityWindow

## §4.18.4 Epoch Transition Barrier (Required)
Epoch transitions affecting correctness-critical policy MUST establish a quiescence point so no commit straddles epochs.

Barrier protocol (normative):
- coordinator creates `EpochBarrier(current_epoch, participants=N, timeout)`
- participants: WriteCoordinator, SymbolStore, Replicator, CheckpointGc
- each participant arrives only after draining in-flight work binding to old epoch
- on AllArrived: coordinator increments `RootManifest.ecs_epoch` (durable), then updates `SharedMemoryLayout.ecs_epoch` (Release)
- on Timeout/Cancelled: transition MUST abort (remain in old epoch) unless explicitly forced

## Test Plan Note
This bead already contains an integration-level test matrix in earlier comments. Keep those tests, but ensure (1) the bootstrap fail-closed rules are explicitly tested and (2) key derivation is replay-stable in lab mode.

- `RootManifest.ecs_epoch` and `SharedMemoryLayout.ecs_epoch` converge correctly
- `SymbolValidityWindow` rules are enforced (fail-closed on future epoch symbols)

The E2E run MUST emit an audit-style trace of the transition steps with old/new epoch and participant drain times.

title: §4.20 Scheduler Priority Lanes (Cancel/Timed/Ready)
description:
Implement scheduler priority lanes for tail latency control (§4.20, spec lines 5528-5547).

THREE LANES:
- Cancel lane (highest): cancellation/drain/finalizers, obligation completion, rollback/cleanup, coordinator cancel responses. MUST NOT be starved by background work
- Timed lane (EDF): user queries with deadlines, commit publication (marker append + response), tiered-storage reads for foreground queries
- Ready lane: background GC, compaction, checkpointing, anti-entropy, stats updates. MUST be rate_limited/bulkheaded (§4.15)

MAPPING: FrankenSQLite maps work to lanes via Cx budgets and task labeling

NORMATIVE RULE: Any long-running foreground loop MUST checkpoint frequently. SHOULD call cx.set_task_type("...") once at task start for deadline monitors and perf dashboards.

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_cancel_lane_highest_priority: Enqueue tasks in all three lanes simultaneously; verify Cancel lane tasks execute before Timed and Ready lane tasks
- test_timed_lane_edf_ordering: Enqueue 5 Timed-lane tasks with different deadlines; verify they execute in earliest-deadline-first order
- test_ready_lane_does_not_starve_cancel: Flood the scheduler with 100 Ready-lane tasks; enqueue 1 Cancel-lane task; verify the Cancel task executes within one scheduling cycle (not starved)
- test_ready_lane_does_not_starve_timed: Flood scheduler with Ready-lane background work; enqueue a Timed-lane user query with 10ms deadline; verify it is scheduled before Ready work and meets deadline
- test_task_type_labeling: Create task with cx.set_task_type("vdbe_query"); verify deadline monitor can inspect and bucket the task by its type label
- test_checkpoint_frequency_in_long_loop: Run a VDBE instruction loop of 10000 opcodes; verify cx.checkpoint() is called at least once per VDBE instruction boundary
- test_lane_assignment_from_cx_budget: Create Cx with deadline budget; verify task is assigned to Timed lane; create Cx with no deadline; verify task is assigned to Ready lane

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_scheduler_lanes_tail_latency.rs: Run a mixed workload with foreground queries (Timed lane, 50ms deadline), background GC/compaction (Ready lane), and triggered cancellations (Cancel lane); verify p99 foreground query latency stays below 50ms even under heavy background load, and Cancel-lane cleanup tasks always complete before the next scheduling epoch.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Cancel lane tasks are never starved by Timed or Ready lane work
- [ ] Timed lane tasks are scheduled in earliest-deadline-first order
- [ ] Ready lane background work is rate-limited and cannot degrade foreground p99 latency beyond configured thresholds
- [ ] All long-running foreground loops call cx.checkpoint() at every yield point
- [ ] Task type labeling enables deadline monitors to bucket and inspect tasks by class
close_reason: Implemented scheduler priority lanes module (scheduler.rs, 694 lines). 12 FsqliteTaskClass variants mapped to 3 SchedulerLane priorities (Cancel > Timed/EDF > Ready). CheckpointTracker for opcode-count-based checkpointing. Integration with asupersync PriorityScheduler via schedule_task() and lane_from_budget(). 11 tests all passing including E2E mixed workload separation.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Missing Algorithmic Detail (Audit Fix): Masked Critical Sections + Async Runtime Interaction

The bead covers the cancellation state machine but omits the masked critical sections protocol, depth bounds, and commit section semantics from §4.12.2-4.12.3.

### Cancellation State Machine (§4.12)

```
Created/Running -> CancelRequested -> Cancelling -> Finalizing -> Completed(Cancelled)
```

Invariants:
- **INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES:** Region cancellation MUST propagate to all descendant regions; parent cannot be cancelled while child remains uncancelled.
- **INV-CANCEL-IDEMPOTENT:** Multiple cancel requests are monotone: strongest cancel reason wins.
- **INV-LOSERS-DRAIN:** Any combinator returning early (race/timeout/hedge) MUST cancel and drain losers to completion before returning.

### Checkpoint Placement Rules (§4.12.1)

FrankenSQLite MUST place `cx.checkpoint()` / `cx.checkpoint_with(...)` at:
- VDBE instruction boundaries (each opcode tick)
- B-tree descent loops (every node visit)
- RaptorQ decode/encode loops (every fixed number of symbol operations)
- Any loop over user data (every N rows; N derived from budget poll_quota)

Rule: Any cancellation-unaware hot loop is a bug.

### Masked Critical Sections (§4.12.2, Cx::masked)

`Cx::masked(...)`: while masked, `checkpoint()` returns `Ok(())` even if cancellation is requested.

Purpose: short, atomic publication steps that must not be interrupted:
- Completing a reserved send/commit
- Publishing a marker after allocating commit_seq
- Releasing resources in required order

**INV-MASK-BOUNDED:** mask depth MUST be finite and bounded (`MAX_MASK_DEPTH = 64`). Exceeding bound = correctness failure (panic in lab; fatal diagnostic in production).

Rules:
- MUST NOT use masking for long operations (remote fetch, bulk decode, long scans)
- MAY wrap tiny durability-critical steps (marker publication + local fsync barriers)
- Every masked section MUST remain explicitly bounded (poll quota + leak-free obligation discipline)

### Commit Sections (§4.12.3, Bounded Masking for Two-Phase Protocols)

For logically atomic multi-operation protocol steps, use asupersync commit section helper:
- Masks cancellation while section in progress
- Enforces poll quota bound (bounded deferral)
- Guarantees finalizers run even on cancellation

Normative usage sites:
- **WriteCoordinator:** once FCW validation passes and commit_seq allocated, proof+marker publication MUST run as commit section (sequencer cannot emit "half a commit" under cancellation)
- **Witness publication:** once reservation committed, commit must complete or reservation must abort deterministically

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Unit Tests

Add focused unit tests for the cancellation protocol layer (asupersync integration). These should be deterministic and assert the invariants explicitly:

- `test_cancel_state_machine_monotone`: state transitions are monotone (`Running -> CancelRequested -> Cancelling -> Finalizing -> Completed(Cancelled)`), strongest cancel reason wins, repeated cancel is idempotent.
- `test_cancel_propagates_to_descendants`: cancelling a parent region cancels all descendants; no child may remain uncancelled if the parent is cancelled (INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES).
- `test_cancel_idempotent_multiple_sources`: cancellation requested from multiple sites yields a single cancellation outcome; repeated requests do not regress state (INV-CANCEL-IDEMPOTENT).
- `test_checkpoint_observes_cancellation_unmasked`: `cx.checkpoint()` returns cancellation promptly when not masked.
- `test_checkpoint_masks_cancellation_when_masked`: within `Cx::masked`, `checkpoint()` returns `Ok(())` even if cancellation is requested; cancellation is observed immediately after exiting the masked region.
- `test_mask_depth_bounded`: exceeding `MAX_MASK_DEPTH` triggers the specified failure mode (panic in lab mode; fatal diagnostic in production mode).
- `test_losers_drain_required`: any combinator that returns early (race/timeout/hedge) cancels and drains losers before returning (INV-LOSERS-DRAIN).

## E2E Test Scenarios

E2E here means: run real async pipelines under LabRuntime fault injection and verify cancellation never creates half-published state.

- `test_e2e_cancel_injected_at_all_checkpoints`: inject cancellation at every `checkpoint()` site (VDBE opcode ticks, btree descent loops, raptorq encode/decode loops). Assert no stuck tasks; all join handles resolve; no resource leaks.
- `test_e2e_cancel_injected_at_every_await`: for a representative pipeline (write coordinator + witness publication), inject cancellation at every `.await` point and verify post-state is coherent (either commit completes atomically, or abort leaves no visible partial artifacts).
- `test_e2e_commit_section_atomicity_under_cancel`: once a commit section begins (after reservation/commit_seq allocation), cancellation must not create a "half commit"; verify commit marker discipline and required finalizers.
- `test_e2e_mask_bounded_under_load`: stress nested masked sections under load; verify masks remain short (budget-respecting) and depth never exceeds bound.

All E2E scenarios MUST log a structured event stream including `trace_id`, `scenario_id`, `injection_point`, and `mask_depth` so failures can be replayed deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All invariants in §4.12 validated by unit tests (propagation, idempotence, bounded masking, losers-drain).
- LabRuntime E2E suite injects cancellation at every checkpoint and every await point for at least one realistic write pipeline.
- E2E failures provide deterministic replay inputs: `seed`, `schedule_fingerprint`, and a structured log including `trace_id` + `injection_point`.

title: §4.3 E-Processes: Anytime-Valid Invariant Monitoring
description:
Implement e-process monitors for all MVCC invariants (§4.3, spec lines 3997-4248).

E-PROCESS: Sequence (E_t) that is non-negative supermartingale under H0. E_0=1. Ville's inequality: P(exists t: E_t >= 1/alpha) <= alpha. Peek at any time, reject if E_t >= 1/alpha. No multiple-testing correction needed.

BETTING MARTINGALE: E_t = E_{t-1} * (1 + lambda * (X_t - p_0)). X_t is binary observation. Under H1 (p1>p0), grows at rate KL(p1||p0).

MIXTURE E-PROCESSES (recommended): E_mix(t) = sum_j w_j * E_{lambda_j}(t). Log grid of lambda values (16-64). Near-oracle power without hand-tuning. Maintain log-space (log-sum-exp).

MULTIPLE INVARIANTS: E-value aggregation (arithmetic mean): E_global(t) = sum_i w_i * E_i(t). Valid e-process under global null regardless of dependence. Alarm when E_global >= 1/alpha_total. Certificate includes top contributing monitors.

PER-INVARIANT CALIBRATION:
- INV-1 (Monotonicity): p0=1e-9, lambda=0.999, alpha=1e-6 (hardware enforced)
- INV-2 (Lock Exclusivity): p0=1e-9, lambda=0.999, alpha=1e-6 (CAS enforced)
- INV-3 (Version Chain Order): p0=1e-6, lambda=0.9, alpha=0.001
- INV-4 (Write Set Consistency): p0=1e-6, lambda=0.9, alpha=0.001
- INV-5 (Snapshot Stability): p0=1e-6, lambda=0.9, alpha=0.001
- INV-6 (Commit Atomicity): p0=1e-6, lambda=0.9, alpha=0.001
- INV-7 (Serialized Mode Exclusivity): p0=1e-9, lambda=0.999, alpha=1e-6

IMPLEMENTATION: EProcess struct wrapping asupersync::lab::oracle::eprocess. Observation function per invariant. Lock Exclusivity example provided in spec (cross-check lock_table vs txn lock sets).

NOTE: Detailed per-invariant tests are in bd-x1ww (framework) and bd-3q2k (MVCC monitors). This bead covers the integration-level tests that verify the e-process system works end-to-end within the lab runtime.

### Integration Tests (fsqlite-harness crate)

**E-process lifecycle:**
1. **test_eprocess_observe_no_violations_stays_near_one**: Run 10,000 observations with X_t=0. Verify E_t fluctuates near 1.0 (martingale property). Assert 0.5 < E_t < 2.0 after 10K steps.
2. **test_eprocess_single_violation_jumps**: Inject one violation (X_t=1) into a stream of clean observations. Verify E_t jumps by factor (1 + lambda * (1 - p0)). For INV-2 config (lambda=0.999, p0=1e-9), jump should be ~2.0.
3. **test_eprocess_repeated_violations_reject**: Inject violations at rate p1=0.01 (10x above p0=0.001 for INV-3). Verify rejection (E_t >= 1/alpha) within expected detection delay N_detect ~ log(1/alpha) / KL(p1 || p0).
4. **test_eprocess_mixture_no_lambda_tuning**: Verify mixture e-process (E_mix) detects violations across a range of true violation rates without hand-tuned lambda. Use log grid of 16 lambda values. Compare power to fixed-lambda at each p1.

**Global aggregation:**
5. **test_evalue_arithmetic_mean_aggregation**: Create 7 monitors (INV-1..INV-7) with equal weights w_i=1/7. Inject violation into INV-3 only. Verify E_global grows while other individual E_i stay near 1.0.
6. **test_evalue_global_rejects_on_single_invariant_failure**: With alpha_total=0.001, verify that persistent violations in any single invariant eventually cause E_global >= 1/alpha_total.
7. **test_evalue_no_false_alarm_under_null**: Run all 7 monitors for 100K steps under H0 (no violations). Verify E_global never exceeds 1/alpha_total. This validates the type-I error guarantee.

**Lab runtime integration:**
8. **test_eprocess_in_lab_runtime**: Create FsLab, spawn MVCC workload with 4 concurrent txns, attach all e-process monitors. Run to quiescence. Assert oracle_report.all_passed() AND all E_i < 1/alpha_i.
9. **test_eprocess_detects_injected_bug**: Modify lab harness to inject a subtle lock-ordering bug (INV-2 violation). Run with e-processes. Verify INV-2 monitor rejects H0 within 1000 observations.
10. **test_eprocess_certificate_on_rejection**: When an e-process rejects, verify it emits a certificate containing: invariant name, E_t value, threshold, observation count, and the violating observation details.

**Calibration validation:**
11. **test_per_invariant_calibration_matches_spec**: Verify each MVCC monitor's (p0, lambda, alpha) matches the spec values (INV-1: p0=1e-9, lambda=0.999, alpha=1e-6; INV-3: p0=1e-6, lambda=0.9, alpha=0.001; etc.).
12. **test_detection_delay_formula**: For each invariant, compute expected N_detect = log(1/alpha) / KL(p1 || p0) at representative p1. Run simulation. Verify empirical detection delay within 2x of theoretical.

### Property Tests
13. **prop_eprocess_supermartingale**: For random observation sequences under H0 (each X_t ~ Bernoulli(p0)), verify E[E_t | E_{t-1}] <= E_{t-1} (supermartingale property) empirically over 1000 sequences.
14. **prop_mixture_is_valid_eprocess**: Verify mixture e-process (sum of weighted components) satisfies E_0=1, E_t >= 0, and supermartingale property for any random weight vector.

### Logging Requirements

- DEBUG: Every 100th observation: current E_t, observation count, trend
- WARN: E_t exceeds 0.1/alpha (approaching rejection threshold)
- ERROR: E_t >= 1/alpha (rejection — invariant violation detected) with full certificate

title: §4.4 Mazurkiewicz Trace Monoid: Systematic Interleaving
description:
Implement Mazurkiewicz trace-based systematic concurrency testing (§4.4, spec lines 4249-4345).

CONCEPT: Standard testing uses random interleaving. Trace monoid enumerates ALL distinct interleavings up to commutativity of independent operations. Provides exhaustive coverage.

FORMAL: Trace monoid M(Sigma, I) with alphabet Sigma (MVCC actions) and independence relation I. Two words trace-equivalent if one can transform to other by swapping adjacent independent actions.

INDEPENDENCE RELATION FOR MVCC:
- read(T1,P1) vs read(T2,P2): Independent (P1!=P2 or same page MVCC snapshots)
- read(T1,P) vs write(T2,P): DEPENDENT
- write(T1,P1) vs write(T2,P2): Independent if P1!=P2
- write(T1,P) vs write(T2,P): DEPENDENT
- commit(T1) vs commit(T2): DEPENDENT (serialized by coordinator)
- begin(T1) vs begin(T2): DEPENDENT (snapshot capture ordering)

FOATA NORMAL FORM: Canonical representative where events organized into layers of mutually independent events. Deterministic sort within layers. Dramatically reduces exploration space.

VERIFICATION: For each trace equivalence class, verify: SI holds, FCW correctly identifies conflicts, GC never reclaims needed versions.

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Mazurkiewicz trace equivalence classes are correctly computed for all pairs of independent operations
- [ ] Trace reduction demonstrably reduces exploration space compared to naive interleaving enumeration
- [ ] For each trace equivalence class, SI holds and FCW correctly identifies conflicts
- [ ] GC never reclaims versions needed by any transaction within the trace exploration

title: §4.5 Two-Phase MPSC Channels: Write Coordinator Pipeline
description:
Implement the cancel-safe two-phase MPSC commit pipeline (§4.5, spec lines 4346-4491).

TWO-PHASE PROTOCOL:
- Phase 1 (Reserve): tx.reserve(cx).await → SendPermit. If cancelled: slot auto-released (cancel-safe)
- Phase 2 (Commit): permit.send(req) — synchronous, cannot fail. Or permit.abort() to release without sending

CANCEL-SAFETY: Between reserve() and send(), dropping permit auto-releases slot. No ghost entries in pipeline, no consumed slots without messages, no coordinator hangs.

CHANNEL CAPACITY (Little's Law derivation):
- C >= lambda * t_commit. Default: 16
- At burst 4x peak (148K/sec), amortized t_commit=40us: C >= 6. With 2.5x jitter margin: 15 ≈ 16
- Adjustable via PRAGMA fsqlite.commit_channel_capacity

BACKPRESSURE: At most C write sets buffered. Full channel signals saturation via blocked reserve(). FIFO ordering prevents starvation.

OPTIMAL BATCH SIZE: N_opt = sqrt(t_fsync / t_validate). For t_fsync=2ms, t_validate=5us: N_opt=20. Capacity of 16 is near-optimal.

CONFORMAL BATCH SIZE CONTROL (recommended): Use conformal upper quantiles within BOCPD regime. Ring buffers of fsync_samples and validate_samples. N_conformal = clamp(round(sqrt(q_fsync/q_validate)), 1, C). Reset calibration windows on BOCPD regime shift.

TRACKED VARIANT: asupersync::channel::session::TrackedSender for safety-critical channels. Dropped permit without send/abort = structurally detected.

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_two_phase_reserve_then_send: Reserve a slot, send a CommitRequest, verify coordinator receives it in FIFO order
- test_two_phase_cancel_during_reserve: Start reserve() on a full channel, cancel the task; verify no slot is consumed and channel capacity is unchanged
- test_two_phase_drop_permit_releases_slot: Reserve a slot (getting SendPermit), drop the permit without calling send(); verify the slot is released and channel has original capacity
- test_backpressure_blocks_at_capacity: Fill channel to capacity (16), attempt another reserve(); verify the caller blocks until a slot is freed
- test_fifo_ordering_under_contention: Submit 100 CommitRequests from 10 concurrent writers; verify coordinator processes them in FIFO reserve order
- test_tracked_sender_detects_leaked_permit: Use TrackedSender in lab mode, reserve a slot and neither send() nor abort(); verify leak detection fires
- test_group_commit_batch_size_near_optimal: Under sustained load, verify the coordinator drains min(C, available) commits per fsync cycle and batch size stays within [1, C]
- test_conformal_batch_size_adapts_to_regime: Feed synthetic fsync_samples with a regime shift (2ms -> 10ms); verify N_conformal adjusts upward after BOCPD detects the shift

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_commit_pipeline_cancel_safety.rs: Run 50 concurrent writing transactions through the two-phase commit pipeline; cancel 20 of them at random points (during reserve, between reserve and send, after send); verify no ghost entries remain in the pipeline, the coordinator never hangs, all non-cancelled commits succeed, and channel capacity is fully recovered.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Dropping a SendPermit without send() or abort() releases the slot with zero state leakage
- [ ] Channel at capacity blocks new reserve() callers and unblocks in FIFO order when slots free
- [ ] Cancelled tasks between reserve() and send() never leave orphaned state in the pipeline
- [ ] Group commit batch size stays within [1, channel_capacity] under all load patterns
- [ ] TrackedSender in lab mode detects permit leaks (reserved but never sent/aborted)

title: §4.6-4.7 Sheaf Consistency + Conformal Calibration
description:
Implement sheaf-theoretic consistency checking (optional) and conformal calibration (§4.6-4.7, spec lines 4492-4602).

SHEAF CONSISTENCY (§4.6, optional):
- Each txn's local view = 'section' over read set
- Sheaf condition: overlapping sections must agree (consistent with global version chain)
- Lab-only verification lens. Adapt asupersync sheaf utilities or equivalent
- check_consistency(&sections, &global_version_chains) → result.is_consistent()

CONFORMAL CALIBRATION (§4.7):
Two distinct uses:
1. Oracle anomaly detection (asupersync-native): calibrate on OracleReports from lab runs, produce prediction sets for invariant behavior (distribution-free, finite-sample)
2. Performance regression detection (FrankenSQLite harness): gate changes using Extreme Optimization Loop

ORACLE CALIBRATOR (§4.7.1): ConformalCalibrator with alpha=0.05, min_calibration_samples=50. Calibrate across 100+ seeds. Predict: if prediction_set !conforming → anomaly. min_calibration_samples=50 derived from order-statistic coverage/width analysis.

PERFORMANCE DISCIPLINE (§4.7.2): Follow Extreme Optimization Loop (baseline→profile→one lever→isomorphism proof→verify). Non-negotiable gate: OpportunityScore >= 2.0 (impact * confidence / effort).

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_sheaf_consistent_non_overlapping_txns: Run two transactions with disjoint read sets; verify sheaf check passes (trivially consistent)
- test_sheaf_consistent_overlapping_agree: Run two transactions that both read page P and see the same version; verify sheaf check passes
- test_sheaf_detects_inconsistency: Construct two sections that read the same page but observe incompatible versions (violating MVCC); verify sheaf check reports obstruction
- test_conformal_calibrator_min_samples: Create ConformalCalibrator with min_calibration_samples=50; feed 49 samples; verify predict() returns None (insufficient calibration)
- test_conformal_calibrator_detects_anomaly: Calibrate on 100 seeds producing normal OracleReports, then feed a report with anomalous invariant score; verify prediction set flags non-conforming
- test_conformal_calibrator_coverage_guarantee: Calibrate on 100 seeds at alpha=0.05; verify that at least 95% of holdout reports from the same distribution are flagged conforming
- test_opportunity_score_gate: Verify optimization changes are rejected when OpportunityScore < 2.0 and accepted when >= 2.0

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_sheaf_plus_conformal_mvcc_verification.rs: Run 20 concurrent transactions under LabRuntime across 100 seeds; capture sections for sheaf checking and oracle reports for conformal calibration; verify sheaf consistency holds for all valid MVCC executions, and conformal calibrator correctly identifies an intentionally injected invariant violation.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Sheaf checker detects zero false negatives (every real MVCC inconsistency is flagged)
- [ ] ConformalCalibrator requires >= min_calibration_samples before producing predictions
- [ ] Conformal coverage guarantee holds: at alpha=0.05, conforming rate >= 95% on in-distribution reports
- [ ] OpportunityScore gate rejects changes below 2.0 threshold
- [ ] Sheaf + conformal pipeline runs entirely within LabRuntime (deterministic, no wall-clock)

title: §4.8 BOCPD: Bayesian Online Change-Point Detection
description:
Implement BOCPD for workload regime shift detection (§4.8, spec lines 4603-4722).

CONCEPT: Database workloads are non-stationary. BOCPD (Adams & MacKay 2007) detects regime shifts in real time via posterior over run length r_t.

RECURSION: P(r_t | x_{1:t}) proportional to sum over r_{t-1} of P(x_t | r_t, ...) * P(r_t | r_{t-1}) * P(r_{t-1} | x_{1:t-1})

MONITORED STREAMS:
- Commit throughput (ops/sec): Normal-Gamma → adjust GC frequency
- SSI abort rate: Beta-Binomial → log warning / relax version chain limits
- Page contention (locks/sec): Normal-Gamma → adjust witness refinement
- Version chain length: Normal-Gamma → tighten/loosen GC watermarks

CALIBRATION (Alien-Artifact):
- Hazard H=1/250: expected regime length 250 obs (~4 min at 1 obs/sec). Derived from typical 1-30 min workload phases (geometric mean)
- Jeffreys priors: mu_0=0, kappa_0=0.01, alpha_0=0.5, beta_0=0.5 (uninformative, adapts within ~20 observations)
- Change-point threshold=0.5: Bayes-optimal under symmetric loss. Could lower to 0.09 with asymmetric costs, but 0.5 conservative for V1 (advisory actions)

MONITORING STACK (merged canonical):
- Layer 0: asupersync deadline monitor (adaptive warnings, stalled task detection)
- Layer 1: e-processes (anytime-valid invariant violation evidence)
- Layer 2: conformal (distribution-free anomaly detection across seeds)
- Layer 3 (optional): BOCPD (regime-shift → retune heuristics)

IMPLEMENTATION: BocpdMonitor in fsqlite-harness (NOT provided by asupersync). Pruning low-probability run lengths for O(1) amortized cost.

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_bocpd_detects_mean_shift: Feed Normal-Gamma BOCPD monitor with 200 observations at mean=100, then 200 at mean=500; verify change-point detected with posterior > 0.5 within 20 observations of the shift
- test_bocpd_no_false_positive_stationary: Feed 1000 stationary observations from N(100,10); verify no change-point detected (posterior stays below 0.5)
- test_bocpd_beta_binomial_abort_rate: Feed Beta-Binomial monitor with low abort rate (0.01) for 200 obs, then high rate (0.15) for 200 obs; verify regime shift detected
- test_bocpd_hazard_function_geometric: Verify hazard H=1/250 produces expected regime lengths of ~250 observations on average across 10000 synthetic sequences
- test_bocpd_pruning_keeps_cost_bounded: Feed 100000 observations; verify per-observation update cost stays O(1) amortized (measure wall time does not grow linearly)
- test_bocpd_deterministic_under_lab: Run same BOCPD sequence under LabRuntime with same seed twice; verify identical change-point detection results
- test_bocpd_jeffreys_prior_adapts_quickly: Verify uninformative Jeffreys prior adapts to observed distribution within ~20 observations (posterior predictive matches empirical)

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_bocpd_regime_shift_gc_adjustment.rs: Run a workload that transitions from read-heavy (low commit throughput) to write-heavy (high commit throughput) after 60 seconds; verify BOCPD detects the regime shift, logs the change-point event, and the GC frequency adjustment is triggered within the expected latency window.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] BOCPD detects a 5x mean shift in commit throughput within 20 observations after the change point
- [ ] No spurious change-point detections on stationary workloads over 1000 observations
- [ ] Run-length pruning keeps per-update cost O(1) amortized for streams of 100K+ observations
- [ ] All four monitored streams (throughput, abort rate, contention, chain length) have functional BOCPD monitors
- [ ] BOCPD results are deterministic under LabRuntime for a given seed

title: §4.9-4.10 TLA+ Export + BlockingPool Integration
description:
Implement TLA+ trace export and BlockingPool I/O dispatch (§4.9-4.10, spec lines 4724-4882).

TLA+ EXPORT (§4.9):
- Asupersync: trace-driven TlaExporter. Export concrete behavior (Vec<TraceEvent>) and parametric skeleton
- FrankenSQLite: MvccTlaExporter for MVCC protocol traces (MvccTraceEvent). Both concrete behaviors and spec skeletons for TLC model checking
- Instrument: MVCC commit/checkpoint/GC with MvccTraceEvent domain trace
- Run deterministic scenarios in harness, export for debugging + bounded model checking

BLOCKING POOL (§4.10):
- All file I/O dispatched to asupersync blocking pool. Async runtime threads never blocked by syscalls
- UNSAFE FORBIDDEN: MUST NOT transmit raw pointers across spawn_blocking boundary
- SAFE PATTERN: Owned pooled buffers (PageBuf) moved into blocking closure, returned by value
- PageBuf: owned, page-sized, page-aligned, Send+'static. Drop returns to PageBufPool
- PageBufPool: bounded pool keyed by page_size (in fsqlite-pager)

FILE I/O PATTERN: cx.checkpoint() → pool.acquire() → Arc::clone(file) → spawn_blocking_io(move || { file.read_exact_at(buf, offset); Ok(buf) }).await

CANCEL SEMANTICS: spawn_blocking is soft-cancel (OS syscall may complete). Acceptable because durable effects guarded by commit protocol.

POOL SIZING (Little's Law):
- Min threads: 1 (always available)
- Max by storage class: HDD=2, SATA=2, NVMe=4 (auto-detected via statfs, overridable via PRAGMA)
- Idle timeout: 10s (survival analysis of L_spawn=50us vs L_idle=8MB)
- Lab mode: blocking pool omitted, closure executes inline for determinism

PARENT: §4 Asupersync (bd-3go)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_tla_export_concrete_behavior: Capture 10 MvccTraceEvents from a deterministic commit scenario; export via MvccTlaExporter; verify output is valid TLA+ behavior module with correct state transitions
- test_tla_export_spec_skeleton: Export a parametric TLA+ skeleton for the MVCC model; verify it contains variable declarations, initial state predicate, and next-state relation
- test_tla_export_deterministic: Run same scenario twice with same seed; verify identical TLA+ output
- test_page_buf_pool_acquire_release: Acquire PageBuf from pool, drop it, acquire again; verify pool reuses the same allocation (no heap allocation on hot path)
- test_page_buf_pool_bounded: Set pool bound to 4; acquire 4 buffers; verify 5th acquire blocks or returns error (bounded memory)
- test_blocking_io_no_unsafe: Verify the read_page pattern compiles without any unsafe blocks; use FileExt::read_exact_at (safe Rust)
- test_blocking_io_cancel_returns_buf_to_pool: Start spawn_blocking_io read, cancel the async task; verify PageBuf is dropped and returned to pool (no leak)
- test_blocking_pool_lab_mode_inline: Under LabRuntime, verify spawn_blocking_io executes closure inline (no real threads) for determinism

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_tla_export_and_blocking_io.rs: Run a 20-transaction MVCC scenario under LabRuntime, capture MvccTraceEvents, export to TLA+; simultaneously verify all page reads go through the blocking pool pattern (cx.checkpoint -> pool.acquire -> spawn_blocking_io) with zero unsafe, and that cancelled transactions return buffers to the pool.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] TLA+ export is deterministic for a given seed (bit-identical output across runs)
- [ ] PageBuf pool reuses allocations with zero heap allocation on the hot path
- [ ] No unsafe code in the file I/O dispatch path (spawn_blocking_io + FileExt only)

comments.text:
## Missing Algorithmic Detail (Audit Fix): Little's Law Derivation + Queue-Depth Formula

The bead references backpressure but omits the formal Little's Law derivation from §4.5 and §4.10.

### Channel Capacity Derivation (§4.5, Little's Law)

Formula: `C >= lambda * t_commit`
- lambda = peak commit arrival rate
- t_commit = mean commit processing time (validate + WAL append + fsync amortization)

For the throughput model in §17.2:
- Group commit batch size N=50, fsync cost 2ms: `t_commit ~ 2ms/50 = 40us` per transaction (amortized)
- At peak 37,000 commits/sec: `C >= 37000 * 40e-6 ~ 1.5`
- At burst 4x peak (148K/sec): `C >= 148000 * 40e-6 ~ 6`
- With safety margin 2.5x for jitter: `C = 6 * 2.5 = 15 ~ 16`

Default of 16 absorbs bursts at 4x sustained peak. Adjustable via `PRAGMA fsqlite.commit_channel_capacity`.

### Optimal Batch Size Formula

N minimizes `t_fsync / N + t_validate * N` (fsync amortization vs. validation latency).
For `t_fsync = 2ms, t_validate = 5us`:
`N_opt = sqrt(t_fsync / t_validate) = sqrt(400) = 20`

Capacity 16 < N_opt, so system naturally batches up to 16 per fsync under saturation (near-optimal).

### Conformal Control for Batch Size (Alien-Artifact Upgrade)

Point estimates are brittle. Coordinator SHOULD choose N using distribution-free upper quantiles within current BOCPD regime:

1. Maintain ring buffers: `fsync_samples = {t_fsync_i}`, `validate_samples = {t_validate_i}`
2. Compute conformal upper quantiles (split conformal; §4.7):
   - `q_fsync := Q_{1-alpha}(fsync_samples)`
   - `q_validate := Q_{1-alpha}(validate_samples)`
3. Choose: `N_conformal = clamp(round(sqrt(q_fsync / q_validate)), 1, C)`

Operational rules:
- On BOCPD regime shift: calibration windows MUST reset
- N changes with hysteresis (2-step improvement required)
- Policy changes logged in evidence ledger (§4.16.1)
- Under LabRuntime: decision MUST be deterministic (lab clock, not wall clock)

### BlockingPool Sizing (§4.10, Little's Law)

Pool uses min/max thread model. `L = lambda * W`:

| Storage class | Mean service time W | Optimal threads at 10K IOPS |
|---------------|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| HDD (7200rpm) | ~8ms               | 80 (but serialized by arm)  |
| SATA SSD      | ~100us             | 1-2                         |
| NVMe SSD      | ~15us              | 1-2 (kernel parallelism)    |

Defaults: HDD: 2, SATA SSD: 2, NVMe: 4. Auto-detected via `statfs()`.

Idle timeout: 10 seconds (derived from survival analysis):
- Minimizes `L_spawn * P(arrival < t) + L_idle * t * P(no_arrival < t)`
- L_spawn ~ 50us (thread creation), L_idle ~ 8MB (stack per thread)
- Optimal range: 5-30s. BOCPD adjusts adaptively on I/O arrival regime shifts.

title: §4.11 Structured Concurrency (Regions)
description:
Implement the region tree lifetime model (§4.11). Every task/actor must be region-owned. Enforce INV-REGION-QUIESCENCE: no region closes until all children complete and finalizers run. Database::close() must await quiescence.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_region_tree_structure: Create DbRootRegion with WriteCoordinatorRegion, SymbolStoreRegion, ReplicationRegion, CheckpointGcRegion, ObservabilityRegion as children; verify tree structure matches §4.11 normative layout
- test_region_quiescence_all_children_complete: Create region with 5 child tasks, close region; verify close blocks until all 5 tasks complete
- test_region_quiescence_finalizers_run: Create region with 3 child tasks that register finalizers; close region; verify all finalizers execute before close returns
- test_region_quiescence_obligations_resolved: Create region with tasks holding obligations (Reserved state); close region; verify close blocks until all obligations are Committed or Aborted (not Reserved/Leaked)
- test_no_detached_tasks: Attempt to spawn a task outside any region; verify it fails (no detached tasks allowed)
- test_database_close_awaits_quiescence: Open a Database with active background workers, call Database::close(); verify it drains all workers and returns only after full quiescence
- test_per_connection_region_child_of_root: Create PerConnectionRegion; verify it is a child of DbRootRegion and closing the root cancels and drains the connection region

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_structured_concurrency_shutdown.rs: Open a database, start 10 connections each running queries, start background GC/compaction/replication workers; call Database::close(); verify all connections drain, all background workers stop, all finalizers run, and close returns within a bounded timeout with zero orphan tasks.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Every background worker runs as a region-owned task (no detached tasks exist)
- [ ] Database::close() returns only after INV-REGION-QUIESCENCE is satisfied (all children done, finalizers run, obligations resolved)
- [ ] Region tree matches the normative structure from §4.11 (DbRootRegion -> service regions -> connection regions -> transaction regions)
- [ ] Subsystem that cannot prove bounded drain is flagged as a spec violation

comments.text:
## Missing Algorithmic Detail (Audit Fix): Structured Concurrency Tree Model (Parent-Child Cancellation Rules)

The bead describes the region tree concept but omits the normative tree structure, quiescence invariant, and close protocol from §4.11.

### Normative Region Tree (§4.11)

```
DbRootRegion
  - WriteCoordinatorRegion          (native marker sequencer + compat WAL path)
  - SymbolStoreRegion               (local symbol logs + tiered storage fetch)
  - ReplicationRegion               (stream symbols; anti-entropy; membership)
  - CheckpointGcRegion              (checkpointer, compactor, GC horizon)
  - ObservabilityRegion             (deadline monitor, task inspector, metrics)

PerConnectionRegion (child of DbRootRegion)
  - QueryExecution tasks
  - Cursor prefetch tasks (bounded; optional)

PerTransactionRegion (child of PerConnectionRegion)
  - Encode/persist capsule tasks (native mode)
  - Witness publication tasks
  - Validation tasks
```

### Rules

- Every background worker, coordinator, replicator, and long-lived service MUST run as a region-owned task/actor.
- No task may outlive the Database root region. There are no detached tasks.
- `Database::close()` MUST close the root region and await quiescence.

### INV-REGION-QUIESCENCE

A region MUST NOT report closed until:
1. All child tasks are completed
2. All finalizers have run
3. All obligations are resolved (Committed/Aborted, not Reserved/Leaked)

### Close Protocol

Closing the database is a protocol, not a `drop`:
1. Request cancellation of root region
2. Drain all child regions (bounded)
3. Run all finalizers
4. Verify all obligations resolved
5. Return

Any subsystem that cannot prove bounded drain is a spec violation.

### Parent-Child Cancellation Propagation

From §4.12 (INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES): Region cancellation MUST propagate to all descendant regions. A parent cannot be cancelled while a child remains uncancelled. This means:
- Closing DbRootRegion cancels WriteCoordinatorRegion, SymbolStoreRegion, etc.
- Each child region then cancels its own children
- Propagation is monotone: once cancelled, a region stays cancelled
- INV-LOSERS-DRAIN ensures no orphan tasks survive

comments.text:
# §4.11 Structured Concurrency (Regions) — Spec Extract (Canonical)

**Spec reference:** COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md, lines ~4885–4927

FrankenSQLite adopts asupersync's region tree as the non-negotiable lifetime model for all concurrency:

- Every background worker, coordinator, replicator, and long-lived service MUST run as a region-owned task/actor.
- No task may outlive the `Database` root region. There are no detached tasks.
- `Database::close()` MUST close the root region and await quiescence.

This is the structural guarantee that makes shutdown/cancellation/failure handling predictable: no orphan tasks, no "still flushing in the background", no half-finished repairs.

## Normative Region Tree (Conceptual)

```
DbRootRegion
  - WriteCoordinatorRegion          (native marker sequencer + compat WAL path)
  - SymbolStoreRegion               (local symbol logs + tiered storage fetch)
  - ReplicationRegion               (stream symbols; anti-entropy; membership)
  - CheckpointGcRegion              (checkpointer, compactor, GC horizon)
  - ObservabilityRegion             (deadline monitor, task inspector, metrics)

PerConnectionRegion (child of DbRootRegion)
  - QueryExecution tasks
  - Cursor prefetch tasks (bounded; optional)

PerTransactionRegion (child of PerConnectionRegion)
  - Encode/persist capsule tasks (native mode)
  - Witness publication tasks
  - Validation tasks
```

## INV-REGION-QUIESCENCE (Normative)
A region MUST NOT report closed until:
- all child tasks completed,
- all finalizers have run,
- all obligations are resolved (Committed/Aborted, not Reserved/Leaked).

## Practical Consequence
Closing the database is a protocol (request cancellation → drain → finalize → return). Any subsystem that cannot prove bounded drain is a spec violation.

## Test Plan Note
This bead already contains an integration-level test matrix in earlier comments. Keep those tests, but ensure they are implemented under `fsqlite-harness` using LabRuntime where possible.

## SUMMARY
Implement miscellaneous extensions (crate: fsqlite-ext-misc) including: generate_series(START, STOP [, STEP]) virtual table for integer sequence generation; dbstat virtual table for B-tree page usage statistics (per-page and per-table aggregate modes); dbpage virtual table for direct read/write access to database pages; csv virtual table for reading CSV files; decimal extension for arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic (decimal, decimal_add, decimal_sub, decimal_mul, decimal_sum, decimal_cmp); and uuid extension for UUID generation and conversion (uuid, uuid_str, uuid_blob). Each extension provides utility functionality commonly used in SQLite applications.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS
- generate_series: virtual table producing rows with columns (value, start, stop, step). Generates integers from START to STOP with STEP increment (default 1). If STEP is positive, generates while value <= STOP; if negative, while value >= STOP. Commonly used in joins and CTEs for generating sequences.
- dbstat: virtual table reading B-tree page metadata. Columns: name (table/index name), path (page path in tree), pageno, pagetype (leaf/internal), ncell, payload, unused, mx_payload. Hidden column 'aggregate' controls per-page (FALSE) vs per-table (TRUE) output.
- dbpage: virtual table providing raw page access. Columns: pgno (page number), data (page content as blob), schema (database schema name). UPDATE on data writes raw bytes to the page (dangerous, bypasses all integrity checks).
- csv: virtual table reading CSV files. Parameters: filename, header (YES/NO), columns (count), schema (explicit column definitions). Implements the xBestIndex/xFilter/xNext virtual table interface for sequential CSV scanning.
- decimal: arbitrary-precision arithmetic using string representation internally. decimal(X) converts to canonical text form. decimal_add/sub/mul perform exact arithmetic. decimal_sum is an aggregate. decimal_cmp returns -1/0/+1. No floating-point precision loss.
- uuid: uuid() generates random UUID v4. uuid_str(blob) converts 16-byte blob to string "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx". uuid_blob(str) converts string to 16-byte blob.

1. generate_series with default STEP=1 includes both START and STOP values.
2. generate_series with STEP=0 is an error or produces no rows (match C SQLite behavior).
3. generate_series with negative STEP counts downward (START > STOP).

5. dbpage UPDATE writes raw bytes to pages; this bypasses all integrity checks and is intentionally dangerous.

## §14.7 Miscellaneous Extensions

### Spec Content (Lines 15662-15714)

Resides in `crates/fsqlite-ext-misc`. Contains several small extensions:

**generate_series(START, STOP [, STEP])** -> virtual table. Generates integer sequence from START to STOP with optional STEP (default 1). Columns: value, start, stop, step. Commonly used in joins:
```sql
SELECT value FROM generate_series(1, 100);
SELECT date(d.value) FROM generate_series(
  unixepoch('2024-01-01'), unixepoch('2024-12-31'), 86400
) AS d;
```

**dbstat** -> virtual table. Reports B-tree page usage statistics:
```sql
SELECT name, path, pageno, pagetype, ncell, payload, unused, mx_payload
  FROM dbstat WHERE aggregate=FALSE;
```
Columns: page number, type (leaf/internal), ncell, payload bytes, unused bytes, max cell payload. `aggregate` hidden column controls per-page vs per-table stats.

**dbpage** -> virtual table. Direct read/write access to database pages:
```sql
SELECT data FROM dbpage WHERE pgno = 1;  -- read page 1
UPDATE dbpage SET data = X'...' WHERE pgno = 5;  -- write (dangerous!)
```

**csv** -> virtual table. Reads CSV files:
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE temp.csv_data USING csv(
  filename='data.csv', header=YES, columns=4
);
```

**decimal** -> arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic:
- decimal(X) -- convert to decimal text
- decimal_add(X, Y), decimal_sub(X, Y), decimal_mul(X, Y) -- arithmetic
- decimal_sum(X) -- aggregate sum with arbitrary precision
- decimal_cmp(X, Y) -- comparison returning -1, 0, or +1

Decimal values represented as strings internally to avoid floating-point precision loss. Useful for financial calculations.

**uuid** -> UUID generation:
- uuid() -- generate random UUID v4
- uuid_str(X) -- convert UUID blob to string
- uuid_blob(X) -- convert UUID string to 16-byte blob

title: §7.4-7.6 Page-Level Integrity + WAL Cumulative Checksum Chain + Double-Write Prevention
description:
Implements §7.4-7.6 of the FrankenSQLite spec: page-level integrity via optional XXH3-128 checksums in reserved space, WAL cumulative checksum chain for append-only integrity and torn write detection, and the four-layer double-write prevention mechanism.

SUMMARY: Defines the optional PRAGMA page_checksum=ON feature that stores XXH3-128 hashes in 16 bytes of reserved space per page (header offset 20 = 16), the WAL cumulative checksum chain that creates a hash chain where modifying any frame invalidates all subsequent checksums, the recovery procedure (sequential read to first invalid checksum = valid WAL end), and the four double-write prevention mechanisms (cumulative checksums, salt values, commit frame markers, tightly-packed frames). Also covers the critical self-healing implication: cumulative chains require independent random-access validation via per-source xxh3_128 in .wal-fec.

KEY DATA STRUCTURES AND ALGORITHMS:
- Page-Level Integrity: Page layout = [data: page_size - 16 bytes][xxh3: 16 bytes]. Header byte offset 20 set to 16. Verification at: every disk read, cache read (optional), before WAL append, before checkpoint write.
- WAL Cumulative Checksum Chain: WAL header checksum chains to frame 0, frame 0 chains to frame 1, etc. Modifying frame i invalidates checksums for frames i through N. Torn write = invalid checksum at torn frame.
- Recovery Procedure: Read+verify WAL header checksum (invalid = entirely corrupt). Chain from header checksums. For each frame: verify salts match header, verify cumulative checksum. Only committed transactions (last frame has db_size > 0) replayed.
- Double-Write Prevention: (1) Cumulative checksums detect modification, (2) Salt values (unique per WAL generation) reject old frames, (3) Commit frame marker (non-zero db_size) marks transaction boundaries, (4) Tightly-packed frames (NOT sector-aligned; torn writes detected by checksum).
- Self-Healing: Cumulative chain means frame i mismatch blocks validation of i+1. FrankenSQLite uses per-source xxh3_128 in .wal-fec (WalFecGroupMeta.source_page_xxh3_128) for independent random-access validation.

NORMATIVE INVARIANTS:
- C SQLite can read databases with reserved-space checksums (reserved bytes are opaque) but WRITES zeros to reserved space, invalidating checksums
- Database SHOULD be read-only for legacy clients when page_checksum=ON
- WAL frames are tightly packed (24B header + page_size, NO padding) — NOT sector-aligned
- Only committed transactions (valid commit frame marker with db_size > 0) are replayed during recovery
- Partial transactions (no valid commit frame marker) MUST be discarded during recovery
- Self-healing requires independent random-access validation — cumulative chain alone is insufficient for repair
- FrankenSQLite RaptorQ turns "detect and discard" into "detect and repair"

UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS:
1. test_page_checksum_xxh3_round_trip: Write page with XXH3 in reserved space, read back, verify
2. test_page_checksum_detect_corruption: Flip bit in page data -> XXH3 mismatch detected
3. test_reserved_bytes_16: Header offset 20 correctly set to 16 when page_checksum=ON
4. test_legacy_reads_reserved_ok: C sqlite3 reads DB with reserved space without error
5. test_legacy_writes_invalidate_checksum: C sqlite3 modifying page zeros reserved space -> checksum mismatch
6. test_wal_cumulative_chain_valid: Chain of 100 valid frames verifies correctly
7. test_wal_cumulative_chain_torn: Partial write at frame 50 -> first 49 valid, rest rejected
8. test_wal_cumulative_chain_modified: Modifying frame 10 invalidates frames 10-99
9. test_wal_recovery_truncation: Recovery truncates at first invalid checksum
10. test_wal_salt_mismatch_rejects: Old generation frames (wrong salt) rejected
11. test_commit_frame_marker: Only frames with db_size > 0 mark commit boundaries
12. test_partial_txn_discarded: Transaction without commit frame marker discarded in recovery
13. test_self_healing_random_access: .wal-fec xxh3_128 validates individual frames independently

E2E TEST: Create DB, write 100 transactions, simulate crash at random points. Verify recovery finds correct WAL end, only committed transactions survive, page_checksum detects single-bit corruption, and all page reads verified without corruption.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Page-level XXH3 checksums correctly stored in and read from 16-byte reserved space
- WAL cumulative checksum chain detects modification, truncation, and torn writes
- Recovery correctly identifies valid WAL end and discards partial transactions
- Legacy SQLite interop: reads succeed, writes invalidate checksums (detected)
- Self-healing via .wal-fec provides random-access validation independent of chain
- Salt values correctly reject old-generation frames after checkpoint

comments.text:
## §7.4-7.6 Page-Level Integrity + WAL Cumulative Checksum Chain + Double-Write Prevention

### Spec Content (Lines 11415-11515)

**§7.4 Page-Level Integrity:**
- Standard SQLite has NO per-page checksums. Corruption detected only by structural checks.
- FrankenSQLite enhancement (PRAGMA page_checksum=ON): reserved space stores XXH3-128 hash (16 bytes)
- Header byte offset 20 set to 16 (reserved_bytes=16)
- C SQLite reads databases with reserved space (opaque bytes) but WRITES zeros → invalidates checksums → DB should be read-only for legacy clients
- Verification points: every disk read, cache read (optional), before WAL append, before checkpoint write

**§7.5 WAL Frame Integrity: Cumulative Checksum Chain:**
- Append-only integrity: modifying any frame invalidates all subsequent checksums
- Torn write detection: partial write → invalid checksum at torn frame
- Recovery: sequential read, first invalid checksum = valid WAL end
- **Critical for self-healing:** cumulative chain means frame i mismatch blocks validation of i+1..
  → Self-healing needs independent random-access validation (per-source xxh3_128 hashes in .wal-fec)

**§7.6 Double-Write Prevention:**
1. Cumulative checksums (§7.5)
2. Salt values (unique per WAL generation, old frames rejected by salt mismatch)
3. Commit frame marker (non-zero db_size = commit boundary; partial txns discarded)
4. Tightly-packed frames (NOT sector-aligned; torn writes detected by checksum, not alignment)
- FrankenSQLite addition: RaptorQ turns "detect and discard" into "detect and repair"

### Unit Tests Required
1. test_page_checksum_xxh3_round_trip: Write page with XXH3 hash in reserved space, read back, verify
2. test_page_checksum_detect_corruption: Flip a bit in page data → XXH3 mismatch detected
3. test_reserved_bytes_16: Header offset 20 correctly set to 16 when page_checksum=ON
4. test_legacy_reads_reserved_ok: C sqlite3 reads DB with reserved space without error
5. test_legacy_writes_invalidate_checksum: C sqlite3 modifying page zeros reserved space → checksum mismatch
6. test_wal_cumulative_chain_valid: Chain of 100 valid frames verifies correctly
7. test_wal_cumulative_chain_torn: Partial write at frame 50 → first 49 frames valid, rest rejected
8. test_wal_cumulative_chain_modified: Modifying frame 10 invalidates frames 10-99
9. test_wal_recovery_truncation: Recovery truncates at first invalid checksum
10. test_wal_salt_mismatch_rejects: Old generation frames (wrong salt) rejected
11. test_commit_frame_marker: Only frames with db_size > 0 mark commit boundaries
12. test_partial_txn_discarded: Transaction without commit frame marker → discarded in recovery
13. test_self_healing_random_access: .wal-fec xxh3_128 validates individual frames (not chain-dependent)

### E2E Test
Create DB, write 100 transactions. Simulate crash at random points. Verify:
- Recovery finds correct WAL end via cumulative checksum chain
- Only committed transactions survive (partial txns discarded)
- After enabling page_checksum, all page reads verified without corruption
- Inject single-bit corruption → detected and reported

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Merged from P2 bead bd-1tnq (§7.4-7.6 Page-Level Integrity + WAL Frame Chain + Double-Write Prevention)

## §7.4 Page-Level Integrity

**On-disk pages:** Standard SQLite has NO per-page checksums. Corruption detected only by structural checks or PRAGMA integrity_check.

**Optional FrankenSQLite enhancement (PRAGMA page_checksum = ON):** Reserved space at end of each page stores XXH3-128 hash:
```
Page layout: [data: page_size - 16 bytes] [xxh3: 16 bytes]
Header byte offset 20 set to 16 (reserved space = 16).
```

C SQLite can read databases with reserved-space checksums (reserved bytes opaque). Default OFF for max interoperability.

**Interoperability Warning:** C SQLite will write zeros/garbage to reserved space when modifying pages, invalidating FrankenSQLite checksum. Database should be Read-Only by legacy clients when page_checksum=ON.

**Verification points:**
- Every disk read: compute XXH3, store in CachedPage
- Every cache read (optional): reverify XXH3
- Before WAL append: verify each page image's integrity hash matches expected
- Before checkpoint write: verify page XXH3

## §7.5 WAL Frame Integrity: Cumulative Checksum Chain

**Append-only integrity:** Inserting or modifying any frame invalidates all subsequent checksums. Detects corruption and tampering.

**Torn write detection:** Partial write produces invalid checksum at torn frame. Recovery reads frames sequentially; first invalid checksum marks valid WAL end.

**Recovery procedure:** Read+verify wal_header checksum (invalid = entirely corrupt, use db file only). Chain from (wal_header.cksum1, wal_header.cksum2). For each frame: verify salts match header (stale frame = stop), verify cumulative checksum. Only committed transactions (last frame has db_size > 0) are replayed.

**Critical implication for self-healing:** Because checksum is cumulative, once mismatch at frame i, WAL format alone cannot validate frames i+1.. (depends on state after frame i). Self-healing MUST provide independent random-access validation. FrankenSQLite: per-source xxh3_128(page_data) in .wal-fec (WalFecGroupMeta.source_page_xxh3_128; S3.4.1) identifies safe source symbols even when chain broken.

## §7.6 Double-Write Prevention

SQLite WAL prevents double-write corruption via:
1. Cumulative checksums (S7.5): torn writes produce invalid checksums
2. Salt values: each WAL generation has unique random salts. After checkpoint RESTART/TRUNCATE, old frames rejected by salt mismatch
3. Commit frame marker: frame with non-zero db_size marks txn boundary. Partial txns (no valid commit frame) discarded during recovery
4. Tightly-packed frames: NOT sector-aligned; 24B header + page_size bytes, no padding. Torn writes detected by cumulative checksum chain, not alignment. (Contrast: rollback journal header IS padded to sector size)

**FrankenSQLite addition:** RaptorQ repair symbols (S3.4.1) turn "detect and discard" into "detect and repair" — corrupted frames within commit group reconstructed if sufficient repair symbols survive.

title: §5.8 Conflict Detection and Resolution Detail
description:
STATUS: CLOSED (superseded rollup)

This bead is a consolidated/rolled-up version of §5.8 created during an earlier spec-to-beads conversion pass.

DO NOT implement from this rollup directly.

Use these replacement beads instead (plan-of-record):
- bd-zppf — §5.8 Conflict Detection and Resolution: First-Committer-Wins + Conflict Response
- bd-1e9x — §5.8.1 Serialized/Concurrent Mode Mutual Exclusion + CAS Protocol

---

SECTION: §5.8 (spec lines ~8981-9167)

PURPOSE: Implement page lock table, FCW commit validation, and serialized/concurrent mode interaction.

## Page Lock Table Implementation (normative)

### Concurrent Mode (cross-process)
- SharedPageLockTable in foo.db.fsqlite-shm (§5.6.3) is THE canonical lock table
- ALL page-level writer exclusion MUST be enforced via shared-memory table, NOT in-process HashMap

### Normal commit/abort (fast path)
- Release page locks by iterating in-process page_locks set (touch only locked pages)

### Crash cleanup (slow path)
- MUST use shared-memory scan release_page_locks_for(txn_id) (§5.6.3) -- crashed process has no in-process set

## Single-Process Reference Implementation (NOT cross-process safe)
- 64-shard InProcessPageLockTable (parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<PageNumber, TxnId>>)
- Shard selection: pgno.get() as usize & (LOCK_TABLE_SHARDS - 1)
- try_acquire: vacant→insert, occupied→check same txn (idempotent) or SQLITE_BUSY
- release: remove entry, panic if not held by txn
- release_all: iterate per-txn lock set (O(W) where W = write set size)
  - Production MAY group by shard to reduce lock acquisitions

## Commit Validation Algorithm (First-Committer-Wins)
- validate_commit(T, commit_index):
  - For each page in write_set: if commit_index.latest_commit_seq(pgno) > T.snapshot.high → conflict
  - On conflict: attempt algebraic merge (§5.10)
    - If merge possible: perform_merge
    - If not: return SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (retryable)

## Serialized ↔ Concurrent Mode Interaction

### While Serialized-mode writer is Active (holding global write mutex):
- Concurrent txns MAY BEGIN and read normally
- Any Concurrent-mode page write lock attempt MUST fail with SQLITE_BUSY
  (allowing concurrent writers would violate SQLite single-writer contract)

### While any Concurrent-mode writer is Active (holds any page locks):
- Acquiring Serialized writer exclusion (BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE/DEFERRED upgrade) MUST fail with SQLITE_BUSY
- DEFERRED read-only begins remain permitted; only writer upgrade excluded

### Cross-Process Implementation
- SharedMemoryLayout maintains serialized_writer indicator (token + lease)
- Set when Serialized txn acquires writer exclusion, cleared at commit/abort
- Concurrent-mode write paths MUST check this indicator before acquiring page locks

### check_serialized_writer_exclusion(shm) Algorithm
- Load token (Acquire); if 0 → Ok
- Check expiry + process_alive(pid, birth)
- If alive and valid lease → SQLITE_BUSY
- If stale (lease expired or owner dead): CAS clear + retry loop
  - CAS failure means token changed (someone else cleared or new writer installed)
  - MUST retry to avoid returning Ok while new serialized writer is active

### Serialized Writer Acquisition Ordering (5 steps)
1. Acquire global serialized writer exclusion
2. Publish shared indicator (serialized_writer_token != 0, Release ordering)
3. Drain concurrent writers: wait until no outstanding page locks from Concurrent-mode txns
4. Perform writes
5. On commit/abort: CAS clear indicator + release global exclusion

### External Interop Hook (Compatibility mode)
- Concurrent-mode exclusion meaningless if legacy writer bypasses .fsqlite-shm
- Compatibility mode with .fsqlite-shm MUST exclude legacy writers (§5.6.6.1, §5.6.7)
- FORBIDDEN: multi-writer MVCC while legacy writers permitted

PARENT EPIC: bd-3t3
DEPENDS ON: bd-3t3.8 (SharedPageLockTable), bd-3t3.3 (Transaction Lifecycle), bd-3t3.1 (Core Types)
