title: V3: Speculative JIT for Prepared DML — Compile Hot INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE to Native Closures
description:
## What
Compile hot prepared DML programs to native Rust closures that bypass the VDBE interpreter entirely. When a prepared INSERT is executed repeatedly (>N times), generate a specialized closure that directly calls B-tree operations with inlined register access, skipping opcode dispatch, bounds checking, and the entire interpreter loop.

## Why — The Ultimate Optimization
The VDBE interpreter has inherent overhead: opcode fetch, dispatch (match/jump table), register file indirection, per-opcode bookkeeping. Even with superinstructions (V2), each execution still pays the interpreter loop overhead. A JIT-compiled closure eliminates ALL of this.

C SQLite achieves ~0.4µs per INSERT row. FrankenSQLite is at ~4µs. The ~3.6µs gap is roughly:
- ~1.0µs VDBE dispatch + ceremony (eliminated by JIT)
- ~1.5µs page access overhead (addressed by V1)
- ~0.5µs MVCC overhead (irreducible for correctness)
- ~0.6µs B-tree operations (close to C SQLite)

A JIT can close the 1.0µs dispatch gap entirely, bringing the total to ~2.6µs (~6.5x vs C).

## Alien Graveyard Connection
- **Trace-based JIT** (LuaJIT, PyPy, HotSpot): Record a trace of opcodes executed by the interpreter, compile the trace to native code, use guards for deoptimization
- **Template JIT** (V8 Sparkplug, Dalvik): Copy pre-compiled native snippets for each opcode, stitch them together with glue code
- **Method JIT** (JVM HotSpot C1/C2, .NET RyuJIT): Compile entire methods/functions to native code

For FrankenSQLite, the **Template JIT** approach is most practical in Rust:
- No runtime code generation (which requires `mmap` + `mprotect` and is complex in safe Rust)
- Instead: generate Rust closures at prepare time that chain pre-compiled opcode implementations
- The "JIT" is really "closure compilation" — type-safe, no unsafe, no platform-specific codegen

## How — The Closure Compilation Strategy
At prepare time, for programs that match known "compilable" patterns:
1. Analyze the opcode stream for a known template (e.g., simple INSERT, UPDATE with WHERE rowid=?)
2. Generate a `Box<dyn Fn(&mut StorageCursor, &[SqliteValue]) -> Result<(usize, Option<i64>)>>` closure
3. The closure directly calls: serialize_record → table_insert_prechecked_absent, with registers inlined as closure captures
4. Store the closure in PreparedStatement alongside the VdbeProgram
5. At execution time, if the closure exists, call it directly instead of engine.execute()

## JIT Infrastructure Already Present
- engine.rs:5874-6009: `maybe_trigger_jit`, `JitDecision` enum, hot threshold tracking, plan hash caching
- These stubs can be repurposed for closure compilation

## Files
- `crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/jit.rs` (NEW) — closure compilation for known templates
- `crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/engine.rs` — JIT integration, maybe_trigger_jit enhancement
- `crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs` — PreparedStatement closure storage + dispatch

## Estimated impact
Eliminates ~1µs per INSERT row of dispatch overhead
At 10K rows: ~10ms saved (from 40ms → 30ms)
Combined with V1+V2: from 40ms → ~15-20ms (5-7x vs C SQLite)

## Risk
High complexity. Must be gated behind a feature flag and thoroughly tested.
Closure compilation only for simple patterns; complex queries fall back to interpreter.

## Verification
- Unit tests for each compiled template
- Conformance oracle suite
- Benchmark section 1: target <20ms at 10K rows

title: WASM T.4: GitHub Actions CI workflow for wasm32 build, test, and npm publish
acceptance_criteria: GitHub Actions workflow builds wasm32, runs the WASM test suite, and publishes to npm on tag; a dry-run publish validates the package; workflow green on main.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# T.4 Detailed Implementation Spec: GitHub Actions CI for WASM

## Goal
Automated CI pipeline that builds the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, runs all test suites (wasm-bindgen-test, Playwright, conformance), publishes npm packages, and gates PRs on binary size regression.

## Workflow File
```yaml
# .github/workflows/wasm-ci.yml
name: WASM CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  WASM_PACK_VERSION: '0.13.1'
  PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS: 'chromium,firefox,webkit'

jobs:
  # ─── Stage 1: Build WASM ───
  wasm-build:
    name: Build wasm32
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
          components: rust-src
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: wasm32
      - name: Install wasm-pack
        run: curl https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/init.sh -sSf | sh -s -- -V $WASM_PACK_VERSION
      - name: Build WASM (release)
        run: |
          echo "::group::wasm-pack build"
          wasm-pack build crates/fsqlite-wasm \
            --target web \
            --release \
            --out-dir ../../packages/core/wasm \
            --out-name frankensqlite
          echo "::endgroup::"
      - name: Record binary size
        run: |
          WASM_SIZE=$(stat -c%s packages/core/wasm/frankensqlite_bg.wasm)
          WASM_GZ=$(gzip -c packages/core/wasm/frankensqlite_bg.wasm | wc -c)
          echo "wasm_raw=$WASM_SIZE" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "wasm_gz=$WASM_GZ" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "### WASM Binary Size" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "| Metric | Size |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "|--------|------|" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "| Raw | $(numfmt --to=iec $WASM_SIZE) |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "| Gzipped | $(numfmt --to=iec $WASM_GZ) |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        id: size
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wasm-build
          path: packages/core/wasm/
          retention-days: 7

  # ─── Stage 2: Rust WASM Unit Tests ───
  wasm-unit-tests:
    name: wasm-bindgen-test
    needs: wasm-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        browser: [chrome, firefox]  # Safari via WebKit in Playwright stage
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@nightly
        with:
          targets: wasm32-unknown-unknown
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: Install wasm-pack
        run: curl https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/init.sh -sSf | sh -s -- -V $WASM_PACK_VERSION
      - name: Run wasm-bindgen-test (${{ matrix.browser }})
        run: |
          echo "::group::wasm-pack test"
          wasm-pack test --headless --${{ matrix.browser }} crates/fsqlite-wasm 2>&1 | tee test-output.txt
          echo "::endgroup::"
          echo "### Test Results (${{ matrix.browser }})" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          tail -20 test-output.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

  # ─── Stage 3: Playwright Browser Tests ───
  playwright-tests:
    name: Playwright (${{ matrix.project }})
    needs: wasm-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        project: [chromium, firefox, webkit]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: packages/tests-e2e/package-lock.json
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wasm-build
          path: packages/core/wasm/
      - name: Install deps
        run: cd packages/tests-e2e && npm ci
      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: cd packages/tests-e2e && npx playwright install --with-deps ${{ matrix.project }}
      - name: Run Playwright tests
        run: |
          cd packages/tests-e2e
          npx playwright test --project=${{ matrix.project }} --reporter=list,json 2>&1 | tee results.txt
          echo "### Playwright ${{ matrix.project }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          tail -30 results.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report-${{ matrix.project }}
          path: packages/tests-e2e/test-results/

  # ─── Stage 4: SQL Conformance ───
  conformance-tests:
    name: SQL Conformance (WASM)
    needs: wasm-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 22 }
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wasm-build
          path: packages/core/wasm/
      - name: Run conformance suite
        run: |
          cd packages/tests-conformance
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
          npx playwright test --reporter=list,json 2>&1 | tee results.txt
          echo "### Conformance Results" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          grep -E '(PASS|FAIL|passed|failed)' results.txt | tail -5 >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

  # ─── Stage 5: Binary Size Gate ───
  size-check:
    name: Binary Size Check
    needs: wasm-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wasm-build
          path: packages/core/wasm/
      - name: Check size regression
        run: |
          WASM_GZ=$(gzip -c packages/core/wasm/frankensqlite_bg.wasm | wc -c)
          MAX_SIZE=$((2 * 1024 * 1024))  # 2 MiB gzipped max
          echo "Gzipped WASM size: $(numfmt --to=iec $WASM_GZ)"
          if [ "$WASM_GZ" -gt "$MAX_SIZE" ]; then
            echo "::error::WASM binary exceeds 2 MiB gzipped ($WASM_GZ bytes)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Size OK: $(numfmt --to=iec $WASM_GZ) < 2 MiB"

  # ─── Stage 6: NPM Publish (main only) ───
  npm-publish:
    name: Publish @frankensqlite/core
    needs: [wasm-unit-tests, playwright-tests, conformance-tests, size-check]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write  # npm provenance
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wasm-build
          path: packages/core/wasm/
      - name: Publish
        run: |
          cd packages/core
          npm publish --provenance --access public
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

## Required Repository Secrets
- `NPM_TOKEN`: npm automation token for @frankensqlite org

## Branch Protection Rules
Configure in repo settings → branch protection for `main`:
- Require status checks: `wasm-build`, `wasm-unit-tests`, `playwright-tests`, `conformance-tests`, `size-check`
- Require branches to be up to date before merging

## Acceptance Criteria
1. CI builds wasm32 target on every push/PR
2. wasm-bindgen-test runs in Chrome and Firefox matrix
3. Playwright runs in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit matrix
4. SQL conformance suite runs against WASM build
5. Binary size gated at 2 MiB gzipped (configurable)
6. NPM publish only on main push, after all tests pass
7. Failure artifacts (Playwright traces, screenshots) uploaded for debugging
8. Job summary shows binary size table and test result counts

title: §5.6.6-5.6.7 Compatibility Mode: Legacy Interop + Hybrid SHM Protocol
description:
Implement the legacy interop boundary (section 5.6.6) and hybrid shared-memory coordination protocol (section 5.6.7) that enables FrankenSQLite to coexist with legacy C SQLite processes reading the same database (spec lines 8148-8305).

SCOPE: Bridge between FrankenSQLite's MVCC system and legacy C SQLite. Two operating postures: (1) with foo.db.fsqlite-shm (default): Hybrid SHM protocol supporting legacy readers while excluding legacy writers; (2) without fsqlite-shm: fallback to standard SQLite file locking (single-writer, no MVCC, no SSI). Covers dual SHM maintenance, WAL-index hash table updates, reader mark protocol, and checkpoint coordination.

DATA STRUCTURES:
- Dual SHM structures: foo.db-shm (standard SQLite WAL-index) + foo.db.fsqlite-shm (FrankenSQLite MVCC)
- WAL-index: hash tables mapping (page_number -> frame_index), WalIndexHdr (dual-copy protocol), aReadMark[0..4], aFrameCksum, aSalt, aCksum
- WAL_WRITE_LOCK (byte 120 of foo.db-shm): held for coordinator lifetime to exclude legacy writers
- WAL_READ_LOCK(i): SHARED to join existing aReadMark, EXCLUSIVE to update aReadMark then downgrade

ALGORITHMS:
- Hybrid SHM Protocol (4 normative steps):
  Step 1 (startup): Acquire WAL_WRITE_LOCK on foo.db-shm and hold for coordinator lifetime; prevents C SQLite from entering WAL-write mode; if cannot acquire, database open MUST fail with SQLITE_BUSY
  Step 2 (on commit): After WAL append + fsync, update foo.db-shm hash tables: insert (page_number, frame_index), update mxFrame in both WalIndexHdr copies, update checksums using dual-copy protocol for lock-free readers. MUST happen AFTER wal.sync() and BEFORE publish_versions()
  Step 3 (reader protocol): FrankenSQLite readers participate in SQLite WAL reader protocol; JOIN fast path (SHARED lock on matching aReadMark[i]) preferred; CLAIM+UPDATE slow path (EXCLUSIVE lock, write aReadMark, downgrade to SHARED without unlock window) when no joinable mark exists; 5 reader marks bound distinct concurrent WAL snapshots (not total readers)
  Step 4 (checkpoint): Update nBackfill in WalCkptInfo during backfill
- No-SHM fallback (section 5.6.6.2): standard file locks, single-writer; BEGIN CONCURRENT MUST return error SQLITE_ERROR_CONCURRENT_UNAVAILABLE, NOT silently downgrade

INVARIANTS:
- Legacy writer exclusion is REQUIRED when using .fsqlite-shm: a legacy writer bypassing .fsqlite-shm corrupts WAL
- WAL_WRITE_LOCK MUST be held for coordinator's LIFETIME (releasing creates window for legacy writer)
- WAL-index update ordering: after wal.sync(), before publish_versions()
- Downgrade from EXCLUSIVE to SHARED MUST NOT introduce unlock window (lock-type transition)
- Native Mode: hybrid SHM protocol does NOT apply

TEST REQUIREMENTS (6 unit + 1 E2E):
- test_legacy_reader_sees_committed_data, test_legacy_writer_blocked, test_hybrid_shm_dual_maintenance, test_fallback_to_file_locking, test_coordinator_crash_recovery, test_read_lock_protocol (SHARED/EXCLUSIVE/downgrade sequence)
- E2E: launch FrankenSQLite + legacy sqlite3 against same DB; verify legacy reads, legacy write blocked, lock handling, crash recovery of either process

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Legacy C SQLite readers can read all committed data while FrankenSQLite coordinator active
2. Legacy C SQLite writers blocked with SQLITE_BUSY when coordinator holds WAL_WRITE_LOCK
3. Both .db-shm and .fsqlite-shm updated consistently on every commit
4. Graceful degradation to file-lock mode when fsqlite-shm unavailable
5. System recovers correctly after crash of either FrankenSQLite or legacy process
6. BEGIN CONCURRENT returns explicit error (not silent downgrade) in no-SHM fallback

Added ConcurrentUnavailable to FrankenError. All 6 required tests pass, clippy clean.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## §5.6.6-5.6.7 Compatibility Mode: Legacy Interop + Hybrid SHM Protocol

### What This Implements
The bridge between FrankenSQLite's MVCC system and legacy C SQLite processes, ensuring backward compatibility for readers while preventing data corruption from incompatible writers.

### Spec Content (Lines 8148-8305)

**§5.6.6 Legacy Interop Boundary:**
- When foo.db.fsqlite-shm is used (default fast path): FrankenSQLite runs Hybrid SHM protocol. Supports legacy readers but MUST exclude legacy writers (they'd bypass .fsqlite-shm and corrupt WAL).
- If foo.db.fsqlite-shm cannot be used: fallback to standard SQLite file locking (single-writer). Can interop with legacy writers but no multi-writer MVCC, no SSI.

**§5.6.7 Hybrid SHM Coordination Protocol (detailed):**
This is the protocol that allows FrankenSQLite processes to coexist with legacy C SQLite processes reading the same database.

**Key invariants:**
- FrankenSQLite coordinator MUST hold WAL_WRITE_LOCK for its entire lifetime
- Legacy readers coordinate via foo.db-shm (standard SQLite WAL-index)
- FrankenSQLite readers use foo.db.fsqlite-shm for MVCC but MUST also maintain valid entries in foo.db-shm for legacy compatibility
- WAL_READ_LOCK(i) acquisition: SHARED to join existing aReadMark[i], EXCLUSIVE only to update aReadMark[i], then downgrade to SHARED

### Implementation Requirements
1. Detect presence of legacy processes via standard SQLite lock probing
2. Maintain dual SHM structures (foo.db-shm + foo.db.fsqlite-shm) simultaneously
3. Ensure WAL checkpoints are visible to both legacy and FrankenSQLite readers
4. Handle graceful degradation when coordinator crashes (legacy processes must not hang)
5. File-lock fallback path when .fsqlite-shm creation fails

### Unit Tests Required
1. test_legacy_reader_sees_committed_data: Legacy SQLite process can read after FrankenSQLite write
2. test_legacy_writer_blocked: Legacy writer gets SQLITE_BUSY when FrankenSQLite coordinator active
3. test_hybrid_shm_dual_maintenance: Both .db-shm and .fsqlite-shm updated consistently
4. test_fallback_to_file_locking: Graceful degradation when fsqlite-shm unavailable
5. test_coordinator_crash_recovery: Legacy processes recover after coordinator crash
6. test_read_lock_protocol: WAL_READ_LOCK(i) SHARED/EXCLUSIVE/downgrade sequence correct

### E2E Test
Launch FrankenSQLite process + legacy sqlite3 process against same DB. Verify:
- Legacy process can read all committed data
- Legacy process cannot write (gets BUSY)
- FrankenSQLite process handles legacy reader locks correctly
- System recovers after crash of either process

SECTION: §5.6.6 + §5.6.7 (spec lines ~8148-8305)

PURPOSE: Implement the legacy interop boundary and hybrid shared-memory coordination protocol for Compatibility Mode.

## §5.6.6 Compatibility: Legacy Interop and File-Lock Fallback

### Two Operating Postures
1. foo.db.fsqlite-shm USED (default fast path): FrankenSQLite runs Hybrid SHM protocol (§5.6.7)
   - Supports legacy READERS but MUST exclude legacy WRITERS
   - A legacy writer would bypass .fsqlite-shm → corrupt WAL
2. foo.db.fsqlite-shm NOT AVAILABLE: Fall back to standard SQLite file locking (single-writer)
   - Interops with legacy writers, but no multi-writer MVCC, no SSI

### §5.6.6.1 Legacy Writer Exclusion (REQUIRED when using .fsqlite-shm)
- Problem: legacy writer can acquire WAL_WRITE_LOCK bypassing MVCC coordination
- Rule (normative): MUST hold legacy-writer exclusion lock
- WAL mode: exclusion lock = WAL_WRITE_LOCK on legacy WAL-index (foo.db-shm)
- MUST be held for coordinator's LIFETIME (releasing creates window for legacy writer)
- Legacy readers remain permitted (WAL_WRITE_LOCK blocks only writers)
- Multi-process: requires single cross-process commit sequencer while exclusion lock held
- If exclusion lock cannot be acquired: database open MUST fail with SQLITE_BUSY

### §5.6.6.2 No-SHM Fallback (File Locks Only)
- WAL_WRITE_LOCK for single-writer mutual exclusion
- Standard WAL reader marks for snapshot isolation
- No multi-writer MVCC, no SSI
- BEGIN CONCURRENT MUST return error (not silently downgrade to Serialized)
- Recommended error: SQLITE_ERROR with extended code SQLITE_ERROR_CONCURRENT_UNAVAILABLE

## §5.6.7 Hybrid SHM Coordination Protocol

### Problem Statement
- Compatibility Mode produces standard SQLite DB+WAL files readable by C SQLite
- FrankenSQLite uses foo.db.fsqlite-shm (FSQLSHM), C SQLite uses foo.db-shm
- Without bridging: (1) legacy readers can't find new frames, (2) legacy writers corrupt data

### Normative Protocol (4 steps, MUST for Compatibility Mode)

#### Step 1: Exclude Legacy Writers (startup)
- Acquire WAL_WRITE_LOCK (byte 120 of foo.db-shm, §2.1) and hold for coordinator lifetime
- Prevents C SQLite from entering WAL-write mode
- MUST be held even when no FrankenSQLite txn active

#### Step 2: Update WAL-Index Hash Tables (on commit)
- After appending WAL frames (§5.9.2 WALAppend), coordinator MUST update foo.db-shm:
  - Insert each frame's (page_number, frame_index) into hash table
  - Update mxFrame in both WalIndexHdr copies
  - Update aFrameCksum, aSalt, aCksum in both header copies
  - Use dual-copy protocol (write copy 1, then copy 2) for lock-free readers

#### Step 3: Maintain Reader Marks + Reader Locks
- FrankenSQLite readers MUST participate in SQLite's WAL reader protocol
- Two paths for readers:
  - JOIN FAST PATH (preferred, enables >5 concurrent readers):
    - If aReadMark[i] == desired_m, acquire WAL_READ_LOCK(i) in SHARED mode
    - Re-check after acquiring (may have changed)
  - CLAIM+UPDATE SLOW PATH (when no joinable mark exists):
    - Acquire WAL_READ_LOCK(i) in EXCLUSIVE mode
    - Write/update aReadMark[i] = m while holding EXCLUSIVE
    - Downgrade to SHARED for snapshot lifetime
    - Downgrade MUST NOT introduce unlock window (lock-type transition)
- Legacy checkpointers consult locks to decide which marks are live
- Interop limitation: 5 reader marks/locks (aReadMark[0..4])
  - Bounds distinct concurrent WAL snapshots, NOT total readers
  - Many readers can share a mark via SHARED lock
- If no slot available: return SQLITE_BUSY

#### Step 4: Checkpoint Coordination
- Checkpoint logic (§7.5) MUST update nBackfill in standard WalCkptInfo during backfill

### Ordering
- Standard WAL-index update (step 2) MUST happen AFTER wal.sync() and BEFORE publish_versions()
- If C SQLite reader sees new mxFrame, frames must already be durable on disk

### Native Mode: This protocol does NOT apply to Native Mode (ECS-based commit streams)

PARENT EPIC: bd-3t3
DEPENDS ON: bd-3t3.5 (SharedMemoryLayout), bd-3t3.1 (Core Types)

Dependencies:
  -> bd-3t3 (parent-child) - §5: MVCC Formal Model (Revised)
  -> bd-3t3.5 (blocks) - §5.6.1 SharedMemoryLayout: Cross-Process Coordination
  -> bd-3t3.1 (blocks) - §5.1 MVCC Core Types

title: §5.9.0.1 Wire Payload Schemas: Tagged Unions + Canonical Ordering + Size Caps
description:
Define the complete field-by-field wire payload schemas for all 7 coordinator IPC message kinds, including tagged union encoding conventions, canonical ordering rules, and wire size caps (spec lines 9319-9505).

SCOPE: Canonical byte-encoded payloads for coordinator wire protocol. All integers little-endian unless stated. Covers RESERVE, SUBMIT_NATIVE_PUBLISH, SUBMIT_WAL_COMMIT, ROWID_RESERVE message kinds and their tagged-union responses.

DATA STRUCTURES:
- Common atoms: ObjectId (16 raw bytes), TxnToken (txn_id:u64_le + txn_epoch:u32_le + pad:u32_le = 16 bytes)
- ReserveV1 (24 bytes fixed): purpose:u8, pad:[u8;7], txn:TxnToken
- ReserveRespV1: tagged union (tag:u8 + pad:[u8;7] + body) with Ok/Busy/Err variants
- SubmitNativePublishV1: permit_id, txn, begin_seq, capsule_object_id, capsule_digest_32, write_set_summary (variable), read/write/edge/merge witness arrays (variable), abort_policy
- NativePublishRespV1: tag + body (Ok/Conflict/Aborted/Err)
- SubmitWalCommitV1: permit_id, txn, mode, snapshot_high, schema_epoch, has_in_rw, has_out_rw, wal_fec_r, spill_pages array (SpillPageV1 = 32 bytes each: pgno, offset, len, xxh3_64)
- WalCommitRespV1: tag + body (Ok/Conflict/IoError/Err); MUST carry exactly one fd via SCM_RIGHTS
- RowIdReserveV1 (32 bytes fixed): txn, schema_epoch, table_id, count

ALGORITHMS:
- Tagged union encoding: outer tag:u8 is the ONLY discriminant; body fields of selected variant have no nested tag; pad bytes for 8-byte alignment
- write_set_summary V1 encoding: raw array of u32_le values, MUST be sorted ascending with no duplicates, len MUST be multiple of 4
- Canonical ordering: ObjectId arrays sorted lexicographically (byte-by-byte), page number arrays sorted ascending, witness arrays sorted by ObjectId

INVARIANTS:
- write_set_summary max 1 MiB (262,144 page numbers)
- Total witness + edge counts MUST NOT exceed 65,536
- Exceeding caps triggers coordinator rejection
- SUBMIT_WAL_COMMIT MUST carry exactly one fd in SCM_RIGHTS; missing/truncated/extra fds rejected

TEST REQUIREMENTS (9 unit + 1 E2E):
- test_reserve_v1_roundtrip, test_reserve_resp_tagged_union_variants, test_write_set_summary_canonical_encoding, test_write_set_summary_len_not_multiple_of_4_rejected, test_native_publish_conflict_response_page_list, test_wire_size_cap_write_set_summary_exceeds_1mib, test_wire_size_cap_total_witness_count_exceeds_65536, test_wal_commit_spill_page_encoding, test_rowid_reserve_roundtrip
- E2E: test_e2e_coordinator_ipc_roundtrip (serialize, send through transport, deserialize, validate canonical ordering + size caps)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. All message kinds round-trip correctly with exact byte sizes matching spec
2. Tagged union encoding uses only outer tag, no nested discriminators
3. Canonical ordering enforced on all ObjectId and page arrays
4. Wire size caps enforced with appropriate error codes on violation
5. SCM_RIGHTS fd passing rule enforced for SUBMIT_WAL_COMMIT

comments.text:
# §5.9.0.1 Wire Payload Schemas: Tagged Unions + Canonical Ordering + Size Caps

**Spec reference:** COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md, lines 9319–9505

## Overview

The coordinator wire protocol uses canonical byte-encoded payloads for all frame types.
All integers are little-endian unless explicitly stated otherwise. This bead covers the
complete field-by-field breakdown of all 7 message kinds, the tagged union encoding
convention, canonical ordering rules, and wire size caps.

## Common Atoms

- **ObjectId:** 16 raw bytes (no length prefix, no alignment padding).
- **TxnToken:** `txn_id: u64_le` + `txn_epoch: u32_le` + `pad: u32_le = 0` (16 bytes total).

## Tagged Union Encoding Convention (Normative)

For all `*RespV1` payloads: the outer `tag: u8` is the **only** discriminant. The `body`
is encoded as the fields of the selected variant with **no nested tag** or additional
discriminator bytes. Pad bytes (`pad0: [u8; 7]`) follow the tag for 8-byte alignment.

## Message Kind 1: RESERVE

```
ReserveV1 := {
  purpose   : u8,      // 0 = NativePublish, 1 = WalCommit
  pad0      : [u8; 7], // reserved (0)
  txn       : TxnToken,
}
```
Total size: 24 bytes (fixed).

### RESERVE Response
```
ReserveRespV1 := {
  tag  : u8,       // 0 = Ok, 1 = Busy, 2 = Err
  pad0 : [u8; 7],
  body : ReserveRespBodyV1,
}
ReserveRespBodyV1 :=
  | Ok   { permit_id: u64_le }              // 8 bytes
  | Busy { retry_after_ms: u32_le, pad1: u32_le = 0 }  // 8 bytes
  | Err  { code: u32_le }                   // 4 bytes
```

## Message Kind 2: SUBMIT_NATIVE_PUBLISH

```
SubmitNativePublishV1 := {
  permit_id           : u64_le,
  txn                 : TxnToken,
  begin_seq           : u64_le,
  capsule_object_id   : ObjectId,           // 16 bytes
  capsule_digest_32   : [u8; 32],           // BLAKE3-256(capsule bytes)
  write_set_summary_len: u32_le,
  write_set_summary    : [u8; write_set_summary_len],
  read_witness_count  : u32_le,
  read_witnesses      : [ObjectId; read_witness_count],
  write_witness_count : u32_le,
  write_witnesses     : [ObjectId; write_witness_count],
  edge_count          : u32_le,
  edges               : [ObjectId; edge_count],
  merge_witness_count : u32_le,
  merge_witnesses     : [ObjectId; merge_witness_count],
  abort_policy        : u8,
  pad0                : [u8; 7],
}
```

### SUBMIT_NATIVE_PUBLISH Response
```
NativePublishRespV1 := {
  tag  : u8,       // 0 = Ok, 1 = Conflict, 2 = Aborted, 3 = Err
  pad0 : [u8; 7],
  body : NativePublishBodyV1,
}
NativePublishBodyV1 :=
  | Ok       { commit_seq: u64_le, marker_object_id: ObjectId }
  | Conflict { conflicting_commit_seq: u64_le, page_count: u32_le, pages: [u32_le; page_count] }
  | Aborted  { code: u32_le }
  | Err      { code: u32_le }
```

## Message Kind 3: SUBMIT_WAL_COMMIT

```
SubmitWalCommitV1 := {
  permit_id          : u64_le,
  txn                : TxnToken,
  mode               : u8,       // 0 = Serialized, 1 = Concurrent
  pad0               : [u8; 7],
  snapshot_high      : u64_le,
  snapshot_schema_epoch: u64_le,
  has_in_rw          : u8,       // 0/1
  has_out_rw         : u8,       // 0/1
  wal_fec_r          : u8,
  pad1               : [u8; 5],
  spill_page_count   : u32_le,
  spill_pages        : [SpillPageV1; spill_page_count],
}

SpillPageV1 := {
  pgno     : u32_le,
  pad0     : u32_le,
  offset   : u64_le,
  len      : u32_le,   // MUST equal page_size in V1
  pad1     : u32_le,
  xxh3_64  : u64_le,
}
```
SpillPageV1 total: 32 bytes each.

**FD passing rule (required):** `SUBMIT_WAL_COMMIT` MUST carry exactly one fd in
SCM_RIGHTS ancillary data (the spill file). Missing/truncated/extra fds → reject.

### SUBMIT_WAL_COMMIT Response
```
WalCommitRespV1 := {
  tag  : u8,       // 0 = Ok, 1 = Conflict, 2 = IoError, 3 = Err
  pad0 : [u8; 7],
  body : WalCommitBodyV1,
}
WalCommitBodyV1 :=
  | Ok       { wal_offset: u64_le, commit_seq: u64_le }
  | Conflict { conflicting_txn_id: u64_le, page_count: u32_le, pages: [u32_le; page_count] }
  | IoError  { code: u32_le }
  | Err      { code: u32_le }
```

## Message Kind 4: ROWID_RESERVE

```
RowIdReserveV1 := {
  txn                : TxnToken,
  schema_epoch       : u64_le,
  table_id           : u32_le,
  count              : u32_le,
}
```
Total: 32 bytes (fixed).

### ROWID_RESERVE Response
```
RowIdReserveRespV1 := {
  tag  : u8,       // 0 = Ok, 1 = Err
  pad0 : [u8; 7],
  body : RowIdReserveBodyV1,
}
RowIdReserveBodyV1 :=
  | Ok  { start_rowid: u64_le, count: u32_le, pad1: u32_le = 0 }
  | Err { code: u32_le }
```

## write_set_summary V1 Encoding (Normative)

- `write_set_summary` is a canonical, deterministic encoding of a set of page numbers (u32).
- V1 encodes it as a raw array of `u32_le` values.
- `write_set_summary_len` MUST be a multiple of 4.
- Interpret as `pages: [u32_le; write_set_summary_len / 4]`.
- `pages` MUST be sorted ascending and MUST contain no duplicates.
- Future versions MAY introduce compressed encoding but MUST be explicitly tagged (no silent changes).

## Canonical Ordering Rules

- **ObjectId fields:** Compared lexicographically (byte-by-byte, left to right).
- **Page number arrays:** MUST be sorted ascending within each array.
- **Witness arrays:** ObjectIds within `read_witnesses`, `write_witnesses`, `edges`, and
  `merge_witnesses` MUST be sorted in ascending lexicographic ObjectId order.

## Wire Size Caps

- **write_set_summary:** Maximum 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) → max 262,144 page numbers.
- **Total witness + edge counts:** Combined `read_witness_count + write_witness_count +
  edge_count + merge_witness_count` MUST NOT exceed 65,536.
- Exceeding either cap → coordinator MUST reject with an appropriate error code.

## Unit Test Specifications

### Test 1: `test_reserve_v1_roundtrip`
Serialize a `ReserveV1` with purpose=0 (NativePublish) and a known TxnToken. Deserialize
and verify all fields match. Confirm total encoded size is exactly 24 bytes.

### Test 2: `test_reserve_resp_tagged_union_variants`
Serialize each `ReserveRespV1` variant (Ok, Busy, Err). Verify the `tag` byte is the only
discriminant and body bytes have no nested tag. Roundtrip each variant.

### Test 3: `test_write_set_summary_canonical_encoding`
Encode page set {5, 1, 100, 3} → verify output is sorted ascending [1, 3, 5, 100] as
u32_le bytes and length is 16 (multiple of 4). Decode and verify set equality.

### Test 4: `test_write_set_summary_len_not_multiple_of_4_rejected`
Attempt to decode a `write_set_summary` with `len = 7`. Verify it is rejected with an
appropriate error (not silently truncated).

### Test 5: `test_native_publish_conflict_response_page_list`
Serialize a `NativePublishRespV1::Conflict` with 3 conflicting pages. Deserialize and
verify `conflicting_commit_seq`, `page_count`, and each page number.

### Test 6: `test_wire_size_cap_write_set_summary_exceeds_1mib`
Construct a `write_set_summary` with 262,145 page numbers (just over 1 MiB). Verify
the coordinator rejects it. Verify 262,144 pages (exactly 1 MiB) is accepted.

### Test 7: `test_wire_size_cap_total_witness_count_exceeds_65536`
Construct a `SubmitNativePublishV1` where total witness+edge counts = 65,537. Verify
rejection. Verify 65,536 total is accepted.

### Test 8: `test_wal_commit_spill_page_encoding`
Serialize a `SubmitWalCommitV1` with 3 spill pages. Verify each `SpillPageV1` is exactly
32 bytes and fields roundtrip correctly including the `xxh3_64` hash.

### Test 9: `test_rowid_reserve_roundtrip`
Serialize a `RowIdReserveV1` with known table_id and count. Verify total size is 32 bytes.
Roundtrip and confirm field equality.

title: §18.1-18.4 Conflict Model: Pairwise + Birthday Paradox + Collision Mass M2 + AMS Sketch
description:
## SUMMARY
Defines the probabilistic conflict model for FrankenSQLite's MVCC concurrent writers. Covers the pairwise conflict probability formula for two transactions writing W pages from P total pages, the birthday paradox generalization to N concurrent writers (P(conflict) ~ 1 - exp(-N(N-1)W^2/(2P))), the sqrt(P) threshold where conflicts become substantial, and the collision mass M2 = sum(q(pgno)^2) formulation that generalizes the uniform model to arbitrary skew (Zipf, structural bursts, hot leaves). The AMS F2 sketch provides bounded-memory online estimation of M2, yielding M2_hat = F2_hat / txn_count^2 and effective collision pool P_eff_hat = 1/M2_hat. The model is intentionally distribution-free: M2_hat captures hot-page concentration directly without assuming Zipf or any parametric form.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS
- **Pairwise conflict formula:** P(conflict T1,T2) ~ 1 - exp(-W^2/P) for uniform writes; generalized to P(conflict) ~ 1 - exp(-M2) using collision mass M2.
- **Birthday paradox N-writer formula:** P(any conflict) ~ 1 - exp(-C(N,2) * M2), where C(N,2) = N(N-1)/2.
- **Collision mass M2:** M2 := sum_pgno q(pgno)^2, where q(pgno) is the probability a random writing transaction includes pgno in its write_set. Under uniform model, M2 = W^2/P.
- **Effective collision pool P_eff:** P_eff := 1/M2; plays role of "year length" in birthday paradox for transactions.
- **AMS F2 Sketch:** R sign hash functions s_r(pgno) in {+1,-1}; signed accumulators z_r := sum(s_r(pgno) * c_pgno); estimator F2_hat := median_r(z_r^2). Default R=12, accumulate in i128, square into u128.
- **Hash/sign function:** seed_r = Trunc64(BLAKE3("fsqlite:m2:ams:v1" || db_epoch || regime_id || window_id || r)); h = mix64(seed_r XOR pgno_u64); sign = +1 if (h & 1) == 0 else -1. mix64 is SplitMix64 finalization.
- **Zipf skew model (approximate):** p(k) = (1/k^s)/H(P,s); M2 ~ W^2 * H(P,2s)/H(P,s)^2. Used for intuition, NOT as a policy input.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS
- NI-1: Any policy using conflict predictions MUST use M2_hat (online estimate) rather than assuming fixed skew parameter s.
- NI-2: M2_hat MUST be computed per BOCPD regime and per fixed deterministic window (e.g., 10s). Windowing MUST be deterministic under LabRuntime (lab time / epoch ticks, not wall-clock).
- NI-3: AMS sketch R MUST be a small constant in [8,32]; default R=12.
- NI-4: z_r accumulation and z_r^2 MUST NOT overflow; use i128/u128.
- NI-5: Sketch memory MUST be bounded O(1 KiB) to O(16 KiB) per regime; update cost O(R) per pgno.
- NI-6: Under LabRuntime, the sketch MUST be deterministic for a given seed and trace.
- NI-7: If txn_count == 0, define M2_hat = 0 and P_eff_hat = +infinity. If M2_hat == 0, P_eff_hat = +infinity.
- NI-8: Hash/sign randomization MUST be seeded from (db_epoch, regime_id, window_id) and recorded in evidence ledger when used for policy decisions.
- NI-9: P_eff_hat MUST be treated as advisory (not an estimate of physical page count).

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
1. `test_pairwise_conflict_uniform` - Verify P(conflict T1,T2) ~ 1 - exp(-W^2/P) for W=100, P=1_000_000 within 1% relative error.
2. `test_birthday_paradox_n_writers` - For N=10, W=100, P=1_000_000: verify exponent = N*(N-1)*W^2/(2*P) = 0.45 and P(conflict) ~ 36%.
3. `test_collision_mass_uniform` - Under uniform q(pgno) = W/P, verify M2 = W^2/P and P_eff = P/W^2.
4. `test_ams_sketch_exact_small` - For a small window (e.g., 50 pages, 20 txns), compute exact F2 and assert F2_hat from AMS sketch is within declared tolerance.
5. `test_ams_sketch_deterministic_replay` - Under LabRuntime with fixed seed and trace, two runs produce identical F2_hat.
6. `test_ams_sketch_sign_hash_deterministic` - Same (seed_r, pgno) always produces same sign via mix64(seed_r XOR pgno).
7. `test_ams_sketch_overflow_protection` - Accumulation in i128 does not overflow for max plausible window sizes.
8. `test_ams_sketch_memory_bound` - Sketch state for R=12 fits within 16 KiB.
9. `test_m2_hat_zero_txn_count` - When txn_count=0, M2_hat=0 and P_eff_hat is +infinity (or omitted).
10. `test_m2_hat_tracks_skew` - Inject Zipf-distributed write sets (s=1.0) and verify M2_hat > uniform M2 by significant margin.
11. `test_birthday_paradox_with_m2` - P(any conflict) ~ 1 - exp(-C(N,2) * M2_hat) matches simulated conflict rate within 20%.
12. `test_mix64_splitmix_golden` - mix64 implementation matches known SplitMix64 test vectors.

## E2E TEST
Run 8 concurrent writers (LabRuntime deterministic schedule) against a 100K-page database with Zipf-skewed keys (s=0.99). Over 500 transactions:
- Verify AMS sketch M2_hat converges to within 25% of exact M2 (computed from full incidence counts).

comments.text:
## §18.1-18.4 Probabilistic Conflict Model: Problem + Pairwise + Birthday Paradox + Skew/M2

### Problem Statement (§18.1)
N concurrent writing transactions, each touching W pages uniformly from P total pages. What is P(≥2 transactions conflict on same page)?

### Pairwise Conflict (§18.2)
P(no conflict T1,T2) = C(P-W,W)/C(P,W) = product((P-W-i)/(P-i)) for i=0..W-1. For W<<P: P(conflict) ~ 1 - e^(-W²/P).

### Birthday Paradox (§18.3)
P(any conflict among N) ~ 1 - e^{-N(N-1)W²/(2P)}. N(N-1) not N² (can't conflict with self).

**Threshold:** Conflicts substantial near N*W ~ sqrt(P). For P=1M: N=10,W=100 → 36%. N=10,W=370 → >99%. P(conflict)>50% requires exponent > ln(2) ≈ 0.693 → N(N-1)W² > 1.386P.

### Non-Uniform Skew (§18.4)
Real write sets are skewed (structural hot pages, internal pages, hot leaves). Zipf p(k) = (1/k^s)/H(P,s). But model is about write-set page distribution, not read path.

**Primary quantity: Collision Mass M2 (§18.4.1.1)**
M2 := Σ q(pgno)². P_eff := 1/M2. Under uniform: M2=W²/P, P_eff=P/W². Birthday approximation: P(conflict) ~ 1 - exp(-C(N,2)*M2). M2 is model-free (no Zipf assumption). P_eff MUST NOT be interpreted as physical page count.

**Normative:** Policy MUST use M2_hat (measured), not assumed s.

**Data Collection (§18.4.1.2):** Based on write-set incidence at commit. Deterministic windowing under LabRuntime. Per window: txn_count, F2 sketch state, optional heavy-hitters. Ties break by pgno. Hash seeded from (db_epoch, regime_id, window_id).

**Estimator A: AMS F2 Sketch (§18.4.1.3.1, required)**
R sign hash functions s_r(pgno)∈{+1,-1}, accumulators z_r. Update: z_r += s_r(pgno) per write-set page per txn. End: F2_hat = median_r(z_r²), M2_hat = F2_hat/txn_count².

Hash: seed_r = Trunc64(BLAKE3("fsqlite:m2:ams:v1" || db_epoch || regime_id || window_id || r)). sign_r(pgno) = if (mix64(seed_r XOR pgno) & 1)==0 then +1 else -1. mix64 = SplitMix64 finalization.

Parameters: R=12 default (8-32). z_r in i128, z_r² in u128. Memory O(1-16 KiB). Update O(R) per pgno. Deterministic under LabRuntime.

**Validation:** Lab harness computes exact F2 for small windows, asserts F2_hat tracks within tolerance.

**Heavy-Hitter Decomposition (§18.4.1.3.2, recommended)**
SpaceSaving-style. K=64 default (32-256). Entry: {pgno, count_hat, err}. Deterministic tie-breaking (min pgno). Bounded error: count_hat-err ≤ c_pgno ≤ count_hat. Head/tail decomposition for explainability. Required in evidence ledger when M2_hat influences decision.

**Estimator B: Zipf s_hat (§18.4.1.4, optional)**
Discrete MLE. Bounded Newton. Clamp s∈[0.1,2.0]. Per BOCPD regime. Interpretability/benchmark generation ONLY. MUST NOT be used as policy input when M2_hat available.

title: §4.13 Obligations: Lifecycle + Leak Detection + FrankenSQLite Registry
description:
Implement asupersync obligation (linear resource) tracking with two-phase lifecycle, leak detection, and the five FrankenSQLite obligation types (§4.13, spec lines ~4996-5070).

SCOPE AND PURPOSE: Asupersync models cancellation-safe effects using obligations (linear resources) with a two-phase lifecycle. Every reserved obligation MUST reach a terminal state (Committed or Aborted). Non-terminal drop from Reserved = Leaked = correctness bug. This turns "best-effort cleanup" into a structural invariant.

KEY DATA STRUCTURES AND APIs:
- Obligation state machine: Reserved -> Committed (via commit) or Aborted (via abort/drop). Reserved -> Leaked (via drop without resolution) = correctness bug.
- TrackedSender: Wraps inner channel sender, holds an obligation; sending commits, dropping without send aborts or leaks.
- ObligationLedger: Global tracker of all outstanding obligations for diagnostic dumps.
- INV-NO-OBLIGATION-LEAKS: Core invariant; every reserved obligation MUST reach terminal state.

5 FRANKENSQLITE OBLIGATION TYPES:
1. SendPermit reservations (commit pipeline two-phase MPSC): Leak = stuck pipeline slot.
2. Commit response delivery (reply obligation on oneshot/session replies): Leak = caller hangs forever.
3. TxnSlot acquisition + renewal (lease obligations): Leak = slot exhaustion.
4. Witness-plane reservation tokens (reserve/commit for symbol/object publication): Leak = phantom reservations blocking GC.
5. Shared-state registration (name/registration that could go stale): Leak = stale entries.

TRACKED TWO-PHASE CHANNELS (§4.13.1): TrackedSender guarantees dropping a permit without resolution is structurally detected. Channel policy rules: non-critical telemetry MAY use send_evict_oldest; commit ordering, durability publication, cross-process coordination MUST NOT drop messages and MUST use obligation-tracked sends.

LEAK RESPONSE POLICY (§4.13.2):
- Lab mode: Obligation leak = test failure (panic). Indicates cancel-safety or protocol bug.
- Production mode: Obligation leak = correctness incident. Response: (1) emit diagnostic bundle (trace + obligation ledger), (2) fail affected connection, (3) keep database process alive IF durability invariants not violated.

CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS: Lab vs production mode for leak response. send_evict_oldest policy for non-critical channels. Channel capacity for telemetry channels.

ERROR HANDLING: Lab mode: panic on leak with "obligation leak" message. Production mode: diagnostic bundle (trace log + obligation ledger), connection close, process kept alive. Diagnostic dump includes leaked entry creation backtrace.

UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS (10 tests): (1) SendPermit commit reaches Committed, no leak. (2) TxnSlot abort reaches Aborted, no leak. (3) Witness reservation drop without resolution panics in lab with "obligation leak" message. (4) Production mode: commit response drop -> diagnostic bundle emitted, connection closed, process alive. (5) TrackedSender commit on send. (6) TrackedSender leak on drop. (7) All 5 obligation types registered: 5 committed, 0 leaked in ledger. (8) Diagnostic dump: 3 obligations (1 committed, 1 aborted, 1 leaked) -> dump contains exactly 1 leaked entry with creation backtrace. (9) Cancel resolves obligations: task with 2 obligations cancelled and drained -> both Aborted. (10) Non-critical channel send_evict_oldest: capacity 2, send 3 -> oldest evicted, no obligation leak.

E2E TEST: Run representative flow creating obligations, inject cancellation at multiple checkpoints. Verify all reach terminal state. Inject one deliberate leak: lab fails fast, production emits diagnostics and closes connection.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: All 5 obligation types correctly implement two-phase lifecycle. TrackedSender structurally detects leaks. ObligationLedger tracks all outstanding obligations. Lab/production leak response policies are enforced. Diagnostic dumps include creation backtraces for leaked obligations.

comments.text:
# §4.13 Obligations: Lifecycle + Leak Detection + FrankenSQLite Registry

**Spec Reference:** COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md, lines 4996–5070

## Overview

Asupersync models cancellation-safe effects using **obligations** (linear resources)
with a two-phase lifecycle. Obligations turn "best-effort cleanup" into a structural
invariant. Every reserved obligation MUST reach a terminal state.

## Obligation State Machine

```
Reserved  ──commit──▶  Committed
    │
    └─abort/drop──▶  Aborted

(Bug) Reserved ──drop without resolution──▶ Leaked  (detected by oracles)
```

Terminal states: Committed, Aborted.
Non-terminal drop from Reserved = Leaked = correctness bug.

## Core Invariant: INV-NO-OBLIGATION-LEAKS

Every reserved obligation MUST reach a terminal state (Committed or Aborted).
Leaked obligations are correctness bugs:
- **Lab mode:** fail-fast (panic)
- **Production:** diagnostic escalation (trace + metrics + connection close)

## The 5 FrankenSQLite Obligation Types

1. **SendPermit reservations** (commit pipeline, two-phase MPSC):
   A reserved permit to send a commit capsule. MUST be committed (send) or aborted
   (release permit). Leak = stuck pipeline slot.

2. **Commit response delivery** (reply obligation on oneshot/session replies):
   The obligation to deliver a commit result back to the caller. MUST be committed
   (send response) or aborted (send error). Leak = caller hangs forever.

3. **TxnSlot acquisition + renewal** (lease obligations):
   Transaction slot leases. MUST be committed (released on txn end) or aborted
   (on expiry/crash). Leak = slot exhaustion.

4. **Witness-plane reservation tokens** (reserve/commit for symbol/object publication):
   A reservation to publish a witness symbol or object. MUST be committed (publish)
   or aborted (release reservation). Leak = phantom reservations blocking GC.

5. **Shared-state registration** (name/registration that could go stale on crash):
   Any entry in shared state (connection registry, subscriber list, etc.). MUST be
   committed (maintained) or aborted (deregistered). Leak = stale entries.

## §4.13.1 Tracked Two-Phase Channels (TrackedSender API)

For safety-critical internal messaging, FrankenSQLite SHOULD use asupersync's
obligation-tracked session channels (`asupersync::channel::session`) rather than
raw MPSC/oneshot.

### TrackedSender Guarantees
- Dropping a permit without resolution is **structurally detected** (not just
  convention-based)
- Lab mode: leaks MUST fail fast (panic-on-leak)
- Production: leaks MUST be trace-visible (log + metrics) AND MUST trigger
  escalation (close the offending region/connection) — NOT silent continuation

### Channel Policy Rules
- **Non-critical telemetry channels**: MAY use `send_evict_oldest` policy
- **Commit ordering, durability publication, cross-process coordination**: MUST NOT
  drop messages. These channels MUST use obligation-tracked sends.

## §4.13.2 Obligation Leak Response Policy (Lab vs Production)

### Lab Runtime Default
- Obligation leak = test failure (panic)
- Rationale: indicates a cancel-safety or protocol bug that must be fixed before
  shipping

### Production Default
- Obligation leak = correctness incident
- Response:
  1. Emit diagnostic bundle (trace + obligation ledger)
  2. Fail the affected connection
  3. Keep the database process alive IF AND ONLY IF invariants for durability objects
     are not violated
- Rationale: contain the blast radius; do not take down the entire database for a
  single connection's protocol bug

## Implementation Notes

- Place obligation types in `fsqlite-harness` or `fsqlite-mvcc` depending on where
  the two-phase protocol lives
- Each obligation type needs a `Drop` impl that checks terminal state and panics/logs
  if leaked
- Consider a global `ObligationLedger` that tracks all outstanding obligations for
  diagnostic dumps
- TrackedSender wraps the inner channel sender and holds an obligation; sending commits
  the obligation, dropping without send aborts or leaks

## Unit Test Specifications

1. **test_obligation_commit_reaches_terminal**: Create a SendPermit obligation. Commit
   it (send the message). Assert state is `Committed`. No leak detected.

2. **test_obligation_abort_reaches_terminal**: Create a TxnSlot obligation. Abort it
   (explicit release). Assert state is `Aborted`. No leak detected.

3. **test_obligation_leak_panics_in_lab**: Create a witness reservation obligation.
   Drop it without commit or abort. Assert panic in lab mode with a message mentioning
   "obligation leak".

4. **test_obligation_leak_diagnostic_in_production**: Create a commit response
   obligation in production mode. Drop it without resolution. Assert: diagnostic bundle
   emitted (trace log contains "obligation leak"), affected connection is closed, process
   stays alive.

5. **test_tracked_sender_commit_on_send**: Create a TrackedSender wrapping a oneshot.
   Send a value. Assert the underlying obligation is Committed.

6. **test_tracked_sender_leak_on_drop**: Create a TrackedSender. Drop it without
   sending. Assert the obligation is detected as leaked (panic in lab).

7. **test_five_obligation_types_registered**: Create one of each of the 5 obligation
   types (SendPermit, commit response, TxnSlot, witness reservation, shared-state
   registration). Commit all. Assert the ObligationLedger shows 5 committed, 0 leaked.

8. **test_obligation_ledger_diagnostic_dump**: Create 3 obligations, commit 1, abort 1,
   leak 1. Request a diagnostic dump from the ledger. Assert the dump contains exactly
   1 leaked entry with its creation backtrace.

9. **test_cancel_resolves_obligations**: Create a task holding 2 obligations. Cancel the
   task and drain it. Assert both obligations reached terminal state (Aborted) during
   the drain phase.

10. **test_non_critical_channel_evict_oldest**: Create a telemetry channel with
    `send_evict_oldest` policy and capacity 2. Send 3 messages. Assert oldest was
    evicted and no obligation leak is reported (policy permits eviction).

description:
# 5I.2: Ensure IndexSchema Available to Codegen for DML

## Objective

Verify and fix that the codegen layer has access to complete index information when generating DML opcodes.

## Background

For the codegen to generate index update opcodes, it needs to know:
1. Which indexes exist on the target table
2. Which columns each index covers
3. The root page number of each index B-tree
4. Whether the index is UNIQUE (affects conflict handling)

This information is stored in `IndexSchema` and must be passed to the codegen functions.

## Current State Investigation

Check how `codegen_insert()`, `codegen_delete()`, `codegen_update()` receive table/index info:

```rust
// Expected signature pattern:
pub fn codegen_insert(
    ctx: &mut CodegenContext,
    table: &TableSchema,
    indexes: &[IndexSchema],  // <-- Is this present?
    ...
) -> Result<(), CodegenError>
```

If `indexes` parameter is missing or always empty, that's the problem.

## Required Changes

### 1. IndexSchema Definition

Ensure `IndexSchema` in `fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen/mod.rs` contains:
```rust
pub struct IndexSchema {
    pub name: String,
    pub table_name: String,
    pub root_page: i32,           // B-tree root page
    pub columns: Vec<ColumnInfo>, // Columns in index order
    pub column_indices: Vec<usize>, // Positions in table schema
    pub is_unique: bool,
    pub is_partial: bool,         // Partial index (WHERE clause)
    pub where_clause: Option<Expr>, // For partial indexes
}
```

### 2. Schema Retrieval in Connection

In `connection.rs`, when executing DML, ensure indexes are fetched:
```rust
fn get_indexes_for_table(&self, table_name: &str) -> Vec<IndexSchema> {
    // Query sqlite_master for indexes on this table
    // Parse CREATE INDEX statements
    // Build IndexSchema for each
}
```

### 3. Pass to Codegen

Ensure the codegen call site passes index information:
```rust
let indexes = self.get_indexes_for_table(&table_name);
codegen_insert(ctx, &table_schema, &indexes, ...)?;
```

## Verification

After fix, add tracing to confirm indexes are passed:
```rust
tracing::debug!(
    table = %table_schema.name,
    index_count = indexes.len(),
    "codegen_insert received {} indexes",
    indexes.len()
);
```

## Test Case

```rust
#[test]
fn test_codegen_receives_index_schema() {
    let conn = Connection::open(":memory:").unwrap();
    conn.execute("CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)").unwrap();
    conn.execute("CREATE INDEX idx_name ON t(name)").unwrap();
    
    // Enable tracing/debugging
    // Execute INSERT
    conn.execute("INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'alice')").unwrap();
    
    // Verify index was seen by codegen (via trace output or internal state)
}
```

## Dependencies

- Depends on bd-1mbd (5I.1) diagnosis to confirm this is the issue
- Blocks bd-3k7h (5I.3) INSERT index maintenance

comments.text:
## Finding: CREATE INDEX Does Not Allocate B-tree

### Root Cause Identified

`execute_create_index` at connection.rs:1871-1922 is incomplete:

```rust
// Line 1914-1918: Hardcoded root_page: 0
table.indexes.push(IndexSchema {
    name: stmt.name.name.clone(),
    columns: col_names,
    root_page: 0,  // <-- PROBLEM: Should be allocated page
});
```

### What CREATE INDEX Should Do (But Doesn't)

Compare with `execute_create_table` (connection.rs:1659-1671):
1. `let root_page = self.allocate_root_page()?;` - allocates B-tree page
2. `self.db.borrow_mut().create_table_at(root_page, ...)` - creates B-tree
3. Records `root_page` in schema
4. `self.insert_sqlite_master_row(...)` - persists to sqlite_master

CREATE INDEX currently:
1. Does NOT allocate a page ❌
2. Does NOT create a B-tree ❌
3. Records `root_page: 0` ❌
4. Does NOT persist to sqlite_master ❌

### Required Changes

1. **fsqlite-types/src/lib.rs**: Add `write_empty_leaf_index` (uses LeafIndex type 0x0A instead of LeafTable 0x0D)

2. **connection.rs**:
   - Add `allocate_index_root_page()` method
   - Fix `execute_create_index()`:
     - Allocate index root page
     - Create B-tree at that page
     - Store real root_page in IndexSchema
     - Insert sqlite_master row

### Impact

Without this fix:
- IndexSchema.root_page = 0 (invalid)
- Codegen would emit `OpenWrite` with root_page 0
- Index operations would corrupt page 0 (database header!)
- Even if codegen generated IdxInsert, it would fail

### Next Steps

This diagnosis confirms bd-3jjd needs implementation work. The codegen DOES have access to IndexSchema (via TableSchema.indexes), but the IndexSchema has invalid data.

title: §6.5-6.7 MVCC Adaptation: Ghost Lists + Eviction Rules + Version Coalescing
description:
Implements §6.5-6.7 of the FrankenSQLite spec: MVCC adaptations to the ARC cache covering ghost list semantics, eviction rules for pinned pages and durability boundaries, and version coalescing.

SUMMARY: Adapts standard ARC to MVCC by changing ghost list hit semantics to require exact (pgno, commit_seq) match, defining the all-pinned overflow safety valve, establishing the critical rule that eviction MUST NOT write to the WAL, and specifying the version coalescing algorithm that reclaims superseded page versions when the GC horizon advances.

KEY DATA STRUCTURES AND ALGORITHMS:
- Ghost List Semantics: Ghost hit ONLY on exact (pgno, commit_seq) match. Different versions of same page are genuinely different access patterns. Ghost pruning: B1.retain/B2.retain for entries with commit_seq >= gc_horizon.
- Capacity Accounting: Each (pgno, commit_seq) counts as one entry. Heavily-versioned pages consume multiple slots (correct behavior — prioritizes needed versions over breadth).
- All-Pinned Overflow: capacity_overflow += 1, log warning, decrement on next unpin(). Pinned count bounded by concurrent_cursors * max_btree_depth (typically < 200).
- Version Coalescing Algorithm: coalesce_versions(cache, pgno, gc_horizon) — get all cached entries for pgno, sort by commit_seq desc, keep newest committed below horizon, remove superseded if unpinned (re-insert if pinned for later), do NOT add coalesced entries to ghost list (permanently dead).
- Coalescing Triggers: (1) During REPLACE (opportunistic), (2) After GC horizon advance (batch), (3) On PRAGMA shrink_memory.

NORMATIVE INVARIANTS:
- CRITICAL: ARC eviction MUST NOT append to .wal — WAL transaction boundaries assume contiguous frames; eviction appending creates uncommitted frames before commit markers = silent corruption
- Only WriteCoordinator (§5.9.2) may append to .wal; buffer pool treats eviction as memory-only
- Uncommitted pages live in transaction write_set, spillable to per-txn temp file (§5.9.2)
- Superseded pages removed by coalescing MUST NOT be added to ghost list (permanently dead, not evicted)
- Ghost hits must match exact (pgno, commit_seq) — different versions are different access patterns
- Ghost entries below gc_horizon MUST be pruned to prevent unbounded ghost list growth

UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS:
1. test_ghost_hit_exact_match: Ghost hit only fires on exact (pgno, commit_seq)
2. test_ghost_miss_different_version: Same pgno, different commit_seq is NOT a ghost hit
3. test_ghost_prune_below_horizon: After gc_horizon advance, ghost entries below horizon removed
4. test_pinned_page_eviction_overflow: All T1 pages pinned triggers capacity_overflow increment
5. test_overflow_decrement_on_unpin: After unpin, capacity_overflow decremented and eviction triggered
6. test_eviction_never_writes_wal: Eviction path never calls wal_write_frame or equivalent
7. test_uncommitted_pages_in_write_set: Uncommitted pages accessible only via transaction write_set
8. test_version_coalesce_keeps_newest: Coalescing keeps newest committed version below horizon
9. test_version_coalesce_removes_superseded: Superseded unpinned versions removed from cache
10. test_version_coalesce_skips_pinned: Pinned superseded versions NOT removed
11. test_coalesced_not_ghosted: Superseded version removal does NOT add to ghost list
12. test_coalesce_trigger_on_replace: Coalescing runs opportunistically during REPLACE
13. test_coalesce_trigger_on_gc_advance: Batch coalescing after gc_horizon advance

E2E TEST: Create DB with 8 concurrent writers, each doing 100 INSERT/UPDATE ops. Verify ghost lists bounded by capacity, old versions reclaimed after GC horizon advances, no .wal corruption from eviction, capacity_overflow never exceeds max(concurrent_cursors * max_btree_depth, 200).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Ghost list semantics correctly differentiate page versions by exact (pgno, commit_seq) match
- Eviction never touches the WAL under any circumstances (verified by I/O tracing)
- Version coalescing reclaims superseded versions when gc_horizon advances
- Ghost lists remain bounded (no unbounded growth from version proliferation)
- All-pinned overflow mechanism prevents deadlock while maintaining bounded growth
- Memory usage decreases measurably after GC horizon advance triggers batch coalescing

comments.text:
## Merged from P2 bead bd-16ks (§6.5-6.8 MVCC Adaptation + Eviction Rules + Version Coalescing + Snapshot Visibility)

## §6.5 MVCC Adaptation: (PageNumber, CommitSeq) Keying

**Ghost list semantics change:** Ghost entry (pgno, old_commit_seq) in B1 and request for (pgno, new_commit_seq) is NOT a ghost hit — it's a different version. Ghost hits only on exact (pgno, commit_seq) match. Correct because different versions have genuinely different access patterns.

**Version coalescing in ghost lists:** When GC horizon advances, prune entries below horizon: B1.retain(|k| k.commit_seq >= gc_horizon), B2.retain(...).

**Capacity accounting:** Each (pgno, commit_seq) counts as one entry. Heavily-versioned pages consume multiple slots — correct behavior (prioritizes needed versions over breadth).

## §6.6 Eviction: Pinned Pages and Durability Boundaries

**All pages pinned scenario:** Temporarily grow capacity by 1 (capacity_overflow += 1). Log warning. On next unpin(), decrement overflow and trigger eviction. Safety valve only. Pinned count bounded by concurrent_cursors * max_btree_depth (typically <200).

**CRITICAL RULE (normative): ARC eviction MUST NOT append to .wal.** In Compatibility mode, WAL transaction boundaries encoded by commit frame marker (db_size != 0). Assumes frames appended contiguously with no uncommitted frames in committed prefix. If eviction appended uncommitted frame and another txn committed, the eviction frame would lie before a commit marker — treated as committed by legacy WAL-index machinery. That is silent corruption. Only WriteCoordinator (S5.9.2) may append to .wal. Buffer pool treats eviction as memory-only.

**Uncommitted pages:** Live in transaction's write_set (S5.1, S5.4). MUST be spillable to per-txn temporary spill file in Compatibility mode (prevents OOM). See S5.9.2 for spill mechanism.

## §6.7 MVCC Version Coalescing

When newer committed version of a page is visible to ALL active snapshots, older versions are reclaimable.

**Coalescing triggers:** (1) During REPLACE (opportunistic: check if candidate superseded), (2) After GC horizon advances (batch scan), (3) On PRAGMA shrink_memory.

**Algorithm coalesce_versions(cache, pgno, gc_horizon):** Get all cached entries for pgno. Sort by commit_seq desc. kept_committed = false. For each: if commit_seq != 0 AND commit_seq <= gc_horizon: keep first (newest committed below horizon), remove rest if not pinned (re-insert if pinned, try later). Do NOT add to ghost list — version is permanently dead.

## §6.8 Snapshot Visibility (CommitSeq, O(1))

Uses commit-seq snapshots (S5). Snapshot.high = latest committed CommitSeq visible to txn. Version visibility checks during version-chain traversal are O(1) — no in_flight set or Bloom filter needed.

**Fast path:** is_visible(version_commit_seq, snapshot) = version_commit_seq != 0 && version_commit_seq <= snapshot.high

Uncommitted versions (commit_seq = 0) never visible through MVCC resolution; only via owning txn's private write_set (self-visibility).

comments.text:
## Untyped column affinity bug

When a column has no type declaration (e.g., `CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, val)`), inserting an integer literal like `10` results in the value being stored as `Text("10")` instead of `Integer(10)`.

### SQLite behavior
A column with no type name should have BLOB/NONE affinity, meaning no type conversion is applied — values are stored in their native type. Integer 10 should remain integer.

### Observed behavior
`INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10)` followed by `SELECT typeof(val), val FROM t` returns `text, "10"`.

### Root cause (likely)
The `Affinity` opcode emission in `codegen_insert_values()` (added in Session 25 for conformance test 017) may be applying TEXT affinity for columns that have no type declaration, when it should apply BLOB/NONE affinity (no conversion).

### Files to investigate
- `crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs` — `codegen_insert_values()` Affinity opcode emission
- `crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/engine.rs` — Affinity opcode execution

title: Fixtures: Ingest selected DBs into golden/work + manifest (sha256 + PRAGMA introspection)
description:
## Goal
Given a selected set of source DB paths, ingest them into `sample_sqlite_db_files/` with reproducible metadata.

## Ingestion Steps
1. Copy source DB -> `golden/<fixture_id>.sqlite3` (or preserve extension).
2. Compute sha256 of golden and store in manifest.
3. Mark golden read-only.
4. Create `work/<fixture_id>.sqlite3` as a copy of golden.
5. Collect lightweight introspection via `sqlite3`:
   - `PRAGMA page_size;`
   - `PRAGMA journal_mode;`
   - `PRAGMA user_version;`
   - `PRAGMA integrity_check;` (on golden)
   - `SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master;`

## Fixture IDs
- Deterministic from source path + sha256 prefix (avoid collisions).

## Acceptance
- Ingest at least 10 fixtures (mix of beads.db + non-beads db) into golden/work.
- Manifest captures sha256 + size + page_size for each.
- Re-running ingestion is idempotent (no accidental rewrites).

title: Migrate WAL Background Workers to the Per-Database Region
description:
**Reasoning:**
WAL flushing, checkpointing, and RaptorQ FEC repair threads must run in the Database Region to ensure coordinated flushing on shutdown. Like MVCC, they need configurable tuning and robust error handling to serve enterprise users.

**Action Items:**
1. **Convert to Async Tasks:** Refactor WAL checkpointing and FEC repair workers to `async fn(cx: &mut Cx) -> Result<()>`. Implement `cx.yield_now()`.
2. **Safe Drain Protocol (Multi-phase):** When `cx` is cancelled, the WAL worker must catch the cancel, enter a 'finalize' phase, and complete any pending `fsync` flushes. 
3. **Fatal I/O Handling:** If `fsync` fails with `ENOSPC` or `EIO`, the worker must immediately return an error to poison the database state, preventing further writes that cannot be durably logged.
4. **Expose Tuning PRAGMAs:** Wire up `PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint` and `PRAGMA wal_flush_delay_ms` to control the background task's batching behavior.

**Testing & Logging:**
- **E2E Test:** `test_wal_shared_graceful_shutdown` and `test_wal_fatal_io_triggers_poisoning`.
- **Logging:** Log structured fields for flush latency and batch size. Emit metrics (`histogram!("fsqlite.wal.flush_latency_us", lat)`).

title: §12.7-12.9 DDL: CREATE VIEW + CREATE TRIGGER + ALTER/DROP/REINDEX/ANALYZE
description:
E2E Test:
- test_e2e_bd_3kin_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

## SUMMARY

Implements CREATE VIEW (S12.7), CREATE TRIGGER (S12.8), and DDL maintenance statements (S12.9): ALTER TABLE (RENAME TO, RENAME COLUMN, ADD COLUMN, remove column via DDL), object removal for TABLE/INDEX/VIEW/TRIGGER with IF EXISTS, REINDEX, and ANALYZE. Views are expanded inline during query compilation (not materialized unless CTE MATERIALIZED). Views are read-only unless INSTEAD OF trigger is defined. Triggers support BEFORE/AFTER/INSTEAD OF timing, OLD/NEW pseudo-tables, WHEN clause, RAISE functions (IGNORE/ROLLBACK/ABORT/FAIL), recursive triggers (PRAGMA recursive_triggers), and SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH (default 1000). Trigger execution MUST use heap-allocated frame stack (Vec<VdbeFrame>), NOT Rust call-stack recursion.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS

- **View Inline Expansion**: Views expanded as subqueries during query compilation. Column aliases override SELECT column names.
- **Trigger Subprogram (OP_Program)**: Each trigger body compiled as a VDBE subprogram. OLD/NEW pseudo-tables implemented as register references.
- **Heap-Allocated Frame Stack (Vec<VdbeFrame>)**: Each nested trigger pushes a VdbeFrame containing program counter, register file, cursor state, and return metadata. MUST NOT use Rust call-stack recursion.
- **RAISE Function Dispatch**: RAISE(IGNORE) skips remainder of trigger body. RAISE(ROLLBACK/ABORT/FAIL) with specified transaction semantics.
- **ALTER TABLE Rewrite**: Column removal always rewrites the entire table to purge removed column data. ADD COLUMN modifies schema only.
- **INSTEAD OF Trigger**: Only valid on views. Replaces DML operation entirely; trigger body performs actual modifications.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS

1. Views MUST be expanded inline (not materialized) unless wrapped in CTE with MATERIALIZED.
2. Views MUST be read-only unless an INSTEAD OF trigger is defined.
3. BEFORE triggers fire before DML and can modify/prevent via RAISE(). AFTER triggers fire after DML.
4. INSTEAD OF triggers are only valid on views and replace the DML operation entirely.
5. INSERT triggers have NEW only. DELETE triggers have OLD only. UPDATE triggers have both OLD and NEW.
6. Trigger execution MUST use heap-allocated frame stack, NOT Rust call-stack recursion.
7. Recursive triggers MUST be disabled by default (PRAGMA recursive_triggers = OFF).
8. Maximum trigger recursion depth MUST be SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH (default 1000).
9. Engine MUST enforce Cx-budgeted memory ceiling for nested frames; exceeding budget MUST fail cleanly (SQLITE_NOMEM or SQLITE_LIMIT).
10. Column removal fails if column is part of PK, has UNIQUE, referenced by index, in CHECK/FK, or is only column.
11. Column removal always rewrites the table to purge the removed column data.
12. Object removal (for TABLE/INDEX/VIEW/TRIGGER) with IF EXISTS MUST NOT error on missing object.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS

1. test_create_view_basic -- CREATE VIEW with SELECT statement
2. test_create_view_column_aliases -- Column aliases override SELECT column names
3. test_create_view_if_not_exists -- IF NOT EXISTS prevents error on duplicate
4. test_create_temp_view -- TEMP VIEW created in temp schema
5. test_view_inline_expansion -- View is expanded inline (not materialized)
6. test_view_read_only -- INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on view without INSTEAD OF trigger fails
7. test_view_with_recursive_cte -- View referencing recursive CTE works
8. test_instead_of_trigger_on_view -- INSTEAD OF trigger enables DML on view
9. test_trigger_before_insert -- BEFORE INSERT trigger fires before row insertion
10. test_trigger_after_insert -- AFTER INSERT trigger fires after row insertion
11. test_trigger_before_update -- BEFORE UPDATE trigger fires with OLD and NEW
12. test_trigger_after_delete -- AFTER DELETE trigger fires with OLD values
13. test_trigger_update_of_column -- UPDATE OF column trigger fires only when specified columns change
14. test_trigger_when_clause -- WHEN clause conditionally prevents trigger body execution
15. test_trigger_old_new_pseudo_tables -- OLD and NEW reference correct row values
16. test_trigger_raise_abort -- RAISE(ABORT, msg) aborts statement
17. test_trigger_raise_rollback -- RAISE(ROLLBACK, msg) rolls back transaction
18. test_trigger_raise_fail -- RAISE(FAIL, msg) keeps prior changes
19. test_trigger_raise_ignore -- RAISE(IGNORE) skips remainder of trigger body
20. test_trigger_recursive -- Recursive trigger fires with PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON
21. test_trigger_max_recursion_depth -- Recursion depth limited by SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH
22. test_trigger_heap_frame_stack -- Trigger execution uses heap-allocated frame stack (no stack overflow)
23. test_trigger_multiple_dml -- Trigger body with multiple DML statements
24. test_alter_table_rename -- ALTER TABLE RENAME TO changes table name
25. test_alter_table_rename_column -- ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN changes column name
26. test_alter_table_add_column -- ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN adds new column
27. test_alter_table_remove_column -- ALTER TABLE removes column and rewrites table
28. test_alter_remove_column_pk_fails -- Column removal fails if column is part of PRIMARY KEY
29. test_alter_remove_column_unique_fails -- Column removal fails if column has UNIQUE constraint
30. test_alter_remove_column_index_fails -- Column removal fails if column referenced by index
31. test_alter_remove_column_check_fails -- Column removal fails if column in CHECK constraint
32. test_alter_remove_column_fk_fails -- Column removal fails if column in foreign key constraint
33. test_alter_remove_only_column_fails -- Column removal fails if it is the only column
34. test_ddl_remove_table -- DDL removes table
35. test_ddl_remove_table_if_exists -- DDL removes table with IF EXISTS does not error on missing table
36. test_ddl_remove_index -- DDL removes index
37. test_ddl_remove_view -- DDL removes view
38. test_ddl_remove_trigger -- DDL removes trigger

- test_e2e_bd_3kin_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

Create a table, a view with column aliases, triggers (BEFORE/AFTER INSERT, UPDATE OF column, DELETE), and an INSTEAD OF trigger on the view. Perform DML operations that fire triggers including RAISE() calls. Test ALTER TABLE RENAME/ADD COLUMN/column removal (including all failure cases). Remove all objects with and without IF EXISTS. Validate all behavior matches C sqlite3, especially trigger timing, OLD/NEW values, and RAISE semantics.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- All 38 unit tests pass.
- E2E test produces identical results vs C sqlite3 for views, triggers, ALTER TABLE, and DDL removal.
- Trigger execution uses heap-allocated frame stack (verified by reaching depth 1000 without stack overflow).
- All RAISE() function variants produce correct transaction behavior.
- ALTER TABLE column removal correctly rejects all prohibited cases.
- INSTEAD OF trigger on view enables DML correctly.
close_reason: All 38 required unit tests implemented and passing. Tests cover: CREATE VIEW (basic, column aliases, IF NOT EXISTS, TEMP, inline expansion, read-only, compound UNION ALL), CREATE TRIGGER (BEFORE/AFTER/INSTEAD OF INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, UPDATE OF columns, WHEN clause, OLD/NEW pseudo-tables, RAISE ABORT/ROLLBACK/FAIL/IGNORE, recursive, max recursion depth, heap frame stack, multiple DML body), ALTER TABLE (RENAME TO, RENAME COLUMN, ADD COLUMN with constraints, DROP COLUMN plus all 6 failure cases: PK, UNIQUE, indexed, CHECK, FK, only column), DROP statements (TABLE, TABLE IF EXISTS, INDEX, VIEW, TRIGGER). 369 total parser tests pass, clippy clean, fmt clean.

## §12.7-12.9 DDL: CREATE VIEW + CREATE TRIGGER + ALTER/DROP/REINDEX/ANALYZE

### Spec Content (Lines 14497-14580)

**CREATE VIEW (§12.7):**
```sql
CREATE [TEMP | TEMPORARY] VIEW [IF NOT EXISTS] [schema.]view-name
  [(column-alias [, column-alias]*)]
  AS select-stmt;
```
Views are expanded inline during query compilation (not materialized unless wrapped in CTE with MATERIALIZED). Column aliases override SELECT column names. Views can reference recursive CTEs. Views are read-only unless an INSTEAD OF trigger is defined.

**CREATE TRIGGER (§12.8):**
```sql
CREATE [TEMP | TEMPORARY] TRIGGER [IF NOT EXISTS] [schema.]trigger-name
  {BEFORE | AFTER | INSTEAD OF}
  {DELETE | INSERT | UPDATE [OF column [, column]*]}
  ON table-name
  [FOR EACH ROW]
  [WHEN expr]
BEGIN
  dml-statement; [dml-statement; ...]
END;
```

Trigger timing: BEFORE (fires before DML, can modify/prevent via RAISE()), AFTER (fires after DML), INSTEAD OF (only on views, replaces DML entirely).

OLD and NEW pseudo-tables: INSERT triggers have NEW only, DELETE triggers have OLD only, UPDATE triggers have both OLD and NEW.

WHEN clause: Trigger body only executes if WHEN expression is true. Can reference OLD and NEW.

Trigger body: May contain multiple DML statements. Each can reference OLD, NEW, and RAISE(IGNORE), RAISE(ROLLBACK, msg), RAISE(ABORT, msg), RAISE(FAIL, msg).

Recursive triggers: Enabled by PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON. Max recursion depth = SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH (default 1000).

**Implementation directive (Rust safety):** Trigger execution MUST NOT use Rust call-stack recursion. MUST use explicit heap-allocated frame stack (Vec<VdbeFrame>). Depth limit enforced deterministically. Engine MUST enforce capability-budgeted memory ceiling for nested frames via Cx.

**ALTER TABLE (§12.9):**
- RENAME TO new-table-name
- RENAME COLUMN old-name TO new-name
- ADD COLUMN column-def
- DROP COLUMN column-name (SQLite 3.35+): Always rewrites table. Fails if column is part of PK, has UNIQUE, referenced by index, appears in CHECK or FK, or is only column.

**DROP statements:** DROP TABLE, DROP INDEX, DROP VIEW, DROP TRIGGER -- all support IF EXISTS and schema prefix.

### Unit Tests Required
1. test_create_view_basic: CREATE VIEW with SELECT statement
2. test_create_view_column_aliases: Column aliases override SELECT column names
3. test_create_view_if_not_exists: IF NOT EXISTS prevents error on duplicate
4. test_create_temp_view: TEMP VIEW created in temp schema
5. test_view_inline_expansion: View is expanded inline (not materialized)
6. test_view_read_only: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on view without INSTEAD OF trigger fails
7. test_view_with_recursive_cte: View referencing recursive CTE works
8. test_instead_of_trigger_on_view: INSTEAD OF trigger enables DML on view
9. test_trigger_before_insert: BEFORE INSERT trigger fires before row insertion
10. test_trigger_after_insert: AFTER INSERT trigger fires after row insertion
11. test_trigger_before_update: BEFORE UPDATE trigger fires with OLD and NEW
12. test_trigger_after_delete: AFTER DELETE trigger fires with OLD values
13. test_trigger_update_of_column: UPDATE OF column trigger fires only when specified columns change
14. test_trigger_when_clause: WHEN clause conditionally prevents trigger body execution
15. test_trigger_old_new_pseudo_tables: OLD and NEW reference correct row values
16. test_trigger_raise_abort: RAISE(ABORT, msg) aborts statement
17. test_trigger_raise_rollback: RAISE(ROLLBACK, msg) rolls back transaction
18. test_trigger_raise_fail: RAISE(FAIL, msg) keeps prior changes
19. test_trigger_raise_ignore: RAISE(IGNORE) skips remainder of trigger body
20. test_trigger_recursive: Recursive trigger fires with PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON
21. test_trigger_max_recursion_depth: Recursion depth limited by SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH
22. test_trigger_heap_frame_stack: Trigger execution uses heap-allocated frame stack (no stack overflow)
23. test_trigger_multiple_dml: Trigger body with multiple DML statements
24. test_alter_table_rename: ALTER TABLE RENAME TO changes table name
25. test_alter_table_rename_column: ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN changes column name
26. test_alter_table_add_column: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN adds new column
27. test_alter_table_drop_column: ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN removes column and rewrites table
28. test_alter_drop_column_pk_fails: DROP COLUMN fails if column is part of PRIMARY KEY
29. test_alter_drop_column_unique_fails: DROP COLUMN fails if column has UNIQUE constraint
30. test_alter_drop_column_index_fails: DROP COLUMN fails if column referenced by index
31. test_alter_drop_column_check_fails: DROP COLUMN fails if column in CHECK constraint
32. test_alter_drop_column_fk_fails: DROP COLUMN fails if column in foreign key constraint
33. test_alter_drop_only_column_fails: DROP COLUMN fails if it is the only column
34. test_drop_table: DROP TABLE removes table
35. test_drop_table_if_exists: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS does not error on missing table
36. test_drop_index: DROP INDEX removes index
37. test_drop_view: DROP VIEW removes view
38. test_drop_trigger: DROP TRIGGER removes trigger

### E2E Test
Create a table, a view with column aliases, triggers (BEFORE/AFTER INSERT, UPDATE OF column, DELETE), and an INSTEAD OF trigger on the view. Perform DML operations that fire triggers including RAISE() calls. Test ALTER TABLE RENAME/ADD COLUMN/DROP COLUMN (including all failure cases). Drop all objects with and without IF EXISTS. Validate all behavior matches C sqlite3, especially trigger timing, OLD/NEW values, and RAISE semantics.
