title: io_uring unreachable in production: shared driver needs a runtime outliving the op, but the sync bridge gives each op its own (same root cause as bd-zavyn)
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-26 (SagePine). The io_uring fast path is never taken on the normal Connection API for Linux file-backed databases. Measured, not inferred.

EVIDENCE
Probe: debug fsqlite-cli, ELF sha256 8ea1d0a198e9ec474d86b9f0aee4269a20c70d687431afa699a2b3e342926e2c (342159600 bytes, built 2026-07-26 13:36:10 -0400).
Workload: 20,000 rows, file-backed WAL, page_size 4096 (4.1 MB db + 4.2 MB wal). Populated in one process; read from a COLD second process (wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) + two full scans) so page reads are genuine misses.
PRAGMA fsqlite.io_uring_stats:
  read_samples_total   = 0
  write_samples_total  = 0
  unix_fallbacks_total = 7520

MECHANISM
IoUringFile::{read,write,write_tracked} gate on cx.attached_native_cx() alone: uring.rs:1069, :1188, :1318.
Cx::attached_native_cx() (fsqlite-types/src/cx.rs:917) reads only the attached field; it never consults ambient asupersync::Cx::current().
set_native_cx is never called on a connection root/op Cx in the normal open/execute path — the only connection.rs sites are a background task (:73826) and a test (:97020). create_child propagates it (cx.rs:1199-1202) but there is nothing to propagate.
page_cache.rs:3421-3422 already resolves this correctly: asupersync::Cx::current().or_else(|| cx.attached_native_cx()).

REGRESSION, NOT LATENT
At control b612eb7b the read gate was 'if self.has_uring_data_path()' with fallback only on I/O error — no native-cx requirement. uring.rs existed and IoUringVfs was already selected for file opens at the control (11 references in connection.rs), so the VFS selection is not new. The always-failing gate is, and it landed inside the b612eb7b..HEAD window that bd-dqdoe measures.

COST OF THE FALLBACK
UnixFile::read (unix.rs:1971-1986) per page: Arc::clone -> spawn_blocking_io (thread-pool hop + reschedule) -> vec![0u8; page_size] in read_owned_at (unix.rs:88-101, alloc + memset) -> pread -> buf.copy_from_slice(&data) (a SECOND full-page memcpy) -> free. Writes are symmetric (buf.to_vec() at unix.rs:2018). UnixFile also does not override write_page_batch, so pager batch writes take the default sequential loop (traits.rs:1012-1023) = N thread hops + N allocs + N copies.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED
That this accounts for any specific share of the bd-dqdoe 1.895x. Two gates exist at HEAD — runtime.is_available() (:1065) and the native-cx gate (:1069) — and unix_fallbacks_total does not distinguish them. No timing claim has been made; the measuring host is loaded and every current artifact is non-citable.

FIX UNDER TEST
Applied NativeCx::current().or_else(|| cx.attached_native_cx()) at all three gates, mirroring page_cache.rs. Discriminating rebuild in flight: read_samples_total > 0 proves the native-cx gate was the blocker; still 0 proves runtime.is_available() is and the change is inert.

FOLLOW-UPS
1. PRAGMA fsqlite.io_uring_stats exposes only unix_fallbacks_total; the struct also carries read_unix_fallbacks_total and write_unix_fallbacks_total (observability lib.rs:144/146). Surface them — the split is needed to attribute read vs write.
2. comprehensive-bench resolves native+linux-asupersync-uring via fsqlite-harness feature unification, so it can assert a fallback-rate receipt per run instead of relying on a separate probe. Candidate Gate 0 provenance field.
3. Fix UnixFile read-into-caller-buffer and add a write_page_batch override regardless of the gate outcome — that cost is paid on every fallback and on every platform without uring.
close_reason: FIXED at dc56e76f (+a14b1629 batch forward). Root cause was deeper than the bead recorded: block_on's ambient request Cx carries NO spawn gateway in asupersync 0.3.9 (build_request_cx_from_inner installs neither with_spawn_gateway nor with_pending_spawn_counter), so ANY ambient-Cx substitution fails ASUP-E001 deterministically. Fix: RuntimeContext.io_native_cx OnceLock minted via RuntimeHandle::try_spawn_with_cx MINT-AND-EXIT (no parked task — RusticBasin's structured-lifecycle objection msg 4363 satisfied by construction; six-probe lifecycle receipt in session scratchpad asup-probe/), attached to the CONNECTION root Cx only when the context has a runtime handle; CLI opts in. FUNCTIONAL RECEIPT: read_samples_total 0->110, write_samples_total 0->4 on the bead's own cold-reader repro — io_uring engages in production for the FIRST time — with the refuted-fix failure repro clean end-to-end. Default open path bit-for-bit unchanged; ambient-capture invariant test green; SharedMvccKey stable. Timing claims deferred to a Gate 0 paired file-backed run (ledger 2026-07-27 LANDED entry).

comments.author: SagePine
comments.text:
REFUTED MY OWN FIX, SAME DAY — the gate is load-bearing. Root cause is upstream and identical to bd-zavyn.

WHAT I TRIED
Substituted NativeCx::current().or_else(|| cx.attached_native_cx()) at uring.rs:1069/:1188/:1318, mirroring page_cache.rs:3421.
Rebuilt CLI SHA-256 5f08e3223009e733246bc5220a63f4a671122ab169a7b62f3878cd22f4ca0711 (341195032 bytes, 2026-07-26 13:46:52 -0400).

RESULT: BREAKS THE ENGINE
A three-statement workload (CREATE TABLE + one INSERT + SELECT) fails:

  cannot start tracked shared io_uring write: cannot start shared io_uring driver:
  [ASUP-E001] runtime is no longer available — the runtime behind this handle was
  dropped or shut down; spawn before shutdown begins, or hold a strong runtime
  reference for the spawner's lifetime

then 'no such table: t' on every subsequent statement.
Counters confirm the path WAS being taken: unix_fallbacks_total 7520 -> 133, while read_samples_total / write_samples_total stayed at 0 — i.e. attempted on every op, succeeded on none.

WHY THE GATE EXISTS
The ambient Cx inside a short-lived block_on belongs to a runtime torn down when that call returns. The SHARED io_uring driver needs a spawner outliving the operation. page_cache.rs can use Cx::current() because it spawns a task on that same runtime and joins it before returning; the VFS data path cannot. attached_native_cx() is the contract by which a caller says 'here is a runtime whose lifetime I guarantee'. It is a deliberate design, not an oversight.

Reverted. The reasoning is now recorded inline at uring.rs:1069 (~20 lines) specifically so the next reader does not repeat this — it is an attractive-looking one-line 'fix' that silently corrupts the engine's write path.

THE ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE, AND THE SYNTHESIS THAT MATTERS
io_uring is unreachable in production because the sync bridge gives EVERY OPERATION ITS OWN RUNTIME, so no caller can offer the lifetime guarantee the driver requires. That is the same per-operation block_on architecture bd-zavyn measured at ~333 ns/entry and identified as the harness's flat per-row cost.

One root cause, two symptoms:
  1. bd-zavyn — measured benchmark inflation (instrument drift).
  2. bd-fo6xw — a production fast path that can never engage.

This reframes the bd-zavyn hoist: it is not only a benchmark-truth fix, it is a precondition for io_uring ever being usable. Whoever lands the hoist should re-measure read_samples_total afterwards; if a runtime then spans a transaction AND a durable native Cx is attached at connection open, the fast path becomes reachable for the first time.

WHAT STANDS UNCHANGED
The original measurement: 100% unix fallback, read/write samples 0, 7520 fallbacks on a 20k-row cold-read workload. Only my proposed remedy is withdrawn.

NOT CLAIMED: any share of the bd-dqdoe 1.895x. No timing measurement was taken; the host is loaded and non-citable.

title: FTS5: make on-disk shadow reads lazy (eliminate per-connection corpus re-tokenization)
description:
## Problem
frankensqlite's FTS5 vtab is an IN-MEMORY engine. On every connection/schema-reload, `rebuild_rootpage_zero_live_vtab_instances_from_reload` (crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs) reads the ENTIRE `<tbl>_content` shadow table and `Fts5Table::rebuild_documents()` RE-TOKENIZES every document to reconstruct the in-memory inverted index — O(corpus) CPU per connection. Because consumers like cass are short-lived CLIs (one query per process), EVERY command pays the full rebuild.

## Impact (measured 2026-06-01)
cass index `~/.local/share/coding-agent-search/agent_search.db`: 4.68M messages; on-disk shadow sizes content 3.4GB/824K pages, _data(postings) 1.4GB/333K pages, _docsize 78MB/4.68M rows, _idx 979KB/53.6K rows, _config WITHOUT ROWID. `cass status`/`search` peg one core for HOURS (a 65h runaway was killed). Stock sqlite3 answers the same `MATCH 'cargo'` (148K hits) in 0.1s. Data + index are HEALTHY (id=1 averages, id=10 structure, fts5_data_rowid-encoded segment leaves, valid _docsize varint blobs — all verified). NOT corruption. Index is also ~24 days stale because indexing is blocked by the same cost.

## Goal
Eliminate the per-connection O(corpus) work for BOTH reads and writes WITHOUT losing any FTS5 functionality. Reads: answer MATCH/bm25/snippet by reading ONLY the persisted on-disk segments the query needs (lazy) — target stock-sqlite parity (<1s on a fresh process). Writes: keep indexing incremental (new docs -> in-memory pending segment -> flush as a NEW on-disk segment), never re-tokenizing the existing corpus.

This is a subsystem rework of frankensqlite FTS5 from "fully in-memory, rebuilt per connection" to "lazy on-disk segments + small in-memory pending segment" — the architecture stock SQLite FTS5 already uses, and which frankensqlite ALREADY has the building blocks for (see design). Epic; implement via the child beads.

## History / status
A first attempt ("shadow-bind": bind Fts5ShadowRows and answer via Fts5ShadowQuery) was implemented then REVERTED after a fresh-eyes review found 3 fatal flaws — see Notes. Tree is currently SAFE (reverted to rebuild_documents, builds green). Validated decoders retained as dead code for reuse. Related upstream: frankensqlite#102 (WITHOUT-ROWID reload — sidestepped here via point-seek), #101 (read-witness cap = confirmed red herring).
design:
## Architecture: lazy on-disk segments + in-memory pending segment

REUSE existing machinery (do NOT rebuild from scratch): persisted multi-segment `_data` (structure id=10, averages id=1, segment leaves at fts5_data_rowid ids); posting-list readers `Fts5SegmentReader`/`Fts5ShadowQuery` (lib.rs ~1916/~5702); pending-segment write path `Fts5Table::flush_pending_segment` (lib.rs:6884), `should_flush` (:1310), `flush_to_segment` (:1397), `encode_shadow_rows` (:6894); merge policy `Fts5MergePlan`/`optimize_plan` (:1717) + automerge/usermerge/crisismerge/delete_merge (config :1671/:2196); `apply_control_command` (:2635); core `persist_materialized_live_vtab_rows` (connection.rs:30570).

### Read path (lazy)
1. Reader trait (fsqlite-ext-fts5): `trait Fts5OnDiskReader { read_data_block(id)->Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>; idx_candidate_page(segid,term)->Result<Option<u32>>; read_docsize(rowid)->Result<Option<Fts5DocsizeRow>>; read_content(rowid)->Result<Option<Vec<String>>>; structure()->Result<Fts5StructureRecord>; averages()->Result<Option<Fts5AveragesRecord>> }`. Structure/averages read once per query; all else point/range read on demand.
2. Core impl (connection.rs; has txn): BtCursor point-reads. `_data`/`_docsize`/`_content` rowid tables -> table cursor + rowid seek (new_header_btree_cursor :9460). `_idx` WITHOUT ROWID (PK (segid,term)) -> index cursor + BtCursor::index_seek (cursor.rs:4108) via new_header_btree_index_cursor (:9479). Resolve rootpages from reload schema by name. Point/range SEEK sidesteps frankensqlite#102.
3. Lazy segment reader/query: parametrize Fts5SegmentReader over a data source (in-memory Vec OR Fts5OnDiskReader); data_row(pgno)=reader.read_data_block(fts5_data_rowid(segid,false,0,pgno)); candidate_page=reader.idx_candidate_page(...). New `Fts5LazyQuery`: bm25 doc_length=reader.read_docsize(rowid) POINT read (NOT the O(N) Vec scan lib.rs:6107); result content=reader.read_content(rowid) for the LIMITed set ONLY; structure/averages once. KEEP in-memory Fts5SegmentRowSet for the pending segment. Add a small per-query DECODED-LEAF cache (id->Fts5SegmentLeaf) so multi-term queries hitting the same leaf decode once.
4. scan_live_fts5_rows (connection.rs:10890): &self; build txn reader; run MERGE query. count(*)=averages.total_rows (read_data_block(1)) + pending live - tombstones, NOT all_rows().

### Read+write coexistence (correctness core)
5. Merge query: results = on-disk-lazy-segments UNION in-memory-pending(self.index). Dedup by rowid (pending shadows on-disk = update); apply tombstones (deletes); bm25 scored over MERGED corpus stats (merged total_docs + avgdl with tombstones EXCLUDED).
6. Reload = LAZY MODE (NOT rebuild_documents): self.index empty; vtab holds a lazy flag; core supplies the reader at query time (least vtab state). No tokenization / no content read on open.
7. Writes incremental: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE -> in-memory pending (self.index). DELETE of an on-disk rowid -> tombstone. should_flush -> flush_pending_segment APPENDS pending as a NEW on-disk segment.

### Segment merge & special commands in lazy mode (DO NOT LOSE — they need on-disk segment reads)
- MERGE POLICY MUST KEEP RUNNING: automerge/usermerge/crisismerge/delete_merge thresholds (should_flush + optimize_plan/Fts5MergePlan). When a flush/append crosses a threshold, MERGE the chosen on-disk segments — which means READING those segments via the lazy reader, merging, and re-persisting the merged segment. Bounded/amortized I/O; REQUIRED so segment count stays bounded and query perf does not degrade over many flushes. A naive append-only lazy mode (no merge) is a perf regression and is NOT acceptable.
- SPECIAL COMMANDS via `INSERT INTO t(t) VALUES(...)` MUST still work through the lazy path: 'optimize'/'merge'(,N) (read+merge on-disk segments), 'integrity-check' (read+verify segments), 'rebuild' (re-derive segments from content — the rebuild_documents path, allowed here since it is explicit), 'delete-all' (frankensqlite#94), 'flush'. apply_control_command config channel preserved.

### Result projection & isolation
- Result content comes from the SOURCE of each result row: pending rows -> in-memory self.documents; on-disk rows -> reader.read_content(rowid). Projection must pick the right source per rowid.
- detail=none / detail=column MUST reject phrase/NEAR exactly as today (same errors = functionality parity), since positions are absent.
- The reader MUST read from the SAME txn snapshot as the running query (build it from the query's txn) so reads are MVCC-consistent with the query.

### Fallback (LAST RESORT, only if merge-query infeasible in scope)
Promote-on-first-write (rebuild_documents from _content, clear lazy mode). Correct but re-introduces slow indexing — AVOID; the merge model is the target.

### MUST NOT LOSE (functionality matrix — every item gets a differential test)
MATCH phrase; prefix term*; boolean AND/OR/NOT; NEAR; column filters col:term; bm25()+custom weights; ORDER BY rank; LIMIT/OFFSET; multiple MATCH constraints; snippet()/highlight()/aux (build_fts5_aux_context_for_source); detail=full|column|none (incl. correct phrase/NEAR rejection on column/none); prefix indexes; UNINDEXED columns; content/contentless modes; secure_delete (config version 4 AND 5); porter/unicode61/ascii/trigram; locale; SPECIAL COMMANDS optimize/merge/integrity-check/rebuild/delete-all/flush; SEGMENT MERGE POLICY automerge/usermerge/crisismerge/delete_merge.

### Key unknowns to resolve during impl (flag, do not assume)
- fts5_data_rowid 1->Averages/10->Structure vs Fts5DataRowid::decode; _idx (segid,term) key encoding; BtCursor table rowid-seek API name; txn reborrow/lifetime across point reads within one filter/column call.
- Does flush_to_segment/flush_pending_segment APPEND (preserve existing on-disk segments) or rewrite from in-memory? If rewrite, FIX to append before enabling lazy-mode writes.
- Whether frankensqlite currently dispatches the VALUES('optimize'/...) special-command channel in update() at all — if partially/ not implemented, the differential test vs the in-memory oracle defines the required behavior (parity, not regression).
acceptance_criteria:
## Definition of done (epic = all children done + these end-to-end gates)

### Correctness — differential parity is THE guarantee
- Differential harness runs an identical query set through (a) legacy rebuild_documents in-memory path [ORACLE], (b) new lazy+merge path, (c) stock sqlite3 (rusqlite, test-only); asserts IDENTICAL rowids, order, bm25 (fp 1e-9), snippet/highlight bytes. Covers EVERY item in the design MUST-NOT-LOSE matrix INCLUDING special commands + detail-mode phrase/NEAR rejection.
- PROPERTY/METAMORPHIC tests: random corpora (varied tokenizers, UNINDEXED cols, deletes, multi-segment) x random queries (phrase/prefix/boolean/NEAR/column/weights/LIMIT) -> lazy result == oracle result. Metamorphic relations (e.g. add-then-delete == no-op; OR(a,b) superset of a; LIMIT k prefix of LIMIT k+1).
- Write+read coexistence: insert/update/delete after reopen -> correct merged results. Existing test_reopen_rebinds_materialized_fts5_for_match_queries_and_new_inserts stays GREEN, plus update-shadows-on-disk, delete-tombstones-on-disk, re-insert-deleted.
- Flush/round-trip: build->flush->reopen->query == pre-flush; existing on-disk segments preserved (ZERO data loss); multi-flush correct.
- MERGE POLICY: after enough flushes to cross automerge/crisismerge, segments are merged (segment count stays bounded); merged result == pre-merge result; query latency does NOT grow with flush count (perf-over-time test). Special commands optimize/merge/integrity-check/rebuild/delete-all/flush behave identically to the oracle.

### Performance gates (assert programmatically)
- Fresh-process MATCH on a synthetic >=1M-doc corpus AND on cass's real 23GB DB < 1s (target 0.1s; hard ceiling 1s). _data/_content page reads O(hits+LIMIT) not O(corpus). No read-witness root_page=38 spin.
- Incremental insert of N docs re-tokenizes ONLY N (tokenizer counter ~= N). Open/connect: 0 content reads + 0 tokenizer calls.
- Sustained: after K flush+merge cycles, MATCH latency stays < ceiling (no unbounded segment growth).

### Tests & logging (user-mandated; see child .5)
- UNIT per component (reader primitives, lazy segment reader, lazy query per feature, merge dedup/tombstone, count, special commands, edge cases empty/single-seg/multi-seg/all-deleted/prefix/phrase/NEAR/column/huge-result).
- Committed E2E script(s) (tests/e2e/) with DETAILED STRUCTURED per-phase logs (open, plan, idx seeks, _data block ids, _docsize/_content point reads, merge stats on-disk-vs-pending+tombstones, segment-count, result, timings); JSON + human modes; logs make non-full-scan OBVIOUS.
- Optional crash/durability: interrupt a flush -> on reopen segments remain consistent (no partial-segment corruption).
- All existing fts5 + reload + vtab + materialized-fts5 tests pass; clippy pedantic/nursery clean; unsafe_code=forbid; CI green.

### Integration
- cass built against patched frankensqlite: cass status, search, AND index (incremental, no full re-tokenize) correct + fast on 23GB DB. Bridges to bd-audit-fsqlite-dependents-fts5-aqn56 (after a frankensqlite release).
notes:
## VALIDATED EMPIRICAL FINDINGS (hard-won vs the real 23GB cass DB — keep, do not re-derive)
- ROUTING: cass `fts_messages` rootpage=0 in sqlite_master => rebuild_rootpage_zero_live_vtab_instances_from_reload (the fixed path), NOT the materialized path (materialized_virtual_tables = entries with rootpage>0; connection.rs:56112/56315). Other consumers MAY use the materialized path -> child .4 must cover both.
- DATA HEALTH: cass `_data` is standard FTS5 — id=1 (averages,27B), id=10 (structure,87B), high ids = fts5_data_rowid-encoded segment leaves; `_idx` 53.6K rows; `_docsize` 4.68M rows (7-9B varint blobs). Stock sqlite3 does MATCH 'cargo' (148K hits) in 0.1s. NOT corruption.
- DOCSIZE DECODER VALIDATED vs real blobs: sz = 1 varint per column (ALL columns; indexed first, UNINDEXED trailing 0). id=1 '01010202130000'->[1,1,2,2,19,0,0] (cross-checks content: source_path 117 chars=19 tok, created_at/message_id=0). id=6 '82081301050D0000'->[264,19,1,5,13,0,0] (multi-byte varint 0x8208=264). column_count=7. decode_docsize_blob + content trailing-N extraction CONFIRMED CORRECT.
- FEASIBILITY: _idx WITHOUT-ROWID via BtCursor::index_seek (fsqlite-btree/src/cursor.rs:4108) + new_header_btree_index_cursor (connection.rs:9479, used L43014/43155); rowid tables via new_header_btree_cursor (:9460). Point/range seek sidesteps #102. Pending+merge machinery ALREADY present: flush_pending_segment(:6884), should_flush(:1310), flush_to_segment(:1397), optimize_plan(:1717), Fts5MergePlan, automerge/usermerge/crisismerge/delete_merge config.

## REVERTED FIRST ATTEMPT (shadow-bind) — 3 fatal flaws (DO NOT REPEAT)
1. WRITE CORRUPTION: store_document/delete_document set self.shadow_rows=None (lib.rs:6421/6454) — bind-then-insert drops the entire persisted index = data loss; broke test_reopen_rebinds_materialized_fts5_..._new_inserts.
2. O(N^2): Fts5ShadowQuery.doc_length (lib.rs:6107) linear-scans all 4.68M _docsize PER result; data_row linear-scans 333K _data; candidate_page without _idx -> full-segment scan. Fts5ShadowQuery is for tiny test data only.
3. CONFIG VERSION: synthesized version=4 ignores secure_delete v5.
=> shadow-bind is the WRONG vehicle. Correct design = lazy on-disk reader + Fts5LazyQuery (POINT-read doc_length) + on-disk UNION pending merge (see Design).

## CURRENT TREE STATE (safe)
Reverted to rebuild_documents (connection.rs:55755); builds GREEN (cargo build -p fsqlite-core --features ext-fts5, exit 0; 74min under 8-way contention). Validated decoders (from_storage_rows/decode_docsize_blob/bind_shadow_rows/read_fts5_shadow_rows_for_reload/all_rows+row_count fallbacks) kept as dead code for reuse. BUILD CONTENTION 12-74min/cycle => use rch for the impl pass; [patch] in cass Cargo.toml is LOCAL-ONLY (fresh-clone CI guard).

## CROSS-REF
memory project_cass_fts5_rebuild_bug.md; sibling upstream issues #102 (WITHOUT-ROWID reload), #101 (read-witness = red herring), #103 (index-only scan). 9-bead epic: .1 reader -> .2 lazy engine -> .3 merge+writes -> .4 core integration -> .5 tests/e2e -> .6 cass verify; then release -> dependents audit.

title: FTS5 lazy: Fts5OnDiskReader trait + core BtCursor point-read primitives
description:
## Scope (foundation)
Define `trait Fts5OnDiskReader` in fsqlite-ext-fts5 and implement it in fsqlite-core over a `&mut dyn TransactionHandle` using BtCursor:
- read_data_block(id:i64) -> table rowid seek on `<tbl>_data` (new_header_btree_cursor connection.rs:9460, SeekRowid).
- idx_candidate_page(segid:u32, term:&[u8]) -> index_seek on `<tbl>_idx` (WITHOUT ROWID, PK (segid,term)) via new_header_btree_index_cursor (:9479) + BtCursor::index_seek (cursor.rs:4108); return leaf pgno.
- read_docsize(rowid) / read_content(rowid) -> rowid seek on `_docsize`/`_content` (decode via validated decode_docsize_blob / trailing-column content extraction already written as dead code).
- structure()/averages() -> read_data_block(10)/(1) decoded via Fts5DataMetadata.
Resolve shadow rootpages from reload schema by name. Reader constructed per filter/column call (borrows current txn) => no stored-borrow/MVCC lifetime issue.

## Acceptance & tests (UNIT)
- Committed deterministic fixture FTS5 DB (small, multi-segment if achievable). Unit tests: read_data_block exact bytes for ids incl 1/10; idx_candidate_page correct leaf for known terms (and lowest leaf for a term before first); read_docsize/read_content correct decoded rows; missing id/rowid -> Ok(None).
- Differential: read_content(rowid) == stock sqlite3 (rusqlite, test-only) SELECT c0.. FROM _content WHERE id=rowid; read_docsize totals == stock token counts.
- Instrumentation: assert each primitive is a point read (bounded pages, not scan). Confirm fts5_data_rowid 1->Averages/10->Structure and _idx (segid,term) key encoding.

DONE 2026-06-02. Implementation + unit test GREEN via rch (cargo test ... test_fts5_live_shadow_reader_reads_persisted_index -> 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 errors).
- fts5-ext: pub trait Fts5OnDiskReader + pub decode_docsize_blob.
- fsqlite-core: Fts5LiveShadowReader<'a>{cx:&'a Cx, txn, page_size, reserved_per_page, data/idx/docsize/content_root, collation_registry} + new(schema,table_name) + with_roots(explicit roots) + Fts5OnDiskReader impl. #[allow(dead_code)] until .4.
- Test (connection.rs mod tests, #[cfg(all(unix, feature=ext-fts5))]): builds a STANDARD FTS5 DB via rusqlite (CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE docs USING fts5(body); 2 rows; optimize-flush) -> doubles as the .5 FORMAT-INTEROP fixture (frankensqlite reads a stock-SQLite FTS5 index). Asserts read_data_block(1)=averages/(10)=structure/absent=None; read_content(1)=['alpha rust beta'],(2)=['gamma rust delta'],absent=None; read_docsize(1).total_tokens()==3. Driven via Connection::with_integrity_txn + parse_database_header_checked + sqlite_master rootpage query.

NOTE: cargo test ran the whole fsqlite-core test suite too (all green alongside).

title: FTS5 lazy: lazy Fts5SegmentReader + Fts5LazyQuery (full read-feature parity)
description:
## Scope (lazy read engine)
Parametrize Fts5SegmentReader over a data source (in-memory Vec<Fts5DataRow> OR Fts5OnDiskReader) so data_row(pgno)=reader.read_data_block(fts5_data_rowid(segid,false,0,pgno)) and candidate_page=reader.idx_candidate_page(segid,term). New `Fts5LazyQuery` mirroring Fts5ShadowQuery BUT: bm25 doc_length=reader.read_docsize(rowid) POINT read (NOT the O(N) Vec scan at lib.rs:6107 — root cause of the reverted shadow-bind O(N^2)); result content=reader.read_content(rowid) for the LIMITed result set ONLY; structure/averages read once. KEEP in-memory Fts5SegmentRowSet for the pending segment (do not delete it).

## Acceptance & tests (DIFFERENTIAL PARITY — the guarantee)
- Differential vs legacy in-memory (rebuild_documents) ORACLE on a fixture corpus across the FULL feature matrix: MATCH phrase, prefix term*, boolean AND/OR/NOT, NEAR, column filters col:term, bm25()+custom weights, ORDER BY rank, LIMIT/OFFSET, multiple MATCH constraints, snippet()/highlight(), detail=full|column|none, prefix indexes, UNINDEXED cols, porter/unicode61/ascii/trigram, locale. Assert identical rowids + order + bm25 (fp 1e-9) + snippet/highlight bytes.
- Per-feature unit tests + edge cases: empty, single-seg, multi-seg, all-deleted, term absent, prefix many hits, large result set.
- Perf: _docsize/_content reads O(hits+LIMIT) (counter); _data leaf reads bounded by touched doclists (no full-segment scan when _idx present).

DONE 2026-06-05 — all of .2 landed + GREEN via rch (clippy+fmt clean, fts5 369 tests + core 2 lazy tests pass).

(a) lazy exact scan — lazy_exact_doclist_entries / lazy_segment_exact_postings (done earlier; dual main/raw lookup keys via segment_lookup_keys handle stock '0'+token AND frank raw-token segments).
(b) SHARED query engine — new pub trait Fts5DoclistProvider (lib.rs ~5963): primitives {columns,tokenizer,detail,exact_entries,prefix_entries,doc_length,total_docs,avg_doc_length} + the ENTIRE ranked-search engine as DEFAULT methods (search_with_weights, term/prefix rowids+spans, phrase/phrase_prefix, near, evaluate_expr, doc_frequency, term_column_frequencies, bm25_score). (c) lazy prefix scan (lazy_prefix_doclist_entries/lazy_segment_prefix_postings, idx_candidate_page-seeked, dual-key) + Fts5LazyQuery<'a> (lib.rs ~6608): impls Fts5DoclistProvider over Fts5OnDiskReader with RefCell<&mut reader> + per-query caches (exact/prefix/docsize) so a MATCH's repeated postings/docsize consultations collapse to ONE on-disk read each. total_docs/avg from averages(id=1); doc_length via read_docsize POINT read; content_for_rowid via read_content for the projected set only. structure(id=10)/averages read once in ::new.

PASSES.

title: FTS5 lazy: merge query (on-disk + pending) + lazy-mode reload + incremental writes
description:
## Scope (read+write coexistence — correctness core)
- Merge query: results = on-disk-lazy-segments UNION in-memory-pending(self.index). Dedup by rowid (pending shadows on-disk = update); apply tombstones; bm25 over MERGED corpus stats (tombstones EXCLUDED from total_docs/avgdl). Result content from the row's source (pending->self.documents, on-disk->read_content).
- Reload = LAZY MODE: no rebuild_documents; self.index empty; vtab holds a lazy flag; core supplies the reader at query time.
- Writes incremental: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE -> in-memory pending. DELETE of an on-disk rowid -> tombstone. should_flush -> flush_pending_segment APPENDS pending as a NEW on-disk segment.
- VERIFY: does flush_to_segment/flush_pending_segment (lib.rs:6884/1397) APPEND (preserve existing on-disk segments) or rewrite from in-memory? If rewrite, FIX to append BEFORE enabling lazy writes (else flush drops the lazily-held corpus = data loss).

## Scope (MERGE POLICY + special commands — DO NOT LOSE)
- Preserve automerge/usermerge/crisismerge/delete_merge (should_flush + optimize_plan/Fts5MergePlan, lib.rs:1690-1717). When a flush/append crosses a threshold, MERGE the selected on-disk segments: READ them via the lazy reader, merge, re-persist the merged segment, update the structure record. REQUIRED so segment count stays bounded and query perf does not degrade over many flushes (append-only-no-merge is an unacceptable perf regression).
- Special commands via INSERT INTO t(t) VALUES(...): 'optimize'/'merge'(,N) (read+merge on-disk), 'integrity-check' (read+verify), 'rebuild' (re-derive from content — rebuild_documents allowed here, explicit), 'delete-all' (#94), 'flush'. Route through the lazy reader for on-disk segment access.

## Acceptance & tests
- Existing test_reopen_rebinds_materialized_fts5_for_match_queries_and_new_inserts GREEN.
- update-shadows-on-disk; delete-tombstones-on-disk (others intact); re-insert-deleted; multi-flush accumulates then merges.
- Flush round-trip: build->flush->reopen->query == pre-flush; existing segments preserved (ZERO loss).
- MERGE: after crossing automerge/crisismerge, segment count bounded; merged result == pre-merge; latency stable across K flush+merge cycles.
- Special commands optimize/merge/integrity-check/rebuild/delete-all behave == in-memory oracle.
- Open: 0 content reads + 0 tokenizer calls; incremental insert of N: tokenizer ~= N.
acceptance_criteria: Lazy FTS5 merge query returns on-disk-lazy UNION pending with rowid dedup (pending shadows on-disk); lazy-mode reload preserves pending state; incremental writes coexist with reads; differential test vs eager mode on mixed workloads is identical.
notes:
PROGRESS 2026-06-05 — MULTI-SEGMENT RECENCY/TOMBSTONE MERGE DONE + GREEN (the bead's flagged correctness core). clippy+fmt clean; fts5 369 tests + 3 core lazy tests pass.

EMPIRICAL FINDING (probe over a stock-built multi-seg index: 5 separate-statement inserts + 1 DELETE + 1 UPDATE, no optimize): stock recorded 7 segments ALL at level 0, ZERO tombstone pages. Deletes/updates are recorded as DELETE-MARKER doclist entries (Fts5Poslist.delete=true) in NEWER segments; the original LIVE postings still physically exist in older segments. The old naive lazy_exact (collect all, filter !delete) WRONGLY kept the stale live entry (e.g. 'rust' returned [1,2,3,4] vs stock [1,4]).

FTS5 RECENCY ORDER (confirmed from legacy_sqlite_code fts5_index.c fts5MultiIterNew + the structure format comment 'for each segment from oldest to newest'): newest-first = pending-hash, then levels ASCENDING (level 0 newest), segments within a level in REVERSE (stored oldest->newest). Tie-break: first (newest) occurrence of a (term,rowid) wins.

IMPL (fts5 lib.rs): collect_doclist_recency() walks segments newest-first keyed by (stored_term, rowid) — NOT rowid alone (so an UPDATE's delete-marker for term t does not shadow a live t2 of the same row; required for prefix correctness). Per (term,rowid) newest occurrence: skip if delete-marker OR rowid_tombstoned_in_segment() (reads the single tombstone hash page rowid%count via Fts5DataRowid::Tombstone + Fts5TombstonePage::contains_rowid — handles secure-delete/tombstone indexes too). lazy_exact_doclist_entries + lazy_prefix_doclist_entries both route through it; prefix keeps per-term groups (lazy_segment_prefix_term_groups). dual main/raw keys preserved.

TEST: core test_fts5_lazy_query_matches_stock_after_multisegment_delete_update — multi-seg delete+update, asserts Fts5LazyQuery == stock for rust/alpha/beta/gamma/replaced/epsilon/zeta/rust*/OR. GREEN.

REMAINING .3 (not yet done — overlaps .4): pending-segment (in-memory self.index) UNION with on-disk lazy (pending newest, shadows on-disk; tombstone for on-disk rowid DELETE); lazy-mode reload (no rebuild_documents; vtab lazy flag); incremental writes; VERIFY flush_pending_segment APPENDS (no rewrite) before enabling lazy writes; merge policy (automerge/crisismerge) reading+remerging on-disk segs; special commands (optimize/merge/integrity-check/rebuild/delete-all/flush) through the lazy reader. These need the core reload wiring (.4) so likely co-developed.

title: FTS5 lazy: core integration — scan_live_fts5_rows + count(*) + reload wiring
description:
## Scope (wire it into the engine)
- scan_live_fts5_rows (connection.rs:10890) -> &self; construct the txn-backed Fts5OnDiskReader; run the MERGE query for idx_num=1 (MATCH) and idx_num=0 (full scan = all on-disk rowids + pending).
- count(*) (try_execute_plain_live_vtab_count_star, ~L10676): use averages.total_rows (read_data_block(1)) + pending live count - tombstones, NOT all_rows().len().
- Reload wiring: route the rootpage-zero FTS5 path to lazy mode (remove/guard the rebuild_documents call at connection.rs:55755). So `MATCH ... ORDER BY rank` (cass's main query) still re-tokenizes _content once per connection. title: FTS5 lazy: comprehensive test suite + e2e scripts + detailed logging + perf gates
description:
## Scope (user-mandated: comprehensive tests + e2e + great detailed logging)
1. Differential harness: oracle = legacy in-memory (rebuild_documents) AND stock sqlite3 (rusqlite, test-only). One driver runs a query set through all three; asserts equality (rowids/order/bm25 1e-9/snippet bytes). Reused by C1-C4.
2. PROPERTY/METAMORPHIC suite (proptest/fuzz): random corpora (tokenizers, UNINDEXED, deletes, multi-segment, content/contentless) x random queries (phrase/prefix/boolean/NEAR/column/weights/LIMIT/OFFSET) -> lazy == oracle. Metamorphic relations: add-then-delete==no-op; OR(a,b) superset of a/b; LIMIT k == prefix of unbounded; merge/optimize is result-preserving; flush is result-preserving.
3. Synthetic large-corpus generator: deterministic >=1M-doc multi-segment FTS5 DB (UNINDEXED cols, deletes) built once + cached; used for perf + scale + sustained-merge tests.
4. Special-command tests: optimize/merge/integrity-check/rebuild/delete-all/flush == oracle, through the lazy path.
5. Sustained-perf test: K flush+merge cycles; assert segment count bounded and MATCH latency stable (no degradation).
6. Committed E2E script(s) under tests/e2e/ (or scripts/): build/locate a large FTS5 DB; run a cass-shaped workload (count, MATCH search, rank+snippet, incremental insert, optimize); emit DETAILED STRUCTURED LOGS per phase — open, plan, _idx seeks, each _data block id read, _docsize/_content point reads, merge stats (on-disk hits vs pending hits, tombstones), segment count before/after, per-phase timings. JSON mode + human (--verbose) mode. Logs MUST make non-full-scan + bounded reads OBVIOUS.
7. Instrumentation: counters for tokenizer calls, _data/_content/_docsize page reads, decoded-leaf cache hits; exposed to tests (feature-gated or tracing layer).
8. Perf gates in CI / make|just target: fresh-process MATCH (>=1M corpus + cass 23GB) < 1s; page reads O(hits+LIMIT); open-time tokenizer == 0; incremental insert tokenizer ~= N; sustained latency stable.
9. Optional crash/durability: interrupt a flush -> reopen segments consistent.

## Acceptance
- Harness + property suite + generator + e2e scripts committed and DOCUMENTED (how to run). Every MUST-NOT-LOSE feature + special command covered. Perf + sustained gates green in CI. Logs reviewed to confirm laziness on a real-ish corpus. No flaky tests.
acceptance_criteria: Comprehensive lazy-FTS5 suite: differential harness against legacy in-memory AND stock sqlite3 oracles, e2e scripts, detailed structured logging, and perf gates showing lazy mode does not regress query latency beyond the agreed budget.
notes:
ADDED TEST CLASS — on-disk FORMAT INTEROP (do not fork the format):
- Round-trip: a DB built + incrementally-written + flushed + merged by the PATCHED frankensqlite is read correctly by STOCK sqlite3 FTS5 (rusqlite, test-only) — MATCH result sets + bm25 ordering match. And the reverse (stock-written FTS5 read by lazy frankensqlite) already implied by the cass DB test.
- Assert the flush/merge writes STANDARD _data segment leaves / structure(id=10) / averages(id=1) / _idx / _docsize encodings (decode via stock sqlite + via frankensqlite both succeed). Guards against silently writing a frankensqlite-only format that breaks interop / older readers.
- Migration check: opening the REAL cass 23GB DB (written by current frankensqlite) with the new lazy reader returns correct results with zero migration step.

title: FTS5 writer must emit pgsz-bounded multi-leaf segments (64KiB-per-flush ceiling)
description: Follow-up to the cass#362 overlong-term skip cap: Fts5PendingHash::flush_to_segment + to_segment_leaf pack every pending term into ONE Fts5SegmentLeaf at pgno=1 (Fts5StructureSegment::new(segid,1,1)), so any flush whose encoded body exceeds 65535 bytes fails Fts5SegmentLeaf::encode ('segment leaf term offset exceeds u16') regardless of individual term sizes. FTS5_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE/FTS5_MAX_PAGE_SIZE are parsed from _config but never consulted by the writer; Fts5PendingHash::should_flush has no production callers; flush emits no idx accelerator rows. The read side already walks pgno_first..=pgno_last and degrades without _idx, so this is writer-only: thread metadata.page_size into flush_to_segment/to_segment_leaf, emit Vec<Fts5SegmentLeaf> at pgno 1..=n (port the C predicate from fts5_index.c:4471 fts5WriteAppendTerm), make Fts5IncrementalInsertFlush.leaf_data_row a Vec, and update the connection.rs incremental-insert upsert (~:35073-35087). Optionally emit Fts5IdxRows as accelerators. Related: bd-c9pi2 (bound segment growth/automerge), bd-2nzo8.3 (storage backend epic). Once landed, the encode_data_rows hard-error path from the cass#362 fix should become unreachable for ordinary corpora; cass#345's atomic-rebuild OOM at FTS5_REGISTER_SQL is a separate allocation-bounding issue.
notes: cass GH #368 (2026-07-30) is the segment-COUNT overflow manifesting in production: 'fts5: corrupt %_data record: structure segment count exceeds FTS5 maximum' on a 484k-message archive — the bd-sf8dx one-segment-per-INSERT append path with no automerge (bd-c9pi2) eventually exceeds the structure's segment maximum, and the resulting artifact blocks even repair opens (validation at open; cass bead gh368-repair-open-deferred-validatio-s0q7l). Bounding segment growth (automerge/leveled merge) is now user-visible breakage, not just perf.
close_reason: Multi-leaf u16-bounded segment writer proven on main (315/315 unit incl. u16-boundary keeper + 4 FTS5 keeper files green); GH #328 bricking failure eliminated; pgsz-config parity refinement split to bd-3e08r

comments.author: ubuntu

Contentless indexes cannot be rebuilt from stored content, so this is unrecoverable capability loss, not a transient defect. Acceptable v0.2.0 resolutions, in preference order: (1) land the bounded multi-leaf writer with a regression keeper at the u16 boundary; (2) fail-closed guard that refuses the overflow write with a clear error BEFORE corrupting the segment, plus a prominent README limitation telling users to avoid large contentless FTS5 in v0.2.0. Shipping silently is not an option. The unrepairable-existing-index aspect (repair/salvage of already-corrupt %_data) can stay post-0.2.0 as its own bead.

title: BUG: frank too permissive — accepts aggregate-in-WHERE, nested aggregates, and window fns in HAVING/GROUP BY that SQLite rejects as misuse
close_reason: reject aggregate/window misuse at Select dispatch (commit 4af99c3a)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## BUG: frank does not reject aggregate/window misuse that SQLite rejects (too permissive)

Oracle parity vs rusqlite. t(id PK, x, g) with a few rows. SQLite rejects all of
these at prepare time; frank runs them and returns (arguably-meaningless) output:

```sql
-- aggregate in WHERE -> SQLite "misuse of aggregate"
SELECT * FROM t WHERE sum(x) > 5;     -- frank: runs   csql: ERROR
SELECT * FROM t WHERE count(*) > 1;   -- frank: runs   csql: ERROR
SELECT * FROM t WHERE max(x) = x;     -- frank: runs   csql: ERROR

-- nested aggregate -> SQLite "misuse of aggregate function count()/avg()"
SELECT sum(count(*)) FROM t;            -- frank: [NULL]        csql: ERROR
SELECT max(avg(x)) FROM t GROUP BY g;   -- frank: [NULL,NULL]   csql: ERROR

-- window function outside SELECT/ORDER BY -> SQLite "misuse of window function"
SELECT g FROM t GROUP BY g HAVING row_number() OVER () > 0;  -- frank: []   csql: ERROR
SELECT x FROM t GROUP BY row_number() OVER ();               -- frank: rows csql: ERROR
```

What frank DOES correctly reject: a window function in WHERE
(`SELECT x FROM t WHERE row_number() OVER () = 1` errors on both). And all the
legitimate forms (aggregate in SELECT/HAVING, window in SELECT/ORDER BY) work.

So frank's semantic validation of aggregate/window *placement* is incomplete:
it lacks the checks that (a) an aggregate may not appear in WHERE, (b) aggregates
may not be nested, and (c) a window function may appear only in the SELECT list
or ORDER BY (not WHERE/HAVING/GROUP BY). The string "misuse of aggregate/window"
does not appear in the codebase — these checks are simply absent.

### Fix area
Add prepare-time validation in the analyzer that walks each clause: reject
aggregates found in WHERE / inside another aggregate, and reject window
functions found anywhere but the SELECT list and ORDER BY. (Likely in
crates/fsqlite-parser/src/semantic.rs or the codegen aggregate/window-context
analysis in crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs.)

### Test
crates/fsqlite-e2e/tests/agg_window_misuse_oracle_e2e.rs — the valid controls and
the window-in-WHERE rejection pass; aggregate-in-WHERE, nested-aggregate, and
window-in-HAVING/GROUP-BY are #[ignore]'d on this bead.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Extension (from bd-bwahg): aggregate in a recursive-CTE term also not rejected

Another instance of frank's missing aggregate-placement validation:
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE c(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT count(*) FROM c) SELECT * FROM c;
  -- frank: runs it (emits a long run of '1' rows until an internal recursion cap)
  -- csql:  ERROR("recursive aggregate queries not supported")
```
SQLite rejects an aggregate in the recursive term of a recursive CTE at prepare
time; frank does not, and instead executes the recursion. Same root as this
bead (frank lacks the semantic checks that constrain where aggregates may
appear); the fix is the same prepare-time validation pass, with this specific
rule ("no aggregate in a recursive term") added.

frank's recursive-CTE engine itself is correct: cycle termination via UNION,
multiple anchor rows, running computed values (factorial), and LIMIT cutting an
infinite recursion all pass oracle parity
(crates/fsqlite-e2e/tests/recursive_cte_edge_oracle_e2e.rs).

Test: recursive_cte_edge_oracle_e2e.rs::recursive_aggregate_in_recursive_term_errors
(#[ignore]'d on this bead).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
# Extension: plain aggregate function in GROUP BY clause not rejected

This bead already documents that `aggregate-in-WHERE`, nested aggregate,
window-in-{HAVING,GROUP BY}, and recursive aggregate are not rejected.
Sibling case found 2026-05-21: a plain aggregate function inside `GROUP BY`
itself is also not rejected.

```sql
CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,10),(1,20),(2,30);

SELECT a FROM t GROUP BY count(*);
-- SQLite: ERROR aggregate functions are not allowed in the GROUP BY clause
-- frank:  OK -> [[1]]   (silently collapses to one group)

SELECT a FROM t GROUP BY sum(a);              -- same error / same wrong behavior
SELECT a FROM t GROUP BY a + count(*);        -- aggregate buried in an expression, same
```
The ordinary form `SELECT a, count(*), sum(b) FROM t GROUP BY a` is correct on both.

## Fix scope
Same site as the other bd-fuxgg cases: when validating GROUP BY terms, walk each
expression and reject any aggregate-function call (matching SQLite's
"aggregate functions are not allowed in the GROUP BY clause"). The
window-in-GROUP-BY rejection is the natural cousin to this.

## Test pin
`crates/fsqlite-e2e/tests/groupby_aggregate_rejection_oracle_e2e.rs`:
- PASS: `ordinary_group_by_ok`.
- IGNORED on bd-fuxgg: `group_by_aggregate_rejected`.

title: Epic: The Bloodstream (Incremental View Maintenance via Differential Dataflow)
description:
**Goal:** Dissolve the query-polling boundary between the DB and the application by pushing algebraic deltas of materialized views directly to clients in O(Δ) time, guaranteeing exactly-once semantics.
**Background & Justification:** Currently, clients repeatedly poll the database for updated views, wasting massive CPU/IO. Shipping a differential delta (+1 or -1 row) is virtually free. By integrating Timely Dataflow concepts into `fsqlite-vdbe`, we compute view differentials at commit time.
**Constraints:** 
- Must preserve SSI isolation and exact `CommitSeq` serializability.
- Must not block the MVCC write coordinator.
- View updates must complete within the `group_commit` budget (<5ms).
**Primary failure risk + countermeasure:**
- Risk: Delta computation slows down write commit, or subscribers lose sync.
- Countermeasure: Budgeted mode. If differential graph execution exceeds 1ms, gracefully degrade to sending an invalidation signal (forcing a client re-poll). Subscribers must be able to gracefully recover via a new snapshot.
**Adoption wedge & Ergonomics:** 
- Opt-in via `PRAGMA fsqlite_differential_views = ON`. 
- New PRAGMA `fsqlite_differential_status` to see active subscriptions, emission rates, and fallback counts.
- **Snapshot + Stream Sync:** Clients subscribing to a view receive an atomic initial payload at `CommitSeq(N)`, and the stream guarantees deltas begin exactly at `N+1`.
notes: 2026-03-15 Codex: claiming the Bloodstream epic after bv robot triage selected it as a top actionable lane. BronzeField already owns the connection-level Differential Registry slice in crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs, so this session will avoid that surface and instead start bd-o0dut with weighted-row/dataflow groundwork on the bloodstream harness side.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Enhanced Testing & Logging Spec (2026-03-08 quality audit)

### Cross-cutting Structured Tracing Fields (all Bloodstream subtasks must emit)
- tracing::info!(target: "fsqlite::differential", event = "subscription_start", view_name = %view, subscriber_id = %id, snapshot_seq = %seq)
- tracing::info!(target: "fsqlite::differential", event = "delta_emit", txn_id = %txn, view_name = %view, inserts = %ins, deletes = %del, latency_us = %us)
- tracing::warn!(target: "fsqlite::differential", event = "budget_exceeded", view_name = %view, computation_ms = %ms, budget_ms = %budget, fallback = "invalidation")
- tracing::debug!(target: "fsqlite::differential", event = "snapshot_bootstrap", subscriber_id = %id, rows_sent = %count, seq = %seq)
- tracing::debug!(target: "fsqlite::differential::registry", event = "subscribe", subscriber_id = %id, active_subs = %total)
- tracing::debug!(target: "fsqlite::differential::registry", event = "unsubscribe", subscriber_id = %id, active_subs = %total)
- tracing::info!(target: "fsqlite::differential::automata", event = "schema_change", view_name = %view, action = "halt_and_rebootstrap")

### Additional Acceptance Criteria (epic-level)
1. Proptest harness proves delta-fold isomorphism with batch query for all SQL operators (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, aggregate)
2. Subscriber never misses a delta or receives a duplicate (exactly-once guarantee under test)
3. Snapshot-to-stream handoff is gap-free: client gets snapshot at CommitSeq(N), first delta at N+1 (no off-by-one)
4. Differential computation that exceeds 1ms budget gracefully falls back to invalidation (budget_exceeded event logged)
5. Schema changes (ALTER TABLE) halt automata and signal re-bootstrap (not silent corruption)
6. Registry supports 10K+ concurrent subscribers without lock contention (EBR/RCU proven)
7. PRAGMA fsqlite_differential_views = ON/OFF works at connection level
8. PRAGMA fsqlite_differential_status shows active subscriptions, emission rates, and fallback counts
9. EXPLAIN DIFFERENTIAL outputs the dataflow graph for debugging
10. Write commit latency not increased by > 5% with differential views active (benchmark evidence)

title: F1: Flat page array for single-connection :memory: mode — Vec<Option<PageData>> indexed by pgno
close_reason: Committed in 9abedc20: flat page array in page_cache.rs (+935 lines)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## What
Replace DashMap<PageNumber, CachedPage> with Vec<Option<PageData>> for :memory: single-connection mode. Page lookup becomes pages[pgno.0 as usize] — zero hashing, zero locking, zero atomic operations.

## Where
- crates/fsqlite-pager/src/pager.rs: PagerInner struct, add `fast_pages: Vec<Option<PageData>>`
- Detect single-connection + :memory: at open time, set `use_fast_pages: bool`
- In read_page(): if use_fast_pages { return fast_pages[pgno] } else { existing DashMap path }

## Why This Matters
Profiling shows 0.15-0.25 µs per page read from lock acquisition + hash lookup. With 3 page reads per INSERT (root + interior + leaf), that's 0.45-0.75 µs — nearly the ENTIRE gap to C SQLite.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. page_read_latency < 10 ns for cached pages in single-connection mode
2. No regression in multi-connection mode (falls back to DashMap)
3. conformance_oracle_s55 passes
4. Memory: Vec pre-allocated to max(1024, database_page_count) entries

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Risk & Fallback
**Risk**: Flat Vec may use too much memory for databases with sparse page numbers (e.g., page 1 and page 100000 with nothing between).
**Mitigation**: Only use flat array for pages 0..max_allocated_page. Sparse databases (max_pgno > 4 * page_count) fall back to HashMap.
**Fallback trigger**: If RSS exceeds 2x expected (page_count × page_size), log warning and switch to HashMap.
**Rollback**: Feature flag `use_flat_page_cache` defaulting to true; set to false to revert.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## CORRECTION (Review Pass 4): Actual Page Cache Implementation
The page cache is NOT a DashMap. It is:
```rust
pub struct ShardedPageCache {
    shards: Box<[Mutex<PageCacheShard>; 128]>,  // 128 sharded mutexes!
    pool: PageBufPool,
    page_size: PageSize,
}
```
Located at: crates/fsqlite-pager/src/page_cache.rs:532

Each page access:
1. Compute shard_index = pgno * GOLDEN_RATIO >> 25 (multiplicative hash)
2. Lock the shard's Mutex
3. Search within shard (likely linear or small map)
4. Return page data
5. Unlock mutex

### Revised F1 Strategy
Replace the sharded mutex cache with a flat `Vec<AtomicPtr<PageData>>` for single-connection :memory: mode. The key change is:
- Old: `shards[hash(pgno)].lock() → search shard → return page`
- New: `pages[pgno.get() as usize].load(Ordering::Acquire)` (1 atomic load, no lock)

### Where
- crates/fsqlite-pager/src/page_cache.rs (ShardedPageCache) — add flat array mode
- crates/fsqlite-pager/src/pager.rs (SimplePager) — detect single-connection + :memory: and use flat mode

### The 128-shard Mutex design is already good for concurrent mode
F2 (atomic page slots) may not be needed if the existing 128-shard design has acceptable contention at 8-32 threads. Profile first: if shard contention is < 5% of time, skip F2 and focus on F1.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## CRITICAL CORRECTION (Review Pass 5): MemDB Is Used as Read Fallback

Connection.db (MemDatabase) is described as "retained as an execution image and limited compatibility fallback" (connection.rs:4564). Some query shapes still READ from MemDB rather than from storage cursors.

### Revised J1 Strategy
Instead of making MemDB sync completely lazy, use a TWO-TIER approach:
1. **For storage-cursor-backed queries** (the fast path): skip MemDB sync entirely. These queries read directly from B-tree via StorageCursor and never touch MemDB.
2. **For compatibility-fallback queries** (CTE, complex JOINs, etc.): MemDB sync is still needed before execution.

### Implementation
In engine.rs INSERT handler (line 7805):
- Check if any pending statement in the current transaction will use the compatibility path
- If NO pending compatibility queries: skip MemDB sync (just set dirty flag)
- If YES or UNKNOWN: do the sync as before

### Simpler Alternative
Just track which tables have been written via storage cursors. When a compatibility-path query touches a dirty table, do a BULK sync from B-tree → MemDB for that table only (not per-row).

### Why This Still Helps
The common case (INSERT-heavy workloads) uses storage cursors exclusively. The MemDB sync is only needed when the next query falls back to compatibility path, which is rare for simple DML.

### Acceptance Criteria UPDATED
1. Storage-cursor-only workloads: zero MemDB sync calls (verify with counter)
2. Compatibility-path queries after INSERT: MemDB synced before execution, correct results
3. conformance_oracle_s55 passes (tests both paths)

title: PERF-P1: IN (SELECT ...) predicates never index-seek — codegen falls back to full scan + ephemeral membership probe
description:
Verified 2026-07-27 (CrimsonFinch) on the debug CLI (binary 7556a865..., mtime 2026-07-26 13:56): with t(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, k INTEGER, v TEXT) and idx_t_k on k:

- SELECT * FROM t WHERE k = 2          -> SeekGE/IdxRowid/SeekRowid (seeks, good)
- SELECT * FROM t WHERE k IN (2, 3)    -> SeekGE/IdxRowid/SeekRowid (seeks, good — fixed since bd-jyyae was filed)
- SELECT * FROM t WHERE k IN (SELECT id FROM r) -> Rewind/Next full scan of t with OpenAutoindex+Found membership probe per row. ZERO seek opcodes.

C SQLite drives this shape as an index loop: iterate the subquery values, SeekGE idx_t_k per value (EQP: SEARCH t USING INDEX idx_t_k (k=?) + LIST SUBQUERY). We scan t (O(N) rows x probe) instead of O(matches) seeks — on a large t with a small subquery result this is the difference between milliseconds and a full-table pass.

Relationship to bd-jyyae: that bead is the EQP TRUTH fix (stop claiming SEARCH for this shape; verification-by-opcode-facts, helpers already in crates/fsqlite-core/src/explain.rs). THIS bead is the engine fix: lower IN(subquery) equality predicates on indexed columns to a value-loop of index probes (materialize subquery -> ephemeral table/rowset -> for each value SeekGE idx). Once this lands, the truthful EQP will naturally report SEARCH again AND match C SQLite parity output.

Suggested entry points: planner_select_directive currently claims IndexEquality for this shape (connection.rs ~53445-53805) while codegen_select declines it — the decline site in fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs is where the alternative lowering belongs. After the fix, extend bd_2dgf5_explain_query_plan_matches_c_sqlite with the IN-subquery row (it should then match C SQLite verbatim).
close_reason: Fixed in 5b49d27a: codegen_select_index_in_subquery_scan lowers uncorrelated indexed IN-subqueries to materialize-once-then-seek (Found-guarded dedup, NULL skip, value-then-rowid order), routed pre-directive like the IN-list/COUNT hooks. Verified: vdbe codegen suite 24/0 (new bd_g5ys1 pin + all existing membership/IN-list pins green); result-correctness oracles 36/0 across in_exists_regression (dup/NULL/mixed-type/large-IN), in_subquery_join_affinity_oracle_e2e (the affinity hazard), subquery_oracle_e2e (rusqlite differential). With bd-jyyae's gate, EQP for this shape truthfully reports SEARCH again.

title: Replace MemDatabase snapshots with MVCC version tokens
description:
## Goal

Replace any MemDatabase snapshot cloning with MVCC version tokens, so snapshot reads reference MVCC state without copying whole databases.

## Scope

- Snapshot identity represented as a lightweight version token
- Readers resolve visible page versions via MVCC using that token
- Remove clone-based snapshotting from the hot path
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria

- Snapshot reads no longer require cloning the entire database state.
- Tests demonstrate: writer commits, reader on older token sees old state, new reader sees new state (no panics, deterministic behavior).
close_reason: MemDatabase snapshots already use lightweight MemDbVersionToken (undo-log index). Removed unused Clone impl, added #[must_use]. 177 VDBE + 685 core tests pass.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## bd-g6eo Completion: Replace MemDatabase snapshots with MVCC version tokens

### Investigation
Audited the full MemDatabase snapshot chain:
- `Connection.snapshot()` (connection.rs:710) captures `MemDbVersionToken` (undo-log length)
- `Connection.restore_snapshot()` (connection.rs:719) calls `MemDatabase.rollback_to(token)`
- `MemDbVersionToken(usize)` is O(1) to create, O(k) to restore (k = ops since token)
- No clone-based snapshotting exists on any hot path
- `Clone for MemDatabase` existed but was NEVER called in production code

### Changes
1. **Removed `Clone for MemDatabase`** (engine.rs:645-654) — prevents future accidental O(n) table cloning. The undo-log path (`MemDbVersionToken`) is the only correct snapshot mechanism.
2. **Added `#[must_use]` to `MemDbVersionToken`** — ensures callers don't discard snapshot tokens.
3. **Added documentation** explaining the MVCC-style undo-log approach and referencing bd-g6eo.

### Architecture (already in place)
- `DbSnapshot` stores lightweight `MemDbVersionToken` + schema vector
- `TransactionHandle.savepoint/rollback_to_savepoint` manages MVCC-layer savepoints
- `Connection` orchestrates both layers in parallel during Phase 4→5 transition
- StorageCursors (Phase 5) already resolve through pager/MVCC VersionStore

### Validation
- cargo check --workspace: PASS
- clippy (pedantic+nursery): PASS
- 177 VDBE tests: ALL PASS
- 685 core tests: ALL PASS
- 10 compat_persist tests: ALL PASS

title: V-TEST-1: Comprehensive unit + e2e test suite for V1 zero-copy page access changes
description:
## What
Write targeted tests that exercise every V1 code path change to catch regressions before they hit conformance tests.

## Test categories

### V1.1 Cell pointer inline tests (cursor.rs)
- `test_inline_cell_pointer_single_cell_page`: page with 1 cell, verify pointer computed correctly
- `test_inline_cell_pointer_max_cells`: page with maximum cells (255 for 4KB page), verify all pointers
- `test_inline_cell_pointer_overflow_page`: page with overflow cells, verify pointer computation handles overflow chain offset
- `test_inline_cell_pointer_empty_page`: leaf page with 0 cells, verify no panic
- `test_inline_cell_pointer_interior_page`: interior (non-leaf) page, verify rightchild pointer handling
- `test_cursor_seek_after_inline_pointers`: full cursor seek + read cycle with inline pointers, compare output to Box<[u16]> baseline

### V1.2 Page cache shared access tests (page_cache.rs)
- `test_get_shared_returns_same_arc`: two calls for same page return Arc with same pointer
- `test_get_shared_after_write_returns_updated`: write a page, read back via get_shared, verify content matches
- `test_get_shared_concurrent_readers`: spawn 4 threads reading same page, verify no data race (Arc refcount)
- `test_get_shared_eviction_and_reload`: fill cache beyond capacity, evict, re-read, verify content
- `test_get_shared_page_alignment`: verify returned PageData bytes are identical to direct PageBuf read

### V1.6 Flat cursor array tests (engine.rs)
- `test_flat_cursor_array_open_close`: open cursor 0, close it, verify slot is None
- `test_flat_cursor_array_multiple_cursors`: open cursors 0, 1, 2, verify all accessible
- `test_flat_cursor_array_reopen_same_slot`: open cursor 0, close, reopen, verify works
- `test_flat_cursor_array_out_of_bounds`: attempt to access cursor beyond array size, verify graceful handling
- `test_flat_cursor_array_concurrent_read_write`: open read cursor + write cursor, verify no interference

### E2E regression tests
- `test_e2e_insert_10k_rows_correctness`: INSERT 10K rows, SELECT COUNT(*), verify = 10000
- `test_e2e_insert_with_index_after_v1_changes`: INSERT into table with secondary index, verify index integrity via SELECT with WHERE clause
- `test_e2e_insert_update_delete_cycle`: full DML cycle (INSERT → UPDATE → SELECT → DELETE → SELECT), verify row counts and values at each step
- `test_e2e_concurrent_writers_after_v1`: 4 concurrent writers, verify all committed data visible
- `test_e2e_large_page_with_many_cells`: INSERT enough rows to create pages with >128 cells, verify no regression

### Logging
All tests should use `tracing::info!` to log:
- Page cache hit/miss counts
- Cell pointer computation count
- Cursor array slot usage (max used slot)
- Total pages read/written
- Arc refcount at key checkpoints

## Files
- `crates/fsqlite-btree/tests/v1_cell_pointer_tests.rs` (NEW)
- `crates/fsqlite-pager/tests/v1_page_cache_shared_tests.rs` (NEW)
- `crates/fsqlite-vdbe/tests/v1_flat_cursor_array_tests.rs` (NEW)
- `crates/fsqlite-core/tests/v1_e2e_regression_tests.rs` (NEW)

- `cargo test -p fsqlite-pager --test v1_page_cache_shared_tests`
- `cargo test -p fsqlite-vdbe --test v1_flat_cursor_array_tests`
- `cargo test -p fsqlite-core --test v1_e2e_regression_tests`
- All existing conformance oracle tests (ext + s55) pass

title: §9 Cx Parameter Enforcement + Sealed Trait Pattern Validation
description:
## SUMMARY
Cross-cutting enforcement bead for §9 (Trait Hierarchy):

1. **Cx Everywhere Rule:** any trait method that touches I/O, acquires locks, or could block MUST accept `&Cx` as its first parameter.
2. **Sealed Trait Pattern:** internal-only traits MUST be sealed to prevent downstream implementations that could violate MVCC safety invariants; user-extension traits MUST remain implementable.

This bead exists to make these rules mechanically checkable (tests + audits) so they cannot regress silently.

## Scope

### Cx Everywhere
- MUST take `&Cx`: VFS I/O, pager operations, cursor operations, checkpoint/writer I/O, coordinator IPC, and any other potentially-blocking path.
- MUST NOT take `&Cx`: pure computation only (example: `CollationFunction::compare`; CPU-only `ScalarFunction::call`).

### Sealed Traits
Open extension points (user-implementable; MUST NOT be sealed):
- `Vfs`, `VfsFile`
- `ScalarFunction`, `AggregateFunction`, `WindowFunction`
- `VirtualTable`, `VirtualTableCursor`
- `CollationFunction`, `Authorizer`

Internal-only (MUST be sealed):
- `MvccPager`
- `BtreeCursorOps`
- `CheckpointPageWriter`

### Test Mocks (Required)
The defining crate for each sealed trait MUST export test mocks usable cross-crate:
- `MockMvccPager`
- `MockBtreeCursor` (implements `BtreeCursorOps`)
- `MockCheckpointPageWriter`

## Unit Test Requirements

- `test_cx_param_audit_vfs_traits`: every I/O method on `Vfs`/`VfsFile` takes `&Cx`.
- `test_cx_param_audit_mvcc_pager_trait`: `begin/get_page/write_page/allocate_page/free_page/commit/rollback` all take `&Cx`.
- `test_cx_param_audit_btree_cursor_ops_trait`: all cursor ops take `&Cx`.
- `test_cx_param_audit_checkpoint_page_writer_trait`: `write_page/sync` take `&Cx`.
- `test_pure_compute_exclusion_collation_compare_no_cx`: `CollationFunction::compare` does not take `&Cx`.
- `test_pure_compute_exclusion_scalar_call_cpu_only_no_cx`: CPU-only `ScalarFunction::call` does not take `&Cx`.
- `test_sealed_mvcc_pager_compile_fail`: downstream impl attempt fails due to sealed trait.
- `test_sealed_btree_cursor_ops_compile_fail`: downstream impl attempt fails.
- `test_sealed_checkpoint_page_writer_compile_fail`: downstream impl attempt fails.
- `test_open_vfs_external_impl_compiles`: downstream crate/module can implement `Vfs`/`VfsFile` (compile-pass).
- `test_open_function_traits_external_impl_compiles`: downstream can implement `ScalarFunction`/`AggregateFunction`/`WindowFunction` (compile-pass).
- `test_mock_exports_available`: mocks are exported and usable from other crates' tests.

## E2E Test

- `test_e2e_bd_ggxs_cx_and_sealed_enforcement_workspace_pass`:
  - Run the signature audit over the whole workspace.
  - Run compile-fail tests for sealed traits and compile-pass tests for open traits.
  - Run a small cancellation smoke (deadline-expired `Cx` causes a real I/O path to fail fast).
  - Emit a deterministic JSON report (see Logging Requirements).

## Logging Requirements

- INFO: enforcement summary: `methods_checked`, `violations`, `compile_fail_cases`, `compile_pass_cases`.
- ERROR: each violation with `crate`, `trait`, `method`, and the observed signature.
- Artifact: deterministic JSON report, e.g. `target/cx_sealed_enforcement_report.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All I/O / lock-acquiring / blocking trait methods accept `&Cx` as first parameter.
- [ ] Pure computation methods explicitly excluded from `Cx` (do not take it).
- [ ] `MvccPager`, `BtreeCursorOps`, and `CheckpointPageWriter` are sealed; downstream impl attempts fail.
- [ ] User-extensible traits are NOT sealed; downstream impl attempts compile.
- [ ] Mocks for sealed traits exist and are usable cross-crate.
- [ ] E2E enforcement pass produces a deterministic JSON report and fails CI on any violation.
close_reason: Implemented Cx+sealed enforcement suite, cross-crate mocks, open trait exports, trybuild compile-fail/pass checks, and deterministic report artifact; validation tests passing.

comments.text:
# §9 Cx Parameter Enforcement + Sealed Trait Pattern Validation

## Spec Reference
COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md lines 12422-12455 (§9)

## Scope

Ensure the "Cx Everywhere" rule is enforced across all I/O and lock-acquiring
trait methods, and that internal-only traits use the sealed trait pattern to
prevent downstream implementations that could violate MVCC safety invariants.

## Cx Everywhere Rule (from spec)

Every trait method that touches I/O, acquires locks, or could block MUST accept
`&Cx` as its first parameter. This enables:
- **Cancellation:** Any operation can be cancelled by the caller's context
- **Deadline propagation:** Timeout budgets flow through the entire call chain
- **Capability narrowing:** Callers can restrict what callees are allowed to do

Pure computation (e.g., `CollationFunction::compare`, `ScalarFunction::call` for
CPU-only work) does NOT take `Cx`. When in doubt, include `Cx`.

## Sealed Trait Pattern (from spec)

```rust
mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} }  // private to the defining crate

pub trait MvccPager: sealed::Sealed + Send + Sync { /* ... */ }
```

**Open extension points (user-implementable):** `Vfs`, `VfsFile`,
`ScalarFunction`, `AggregateFunction`, `WindowFunction`, `VirtualTable`,
`VirtualTableCursor`, `CollationFunction`, `Authorizer`.

**Internal-only (sealed):** `MvccPager`, `BtreeCursorOps` (and any similar
trait whose implementations must preserve engine invariants).

Test mocks for sealed traits live alongside the trait definition and are
exported as values/types for other crates to use in tests.

## Unit Test Specifications

### Test 1: Cx parameter audit — VFS traits
Programmatically (or via compile-time assertion) verify that every method on
the `Vfs` and `VfsFile` traits that performs I/O takes `&Cx` as the first
parameter. Methods: `open`, `delete`, `access`, `full_pathname`, `read`,
`write`, `truncate`, `sync`, `file_size`, `lock`, `unlock`, `check_reserved_lock`.

### Test 2: Cx parameter audit — MvccPager trait
Verify that all MvccPager methods that acquire locks or perform I/O take `&Cx`:
`begin`, `acquire_page`, `release_page`, `commit`, `rollback`, `checkpoint`.

### Test 3: Pure computation exclusion
Verify that `CollationFunction::compare` and `ScalarFunction::call` (when
CPU-only) do NOT take `&Cx`. This confirms the rule is not over-applied.

### Test 4: Sealed trait — MvccPager cannot be implemented externally
Write a compile-fail test (using `trybuild` or `compile_fail` doctest):
```rust
struct FakePager;
impl MvccPager for FakePager { ... }  // MUST fail: Sealed not implemented
```
Verify the compiler error mentions the sealed trait bound.

### Test 5: Sealed trait — BtreeCursorOps cannot be implemented externally
Same pattern as Test 4 for `BtreeCursorOps`. Verify compile-fail.

### Test 6: Open traits CAN be implemented externally
Write a positive test: implement `Vfs` and `VfsFile` in a downstream test
crate/module. Verify it compiles and can be used. This confirms sealed is
NOT applied to user-extensible traits.

### Test 7: Test mock for sealed trait is available
Verify that the crate defining `MvccPager` exports a `MockMvccPager` (or
similar) that implements the sealed trait. Verify it can be used in tests
from other crates.

### Test 8: Cancellation via Cx works end-to-end
Create a `Cx` with a deadline in the past. Call a VFS `read` method with it.
Verify the operation returns a cancellation/timeout error rather than
performing I/O.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All I/O and lock-acquiring trait methods confirmed to take `&Cx`
- Pure computation methods confirmed to NOT take `&Cx`
- `MvccPager` and `BtreeCursorOps` confirmed sealed via compile-fail tests
- User-extensible traits (Vfs, VfsFile, etc.) confirmed NOT sealed
- Test mocks for sealed traits are available for cross-crate testing
- Cx cancellation propagation works end-to-end
- All tests pass under `cargo test`

comments.text:
## CORRECTION: MvccPager Method Names (Audit Fix)

Test 2 in the original comment incorrectly listed MvccPager methods as:
`acquire_page`, `release_page`, `checkpoint`

The CORRECT MvccPager methods per spec (lines 12632-12668) are:
- `begin(&self, cx: &Cx, mode: TxnMode) -> Result<Transaction>`
- `get_page(&self, cx: &Cx, txn: &Transaction, pgno: PageNumber) -> Result<PageRef>`
- `write_page(&self, cx: &Cx, txn: &mut Transaction, pgno: PageNumber, data: PageData) -> Result<()>`
- `allocate_page(&self, cx: &Cx, txn: &mut Transaction) -> Result<PageNumber>`
- `free_page(&self, cx: &Cx, txn: &mut Transaction, pgno: PageNumber) -> Result<()>`
- `commit(&self, cx: &Cx, txn: Transaction) -> Result<()>`
- `rollback(&self, cx: &Cx, txn: Transaction)`

### Corrected Test 2: Cx parameter audit — MvccPager trait
Verify that all MvccPager methods that acquire locks or perform I/O take `&Cx`:
`begin`, `get_page`, `write_page`, `allocate_page`, `free_page`, `commit`, `rollback`.

Note: `rollback` also takes `&Cx` even though it never fails (it still needs cancellation context for cleanup).

### Additional Test: BtreeCursorOps Cx audit  
Verify all BtreeCursorOps methods take `&Cx`:
`index_move_to`, `table_move_to`, `first`, `last`, `next`, `prev`, `key`, `data`, `insert`, `delete`, `count`.

### Additional Test: CheckpointPageWriter Cx audit
Verify CheckpointPageWriter methods (`write_page`, `sync`) take `&Cx`.

### Additional Test: Mock availability for sealed traits
Verify exports: `MockMvccPager`, `MockBtreeCursor` (for BtreeCursorOps), `MockCheckpointPageWriter`.
Each mock must live in the defining crate and be re-exported for cross-crate test use.

The E2E run MUST produce a single summary report listing any Cx-rule violations (method signature + crate path).

severity=wrong_result effort=medium

EVIDENCE: Repro (fsqlite debug binary built Jul 14, file-backed DB): `CREATE TABLE t(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, v UNIQUE); INSERT INTO t(v) VALUES('a'); INSERT OR IGNORE INTO t(v) VALUES('a'); SELECT seq FROM sqlite_sequence; INSERT INTO t(v) VALUES('b'); SELECT id,v FROM t; SELECT seq FROM sqlite_sequence;` -> fsqlite: seq_after_ignore=1, rows (1,'a'),(2,'b'), seq_final=2. /usr/bin/sqlite3 3.46.1 oracle: seq_after_ignore=2, rows (1,'a'),(3,'b'), seq_final=3 (matches issue's SQLite 3.53.2 claim). Root cause: crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs:39222 `try_fast_path_autoincrement_sequence_after_insert` and :39265 `refresh_autoincrement_sequence_after_insert` write sqlite_sequence AFTER the statement from rows actually inserted (last_insert_rowid, or `table_max_rowid_in_txn` scan) — an OR IGNORE'd conflict inserts nothing, so the allocated rowid 2 is never recorded. C SQLite instead reco
close_reason: Fixed in 94f8a2530 (pushed main+master). An INSERT OR IGNORE that allocated an AUTOINCREMENT rowid via NewRowid but discarded the row on a conflict left sqlite_sequence at the last inserted rowid (fsqlite next-id 2 vs sqlite3 3), because the connection's sequence write-back only observes affected=0 / last_insert_rowid / table_max_rowid_in_txn — not the burned allocation. Fix: the VDBE engine records the max AUTOINCREMENT rowid ALLOCATED per table root_page during a program (new autoinc_alloc_high_water map, updated in the NewRowid handler for RowIdMode::AutoIncrement, reset at program start, exposed via getter); refresh_autoincrement_sequence_after_insert folds that high-water — read from the just-executed engine parked in cached_vdbe_engine, keyed by root_page — into new_seq via max(). It only advances the sequence (never regresses) and a different table's root_page cannot false-match. Verified GREEN: keeper autoincrement_or_ignore_gh186_probe 2/2 (OR IGNORE advances seq + next id 3, plain control); regressions clean: alter_rename_sqlite_sequence 1/1, insert_or_ignore_returning_rowid_gh158 3/3, autoincrement_edge_oracle_e2e 3/3. NOTE: an AFTER-INSERT trigger that itself runs a program between the outer insert and the refresh could park a different engine in cached_vdbe_engine (untested edge); the root_page-keyed max() keeps that safe (no false advance).

title: GH triage: cte-compiled-cache-stale-root (#255)
description:
LIKELY ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (GreenGull, during the bd-ybde3 migration).

`Connection::compile_with_cache` (crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs ~23877)
branches on `self.bypass_compiled_cache.get()` and, when set, SKIPS the
compiled-program cache and recompiles.

The only code that can set that flag is
`Connection::with_compiled_cache_bypass` (~23705), and it has ZERO call sites.
The field is otherwise only initialised to `false` in the two constructors.
So the bypass branch is unreachable in practice and the compiled cache is
ALWAYS consulted.

Why that produces this bug: CTE and view materialization allocate temp tables in
MemDatabase with DYNAMIC root pages (see reserve_clean_memdb_root_pages and the
materialize_with_clause path). A program compiled against an earlier root page
stays cached and keeps using that stale root -- exactly 'cte-compiled-cache-stale-root'.

The bypass helper looks like it was written precisely to prevent this and was
then disconnected (or never connected) from the CTE/view materialization path.

SUSPECTED FIX: wrap the CTE/view materialization compile in
`with_compiled_cache_bypass`, or set the flag around root-page reservation, so
that compilation against a freshly-allocated root cannot be served from cache.
Needs a regression test that materializes a CTE twice with different root pages
and asserts the second execution does not reuse the first program.

NOT done as part of the migration: this is a behavioural fix needing its own
change and test, not a lint cleanup. The two helpers now carry
`#[allow(dead_code)]` plus an explanatory comment so a future dead-code sweep
does not delete the evidence -- deleting them would have silently removed the
only remaining trace of the intended guard.

Related: bd-7y8ff (the dead-code cluster this came from).
close_reason: GH #255 already fixed (compiled-cache bypass); keepers green at HEAD

## GH #212: JSON functions reject REAL infinity accepted by SQLite
severity=error_instead_of_result effort=medium
FIX: crates/fsqlite-ext-json/src/lib.rs:1655 (sqlite_to_json), crates/fsqlite-ext-json/src/lib.rs:368 (json_quote), parse_json_text/serde_json number handling, lib.rs:1031 (JSONB float decode), lib.rs:4470 (wrong-behavior unit test to update)

- `SELECT json_array(1e999);` → `error: non-finite float is not representable in JSON` (oracle /usr/bin/sqlite3 3.46.1: `[9.0e+999]`)
- `SELECT json_object('a',1e999);` → same error (oracle: `{"a":9.0e+999}`); `json_array(-1e999)` oracle: `[-9.0e+999]`
- `SELECT json_quote(1e999);` → `null` — wrong result, not an error (oracle: `9.0e+999`; only NaN maps to null, and bare SQL NaN is already NULL so `json_array(0.0/0.0)` → `[null]` on both)
- Parse side also broken: `SELECT json('[9e999]');` and `json_extract('[9e999]','$[0]')` → `error: invalid JSON input: number out of range`; `json_valid('[9e999]')` → 0 (oracle: `[9e999]`, `Inf`, `1`)
Code root cause, all in crates/fsqlite-ext-json/s
close_reason: Fixed (92cd302ef). JSON layer now follows SQLite's non-finite REAL convention: +Inf->9.0e+999, -Inf->-9.0e+999, NaN->null. serde_json arbitrary_precision enabled (holds raw/non-finite number text); float_to_json + render_non_finite_number + json_number_from_raw handle construct/quote/JSONB/extract; write_canonical_json_text renders non-finite via raw text; constructor/serializer sites routed off serde_json::to_string onto the canonical writer (also restores finite exponent form). Oracle-verified vs sqlite3 3.46.1: json_array(1e999)=[9.0e+999], json_object('k',1e999)={"k":9.0e+999}, json_quote(1e999)=9.0e+999, NaN->null, json('[9e999]')=[9e999] (source preserved), json_extract('[9.0e+999]','$[0]')=Inf, json_valid('[9e999]')=1. Verified: ext-json 203 passed/0 failed (independent re-run), clippy+build clean, forbid(unsafe) intact; 3 wrong-behavior tests corrected + 12 differential tests added. KNOWN MINOR DEVIATIONS (non-required, both strict improvements over the prior error): (1) mutators json_set/insert/replace with a bare-REAL Inf render 9.0e+999 vs stock's minimal 9e999 (SQLite's own construct-vs-mutator quirk; shares sqlite_to_json; parsed non-finite still preserves 9e999); (2) exotic parsed source (9.5e999, uppercase 9E999) keeps serde's canonical form since arbitrary_precision normalizes the token. GH #212 remains for maintainer to close.

comments.text: TRIAGE NOTE (Claude/Opus, 2026-08-15) — effort is UNDER-estimated (medium is optimistic). Root blocker: the crate models JSON internally as serde_json::Value, whose Value::Number CANNOT represent Inf/NaN (Number::from_f64 rejects non-finite), so a non-finite float errors at Value construction (sqlite_to_json lib.rs:1918-1928) before serialization is even reached. Also the parse side: serde_json parses 9e999 -> f64 Inf -> from_f64 fails -> 'number out of range', but stock SQLite PRESERVES number text (json('[9e999]') -> [9e999], only converting to REAL Inf at extract). A correct fix therefore needs number-TEXT preservation (serde_json arbitrary_precision feature, string-backed Number) or a custom JSON value model, then non-finite serialization rules (+Inf->9.0e+999, -Inf->-9.0e+999, NaN->null) in write_canonical_json_text (lib.rs:149) + json_quote (454) + JSONB decode (1029/1198). NOT a bounded 5-site edit. Left OPEN/unclaimed for a lane that can budget the value-model change.
