## GH #200: Unix VFS write does not retry EINTR after partial progress
severity=error_instead_of_result effort=small
FIX: crates/fsqlite-vfs/src/unix.rs:1892 (write Err arm); also unix.rs:1858 (read), unix.rs:1786 (shm header write), unix.rs:1899 (ftruncate), and crates/fsqlite-vfs/src/uring.rs sync/async read/write loops (~552, ~683, ~949, ~1013)

Rust std's FileExt::write_at is a single pwrite and does not retry EINTR (unlike Write::write_all). `rg -n "Interrupted|EINTR" crates/fsqlite-vfs/src/` shows the ONLY EINTR retry in the crate is the fcntl F_SETLK lock loop at unix.rs:311; the data-path loops have none. title: RELEASE-P0: finish snapshot-safe committed-freelist reuse under continuous overlap (GH #302)
description:
## Context

GitHub #302 remains open after the bounded f0d5b895 fix. That commit proves committed-freelist reuse for a sole current snapshot and preserves conservative deferral for local older snapshots. The issue explicitly retains two release-relevant gaps: continuous reader/writer overlap can still force unbounded EOF allocation, and no keeper proves that an external WAL reader at an old mark retains its original bytes while another connection safely reuses a committed-free page below db_size.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a file-backed database in the required default concurrent mode with auto_vacuum=NONE.
2. Keep a reader or writer snapshot continuously active while later transactions repeatedly create/drop or delete/reinsert enough indexed rows to allocate and free multiple pages.
3. Commit and checkpoint each churn cycle and record page_count plus freelist_count.
4. Observe that, without a quiescent point, committed freelist pages remain pinned and allocation can continue at EOF.
5. Separately hold an external WAL reader at an old mark while a sole local writer reuses a committed-free page below db_size; the missing keeper must prove the reader retains its original snapshot bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Deterministic file-backed churn with sustained reader/writer overlap reaches bounded page_count after warm-up while reusing only pages safe for every local and cross-process snapshot.
2. An external WAL reader held at an old snapshot mark continues to observe its original bytes while another connection safely reuses a committed-free page below db_size.
3. Deterministic multi-writer WAL tests cover reuse, commit, rollback, crash/reopen, and checkpoint boundaries.
4. Reuse never aliases two B-trees, loses a page from both ownership and freelist accounting, or fails stock SQLite integrity_check.
5. Concurrent-writer mode remains enabled by default.
6. Focused and frozen-candidate remote receipts are attached; no blanket waiver or unrelated green subset closes this blocker.

Source: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite/issues/302

Safe continuous-overlap reuse cannot be a gate relaxation: current freelist is an unversioned global Vec projected into page-1/trunk pages only at commit, WAL only pins a per-backend publication snapshot for writer conflict detection, and checkpoint rejects any active transaction because it has no oldest-reader horizon. Correct repair needs durable per-page retirement/reuse generations plus shared local/cross-process reader horizon; begin/commit/rollback/savepoint must atomically reserve/restore generations, recovery must reconstruct only published retirements, and checkpoint must retain frames through the oldest horizon. Existing churn keeper has no continuously held reader; existing child-process keeper proves one delete/reuse snapshot only. comments.text:
[bd-gh302] CLAIMING the committed-freelist resurrection fix (bd-0shxy residual, ledger-pinned at 75786e4f7/0749b7502) — this is this bead's exact domain: snapshot-safe committed-freelist reuse under concurrency.

MECHANISM (0shxy's ledger receipts, restated): WAL commit-time durable-freelist serialization (serialize_freelist_to_write_set) publishes predicted = BEGIN-TIME inner.freelist + own pending frees. A committer whose begin predates a peer's consumption of free page N re-publishes N as free; every later begin-refresh reloads N; the sole_current_snapshot gate is connection-local and cannot see it. Ledger: page 333 granted 5x across 4 pagers, page 328 3x across 3, all via alloc_freelist_gated, zero legitimate frees between. FCW is structurally blind: the resurrector never writes N (it only lists N in page-1/trunk content), the consumer's frame for N doesn't intersect the resurrector's write set.

FIX (fail-closed variant of 0shxy's merge spec — validation instead of under-gate frame rewriting, so no re-serialization/checksum surgery):
1. serialize_freelist_to_write_set returns the exact durable freelist it published; the commit threads it (+ the txn's own freed pages) onto the group-commit batch metadata.
2. Any batch carrying a freelist publication routes to the serialized append path (new ParallelWalFallbackReason::FreelistPublication, same pattern as EofGrowth) — consumers always qualify (allocated_from_freelist => freelist_dirty), so no two freelist-publishing commits validate concurrently.
3. Under the append gate (post refresh, same site as conflicting_pages_since_batch_snapshots): read the CURRENT durable freelist (page-1 header + trunk chain through the WAL backend) and fail the batch closed with BusySnapshot if its published list contains any page NOT in (current durable freelist UNION its own freed pages) — i.e., it would resurrect a page some peer consumed since its begin. Retry re-begins with a fresh freelist and publishes correctly. Inductively the durable freelist stays exact under serialized freelist commits.
4. Same-epoch multi-batch freelist publishers: keep the first, abort the rest (BusySnapshot).

VERIFICATION PLAN: extreme_index_punishment 12x (0shxy residual baseline 2-4/12 -> expect 0), conservation x15 (stay 0), gh302 keepers (stay green), pager/core suites. - Decode failures produce explainable DecodeProof/failure artifacts.

- `proptest` for structured random cases:

  - random erasure positions

  - decoder entrypoints with adversarial symbol streams

- Fuzz targets are deterministic-seeded in CI mode.
- Crashes / panics are treated as failures.
- Proof verifier can replay-check a sample of fuzz-produced proofs.

title: §10.7-10.8 VDBE Instruction Format + Coroutines
description:
## SUMMARY

Defines the VDBE (Virtual Database Engine) instruction format and the coroutine mechanism used for subqueries and CTEs. The VdbeOp struct is a fixed-size 6-field instruction with opcode (u8), three i32 operands (p1/p2/p3), a polymorphic P4 extended operand, and a u16 flags field (p5). The coroutine subsystem uses InitCoroutine/Yield/EndCoroutine opcodes to implement cooperative PC-swapping between outer queries and CTE/subquery bodies without materializing entire result sets.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS

- **VdbeOp struct**: `{ opcode: Opcode (u8), p1: i32, p2: i32, p3: i32, p4: P4, p5: u16 }`. 190+ opcodes covering control flow, data access, comparison, arithmetic, string, row operations, cursor, sorting, aggregation, transactions.
- **P4 enum**: `None | Int32(i32) | Int64(i64) | Real(f64) | String(String) | Blob(Vec<u8>) | FuncDef(Arc<dyn ScalarFunction>) | CollSeq(Arc<dyn CollationFunction>) | KeyInfo(KeyInfo) | Mem(Mem) | Vtab(Arc<dyn VirtualTable>) | Table(TableInfo) | Subprogram(VdbeProgram)`.
- **Label system for jump resolution**: `emit_label()` returns a `Label` handle; `resolve_label(label, address)` patches all forward-referencing instructions. All labels MUST be resolved before execution begins.
- **Register allocation**: Registers numbered starting at 1. Sequential allocation via `alloc_reg()` / `alloc_regs(n)`. Temporary registers returned to pool after use; persistent registers held for statement lifetime.
- **Coroutine mechanism**: `InitCoroutine r_yield, P2, <cte_body>` sets r_yield to CTE body PC. `Yield r_yield` swaps PCs (saves current PC into r_yield, jumps to old r_yield). `EndCoroutine r_yield` performs final swap back to caller. NOT async -- cooperative state machines within the VDBE VM.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS

1. p5 is u16 matching C SQLite's declaration; per-opcode P5 flag usage MUST match C SQLite exactly.
2. All labels MUST be resolved before execution begins; unresolved labels are a codegen bug.
3. Register numbering starts at 1 (not 0).
4. Coroutines are NOT async; they are cooperative PC-swap state machines.
5. `Yield` saves current PC into r_yield and jumps to old r_yield (bidirectional swap).
6. `EndCoroutine` marks exhaustion and performs final return to caller.
7. In `BEGIN CONCURRENT`, `OP_NewRowid` MUST allocate via the snapshot-independent RowId allocator (per section 5.10.1.1), NOT by scanning snapshot-visible max(rowid).

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS

1. `test_vdbe_op_struct_size` -- VdbeOp struct fields are accessible and correctly typed (opcode u8, p1/p2/p3 i32, p4 P4 enum, p5 u16).
2. `test_p4_variant_all_types` -- Each P4 variant (None, Int32, Int64, Real, String, Blob, FuncDef, CollSeq, KeyInfo, Mem, Vtab, Table, Subprogram) can be constructed and matched.
3. `test_label_emit_and_resolve` -- emit_label returns distinct handles; resolve_label patches instruction p2 targets; unresolved label detection panics/errors.
4. `test_register_alloc_sequential` -- alloc_reg returns 1, 2, 3, ...; alloc_regs(3) returns contiguous block.
5. `test_register_temp_pool_reuse` -- Temporary registers are returned to pool and reused in subsequent allocations.
6. `test_coroutine_init_yield_end` -- InitCoroutine sets r_yield correctly; Yield swaps PCs bidirectionally; EndCoroutine returns to caller and marks exhaustion.
7. `test_coroutine_multi_row_production` -- CTE body yields 5 rows; outer query consumes all 5 via Yield loop.
8. `test_all_opcode_dispatch_coverage` -- Every Opcode enum variant has a matching handler in the dispatch table (no unimplemented arms).
9. `test_p5_flags_u16_range` -- p5 values above 0xFF are accepted (confirms u16, not u8).

## E2E TEST

Execute `WITH cte AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM cte WHERE x < 5) SELECT * FROM cte` through the full pipeline (parse -> plan -> codegen -> VDBE execution). Verify the coroutine mechanism produces rows [1,2,3,4,5] without materializing the entire CTE. Compare result against C SQLite output.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- VdbeOp struct matches the 6-field layout specified in section 10.7 exactly.
- All P4 variants are implemented and functional.
- Label system correctly resolves forward jumps; unresolved labels produce errors before execution.
- Register allocator produces sequential numbering starting at 1, with temp pool reuse.
- Coroutine InitCoroutine/Yield/EndCoroutine cycle produces correct row-by-row iteration for CTEs and subqueries.
- All 190+ opcodes have dispatch handlers (no panics on valid opcode).
- WITH RECURSIVE queries execute correctly using coroutine mechanism.
close_reason: Implemented VDBE program builder, label system, register allocator, coroutine mechanism, KeyInfo, disassembler in fsqlite-vdbe. All 18 unit tests pass. Clippy clean. Unblocks bd-1mtt (code generation).

comments.text:
## §10.7-10.8 VDBE Instruction Format + Coroutines

### Spec Content (Lines 13578-13650)

**VDBE Instruction Format:**
Each instruction is a fixed-size struct:
```
VdbeOp := {
  opcode  : u8,          // operation code (OP_Init, OP_Goto, OP_Column, etc.)
  p1      : i32,         // first operand (register number, cursor number, etc.)
  p2      : i32,         // second operand (jump target, count, etc.)
  p3      : i32,         // third operand
  p4      : P4Union,     // polymorphic fourth operand (string, function ptr, etc.)
  p5      : u16,         // flags/modifiers
}
```

**Opcode categories (all from C SQLite, must be implemented):**
- Control flow: OP_Init, OP_Goto, OP_If, OP_IfNot, OP_Halt, OP_Return
- Data access: OP_OpenRead, OP_OpenWrite, OP_Column, OP_Rowid
- Comparison: OP_Eq, OP_Ne, OP_Lt, OP_Le, OP_Gt, OP_Ge
- Arithmetic: OP_Add, OP_Subtract, OP_Multiply, OP_Divide, OP_Remainder
- String: OP_Concat, OP_Function
- Row operations: OP_Insert, OP_Delete, OP_NewRowid, OP_MakeRecord
- Cursor: OP_Rewind, OP_Next, OP_Prev, OP_SeekGE, OP_SeekGT, OP_SeekLE, OP_SeekLT
- Sorting: OP_SorterOpen, OP_SorterInsert, OP_SorterSort, OP_SorterNext
- Aggregation: OP_AggStep, OP_AggFinal
- Transaction: OP_Transaction, OP_Savepoint, OP_AutoCommit

**P4 union types:** String, Int64, Real, FuncDef, CollSeq, KeyInfo, Mem, SubProgram

**§10.8 Coroutines:**
VDBE uses coroutine-style execution for subqueries and multi-row returns:
- OP_InitCoroutine: Initialize coroutine state
- OP_Yield: Yield control between main program and coroutine
- OP_EndCoroutine: Clean up coroutine

Coroutines are NOT async — they are cooperative state machines within the VDBE VM.

### Unit Tests Required
1. test_all_opcode_dispatch: Every opcode enum variant has a handler
2. test_vdbe_op_encoding: VdbeOp struct serialization round-trip
3. test_control_flow_opcodes: Goto, If, IfNot, Halt, Return
4. test_comparison_opcodes: All 6 comparisons with type coercion
5. test_arithmetic_opcodes: Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Rem with overflow handling
6. test_cursor_seek_opcodes: SeekGE/GT/LE/LT with B-tree integration
7. test_coroutine_yield: Yield produces correct rows
8. test_sorter_opcodes: SorterOpen through SorterNext
9. test_aggregate_opcodes: AggStep + AggFinal for count/sum/avg

Compile known SQL queries to VDBE bytecode. Execute and verify results match C sqlite3.
Log each opcode execution with register state for debugging.

comments.text:
## Missing Detail (Audit Fix): OP_NewRowid Concurrent-Mode Allocation Algorithm

### Problem
The bead documents VDBE opcodes and coroutines but does not detail how `OP_NewRowid` changes behavior under `BEGIN CONCURRENT`. This is a critical implementation detail since the standard `max(rowid)+1` approach fails with concurrent writers.

### Spec Content (§10.6 line 13537 + §5.10.1.1 lines 10043-10131)

**Normative rule:** In `BEGIN CONCURRENT`, `OP_NewRowid` MUST allocate via the snapshot-independent RowId allocator (§5.10.1.1), NOT by scanning the transaction's snapshot-visible `max(rowid)`. This is required for commutative insert merges and deterministic rebase to work for append-heavy workloads.

**Why standard approach fails:** C SQLite implements `OP_NewRowid` as `max(rowid)+1` because writers are serialized by the WAL write lock. In `BEGIN CONCURRENT`, two writers starting from the same snapshot would choose the same RowId, making `IntentOpKind::Insert { key: RowId, ... }` replay impossible (deterministic rebase would fail with `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_PRIMARYKEY`).

**Minimum semantics (V1):**
- **Non-AUTOINCREMENT rowid tables:** Initialize the allocator (per schema epoch) to `max_committed_rowid(table) + 1` (computed by seeking to the rightmost committed row at the latest durable tip, NOT the transaction snapshot), then allocate monotonically. Allocations are NOT rolled back on abort; gaps are permitted.
- **AUTOINCREMENT tables:** Initialize to `max(sqlite_sequence.seq, max_committed_rowid(table)) + 1`. The committing transaction MUST persist AUTOINCREMENT state by updating `sqlite_sequence` to at least the maximum rowid actually inserted (monotone max merge: `seq = max(seq, inserted_rowid)`).
- **Bump-on-explicit-rowid:** If a statement inserts an explicit rowid `r`, the engine MUST ensure the allocator's next value is at least `r+1` (atomic max).
- **Cross-process:** Uses `ROWID_RESERVE` IPC wire message (kind_be=4) to reserve a monotone RowId range from the coordinator.
- **MAX_ROWID saturation:** The allocator MUST NOT allocate a RowId greater than `2^63-1`. If exceeded in `BEGIN CONCURRENT`, fail with `SQLITE_FULL`. Layer 1/Serialized mode retains C SQLite's random-rowid fallback.

**Allocated RowId stability:** The allocated RowId MUST be stable for the lifetime of the statement/transaction. Commit-time deterministic rebase (§5.10.2) MUST NOT change rowids, because that would invalidate `last_insert_rowid()` and RETURNING results.

## Test Requirements
- test_concurrent_newrowid_unique: Two concurrent transactions each insert 100 rows via auto-rowid; all 200 rowids are unique after both commit
- test_concurrent_newrowid_monotone: RowIds allocated in concurrent mode are monotonically increasing within each transaction
- test_concurrent_autoincrement_merge: Two concurrent transactions insert into AUTOINCREMENT table; sqlite_sequence reflects the max of both
- test_concurrent_explicit_rowid_bump: After explicit INSERT with rowid=1000, next auto-rowid >= 1001
- test_concurrent_newrowid_abort_gaps: Aborted transaction's rowids are NOT reused (gaps permitted)
- test_concurrent_max_rowid_full: Allocator near MAX_ROWID returns SQLITE_FULL in concurrent mode

title: audit(mvcc): drain_orphaned holds draining Mutex while invoking user is_active_txn closure — callback-under-lock (currently test-only caller)
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria:
- The described defect or performance finding is reproduced with a focused unit, integration, or benchmark test before the fix is accepted.
- The implementation removes the root cause without changing concurrent-writer defaults or weakening correctness checks.
- Regression coverage fails on the old behavior and passes on the fixed behavior.
- Structured logs, counters, or benchmark artifacts show the before/after effect and any remaining limitation.
close_reason: FIXED (this commit). drain_orphaned no longer holds the draining mutex (or a shard lock) across the caller is_active_txn closure — restructured to snapshot distinct txn ids under the lock, evaluate the predicate lock-free, then re-acquire (epoch-validated) and remove orphans. Removes the callback-under-lock fragility (deadlock-finder Class 1). Keeper test_drain_orphaned_predicate_not_called_under_lock_bd_gq0bi: a re-entrant predicate (calls holder(), which takes self.draining) now completes + cleans the orphan; under the old code it would deadlock. fsqlite-mvcc --lib 1522/0, clippy clean. No change to concurrent-writer defaults.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Location: crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/core_types.rs:1215-1242 (InProcessPageLockTable::drain_orphaned).

Pattern: holds self.draining (parking_lot::Mutex) across invocation of the caller-supplied closure is_active_txn inside the inner map.retain() loop. Per /deadlock-finder-and-fixer Class 1 guidance, 'Don't hold a lock across a call you don't own. Never call user callbacks, foreign functions, or allocator hooks while holding a lock — they may re-enter.'

Production call-chain today: full_rebuild (core_types.rs:1322) is only called from tests (core_types.rs:4532) and from shared_lock_table.rs:773, which passes a closure the audit confirmed does not re-enter the InProcessPageLockTable. No production path reaches this callback with a lock-reentrant closure.

Verdict per skill validation checklist: architecturally safe today, FRAGILE IF REFACTORED. No concrete deadlock interleaving exists in production. File as documentation/fragility bead, not a live bug.

Suggested fix (if ever promoted to live caller): collect the (page, txn_id) pairs under the draining lock into a Vec, drop the lock, then call is_active_txn on each outside, then re-acquire the lock to apply removals. Trades one lock/unlock pair for callback safety.

Related: same pattern applies if shared_lock_table::full_rebuild (shared_lock_table.rs:773) is extended to accept a closure that could call back into the lock table.

title: asupersync/quiescence: WalFecRepairPipeline Drop detaches its async worker (cancel-only, no join)
description: bd-1is5z site. crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal_fec.rs:1672 Drop calls cancel()+drops sender+warn but never awaits worker: Option<AsyncJoinHandle<()>> (spawned :1556 via try_spawn, worker_cx=parent_cx.create_child() = cap-correct). Only async shutdown() (:1656) joins via worker.await. NUANCE (corrects the audit sketch): the worker is an AsyncJoinHandle (await-only) — it CANNOT be sync-joined in Drop like parallel_wal's BlockingTaskHandle::wait() (parallel_wal.rs:3462). Correct fix is STRUCTURAL: either (a) convert the worker to a spawn_blocking BlockingTaskHandle so Drop can wait(), or (b) register the task in a RegionTree node so close_and_drain accounts for it. Also verify asupersync AsyncJoinHandle Drop semantics (detach vs scope-cancel) — the worker_cx is a child of parent_cx, so the task may already be cancelled when parent region closes. LATENT: only tests/wal_fec_pipeline.rs constructs it and they call shutdown(); fix sets the correct precedent before FEC is Connection-wired.
close_reason: Landed 3b8ef34ef: cancel-correct Drop. asupersync 0.4.5 builder::JoinHandle has no abort()/no cancel-on-drop (drop=detach; verified via runtime_three_way_drop_vs_abort_distinction_audit + runtime_join_handle_no_separable_abort_handle_audit) — so the prior worker.abort() edit could not compile and no handle-level cancel exists. Fix requests structured cancellation from sync Drop by retaining a clone of the worker child Cx (create_child_for_spawn, spawn-correct) and cancel()ing it in Drop; Cx clones share Arc<CxInner> so it propagates to the worker + its attached native cx (wakes idle recv with Cancelled) + all per-work work_cx descendants (INV-CANCEL-PROPAGATES), atop existing cancel_flag + sender-drop. Drop stays cancel-only; quiescence via awaited shutdown() (mirrors Connection close(), bd-2lwkg). Region-registered quiescence-by-construction (Connection::try_spawn_in_region, bd-54ulg/795b91cc0) is unreachable from fsqlite-wal (RegionTree is Connection-private) and semantically needs an awaitable handle for shutdown()'s stats/failure contract, so it is deferred to Connection-wiring time = bd-ewwia. So the bind carries a STALE (older) seq while the reload's begin observes the current (newer) seq -> prebound sibling's `!=` fires as `txn_seq > pub_seq` -> BusySnapshot. The prescribed "restart from a fresh bind" recovery CANNOT converge because every rebind re-hits the same early return (per Addition 2: a LEAKED active_transactions count or stuck checkpoint_active flag on the live connection's own pager wedges it PER-CONNECTION + PERMANENTLY; reads inside an explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE succeed, autocommit reads stay BusySnapshot, PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=[0,-1,-1] does not clear it). Addition 1: the error text "pager publication advanced between metadata bind and reload transaction" names the OPPOSITE cause (a forward-moving writer) and cost them 3 triage investigations — worth fixing the wording too.

WHY THE PRIOR PATCH WAS WRONG: (1) it tolerated txn_seq < pub_seq (external reset) and KEPT txn_seq > pub_seq erroring — but `>` is exactly the failing case. (2) Naively tolerating `>` would BREAK the existing keeper test_stale_prebound_reload_fails_closed_before_live_vtab_preservation (connection.rs:186094), which deliberately asserts `>` fails-closed for a REAL peer advance (conn_b commits rowid=2 after conn_a binds). That keeper is CORRECT: the prebound publication ESCAPES + is reused by prepared-DML admission, so tolerating a real advance risks an epoch mix — unlike the tolerant sibling reload_memdb_from_pager_with_mode, whose publication is local + never escapes. The seq comparison alone CANNOT distinguish "phantom stale bind (tolerate)" from "real peer advance (fail-closed)".

  Option B (convergence): in the 14538 skip-path, still publish/return the current `inner.commit_seq` (as the full path does at 14556-14566) instead of the stale `self.published.snapshot()`, so a rebind is never spuriously stale. title: GH#355: Windows initialize_reserved_schema_only_builder fails CannotOpen on a just-returned reserved handle
description: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite/issues/355 — Windows-only: reserved handle returned by the builder immediately fails CannotOpen on open. Likely Windows path/share-mode handling in fsqlite-vfs. No Windows box in the fleet — code-inspection + CI matrix repro path.
notes:
CODE-INSPECTION (CobaltHarbor, no Windows box). Reporter (real Win hw) proved: VFS reserved open + ns-binding + 3 lock sidecars all COMPLETE; CannotOpen is DOWNSTREAM in the ReservedEmpty bootstrap (pager.rs open_reserved_with_page_buffer_max, block 15960-16038) or connection.rs 12585+ registration. Ordinary opens (single handle) work on Windows; ONLY the reserved-builder path (which keeps TWO overlapping main-file handles: the reservation retained descriptor + the initialize bootstrap handle) fails.

CONFIRMED Win32 DIVERGENCE FROM STOCK (strongest, H1): fsqlite Windows VFS NEVER sets FILE_SHARE_DELETE. windows.rs:34-36 defines only FILE_SHARE_READ(0x1)|WRITE(0x2); WINDOWS_SHARE_READ_WRITE is the ONLY share mode (windows_open_options:298-301, main open 300, lock sidecars open_windows_lock_sidecar:421). Stock SQLite winOpen ALWAYS uses FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE|FILE_SHARE_DELETE. The deliberate omission (comments windows.rs:1334/1401 "prevents pathname replacement between preflight and final handle") is only safe for single-handle opens; the reserved path holds a 2nd overlapping handle, and any bootstrap op the OS treats as needing delete-share against a file already open w/o FILE_SHARE_DELETE fails Windows-only. FIX: add FILE_SHARE_DELETE(0x04) to WINDOWS_SHARE_READ_WRITE (match stock); the TOCTOU the omission guarded is already covered by the from_file identity re-checks (windows.rs 1349/1355/1385, pager 15977), so the mitigation survives.

H2 (per-handle lock): reserved bootstrap acquires EXCLUSIVE via AdvisoryFileLock=LockFileEx (per-HANDLE on Win; fcntl is per-PROCESS on Linux) on -lock-shared (pager 15970, WindowsOsLockFiles try_lock_exclusive windows.rs ~730). If any 2nd same-process handle locks that sidecar, Win conflicts where Linux merges. Weaker (reserve does not pre-create sidecars) — needs instrumentation.

H3 (lower, reporter suggests identity/size fine): file.file_size!=0/identity re-check pager 15977, or write-coordinator open (connection.rs ensure_write_coordinator_service_started 12592) opening main w/ conflicting mode.

LANDABLE NOW regardless of root cause (reporter explicitly asked): make CannotOpen self-diagnosing. ~9 CannotOpen{path} sites in the reserved bootstrap carry NO source (pager 15962/15978/16048/16062; ensure_reserved_recovery_artifacts_absent; validate_reserved_database_artifacts namespace.rs; windows.rs open_reserved_with_expected_identity 1385/1391). Also reopen_reserved_schema_only_bounded_writer returns the SAME CannotOpen for the phase-gate refusal (overloaded, both platforms). FIX: add reason/source to CannotOpen (or a distinct ReservedPhaseRefused variant) so each site self-identifies. This directly unblocks the reporter (0.03s Win loop, 2 hosts).

CI-MATRIX REPRO PLAN: .github/workflows/windows-vfs-interop.yml already runs on windows-latest incl. `cargo test -p fsqlite --features native <test>` (line 107). Add the reporter minimal reproducer as a #[cfg(windows)] test in fsqlite (or fsqlite-vfs) asserting initialize_reserved_schema_only_builder->Ok on a fresh reservation; wire its name into the workflow test list. SEQUENCE: (1) land self-diagnosing CannotOpen so CI names the exact site; (2) apply H1 (FILE_SHARE_DELETE) + re-run; (3) if still red, the named site + H2/H3 bisect. Full analysis: scratchpad/wr... see agent session. NEXT: dropping to WR atomic core the moment connection.rs frees (priority).

title: Gate 0: benchmark artifacts must carry a per-arm executed-work receipt and fail closed on zero
description:
Agreed in Agent Mail (GreenGull proposed, RusticBasin accepted as a Gate 0 requirement) but never filed as a tracker item, and verified NOT implemented in comprehensive_bench.rs as of 2026-07-26 (grep for statements_executed/rows_returned/work receipt: zero hits).

REQUIREMENT
Record a statements-executed and rows-returned counter per measured arm, and FAIL artifact generation when either is zero for an arm that is supposed to have done work.

WHY THIS SPECIFIC SHAPE
bd-i8pt6 is the proof case: mt_oltp's reader loop was 'let _ = stmt.query_with_params(..)' — it constructed a future, dropped it unpolled, and timed that. Every reader number the bench produced measured future construction rather than query execution, and the error had the dangerous sign (made FrankenSQLite look FAST). It was silent under a green compile.

Neither a lane counter nor a fallback counter would have caught it. An executed-work counter would have: the arm executed zero statements and returned zero rows while reporting a throughput number.

SCOPE
- Per-arm counters threaded through the measured region, not the setup region.
- Fail-closed at artifact emission, consistent with the rest of the Gate 0 fail-closed provenance work (dirty source, profile/toolchain mismatch, tracing lane switches, effective durability mismatch).
- A unit test asserting that a zero-work arm refuses to produce an artifact.
- Apply to mt-oltp-bench and mt-mvcc-bench as well, not only comprehensive-bench.

OWNERSHIP
crates/fsqlite-e2e/src/bin/** is RusticBasin's Gate 0 lane. Filed by SagePine so the requirement is tracked rather than living only in mail; not implemented by me to avoid colliding with the in-flight Gate 0 redesign.

RELATED

title: Crash injection harness: SIGKILL + fsync-failure injection at 8 phase boundaries with statistical confidence
description: Build a crash-injection layer that adds the 'crash actively kills the writer at boundary X' axis to the existing harness (1.1). 8 phase boundaries (was 5), each parametrized over 100+ iterations with deterministic seeds. Parent process opens stock C SQLite via rusqlite to verify post-crash state and per-process self-consistency (each caller's own committed writes are readable after restart).
design: Phase boundaries (env var FRANKENSQLITE_CRASH_AT): before-wal-header-write, before-wal-frame-append, after-wal-frame-append-before-fsync, after-fsync-before-publish, between-page-table-rebuild-steps, after-publish-before-checkpoint, mid-checkpoint, after-checkpoint. At each boundary the child process self-SIGKILLs after emitting a 'crash_armed' structured-log line. Parent waits, opens stock C SQLite + integrity_check, opens fsqlite + reads per-process committed-seq from a sidecar log, compares for consistency. Fault-injection layer: optional FUSE shim (via fuser crate) under tests/crash_injection/fault-fuse/ that proxies real-fs operations and can inject EIO on fsync, partial-writes on write, EBUSY on open — configurable per-test. Statistical confidence: target 99.9% reliability (1 in 1000 iterations may show benign timing artifact but zero may show integrity_check failure); achieved via >=1000 iterations per boundary in CI, with confidence interval reported in the test output.
acceptance_criteria: (1) All 8 boundaries implemented and exercised. (2) 1000 iterations per boundary on Linux x86_64 + Linux ARM64 + macOS arm64; zero integrity_check failures, zero half-committed rows visible to a fresh open, zero stuck WAL frames. (3) FUSE fault-injection layer produces EIO on fsync at the appropriate boundary; system recovers correctly on restart. (4) Seeded reproducibility: same --seed produces same sequence of kills. (5) Per-iteration JSONL output is parsed by the parent; statistical confidence interval emitted at end-of-run. (6) Integrated with bd-073kf as 'workload-mix=ddl-occasional --crash-mode random' for the soak (1.10).

Additionally, row_build_ns cannot have been the largest component of the tiny_1col gap, because for that shape the row-build path is skipped entirely.

title: PARITY-B3: Handle NULL IPK values with NewRowid auto-increment fallback
close_reason: Merged into B1 (bd-13b8): NULL handling is integral to the IsNull conditional branch, not a separate code change. Test cases absorbed into B1 acceptance criteria.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# PARITY-B3: Handle NULL IPK values with NewRowid auto-increment fallback

## Context

In SQLite, `INSERT INTO t(id, name) VALUES(NULL, 'test')` where `id` is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
causes an auto-generated rowid — the NULL is treated as "let SQLite pick". This is the standard
auto-increment idiom used by ORMs (Django, SQLAlchemy, ActiveRecord) and most application code.

This is NOT a separate code change from B1/B2 — it's part of the same conditional logic. This
bead exists to document the semantics and ensure the edge case is explicitly tested.

## SQLite Semantics for NULL IPK

Per SQLite documentation (https://sqlite.org/lang_createtable.html#rowid):

> If no ROWID is specified on the insert, or if the specified ROWID has a value of NULL, then an
> appropriate ROWID is created automatically.

So `INSERT VALUES (NULL, 'x')` with IPK should:
1. Detect the NULL in the IPK position
2. Auto-generate a rowid (equivalent to NewRowid)
3. Sync the generated rowid back into the IPK record position

## Implementation

This is handled by the IsNull conditional branch in the B1/B2 fix:

```rust
// Emit IsNull check — if IPK value is NULL, jump to auto-generate
b.emit_op(Opcode::IsNull, ipk_reg, auto_label, 0, P4::None, 0);
// ... non-NULL path (use supplied value) ...
b.resolve_label(auto_label);
b.emit_op(Opcode::NewRowid, cursor, rowid_reg, concurrent_flag, P4::None, 0);
b.emit_op(Opcode::Copy, rowid_reg, ipk_reg, 0, P4::None, 0); // sync back
```

## Additional Edge Cases

1. **AUTOINCREMENT keyword**: `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` adds the constraint that
   rowids never reuse deleted values. This requires reading from `sqlite_sequence` table. For
   now, basic NULL→NewRowid is sufficient; AUTOINCREMENT is a separate enhancement.

2. **Negative IPK values**: SQLite allows negative integers as explicit IPK values. These should
   work with the MustBeInt validation (which allows negatives).

3. **Very large IPK values**: Values near i64::MAX. NewRowid has logic to handle overflow.
   Explicit values should work up to i64::MAX.

4. **Zero as IPK**: `INSERT VALUES (0, 'x')` should use 0 as rowid. Zero is a valid rowid in
   SQLite (though unusual).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `INSERT INTO t VALUES (NULL, 'test') RETURNING id` returns a positive auto-generated integer
- `INSERT INTO t(name) VALUES('test') RETURNING id` returns auto-generated integer (IPK omitted)
- Successive NULL inserts produce incrementing rowids
- Explicit non-NULL IPK values still work (verified by B1)
- No regressions

## Note

This bead is primarily a testing/verification concern. The actual code change is part of B1/B2's
conditional branch. However, this bead ensures the NULL path is explicitly tested and not
accidentally broken.

## Fresh-eyes review: bd-hjkbr.1 commit-phase timing (FuchsiaMink, read-only)

### Finding 1: MINOR — commit_pre_txn_start lost on vtab-sync-failure early return

`commit_pre_txn_start` is set at line 12110 but `record_hot_path_duration(&FSQLITE_COMMIT_PRE_TXN_TIME_NS, commit_pre_txn_start)` only fires at line 12171 — AFTER the vtab-sync-failure early return at line 12129. **Impact:** Low — vtab sync failures are rare and the failure path is not a performance-critical attribution target. But it violates the "closed ledger" principle.

**Fix:** Move the `record_hot_path_duration` call to before each early return, or wrap the entire block in a scope guard.

### Finding 2: OK — hierarchical timer structure is correct

## Pane 1 read-only: smallest safe ceremony step to eliminate first

### The single smallest safe cut

**`execute_precompiled_prepared_insert` at line 6490 calls `ensure_autocommit_txn_with_cx(execution_cx)` which passes `None` for the publication hint, forcing a second `bind_pager_publication()` inside `ensure_autocommit_txn_mode_with_cx` (line ~11610).**

The caller at line 6261-6268 already passes `prebound_publication` from `ensure_schema_unchanged_with_prebound_publication()`. But `execute_precompiled_prepared_insert` discards it — it never passes it to the autocommit begin path.

The `_fast` variant (`execute_precompiled_prepared_insert_fast`, line 6595-6597) already does this correctly: it calls `ensure_autocommit_txn_with_publication_hint(execution_cx, prebound_publication)`.

### Fix
Change line 6490 from:
```rust
let was_auto = self.ensure_autocommit_txn_with_cx(execution_cx)?;
```
to:
```rust
let was_auto = self.ensure_autocommit_txn_with_publication_hint(execution_cx, prebound_publication)?;
```

This eliminates one redundant `bind_pager_publication()` per autocommit prepared INSERT. The publication was already bound at line 6254 and passed through at line 6268.

### Why this is safe
- The `_fast` variant already does exactly this (line 6597).
- `prebound_publication` is a `BoundPagerPublication` which is a snapshot — it cannot go stale between line 6254 and 6490 since no schema changes can occur within the same statement execution.
- `ensure_autocommit_txn_with_publication_hint` is designed to accept an optional pre-bound publication and skip the re-bind when present.

### Expected impact
Eliminates 1 of the 4 per-statement boundary refreshes measured by bd-db300.5.2.2.1 (publication_bind: 1.00/stmt → 0.00/stmt for the fast path). At c1 where synchronization is 95.8% of wall time, this is a direct cut to the ceremony cost.

### What it does NOT fix
The `ensure_autocommit_txn` path also calls `refresh_memdb_if_stale_with_publication()` (line ~11610) which does its own publication bind. That's a separate redundancy — fixing the passed-through hint only eliminates the publication bind inside `ensure_autocommit_txn`, not the memdb staleness check itself.

## bd-hjkbr.3: Smallest Implementation Slice for Fused-Entry (pane 6)

### Evidence basis
A.2 pack: synchronization = 95.8% of c1 wall time (38.3ms of 40ms for 51 ops).
Census (FUSED_ENTRY_TICKET_DESIGN.md §6): 4 of 5 per-stmt phases are collapsible.

### The one redundant phase to remove first

**Target: eliminate the duplicate `bind_pager_publication()` call in `ensure_autocommit_txn`.**

Current flow per prepared INSERT (from census):
```
1. schema_unchanged_check() → bind_pager_publication() [1.00/stmt]
2. ensure_autocommit_txn()  → refresh_memdb_if_stale_with_publication()
                             → bind_pager_publication() [DUPLICATE — 1.00/stmt]
```

The D5.2 fix already passes the publication from `refresh_prepared_schema_state` through to `ensure_autocommit_txn` via `prebound_publication`. But the `ensure_autocommit_txn` path still calls `refresh_memdb_if_stale_with_publication()` which calls `bind_pager_publication()` again — even when the prebound publication is available and identical.

### Exact functions to change

1. **`ensure_autocommit_txn_mode_with_cx` (connection.rs:11889):** When `prebound_publication` is `Some(pub)`, skip the `refresh_memdb_if_stale_with_publication()` call entirely. The prebound publication already proves the memdb is fresh (it was checked 10 lines ago in `refresh_prepared_schema_state`).

2. **Counter to move:** `FSQLITE_PAGER_PUBLICATION_REFRESHES` should drop from ~100 to ~50 for 100 prepared INSERTs (one call eliminated per stmt).

### Why this is safe

Between `refresh_prepared_schema_state` (which binds the publication) and `ensure_autocommit_txn` (which uses it), execution is synchronous within a single connection. No concurrent mutation can change the pager state. The `visible_commit_seq` in the prebound publication is identical to what a fresh `bind_pager_publication` would return.

This is the SAME correctness argument the D5.2 fix used for the FullReload arm — extended to the Noop/Lightweight arms.

### What this does NOT do

- Does NOT implement the full ticket system (that's bd-db300.5.2.2.3)
- Does NOT remove background_status checks (separate phase)
- Does NOT remove commit_refresh (required per-boundary)
- Does NOT change the schema check path

### Expected impact

From ~4 publication binds per stmt → ~3. Saves one `pager.refresh_published_snapshot()` call (involves WAL header read for file-backed). At ~7us per call × 100 stmts = ~700us savings. This is modest (2% of 35ms wall) but it's the narrowest safe slice before the full ticket.

### Verification

```bash
# Same D5.1 proof test — pager_publication_refreshes should drop
cargo test -p fsqlite-core --test prepared_hit_rate_proof -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

## Read-only analysis: Is it safe to skip refresh_memdb_if_stale when prebound_publication is Some?

### Answer: YES, it is already safe and already done.

### Call ordering on the fast INSERT lane

1. **Line 6269:** `ensure_schema_unchanged_with_prebound_publication(&op_cx)` calls `refresh_prepared_schema_state(cx, ...)` (line 5526). This reads the seqlock publication plane, checks MemDB staleness, and may trigger a full reload. Returns `BoundPagerPublication` capturing the publication snapshot at that moment.

2. **Line 6283:** `prebound_publication` passed to `execute_precompiled_prepared_insert()`.

3. **Line 6607 (inside fast path):** `ensure_autocommit_txn_with_publication_hint(execution_cx, prebound_publication)` → line 11895 → `ensure_autocommit_txn_mode_with_cx(mode, cx, prebound_publication)`.

4. **Line 12014:** If `prebound_publication` is `Some`, it's used directly. The `refresh_memdb_if_stale_with_publication()` call at lines 12017/12025 is **skipped**.

### Race window analysis

Between step 1 (prebind at line 6269) and step 4 (use at line 12014), another writer on a different connection could commit, advancing the global `visible_commit_seq`. This would make the prebound publication "stale" in the sense that it doesn't reflect the latest commit.

**This is safe.** The existing code documents this at line 12033-12036:
> "if a writer commits between the bind and `pager.begin`, FCW may over-abort, but it cannot false-clean."

The safety argument:
- The prebound publication captures a **lower bound** on visibility. Using a slightly-stale snapshot means the transaction sees fewer committed pages, not more.
- FCW validation at commit time checks against the **current** commit_index, not the snapshot. A stale snapshot can cause FCW to report a conflict that wouldn't exist with a fresher snapshot (over-abort), but it cannot miss a real conflict (false-clean).
- The MemDB staleness check in `refresh_prepared_schema_state` at step 1 already handled the reload if needed. Between steps 1 and 4, only microseconds elapse (schema validation + parameter binding) — the probability of a meaningful staleness event is negligible, and even if it occurs, the worst case is a conservative abort, not corruption.

### Within one statement execution: no schema race possible

Steps 1-4 execute synchronously on one thread within a single `execute_with_params()` call. No DDL can interleave (DDL requires its own statement execution). The schema_cookie/schema_generation check at lines 2089-2091 guards against DDL that happened *before* this call. No DDL can happen *during* it.

### Conclusion
Using prebound_publication directly at the begin path is safe. It's already the designed fast-lane behavior. The only cost is a marginally stale MVCC snapshot (microseconds), which is handled conservatively by FCW over-abort at commit time.

title: WASM-BROWSER: FrankenSQLite in the Browser via WebAssembly with JS/TS/React/Next.js Bindings

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# WASM-BROWSER Epic: FrankenSQLite in the Browser

## Vision
Make FrankenSQLite the first pure-Rust SQLite reimplementation available in the browser via WebAssembly, with first-class TypeScript bindings, React hooks, and Next.js integration. Unlike sql.js/wa-sqlite/official sqlite-wasm (which compile C SQLite via Emscripten), FrankenSQLite compiles directly from Rust to wasm32-unknown-unknown — yielding smaller binaries, memory safety guarantees, and the unique ability to support concurrent writers in the browser via SharedArrayBuffer + Web Workers.

## Strategic Advantages Over Existing Solutions
1. **Pure Rust → WASM**: No Emscripten toolchain, no C compilation. Direct wasm-bindgen integration.
2. **MVCC Concurrent Writers**: FrankenSQLite's page-level MVCC can be mapped to browser Workers, enabling true concurrent writes — no other browser SQLite can do this.
3. **Zero unsafe code**: Memory safety is a compile-time guarantee, not a testing target.
4. **VFS trait already exists**: The `Vfs`/`VfsFile` trait abstraction means adding OPFS/IndexedDB backends is architecturally clean.
5. **Type-safe TypeScript bindings**: wasm-bindgen generates TypeScript types automatically from Rust types.
6. **Smaller binary**: Rust's wasm32 output is typically 30-50% smaller than Emscripten-compiled C.

## Architecture Overview
```
React/Next.js App
    |
    | useQuery() / useMutation() hooks
    |
@frankensqlite/react (React Context + Hooks)
    |
    | Comlink RPC / postMessage
    |
Web Worker (owns FrankenSQLite WASM instance)
    |
    | wasm-bindgen bridge
    |
fsqlite-wasm (Rust crate → WASM binary)
    |
    | VFS trait dispatch
    |
    ├── MemoryVfs (in-memory, default)
    ├── OpfsVfs (OPFS SyncAccessHandle, primary persistence)
    └── IdbVfs (IndexedDB, fallback persistence)
```

## Persistence Strategy
- **Primary**: OPFS with SyncAccessHandle (Chrome 108+, Safari 16.4+, Firefox 111+) — 3-4x faster than IndexedDB
- **Fallback**: IndexedDB with batch atomic transactions (Chrome 69+, universal)
- **In-memory**: MemoryVfs for ephemeral databases (already implemented)

## Phases
1. **Foundation** (P0): Feature flags, dependency abstraction, wasm32 compilation
2. **WASM Binding Layer** (P0): fsqlite-wasm crate, wasm-bindgen API, npm packaging
3. **Browser Persistence** (P1): OPFS VFS, IndexedDB VFS, Worker architecture
4. **JS/TS SDK** (P1): TypeScript types, async API, streaming results
5. **React/Next.js Integration** (P1): Hooks, Context provider, SSR safety
6. **Concurrent Writers in Browser** (P2): SharedArrayBuffer MVCC, Worker pool
7. **Developer Experience** (P2): CDN, playground, docs, benchmarks
8. **Advanced Features** (P3): CRDT extension, sync protocol, offline-first

## Key Technical Decisions
- Target: `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (not wasm32-wasi) for browser deployment
- Binding: `wasm-bindgen` + `wasm-pack` (industry standard for Rust→WASM)
- Worker pattern: Dedicated Worker per connection (not SharedWorker) initially
- Persistence: OPFS primary, IDB fallback (following Notion/PowerSync patterns)
- Multi-tab: Web Locks API for coordination (no SharedArrayBuffer requirement for basic usage)
- Async bridge: Native sync access handles on OPFS (no Asyncify needed)

## Existing Codebase Compatibility Analysis
- MemoryVfs: Already wasm-compatible
- Parser/AST/Planner/VDBE: Pure Rust, no OS deps — compile directly
- VFS trait: Trait-based abstraction ready for new implementations
- Dependencies needing wasm gates: parking_lot, nix, crossbeam-epoch, crossbeam-deque, asupersync
- Dependencies that compile fine: serde, blake3, xxhash-rust, chacha20poly1305, thiserror, tracing, smallvec

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SQLite has a backward-compat "misfeature" (DQS): a double-quoted token that does
not resolve to any identifier is silently treated as a STRING LITERAL.
FrankenSQLite instead raises an error.

Repro (FrankenSQLite errors; rusqlite returns the string):
```sql
CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b TEXT);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,'x'),(2,'y');
SELECT "no_such" FROM t;   -- "no_such" is not a column
```
frank => ERROR (no such column)
csql  => 'no_such' for every row (DQS string fallback)

Note: this is a LOW-priority divergence. SQLite's own docs discourage relying on
DQS and provide SQLITE_DQS to disable it; frank's stricter behavior is arguably
preferable. But default SQLite (and the rusqlite build used as the oracle) still
accept it, so for strict conformance frank would need to mirror it (likely gated
by a DQS-compat flag). When "b" IS a column, frank correctly treats `"b"` as a
column reference (that case passes).

Fix (if desired): in name resolution, when a double-quoted identifier matches no
column/table, fall back to treating it as a TEXT literal (optionally behind a
DQS-compatibility setting), matching default SQLite.

Test (currently #[ignore]d on this bead):
crates/fsqlite-e2e/tests/identifier_quoting_oracle_e2e.rs::quoting_double_quoted_string_fallback

title: .fsqlite-history on-disk format: append-only chained 64B records + optional sparse index sidecar
description: Define a stable, durable, crash-safe on-disk record format for the commit-snapshot log. Versioned, page-aligned for future growth, hash-chained for tear detection, optional sparse-index sidecar for fast bisect.
design: On-disk format for the per-database commit-snapshot log at <db_path>.fsqlite-history: fixed-size 64-byte records, little-endian, page-aligned (4096-byte slots reserved per record for future growth — only the first 64 bytes are populated by v1). Record layout v1: { commit_seq: u64, root_page: u64 (NOT u32 — future-proof for >4G-page databases), wall_ts_unix_nanos: u64, prev_record_blake3_64: u64 (first 64 bits of blake3 of the previous record, anchoring the chain), this_record_blake3_64: u64, schema_epoch: u64, flags: u32 (bit 0 = checkpoint_anchor; remaining bits reserved), record_version: u16, padding: u16, reserved: [u8; 8] }. Append protocol: open, seek to end, write, fdatasync (FullDurable per bd-qkeae). Chain validation algorithm: read records in reverse from tail; for each, verify this_record_blake3_64 == blake3(record[0..56])[..8]; if mismatch, declare the record torn and truncate to the previous valid record (this handles partial writes). Optional sparse index sidecar at <db>.fsqlite-history-idx — { commit_seq, byte_offset } pairs sampled every 1024 records — enables O(log N) bisect without scanning the full log; rebuilt on demand if missing.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Format documented in docs/design/fsqlite-history-format.md with hex dump of a sample record. (2) Round-trip serde tests: 10,000 random records survive write -> fsync -> read -> verify. (3) Crash-mid-append safety: proptest harness writes a record, simulates SIGKILL at every byte offset, verifies post-restart chain validation truncates exactly to the last fully-written record. (4) Byte-for-byte stable across endianness (cross-test from x86_64 -> aarch64 produces bitwise-identical files). (5) Sparse index sidecar reduces bisect from O(N) to O(log N) on a 10M-record corpus (benchmark in tests/perf/history_bisect_bench.rs). (6) Forward-compatibility: a v1 reader opening a hypothetical v2-augmented record (extra bytes in the 4096-byte slot) ignores them and reads the v1 fields correctly.
notes: u64 root_page is deliberately wider than C SQLite's u32; future scaling to >4G pages costs nothing in this format. The 4096-byte slot reservation is page-aligned so future field additions do not require a migration.
close_reason: Implemented and proven: durable lineage-bound 4096-byte history slots, crash-tail recovery, forward-compatible v1 decoding, full-image little-endian golden/cross-target proof, durable sparse index, and true cold O(log N) on-disk lookup with tail-bound per-entry checksums and complete VFS read budgets. Strict remote 16/16 tests and all-target clippy -D warnings pass.

comments.text:
# §4.19.2 Networking Stack: TLS + HTTP/2 Limits + VirtualTcp for Lab

## Spec Reference
COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md lines 5495–5527 (§4.19.6)

## Overview
When remote effects are enabled, FrankenSQLite MUST use asupersync's cancel-safe
network stack (TCP + TLS + HTTP/2) so that cancellation is not a "drop the future"
footgun, deadlines/budgets bound network I/O, and transport behavior is deterministic
in lab mode.

## Production Transport Requirements

### TLS by Default (Required)
- Remote effects over the network SHOULD use TLS via **rustls** (NOT openssl).
- Plaintext transport is permitted ONLY when explicitly configured for local development.
- Plaintext MUST be gated by an explicit capability/config knob (not silent fallback).

### Handshake + Protocol Timeouts (Required)
- Remote handshakes MUST be budgeted and time-bounded (deadline or explicit timeouts).
- Protocol parsing MUST also be time-bounded.
- No unbounded blocking on handshake or protocol negotiation.

### HTTP/2 Hard Limits (Normative, if HTTP/2 is used)
| Parameter                  | Value     | Notes                              |
|----------------------------|----------:|-----------------------------------:|
| max_concurrent_streams     | 256       | default                            |
| max_header_list_size       | 65536     | 64 KiB                            |
| continuation_timeout_ms    | 5000      | 5 seconds                         |
| header_fragment_cap        | 262144    | 256 KiB absolute cap              |

These prevent stream exhaustion and header-compression bombs from turning tiered
storage into a DoS vector.

### Message Size Caps (Required)
- Any remote RPC framing MUST enforce max send/recv sizes.
- Default: 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes).
- Larger messages MUST be rejected deterministically.

## Deterministic Network Testing Requirements

### VirtualTcp (Required for Lab)
- In lab tests, remote transport MUST be swappable to `VirtualTcp`.
- VirtualTcp is in-memory, deterministic, no kernel sockets.
- Required to make replication and tiered-storage behaviors reproducible.
- DPOR-explorable under LabRuntime.

### Drop/Reorder/Corrupt Network Shim (Required for Lab)
- Harness MUST provide a "drop/reorder/corrupt" virtual network shim.
- Simulates lossy replication while preserving deterministic replay.
- Loss patterns derive from the lab seed and are trace-visible.

## Unit Test Specifications

### T1: tls_by_default
Create remote transport with default config. Verify TLS (rustls) is enabled, not plaintext.

### T2: plaintext_requires_explicit_config
Attempt plaintext transport without explicit config knob. Verify refusal.
Then set explicit plaintext knob and verify it works.

### T3: handshake_timeout_enforced
Set handshake timeout to 10ms. Connect to a non-responding mock endpoint.
Verify timeout fires within bounded time.

### T4: http2_max_concurrent_streams_enforced
Configure HTTP/2 with max_concurrent_streams=256. Attempt 300 concurrent streams.
Verify excess streams are rejected/queued.

### T5: http2_header_size_limit
Send request with headers exceeding 64 KiB. Verify rejection per max_header_list_size.

### T6: message_size_cap_enforced
Send RPC message exceeding 4 MiB. Verify deterministic rejection.

### T7: virtual_tcp_deterministic
Run same network scenario twice with same seed under LabRuntime + VirtualTcp.
Verify identical byte sequences and timing.

### T8: drop_reorder_corrupt_shim
Configure virtual network shim with known seed. Inject drops/reorders/corruptions.
Verify patterns are deterministic across replays and trace-visible.

### T9: continuation_timeout_enforced
Send HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame sequence and delay beyond 5s.
Verify connection is terminated per continuation_timeout_ms.

## Dependencies
- §4.19 (remote effects parent), §4.17.1 (PRAGMA config), LabRuntime (§4.1),
  asupersync net stack, rustls

title: PERF/DESIGN-P1: move physical page write outside the concurrent_registry lock (validate+alloc under lock → I/O outside → short publish re-acquire)
description: DESIGN BEAD — implementation belongs to/with RusticBasin's commit-path lane; review requested (platform-perf thread 4540; DustyOrchid asked for async-contract review of the split's cancellation/obligation implications). Evidence: complete 1-128 matrix (highwriter-full-20260728T0645Z): F throughput declines 150k->52k wps 8->128 writers while C floors at 12.5k; p95 txn latency 10x jump 16->32 writers at flat throughput = convoying at the guard held across validate->physical write->publish (connection.rs:39285 commit_registry_guard, held through plan_concurrent_commit_with_registry -> txn.commit -> publish, four explicit drop sites). Design shape (native-commit-protocol precedent, README FSYNC_1/FSYNC_2 discipline): under the lock do FCW/SSI validate + commit_seq allocation + logical reservation; release; perform pager physical write + WAL append outside; re-acquire briefly for publication (visibility flip + registry cleanup); on I/O failure the reserved seq must abort cleanly (obligation two-phase — DustyOrchid's lens). Hazards to design around (from the guard's own comment): two concurrent autocommit writers must not both physically write the same freshly-allocated EOF page — page allocation must move INTO the locked reservation phase or use per-writer extents. GATES: land only after RegistryCommitLockMetrics decomposes hold into validate/IO/publish (shim queued with lease holder), with 1-128 A/B + zero-regression at 1-8 writers, ledger review. Expected: restores most of the 150k peak at high N.

comments.text: ACCEPTANCE CONSTRAINTS (RusticBasin first contract review, platform-perf msgs 4541+4543 — design must satisfy ALL before code is admitted): (1) pre-I/O phase produces an owned Drop-safe cleanup receipt covering every registry slot/page alloc/MVCC marker/page lock/certificate interval/synthetic page-1 state established under the first acquisition — cancellation before I/O restores exactly. (2) A dropped I/O future is NOT proof zero bytes hit storage — once an append may have started, retain completion evidence and reconcile the exact WAL generation/frame interval before publish OR abort; never release the reservation just because the wrapper future dropped. (3) Publish re-acquire needs an explicit validation contract: what can change while unlocked, how page-number/alloc ownership stays collision-free, whether the WAL interval is reserved, which conflict/SSI checks repeat after re-acquisition. (4) Publication wins are monotonic: once durable commit is authorized, cancellation cannot become rollback — settle as published or poison admission until reconciliation reports; abort only if the exact interval is proven uncommitted. (5) No transaction-owner borrow crosses the pager await (SharedTxnPageIo audit found this drop hole) — RAII claim before await, synchronous return on Drop, fixed-size mutation receipt for MVCC/page-1 pre-states. (6) Outer Connection ownership needs a lease too: six direct-B-tree callers take active_txn out before awaiting, three pending-run flushers also take buffered work — neither may strand on cancellation. (7) No new global writer serialization: short validate/reserve window, unlocked I/O, short reconcile/publish window, concurrent-mode default stays ON. (8) Telemetry must separate initial lock wait/hold, validate+reserve, unlocked I/O, re-acquire wait/hold, revalidation/rebase, publish, reconciliation — plus per-phase attribution (validation vs I/O vs publish) in the keeper receipt to prove the bottleneck moved rather than hid. STATUS: implementation queued behind RusticBasin's green core checkpoint on the cancellation/admission slice; they will review the design text against these constraints before code.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DESIGN-OF-RECORD v2 (WildFrog, 2026-07-28, supersedes the naive three-phase sketch; incorporates the 8 acceptance constraints AND the 4549 irrevocable-marker audit — this is the text submitted for RusticBasin review):

CORE CORRECTNESS FACT (from the 4549 audit; governs everything): pager txn.commit() is ALREADY the irrevocable stock-WAL commit boundary — it writes the final db_size!=0 marker, publishes WAL/page planes, decrements pager activity. Crash after marker but before ConcurrentRegistry/CommitIndex publication recovers the change AS COMMITTED. Therefore the design is NOT unlock->commit->reacquire->revalidate. ALL semantic validation and ordering authority moves BEFORE the marker; post-marker work is publication-only and monotonic.

PROTOCOL (per 4549's minimum-correct, restated as the implementable spec):
P0 FREEZE: atomically claim pager txn + outer session into an owned lease (Drop-safe). Binds: DB namespace, nonwrapping reservation generation, full TxnToken, schema/snapshot/read-write witness digest, page/freelist/EOF/allocation claims. All mutators reject after freeze. (Kills the session_id/TxnId ABA hazard: operational lookup today is by recyclable ids and missing sessions only warn.)
P1 RESERVE (short registry hold #1): ALL semantic validation (SSI/FCW, page-set conflicts vs later validators, EOF/freelist/page-1) + install an immutable reservation/order ticket visible to later validators. This is the ONLY semantic decision point. If a second revalidation is ever desired it happens before certificate/marker, never after.
P2 PHYSICAL (NO registry lock): pager preparation, queue/batch, WAL append. Entering P2 requires a live exact outer reservation for every group member — no member may be admitted to a physical batch unauthorized. A dropped I/O future is NOT evidence of zero bytes durable: once append may have started, the obligation holds completion evidence and reconciles the exact WAL generation/frame interval before publish OR abort (InDoubt until proven).
P3 CERTIFY: one authoritative certificate/member order drives pager visibility, CommitIndex, SSI history, stable clock, and evidence. Waiter-callback wake order is explicitly NOT authoritative (today it can be reversed).
P4 PUBLISH (short registry hold #2, masked DB-root owner): idempotently publish the ENTIRE authorized group in certificate order, release exact claims (generation+token checked — stale receipt = zero mutation + fence), then complete waiters. Cancellation changes delivery only, never outcome. Missing/mismatched ownership fences new begins/commits for reconciliation; never ordinary rollback.
P5 RECONCILE: typed physical outcome required — pager commit Result<()> today cannot distinguish pre-durable failure from post-durable completion error (tests deliberately Err after a durable epoch; core can misclassify as rollback). New enum: PreDurableFailed | DurableThenFailed{interval} | Durable. InDoubt retained until frame-interval/marker/cert reconciliation proves Committed or NotCommitted. Checkpoint waits for unresolved owners and consumes only an authorized prefix (today checkpoint gates only on pager activity and can copy an already-marked group during an outer-publication gap).

STAGED ROLLOUT (each stage independently landable + gated, no behavior cliff):
S1 typed physical outcome + exact-identity receipts (generation+token+digest) — pure correctness hardening, zero perf intent, unblocks everything; overlaps RusticBasin's mutation-receipt work, THEIRS by lease.
S2 freeze/lease + P1 ticket while I/O STAYS inside the guard — no perf change expected; proves the protocol under the full deterministic matrix.
S3 move physical I/O outside (P2) with singleton groups — the perf lever; expected to cut mean hold from 0.7-7ms to the validate+publish sum (target <100us) and lift 64-128w throughput toward the separate-tables ceiling (~2-3x at 64w).
S4 group certify/publish (merges bd-6a8a5 group-commit into P3/P4 naturally).

DETERMINISTIC TEST MATRIX (all required before S3 ships; from 4549): registry demonstrably free while A pauses post-reservation with disjoint B progressing; same-page/EOF B claimed-or-rejected pre-WAL; stale-receipt/ABA zero-mutation; freeze rejects all mutators; late SSI edge matrix; reversed waiter order + cancelled first waiter; crash/fault at reserve/cert/partial-frames/marker/outer-publish; autocommit + explicit-COMMIT cancellation; checkpoint at every boundary; retry exactly-once; page1/freelist/EOF/schema mutations; 1..128 disjoint writers with concurrent mode default-on. Existing interleaved keeper/SHA gate preserved.

TELEMETRY (extends the landed RegistryCommitLockMetrics): initial wait | validate+reserve hold | unlocked pager phase A | queue/batch wait | WAL reserved/cert/frame-sync | reacquire wait | exact group publish hold | reconciliation | cancellation/InDoubt counts | group size + overlap/EOF conflicts. Keeper receipt must show WHERE recovered time came from (phase attribution), not just total.

EVIDENCE BASELINE (to beat): mean hold 713-2340us @64w, 2436-6949us @128w, max 60ms; F p50 declines 150k->52k wps 8->128w while separate-tables shows the ~80% registry share. Keeper = same 1-128 matrix, all arms CI-gated FASTER-or-equal, hold p50 <100us at 64w, zero correctness-gate diffs.

OWNERSHIP: S1 belongs to RusticBasin's current correctness slice (their SharedTxnPageIo/mutation-receipt lane, connection.rs+vdbe leased). S2-S4 implementation assignment decided at their checkpoint; my lane contributes begin_concurrent.rs-side structures (lease/ticket types, metrics) which are lease-clear today but will NOT start until this design text is approved.

comments.text:
DESIGN-OF-RECORD v2 ADDENDUM (2026-07-28, from EmeraldPrairie's read-only boundary audit, thread msg 4560 — NORMATIVE, folds into the P0-P5 spec):
1. TxnBoundaryReceipt state machine is the authoritative phase model: PreDurable -> InDoubt -> DurableNeedsPublication -> Terminal{Committed,RolledBack}. NotCommitted verdicts stay PreDurable through cleanup; FullRollback discovering a prior dropped commit's marker transitions THROUGH DurableNeedsPublication (commit wins). Group queue (not caller futures) retains pending publication/completion tokens.
2. PROVEN LIVE DEFECT motivating S1a, now beaded separately: bd-zvxay (P1) — execute_commit_with_cx publishes only on commit_res.is_ok() while the group callback can Err after durable epoch; Result<()> conflates NotCommitted/InDoubt/DurableNeedsPublication TODAY.
3. finalize_prepared_session_state (begin_concurrent.rs ~1829-1853) warn-and-continue on missing session is incompatible with stale-receipt safety — publication API must require generation+TxnToken+digest+exact certificate membership, be idempotent (AlreadyPublished(same receipt)), and fence on mismatch with zero mutation.
4. ORDER AUTHORITY: ParallelWalDurabilityReceipt.member_commit_seqs is the certificate. Either P1 reserves those exact seqs (then stable-frontier needs a Pending/Committed/Aborted ordered ledger so aborted holes neither wedge nor skip) or the combiner assigns and P1 tolerates/reconciles. NEVER allocate a second Connection seq after pager durability (current behavior).
5. Checkpoint fence: active_transactions decrements before Phase-C hook + CommitIndex publication happens later still — checkpoint must block on (or consume only a prefix excluding) unresolved InDoubt and authorized-but-outer-unpublished receipts, incl. the group-queue InDoubt preflight check that is missing today.
6. Drop discipline: never awaits/spawns/aborts/recycles/publishes/interprets dropped I/O as zero writes; only republish/hand off the exact record + proven-synchronous PreDurable withdrawal + poison/fence on identity collision. Transaction::drop = 'request rollback iff NotCommitted'.
7. STAGE REFINEMENT: S1 splits into S1a (typed pager outcome + DB-root exact receipt + checkpoint fence) and S1b (connection commit/full-rollback resumable settlement, incl. idempotent first-COMMIT skipping symmetric with first-ROLLBACK). LabRuntime pause/cancel gate list per msg 4560 is the S2/S3 acceptance matrix. No unlocked-I/O patch lands before S1 gates are green.
Review state: RusticBasin ack'd P0-P5/S1-S4 as the review shape (4557); S2/S3 remain design-only until their explicit lease/window decision.

comments.text: INDEPENDENT S1a REVIEW 2026-07-29 (RusticBasin/Sol-max, read-only): BLOCK confirmed. Existing ParallelWalDurableCertificateRecord plus the original WAL generation, exact closed frame interval, commit marker, and digest can prove physical authorization; no second on-disk receipt is required for current correctness. The missing contract is an immutable typed outcome retained through all layers: PreDurableFailed with exact NeverAccepted/NotCommitted proof, InDoubt with exact attempt, DurableNeedsPublication with exact member receipt and stage, then Durable only after pager Phase C plus CommitIndex/SSI/session/schema/stable-clock publication. Vfs terminal Error is never NotCommitted proof. Required owner is a strongly retained DatabaseCommitRoot keyed by file identity plus database/WAL generation, with nonterminal attempt map, ABA-safe claim version and lease nonce, stale queue rejection, and refusal of last-close/queue removal/checkpoint/reset/VACUUM while obligations remain. Reconcile against the retained original generation, never the backend current generation. Move all Phase-C inputs and PreparedConcurrentCommit publication progress into idempotent root-owned continuations before physical admission. SimpleTransaction Drop may roll back only proven NotCommitted; InDoubt transfers ownership; durable states never roll back. Dependency order remains VFS source-admission receipts, neutral proof types, exact WAL reconciliation, persistent root, pager publication, generation fences, pending semantic reservations, resumable outer publication, Connection typed-outcome consumption, then unlocked-I/O performance work. Acceptance must fault/drop/reopen at every boundary including two-member cancellation and stable-sequence holes.

comments.text:
## Task: Recovery demo — WAL corruption during transaction (WAL-FEC self-healing)

### What
Demonstrate WAL-FEC: corrupt WAL frames from an in-flight transaction, FrankenSQLite recovers them using .wal-fec repair symbols.

### Test Flow
1. Start with golden copy
2. Open database, begin a large transaction (insert 1000 rows)
3. COMMIT (creates WAL frames)
4. Generate .wal-fec sidecar from the WAL
5. Corrupt specific WAL frames (e.g., frames 5-8 of the commit group)
6. **C SQLite attempt**: Reopen database. WAL replay fails or partially succeeds. Some committed rows are lost. Database in inconsistent state.
7. **FrankenSQLite attempt**: Detects frame corruption via per-frame checksums → consults .wal-fec → RaptorQ decode recovers corrupted frames → WAL replay succeeds → all 1000 rows present.
8. Verify all rows present in recovered database

### Why WAL Corruption Is Especially Dangerous
WAL corruption is the worst-case scenario for C SQLite:
- If corruption happens before checkpoint, the corrupted frames contain committed data that hasn't been written to the main database yet
- Checkpointing corrupted WAL can SPREAD corruption to the main database
- Without FEC, the only option is to discard the corrupted frames (data loss)

### Simulating Power Failure
This demo also simulates a common real-world scenario: power loss during WAL checkpoint. The WAL is partially written, some frames are torn:
```
CorruptionPattern::WalFrameCorrupt {
    frame_numbers: vec![5, 6, 7, 8],
    seed: 42,
}
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- WAL frames successfully corrupted
- C SQLite loses committed data from corrupted frames
- FrankenSQLite recovers all committed data via WAL-FEC
- Recovered database contains all 1000 rows
- Row-level verification against expected data

title: BENCH-P0: mt_oltp reader loop timed future construction, not query execution
description:
Found during the bd-ybde3 async migration.

crates/fsqlite-e2e/src/bin/mt_oltp_bench.rs:325 -- the reader benchmark's hot
loop was:

    let _ = stmt.query_with_params(...);   // no block_on, no await

Because the engine is now async, that constructs a future, drops it unpolled,
and TIMES THAT. No query ran. Every FrankenSQLite reader throughput and latency
number mt-oltp-bench has produced since the async migration measured future
construction rather than query execution.

DIRECTION OF ERROR IS THE DANGEROUS ONE: it makes FrankenSQLite look
artificially FAST on the reader arm. Contrast bd-fd1ra (dropped bench PRAGMAs),
which made FrankenSQLite look slow by leaving it unconfigured. Both are silent
under a green compile because `let _ =` suppresses #[must_use].

FIXED: the call is now driven through fsqlite_e2e::block_on. The PRAGMA
appliers in the same file were already correctly wrapped, so only the query
loop was affected.

ACTION REQUIRED
  - Re-run and re-publish any mt_oltp reader numbers. Treat prior reader
    figures from this bench as void, not merely stale.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Problem (from C SQLite analysis: vdbeaux.c Mem struct)
C SQLite stores register values as a C union: i64, double, or char* pointer with manual lifecycle. Zero atomic operations. Cost: 0 cycles per value move.

FrankenSQLite uses SqliteValue enum with Arc<> for Text/Blob. Every clone = atomic fetch_add (5ns). Every drop = atomic fetch_sub (5ns). For a 5-column row: 10+ atomic operations = 50+ ns pure refcounting overhead.

## Solution: Epoch-scoped borrowed values in the register file
Instead of SqliteValue owning its data via Arc, make register values BORROW from the source (page buffer, literal pool, or scratch arena). Only upgrade to owned when the value must outlive the current statement.

Pattern: `RegisterValue` = union of { i64, f64, &[u8] borrowed from page, SmallText inline }. No Arc at all in the hot path. Values are valid for the duration of one opcode's execution (like C SQLite's Mem).

## C SQLite Reference: vdbeaux.c Mem struct
- Mem.u.i (integer), Mem.u.r (float), Mem.u.s.z (string pointer)
- Mem.zMalloc: reusable heap buffer for strings that need to persist
- NO reference counting — Mem owns its buffer directly

## Expected Impact: -50 cycles per row (eliminate 10+ atomic ops)
For 10K rows: saves ~0.5 ms

## Risk: Major refactor — SqliteValue is used throughout the codebase
Mitigation: Introduce RegisterValue ALONGSIDE SqliteValue. Convert only in the VDBE hot path. External API continues to use SqliteValue (with Arc for safety).

comments.author: SageBluff
comments.text:
NO-GO — data-backed (SageBluff, 2026-08-17). Full entry in docs/progress/perf-negative-results.md (2026-08-17 header).

Measured (release-perf, Threadripper fleet box, target-cpu=native, A/A+A/B interleaved): Arc atomic refcounting is 1.4-1.7% of a wide SELECT (1773 ns/row) and ~3.4% of an UPDATE/DELETE full-scan (522 ns/row) — BELOW the fleet's ~10% measurement floor and ~10x short of the bead's 15% goal. Arc-free int-only control = 1021 ns/row proves the per-row cost is decode + async-per-row machinery + result mechanics, NOT refcounting. One atomic pair ~8 ns; malloc/free dominates the value lifecycle and REMAINS after de-Arc'ing (de-Arc to Box/Vec would ADD a deep copy = regression).

Feasibility: the borrowed RegisterValue<'a> design is INFEASIBLE in safe Rust — VdbeEngine owns both `registers` and the StorageCursor.payload_buf it would borrow (self-referential), borrowed regs dangle on cursor.Next, ~285 register sites force VdbeEngine<'a> across a 38K-line file; Rc ruled out (Send-bound). Already captured ~90% of C-SQLite's zero-atomic Mem win via inline SmallText SSO + lazy OnceLock<Arc> + move-based ResultRow.

Confirms + strengthens the 2026-04-01 bd-b3yw2 deferral (which already deferred the RegisterValue type as low-ROI). Redirect Track S to the decode + async-per-row bridge cost (~333 ns/row + ~700 ns/statement per ledger) where the 1021 ns/row Arc-free floor shows the real headroom.

EPIC NOTE: bd-i9sov is a Track-S sub-item of bd-e1hty (EPIC: C-SQLite Parity, 5 structural changes) with a benchmark-gate dependent bd-z4zl7. This NO-GO closes the register-file structural change specifically; the epic's other 4 structural levers + the redirect target are unaffected. Operator to decide the epic's framing.

comments.text:
## Goal
The 2026-04-19 gap analysis identified UPDATE/DELETE-100 microbench at ~12x slower than C SQLite (down from 354x / 369x after OPT wave). Residual is "cumulative per-statement ceremony": compile-cache lookup, plan-cache probe, direct-simple gate, cursor construction, concurrent-mode probe, Cx checkpoint, page probe.

## Audit surface (in order of suspected weight)
- `execute_prepared_with_params_after_background_status` (was 0.48% self-time)
- `execute_prepared_direct_simple_insert` (was 4.24% self-time)
- `begin_pager_txn_with_busy_timeout` — per-statement txn setup
- `plan_cache_probe` / `compile_cache_lookup`
- `concurrent_mode_probe`
- `Cx checkpoint` pointer chasing

## Approach
1. samply flamegraph on `update-100-rows-update-10` workload; rank ceremony frames by self-time.
2. Identify the LARGEST ceremony frame. Peel one layer.
3. Candidate levers:
   - Cache the "fast-path eligibility" decision on PreparedStatement (eligibility doesn't change across calls unless schema changes).
   - Skip `reload_memdb_from_txn` on strict-no-fallback path when schema cookie unchanged (already done in OPT-B2; verify coverage).
   - Inline `execute_prepared_with_params_after_background_status` at top of hot dispatch when bound_params are empty.
   - Pre-compute the concurrent-mode branch at PreparedStatement time (avoid per-call probe).

## Measurement
- Before/after `update-100-rows-update-10` scenario from comprehensive-bench.
- Target: reduce residual ratio from ~12x to ≤4x.
- Property test: conformance oracle must stay green.

## Non-goals
- NOT a prepared-statement cache rewrite (that is W5-3-unrelated and out of scope).
- NOT changing the Connection API surface.

title: PERF-P2: COUNT(*)/SUM WHERE a IN (list) does not seek a composite (a,b) index (only single-column)
description: The aggregate IN-list seek (index_integer_in_list_target + emit_aggregate_index_value_seek) requires a SINGLE-column index because its probe [value, i64::MIN] uses i64::MIN as the rowid floor. Against a composite (a,b) index the second probe field lines up with column b, and a NULL b (which sorts BEFORE i64::MIN in index order) would be SKIPPED by SeekGE — dropping a=value,b=NULL rows. To seek a composite index's leading column correctly, use a 1-field PREFIX probe [value] (SeekGE anchors at the first a=value entry regardless of b, including NULLs) and keep the Column-0-only run stop. Gate: leading column INTEGER affinity + ascending. Byte-exactness: same rows as the scan. Value: common — a table with only a composite (a,b) index and no redundant idx_a currently full-scans a=IN(list); SQLite uses the composite index. Sibling of the just-shipped single-column-shadow fix (find idx_a even when idx_ab is listed first).
acceptance_criteria: 1) COUNT(*) and SUM over WHERE a IN (...) can seek the leading column of an ascending composite (a,b) index with a one-field prefix probe, including a=value rows whose trailing b is NULL. 2) Oracle tests match C SQLite for duplicate IN values, empty/no-match lists, NULL and mixed trailing values, multiple matching rows, and both aggregates without double counting. 3) Bytecode/EQP proof shows bounded index seeks with a column-0 run stop and no table/full-index rewind; unsupported affinity, collation, direction, and index shapes fall back to the existing correct scan. 4) A reproducible benchmark demonstrates the retained win and the relevant conformance, fmt, clippy, and workspace test gates pass.

title: 5G.2: Fire BEFORE triggers on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
description: When executing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, check if BEFORE triggers exist for the target table and event type. For each matching trigger: (1) set up OLD/NEW pseudo-tables with the affected row, (2) evaluate the WHEN clause if present, (3) if WHEN is true or absent, execute the trigger body statements sequentially. BEFORE triggers fire before the actual DML operation. If a trigger body raises an error or executes RAISE(ABORT/ROLLBACK/FAIL), the DML should fail accordingly. title: octet_length numeric values ignore database UTF-16 encoding

FULL FIX PLAN (investigated by SilentRobin; blocked for a CONSISTENT fix on connection.rs, held+queued by IvoryFortress until ~03:06). Three sites all render numeric/text length in UTF-8, ignoring the DB text_encoding:
