title: CONCURRENT-SCALING-P1: separate-tables write scaling collapses under disk contention (F 8w ~30-53k wps vs README 1022k); F-specific commit-path disk I/O (certificate sidecar open/close + WAL) is the bottleneck, not hardware

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: WhiteDeer/Opus 2026-07-23 EVIDENCE (mt-mvcc-bench at HEAD, release-perf, /data/tmp ext4 shared host, load 6-11 with competing builds). SEPARATE-TABLES (250 rows/thread, no page contention — each writer owns its table but ALL share one .db/WAL/group-commit-queue): README claims 1w 0.42x / 2w 1.51x / 4w 7.66x / 8w 40.99x (F 264k->1022k wps on a quiet dedicated host). My HEAD runs: Run#1 1w 2.58x/2w 2.03x/4w 2.08x/8w 3.00x (F 23k->29k wps, ~FLAT); Run#2 (iters=5, quieter) 8w 3.33x (F 53k). SHARED-TABLE (1000 rows/thread): README 8w 3.42x, mine 8w 3.73x (CLOSE). KEY DISCRIMINATOR (rules out pure slow-hardware): at 8w separate-tables my C=15.9k wps is only ~1.5x below README C=24k, while my F=30-53k is ~20-35x below README F=1022k. If the disk were uniformly 20x slower, C would be 20x slower too — it isn't. So the collapse is F-SPECIFIC: F's shared per-commit disk I/O serializes ALL writers through the group-commit flusher regardless of separate tables. Prime suspect: the certificate-sidecar (wal_adapter.rs) does 2 file OPEN/CLOSE + backward-scan read + append PER COMMIT inside the flush critical section — metadata-heavy ops that are cheap on a fast quiet disk (README) but dominate on a contended ext4, so parallelism collapses 40x->3x. This RE-ELEVATES the sidecar/commit-path lever (flagged marginal in the bd-6hgad reject) to THE concurrent-writer scaling lever: a persistent sidecar file handle (avoid per-commit open/close) + cached authorized-certificate read (preserve cross-process reconcile_authorized_seed) would make F's scaling robust to disk speed. CANNOT yet separate 'regression since README' from 'environment' without the README's exact host — but the C-vs-F asymmetry strongly implicates F's commit-path I/O. ALSO: README's 40.99x is a best-case quiet-fast-disk number; it should be caveated as disk-speed-sensitive. Preflight ConcurrentCommitPathDiskIO=allowed. NEXT: profile the flush critical section's sidecar vs WAL-append vs fsync time under the mt-mvcc separate-tables 8w shape; if sidecar open/close dominates, implement the persistent-handle + read-cache lever with same-worker A/B on a quiet host. concurrent_mode stays true.

FrankenSQLite does a per-operation FILE-OPEN STORM that C SQLite lacks: main DB reopened 270x, -wal 147x, -fsqlite-ns-use 95x, -fsqlite-ns-gate 95x, -wal-cert (certificate sidecar) 31x (843 total openat). The -fsqlite-ns-gate/-ns-use files are cross-process MVCC namespace-coordination LOCK files (crates/fsqlite-vfs/src/namespace.rs, NamespaceOpenIntent::begin opens BOTH gate+use via open_secure_lock_file); -wal-cert is the durable-certificate sidecar (wal_adapter.rs). Every openat/close is a metadata syscall — negligible on a quiet fast disk (README host => 40.99x scaling) but under disk contention these serialize and dominate the shared commit path, so ALL writers block on file metadata ops regardless of separate tables => parallelism collapses 40x->3x. The ~95 ns-gate/ns-use opens for 8 threads (~12/thread) suggests namespace admission re-runs per-transaction or per-generation-check, not once per connection — a possible inefficiency to investigate. LEVER (broader than the sidecar alone): hold PERSISTENT file handles for the coordination (gate/use) + certificate sidecar files across commits instead of open/close per operation; and cache the authorized-certificate read (preserving cross-process reconcile_authorized_seed) — CORRECTNESS-SENSITIVE (these are cross-process locking/durability primitives; the gate open may BE the lock acquisition). NEXT (needs quiet host + rebuild): (1) attribute the flush-critical-section time among ns-gate/ns-use/wal-cert/wal-append via added timing; (2) determine if ns admission is over-invoked (per-txn vs per-conn); (3) implement persistent handles with same-worker A/B on a quiet host. This is THE concurrent-writer scaling lever under realistic disk conditions and reframes the sidecar as high-value (not marginal). concurrent_mode stays true.

The DB/WAL re-open volume dominates — FrankenSQLite's VFS/pager appears to open/close the DB and WAL files repeatedly per operation rather than caching the fd across a connection's lifetime (C SQLite opens once per connection and holds the fd). LEVER (refined): VFS-level FILE-DESCRIPTOR CACHING / persistent handles for DB + WAL + certificate sidecar across a connection's commits, eliminating the per-commit open/close metadata-syscall churn that serializes under disk contention. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: WhiteDeer/Opus 2026-07-23 PRECISE ROOT CAUSE (the 222 O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW DB opens). They are FILE-IDENTITY PROBES: validate_path_identity (namespace.rs:238) does open_identity_probe -> open(O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK) + FileIdentity::from_file (fstat dev/inode) + close, to verify the DB file was not substituted. It is invoked at EVERY operation boundary: ensure_current_wal_path (wal_adapter.rs:1598, called at the start of ~every WAL op: read_page/append/refresh/conflict-check/certificate) AND validate_namespace_binding (pager.rs:6381, called at ~9 pager boundaries incl. commit 12762/13734). So a single commit that does N WAL ops re-probes identity N times -> the ~17 DB-reopens/commit. This is a DELIBERATE TOCTOU security feature (commit 1136c171 'fix(vfs): bind native database namespaces to stable identities'; comment: 'identity validation for operation boundaries'); there is NO runtime flag to disable it. C SQLite has none of this — it holds ONE fd per connection, and the held fd inherently guarantees identity (same inode) with zero per-op syscalls. THE FIX (elegant, preserves security): hold the DB (and WAL) fd open across a connection's operations and operate on the held fd; the held inode IS the identity guarantee, so per-op path re-probing becomes unnecessary AND the reopen churn vanishes — one change kills both symptoms without weakening the substitution protection. This is a MAJOR fsqlite-vfs architecture change (open-per-op -> hold-fd) touching deliberately-added security machinery, so it needs a design review + careful preservation of the identity/locking invariants + quiet-host A/B. A cheaper interim (reduce probe FREQUENCY, e.g. once per transaction not per WAL-op) is possible but WEAKENS the TOCTOU window and should not be done without security sign-off. NOT implemented this session (major + security-sensitive + A/B-blocked); fully diagnosed and handed off. concurrent_mode stays true.

The bead's 'covering-index column-output' hypothesis was a MISDIAGNOSIS: the covering/index-cursor column path (cursor_column/column_to_reg_direct) is already encoding-aware (why index SEEK/SCAN queries 1-2 always passed); no raw covering-index output site exists. The prior traces' two dead-ends: (1) decode_value_into 'never fires on the city READ' = correct, decode happens at SorterInsert time + read is an early-return of the cached prefix; (2) 'ruled out sorter' = instrumented the lazy-decode branch (~16388), missed the early-return values path (16357). VERIFIED: full utf16_database_oracle_bld9w = 11/0/0 (both bd-spsnt arms green); instrumented probe = ZERO raw-UTF-16 Text register-writes; fsqlite-vdbe --lib 1148/0 (engine.rs byte-identical to HEAD). title: TEST-FAILURE: SSI CI-scale writers strand recovery state before oracle validation
description:
The existing CI-scale SSI serialization workload fails before the shared serializability oracle runs. On candidate d71b3563578208286d2c8858784b01b23f6d7b29 (oracle implementation introduced by 275e6814), the target reports hard failures including `database is busy (recovery in progress)`, rollback attempts with `cannot rollback - no transaction is active`, and reopen failures. The assertion is at crates/fsqlite-e2e/tests/bd_3plop_5_ssi_serialization_correctness.rs:433 and is blamed to original commit e803849a; the new oracle call begins at line 459. The same binary passes both cycle-detector tests and the public-path single-writer oracle smoke.

Exact reproducer:
`rch exec -- cargo test --locked -p fsqlite-e2e --test bd_3plop_5_ssi_serialization_correctness -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`

Investigate transaction/recovery ownership and retry/rollback state transitions under concurrent file-backed writers. Preserve concurrent_mode=true; do not serialize writers at connection or file-lock scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- The exact CI-scale reproducer completes without `recovery in progress`, rollback-state, or reopen hard failures across at least three fixed-seed runs.
- Recovery ownership/state transitions are root-caused and covered by focused unit or integration tests.
- Concurrent writer defaults remain true and the fix does not add connection-level or file-level writer serialization.
- The full bd_3plop_5 SSI target passes, including the authoritative typed-history oracle.
- Workspace formatting, check, strict Clippy, and tests pass, with RCH receipts recorded.
notes:
Acceptance proof (2026-08-07, OrangeKnoll)

Root cause and fix:
- `refresh_concurrent_begin_from_open_txn()` advanced a pager transaction snapshot to process-wide `CommitIndex::latest_seq()` even when that pager transaction could not see the newer commit. A stale full-page execution image could then evade first-committer-wins validation and overwrite committed effects.
- Commit 009fd2fcc pins provisional and execution snapshots in both directions to `published_visible_commit_seq_hint()`. The focused regression opens a pager transaction, advances the shared commit index with a peer commit, begins from the newer provisional sequence, and proves the refresh lowers/pins the execution image to the pager-visible snapshot.
- The SSI workload now retries the same deterministic operation, validates exact affected-row counts, and checks per-account committed balance deltas. Concurrent-writer defaults remain true; no connection/file writer serialization or Tokio was introduced.

Terminal RCH receipts:
- Full CI-scale SSI target: worker vmi1149989, `cargo test --locked -p fsqlite-e2e --test bd_3plop_5_ssi_serialization_correctness -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`, total 662.4s, 5 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. Three fixed seeds completed 4x120 operations each with no recovery, rollback, or reopen hard failure; the typed history and per-account state oracles passed.
- Focused root regression: worker vmi1227854, `cargo test --locked -p fsqlite-core test_concurrent_begin_rebases_execution_image_to_opened_pager_visibility -- --nocapture --test-threads=1`, total 1050.1s, 1 passed / 0 failed.
- Strict E2E Clippy: worker ovh-b, `cargo clippy --locked -p fsqlite-e2e --test bd_3plop_5_ssi_serialization_correctness -- -D warnings`, total 280.3s, exit 0.

- Workspace check: worker ovh-b, `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, total 328.2s, exit 0.
- `rustfmt --check` over all touched source/tests and `git diff --check` passed. UBS completed on every touched file; reported only the existing test-heavy assert/expect/indexing heuristic inventory, no new unsafe/security/resource/correctness defect.

Source commits 009fd2fcc and bff78ab4 are on origin/main; origin/master was mirrored to bff78ab4. The cross-phase `.17` bead retains ownership of final repository-wide promotion gates.

close_reason: Committed 8df21529: added precomputed-header serializer regression assertion in record.rs; focused RCH test passed after commit.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## What
For INSERT INTO table VALUES (?, ?, ?), the record header is FIXED if all column types are known. Pre-compute the header bytes at compile time and memcpy them directly instead of encoding varints per column at runtime.

## Where
- crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs: At MakeRecord emission, if all column types are statically known, emit P4::PrecomputedHeader(header_bytes)
- crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/engine.rs: execute_make_record_hot() checks for P4::PrecomputedHeader and memcpy's instead of iterating

## Why It Works
For INTEGER columns: serial type is always 1-6 (known from value range)
For TEXT columns with known max length: serial type range is bounded
For NULL: serial type is always 0
Pre-compute the header template, fill in only variable-length serial types at runtime.

## Expected Impact: -0.05 to -0.08 µs per row

## Acceptance Criteria
1. MakeRecord benchmark: ≥ 30% faster for fixed-schema tables
2. Correct for all column type combinations (proptest)
3. Falls back to per-column encoding for dynamic schemas

title: IDEA-WIZARD: Swarm SLO resource governor for high-core agent workloads
description:
## Background
FrankenSQLite is aimed at massive agent-swarm workloads on high-core/high-RAM hosts, and prior beads already produced a closed admission-control design (`bd-db300.5.4.3`) plus a closed deterministic agent-swarm replay lab (`bd-agent-swarm-replay-lab-1cc5y`). Open telemetry/operator beads also exist (`bd-zywqc.11`, `bd-316l0`, `bd-17uo0`, `bd-yxsqo`). The missing product slice is an operational resource governor that turns those ingredients into live shadow-mode and enforced-mode decisions without weakening concurrent-writer defaults.

## Idea-wizard synthesis
Generated 30 candidates across replay, admission, current-vs-design auditing, fallback visibility, resource saturation control, negative-result guardrails, query cancellation, parity triage, and operator diagnostics. The top five were: (1) Swarm SLO resource governor, (2) current-vs-design claim auditor, (3) fallback boundary burn-down dashboard, (4) agent/build wedge guardrails, and (5) resource-saturation benchmark control plane. The next ten ideas mostly refine these into replay minimization, negative-results protection, cancellation coverage, forensic recorders, parity clustering, and readiness gates.

## Goal
Build an operational governor that observes agent-swarm workload pressure, predicts SLO risk, and can recommend or enforce admission/backpressure/safe-mode decisions while preserving page-level MVCC concurrency as the default.

## Non-goals
Do not replace the existing replay lab, Prometheus metrics bead, or doctor/wedge bugs. This epic should connect and operationalize them. Do not introduce SQLite-style serialized writer locking or turn concurrent mode off by default.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A current-state overlap manifest links the closed design/replay beads and the open telemetry/operator beads, with clear ownership boundaries.
2. A shadow-mode policy engine computes governor decisions from queue depth, retry/fallback rates, p95/p99 latency, memory pressure, CPU/core pressure, and build/test saturation.
3. Replay and live-harness adapters feed the same decision inputs and emit comparable evidence bundles.
4. Operator output explains decisions, SLO budgets, kill switches, and safe-mode recommendations without hiding fallback or serialization risks.
5. Enforced mode has explicit rollout gates, regression tests, and proof that concurrent writer defaults remain enabled.
6. Heavy proof runs are documented for `rch`; lightweight smoke gates are suitable for normal CI.
close_reason: Completed: six child beads are closed, artifacts are committed, focused SLO governor harness proof passed, and swarm-slo graph has no active dependency cycles.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## §8.3 Per-Crate Detailed Descriptions

### fsqlite-types (~3,500 LOC)
Foundational types, zero internal deps. Modules: page.rs (PageNumber/NonZeroU32, PageBuf/PageData page-aligned, PageSize), value.rs (SqliteValue enum), opcode.rs (190+ Opcodes + OpcodeInfo), serial.rs (SerialType encoding/decoding), record.rs (Record struct, header, ser/de), txn.rs (TxnId u64, TxnMode enum), flags.rs (OpenFlags, SyncFlags, AccessFlags, LockLevel), limits.rs (SQLITE_MAX_*), affinity.rs (TypeAffinity), collation.rs (CollationId, BINARY/NOCASE/RTRIM). ~80 types, all Debug+Clone, most Copy.

### fsqlite-error (~800 LOC)
Error types via thiserror. FrankenError enum (~40 variants), ErrorCode (~30 primary), extended codes (SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY etc.), Result type alias. Every variant carries context (operation, page/table, source error).

### fsqlite-vfs (~2,500 LOC)
VFS abstraction = sqlite3_vfs + sqlite3_io_methods. traits.rs (Vfs/VfsFile), memory.rs (MemoryVfs with HashMap<PathBuf, Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>>), unix.rs (UnixVfs via asupersync blocking I/O, fcntl F_SETLK, 5 lock levels), flags.rs (VfsOpenFlags). Deps: fsqlite-types, fsqlite-error, asupersync.

### fsqlite-pager (~4,000 LOC)
Page cache + txn state machine. pager.rs (state: Open->Reader->Writer->Error, manages db file + journal + ARC cache, defines MvccPager + CheckpointPageWriter traits), cache.rs (ArcCache impl S6), page_ref.rs (RAII PageRef, decrements ref_count on drop), journal.rs (rollback journal, hot journal detection), state.rs (PagerState enum), header.rs (100-byte db header). Deps: fsqlite-vfs, fsqlite-types, fsqlite-error.

### fsqlite-wal (~3,500 LOC)
WAL implementation. wal.rs (Wal struct, header parsing, frame append, cumulative checksum S7.1), frame.rs (WalFrame 24B header + page data), index.rs (WalIndex SHM hash table, linear probing, reader marks, lock bytes), checkpoint.rs (PASSIVE/FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE), recovery.rs (checksum chain validation, committed txn replay, RaptorQ self-healing), raptorq.rs (repair symbol gen on commit, decode during recovery). Deps: fsqlite-vfs, asupersync. Does NOT depend on fsqlite-pager (cycle broken via CheckpointPageWriter trait).

### fsqlite-mvcc (~3,000 LOC)
MVCC version management — heart of concurrency innovation. manager.rs (MvccManager: txns, version store, lock table, commit index, witness hooks, GC), snapshot.rs (Snapshot{high, schema_epoch}, capture, visibility predicate), version.rs (PageVersion, arena-backed version chains), lock_table.rs (InProcessPageLockTable sharded HashMap + ShmPageLockTable adapter), transaction.rs (Transaction lifecycle Active->Committed/Aborted, write set, intent log, witness keys), commit.rs (FCW via CommitIndex + merge ladder, coordinator publication), gc.rs (horizon, chain pruning, reclaimability), coordinator.rs (WriteCoordinator wrapping asupersync two-phase MPSC). Deps: fsqlite-wal, fsqlite-pager, parking_lot, asupersync.

### fsqlite-btree (~5,000 LOC)
B-tree storage engine, most complex after VDBE. cursor.rs (BtCursor, page stack max depth 20@4KB/40@512B, save/restore), cell.rs (IntKeyCell, BlobKeyCell, InteriorCell, varint), balance.rs (balance_nonroot redistribution, balance_deeper new root, balance_quick fast append), overflow.rs (overflow page chains), free_list.rs (trunk/leaf, allocate/grow/deallocate), payload.rs (BtreePayload spanning local+overflow), table.rs (table B-tree intkey ops), index.rs (index B-tree blobkey ops). Deps: fsqlite-pager (MvccPager trait), fsqlite-types.

### fsqlite-ast (~2,000 LOC)
SQL AST nodes. stmt.rs (~20 Statement variants), expr.rs (~30 Expr variants), select.rs (SelectStatement, SelectCore enum with Select{}/Values(), CompoundOp, JoinClause, OrderingTerm, LimitClause, WithClause, Cte), table_ref.rs (TableRef enum), ddl.rs (ColumnDef, TableConstraint, IndexedColumn, ForeignKeyClause), literal.rs (Literal enum incl CurrentTime/Date/Timestamp), operator.rs (BinaryOp, UnaryOp), span.rs (Span byte offset range). All nodes carry Span.

### fsqlite-parser (~4,500 LOC)
Lexer + recursive descent. lexer.rs (~150 TokenType variants, memchr-accelerated, line/column tracking), parser.rs (one method per production, Pratt precedence for expressions), keyword.rs (perfect hash for 150+ keywords via phf), error.rs (parse errors with span, expected tokens, recovery hints).

### fsqlite-planner (~3,000 LOC)
Query planning. resolve.rs (name resolution, alias binding, column refs, star expansion, subquery scoping), where_clause.rs (index-usable terms, range constraints, OR optimization), join.rs (join ordering, beam search best-first mxChoice=12/18 matching wherePathSolver), cost.rs (I/O cost per access path, selectivity from sqlite_stat1/stat4), index.rs (usability, covering detection), plan.rs (QueryPlan output).

### fsqlite-vdbe (~6,000 LOC)
Bytecode VM, largest crate. vm.rs (fetch-execute loop, match dispatch, PC management), mem.rs (Mem/sqlite3_value, multi-representation, affinity, comparison), cursor.rs (VdbeCursor wrapping BtCursor, deferred seek, cached row decode, pseudo-table), program.rs (VdbeProgram Vec<VdbeOp>, register allocation, coroutine state), op.rs (VdbeOp struct, P4 enum), sort.rs (external merge sort), compare.rs (record comparison with collation), func_dispatch.rs (scalar/aggregate/window dispatch), subtype.rs (JSON subtype management).

### fsqlite-func (~2,500 LOC)
~80 built-in functions. scalar.rs (~60: abs, char, hex, instr, length, lower...), aggregate.rs (~12: avg, count, sum, group_concat...), window.rs (~11: row_number, rank, lag, lead...), math.rs (acos, sin, sqrt, log...), info.rs (sqlite_version, changes, total_changes, last_insert_rowid), registry.rs (FunctionRegistry: (name, arg_count) -> impl).

### Extensions
- fsqlite-ext-json (~2,000 LOC): JSON1, json(), json_extract/set/remove/type/valid, json_each/tree vtabs, JSONB, ->/-->>
- fsqlite-ext-fts5 (~4,000 LOC): FTS5, Porter stemmer, unicode61, inverted index, BM25, highlight/snippet, custom tokenizer API
- fsqlite-ext-fts3 (~2,000 LOC): FTS3/4 compat, matchinfo/offsets/snippet, wraps FTS5
- fsqlite-ext-rtree (~2,000 LOC): R*-tree spatial index, nearest-neighbor, geopoly
- fsqlite-ext-session (~1,500 LOC): Changeset/patchset gen/apply/invert
- fsqlite-ext-icu (~800 LOC): ICU collation, unicode comparison, case folding, FTS tokenizer
- fsqlite-ext-misc (~1,500 LOC): generate_series, dbstat, dbpage, csv vtab, decimal, uuid, ieee754, carray

### fsqlite-core (~5,000 LOC)
Orchestration layer. connection.rs (Connection, open/close, ATTACH/DETACH, schema cache, auto-commit, busy handler, auth callback), prepare.rs (SQL pipeline: parse->resolve->plan->codegen, LRU statement cache), schema.rs (sqlite_master loading, Table/Index/View/Trigger objects, schema cookie), codegen.rs (AST->VDBE for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, expression codegen, subquery/CTE coroutines), pragma.rs (~80 pragmas), auth.rs (authorization dispatch), vtab.rs (virtual table registration/lifecycle).

### fsqlite (~1,000 LOC)
Public API facade. Database wraps Connection. Re-exports Statement, Row, Transaction, SqliteValue, PageNumber, FrankenError, ErrorCode, Result, Vfs, VfsFile, MemoryVfs. Convenience: open(), open_in_memory(), execute(cx, sql).await, query_row(cx, sql).await.

### fsqlite-cli (~2,000 LOC)
Interactive shell via frankentui. Dot-commands (.tables, .schema, .mode, .import, .dump, .headers, .separator). Output modes (column, csv, json, line, list, table). Tab completion, syntax highlighting, history.

### fsqlite-harness (~1,500 LOC)
Conformance test runner. Runs identical SQL against FrankenSQLite + C sqlite3. Row-by-row comparison. Error code matching. Golden file management.

title: RELEASE-P0: T16 concurrent-write showcase fails during worker prepare with BusyRecovery
description: At exact source d5153bbc17fab4275431f3551e990aafb34f3bd7, the host-tuned release-perf T16 keeper fails before measurement on threadripperje. Two unchanged runs of binary SHA-256 eb398a5ba4482bcc9de1d95bececd6f1f97aaf8227d72b2402396df9f1e65827 returned BusyRecovery from conn.prepare at bd_wsw3p_concurrent_write_showcase.rs:438 after concurrent worker opens. The setup barrier then aborts peers. Evidence: /data/releases/frankensqlite-v020-perf-20260804/t16-run.d5153bbc17fab4275431f3551e990aafb34f3bd7.log and t16-run2.d5153bbc17fab4275431f3551e990aafb34f3bd7.log. T4 was correctly not run. comments.text: ROOT-CAUSED + FIX LANDED 55d7fe2c5 (session 88777e0b). LOCAL REPRO ACHIEVED for the first time (all prior datapoints were perf-host-only): crash-seeded live-WAL family + 16-32 concurrent worker opens with private runtimes (matching the showcase and mvcc-matrix shape) yields conn.prepare -> Busy at ~0.5%/worker locally (6/1280 pre-fix; repro scratchpad/t16-repro, trace scratchpad/t16-trace.log). TRACED MECHANISM: legacy shm lock protocol conflicts (fsqlite_vfs::unix, lock_byte=120, exclusive-vs-exclusive) during concurrent WAL-index recovery — the prepare-side refresh prologue (memdb refresh/reload + prepared-schema refresh) failed FAST on the transient class instead of honoring any busy window; this is why 4884b6a99 (autocommit-retry broadening) never covered it. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
TEST IMPACT MEASURED (GreenGull, 2026-07-30): this defect makes 9 tests
permanently RED in the default 'cargo test -p fsqlite-core --lib' configuration.
It is not only a silent perf deopt -- it is a release blocker for 'all tests pass'.

Failing (all in connection::pager_routing_tests):
  test_prepared_direct_update_leaf_patch_run_rolls_back_without_flush
  test_prepared_direct_insert_preserialize_fallback_does_not_publish_child_profile
  test_prepared_direct_delete_leaf_run_rolls_back_without_flush
  test_prepared_direct_delete_leaf_run_flushes_before_read
  test_prepared_direct_delete_monotone_leaf_runs_flush_before_read
  test_prepared_direct_delete_monotone_leaf_runs_roll_back_without_flush
  test_prepared_direct_simple_insert_large_profile_breakdown
  test_prepared_file_backed_single_writer_insert_reuses_schema_bound_publication
  test_prepared_update_write_after_write_defers_active_txn_memdb_reload_until_read_boundary

Mechanism, confirmed by the one-time WARN added in 12d6c590 firing during the
failing run:
  'tracing is enabled for fsqlite.statement/fsqlite.statement_reuse, so the fused
   prepared-DML fast lane is disabled on this connection and DML takes the slower
   instrumented path' statement_trace_enabled=true statement_reuse_enabled=true

asupersync::test_utils::run_test -> init_test_logging() installs a process-global
TRACE subscriber, so every one of these tests runs with the fused lane disabled,
while each asserts the lane DID run (pending_direct_*_run.borrow().is_some(),
prepared_direct_insert_preserialize_time_ns > 0, etc.).

Reproduces identically whether run as a full suite or with --exact in isolation
(0.60s for all 9), so it is not a test-ordering or cross-test-contamination
issue. RUST_LOG=off does not help: init_test_logging forces the subscriber.

NOT caused by the prepared-statement settlement work in flight: that adds
settle_pending_transaction_cleanup() to the prepared entry points, whose body
early-returns when pending_transaction_cleanup is false. That flag is only set by
mark_transaction_cleanup_required(), called solely from compat::Transaction::drop,
which no fsqlite-core test uses. Verified by reading the body, then confirmed
empirically by the WARN above identifying an unrelated cause.

IMPLICATION BEYOND TESTS: any production consumer running with tracing at
DEBUG/INFO on those targets silently loses the fused prepared-DML fast lane. The
narrow fix (test-only override to force the lane) would mask that. RusticBasin's
stated principle -- the fast lane should EMIT events rather than be skipped -- is
the fix that recovers both the tests and the production path.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
RETRACTION (GreenGull, 2026-07-30) of my previous comment on this bead.

I claimed the 9 failing connection::pager_routing_tests were caused by THIS
defect -- tracing disabling the fused prepared-DML fast lane. That is WRONG and
I retract it. Do not treat those 9 failures as evidence for or against bd-t56wv.

Counterfactual I should have run before claiming causation:

  RUST_LOG=error cargo test -p fsqlite-core --lib -- connection::pager_routing_tests::test_prepared
  -> test result: FAILED. 104 passed; 9 failed   (SAME 9)

Raising the targets above DEBUG/INFO -- exactly the remedy the bd-t56wv warning
itself recommends -- does not fix them. So tracing suppression is not the cause.

My error: I observed the one-time suppression WARN firing during the failing run
and inferred causation. All that WARN proves is that the fused INSERT lane was
suppressed on that connection. It says nothing about why
pending_direct_update_leaf_patch_run is None, which is what the assertions check.
Post-hoc, and I had a counterfactual available for the cost of one env var.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE about bd-t56wv: the suppression is real, the WARN fires
correctly, and a production consumer logging at DEBUG/INFO on
fsqlite.statement / fsqlite.statement_reuse does silently lose the fused
prepared-DML fast lane. That remains a genuine perf deopt worth the
emit-events-instead-of-skipping fix. It is simply NOT this test failure.

ALSO RULED OUT as the cause of the 9:
  - test ordering / cross-test contamination: reproduces with --exact in
    isolation, 0.01s, and as a 9-test batch in 0.60s
  - prepared_direct_update_fixed_real_for_bench_enabled(): bench-internals is
    NOT a default feature (default = native, linux-asupersync-uring) and the
    backing atomic defaults to true, so that gate is open
  - the in-flight prepared-statement settlement work: settle_pending_transaction_
    cleanup() early-returns unless pending_transaction_cleanup is set, and that
    flag is only set by compat::Transaction::drop, which no fsqlite-core test uses

STILL UNKNOWN: the actual cause. The working tree currently carries substantial
uncommitted work from several agents (connection.rs, fsqlite-btree/cursor.rs and
instrumentation.rs, multiple fsqlite-mvcc files, fsqlite-parser/fsqlite-ast), so
the next step is to determine whether these 9 fail at HEAD in a clean worktree or
only in the dirty shared checkout. That distinction decides whether main is
actually red. Filing that as the open question rather than guessing again.

title: MVCC Conflict Analytics & Observability Suite
description:
**Idea #1 - Top Priority**

Build comprehensive conflict observability into the MVCC layer, extending the existing `tracing` instrumentation (70+ usages across 18 MVCC source files).

**Components:**
1. **ConflictTracer** - Extend fsqlite-mvcc conflict instrumentation
   - Page lock contention: which txn, which page, resolution (extend `shared_lock_table.rs`, `conflict_model.rs`)
   - FCW (First Committer Wins) activations with before/after state (extend `conflict_model.rs`)
   - SSI serialization failures with dependency graph (extend `ssi_validation.rs`)
   - Zero-cost path when tracing disabled (compile-time feature gate)

2. **ConflictMetrics** - Aggregated statistics via connection pragma
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_conflict_stats: conflicts_total, conflicts_by_page, avg_resolution_time
   - Per-table conflict hotspot detection
   - Temporal conflict density (conflicts/second)

3. **ConflictLog** - Persistent conflict history for debugging
   - Ring buffer of last N conflicts (configurable via PRAGMA)
   - Export to JSON for external analysis
   - Integration with deterministic replay (bd-t6sv2.12)

4. **Shared Observability Infrastructure** - Foundation for beads 2, 3, 5, 8, 9
   - NEW: crates/fsqlite-observability/ with metrics registry, ring buffer, PRAGMA helpers
   - Trait-based observer pattern for zero-overhead opt-in
   - Structured event schema shared across all observability features

**Implementation:**
- Extend `conflict_observer` callback pattern in InProcessPageLockTable (`shared_lock_table.rs`)
- Extend Transaction struct in `lifecycle.rs` with conflict_history vec
- NEW: crates/fsqlite-observability/src/lib.rs (shared cross-cutting infrastructure)
- Build on existing `tracing` spans already in `core_types.rs`, `lifecycle.rs`, `gc.rs`
- Proptest: verify conflict emission matches actual contention

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/shared_lock_table.rs (lock contention events)
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/conflict_model.rs (FCW/SSI events)
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/ssi_validation.rs (SSI failure detail)
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/lifecycle.rs (transaction-level conflict history)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (new PRAGMAs)
- NEW: crates/fsqlite-observability/src/lib.rs (shared infrastructure)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
This feature ONLY observes conflicts - it MUST NOT introduce any serialization or blocking. Conflict tracing is purely diagnostic. The observer callback must be non-blocking and must not acquire any page locks.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: conflict event emission correctness with tracing enabled
  - Log: event type, txn_id, page_id, timestamp_ns, resolution outcome
  - Verify: zero events emitted when tracing disabled (feature gate test)
  - Verify: overhead < 1% when tracing disabled via criterion micro-benchmark
- Unit: ring buffer capacity and eviction behavior
  - Log: buffer size, oldest event age, eviction count
- Integration: multi-writer scenarios produce expected conflict events
  - Log: full conflict chain with page-level detail, txn lifecycle
  - Scenario: 4 writers hitting same page, verify exactly 3 FCW events
  - Scenario: SSI write-skew detection emits rw-antidependency edges
- E2E: PRAGMA returns accurate stats after conflict workload
  - Log: before/after stats, query execution time, conflicts/second
  - Verify: stats reset via PRAGMA fsqlite_conflict_reset
  - Verify: stats survive connection close/reopen within same process
- Proptest: conflict events match actual lock contention outcomes
  - Log: seed values for reproducibility, operation sequence
  - Property: every lock contention produces exactly one conflict event
  - Property: conflict_count == sum(conflicts_by_page)

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_conflict_tracing.sh that:
1. Runs a known-conflict workload (4 concurrent writers, overlapping pages)
2. Captures conflict events via PRAGMA fsqlite_conflict_log
3. Verifies event count matches expected (with tolerance for timing)
4. Verifies each event has complete metadata (txn_id, page, resolution)
5. Outputs pass/fail with detailed diff and JSON evidence

**Success Criteria:**
- Developers can trace exactly why a transaction failed
- Hotspot detection identifies tables needing schema redesign
- Stats reset via PRAGMA fsqlite_conflict_reset
- Zero overhead when observability disabled
- All tests include comprehensive logging for debugging
- Shared infrastructure reusable by beads 2, 3, 5, 8, 9

All 1754+ tests pass, zero clippy warnings.

title: Connection Pooling Best Practices & Validator
description:
**Idea #10 - Phase 3**

Guide users toward optimal connection management for concurrency. This bead is primarily guidance and validation tooling, building on transaction lifecycle data from bd-t6sv2.5.

**Components:**
1. **PoolPatternDetector**
   - Detect anti-patterns: single connection for concurrent use (serialized writes)
   - Identify over-pooling: more connections than useful (too many snapshots block GC)
   - Find connection leaks: long-idle connections holding snapshots
   - Detect rapid connect/disconnect cycling (connection thrashing)

2. **PoolAdvisor**
   - Recommend pool size based on workload: min(CPU_cores, write_concurrency_needed)
   - Suggest connection lifecycle settings (max idle time, max age)
   - Warn about statement preparation patterns (unprepared queries in hot loops)
   - Use transaction lifecycle data from bd-t6sv2.5 for recommendations

3. **BestPracticesDoc**
   - Connection pooling guide specific to FrankenSQLite MVCC model
   - Key insight: unlike C SQLite, FrankenSQLite benefits from multiple writer connections
   - Comparison with C SQLite patterns (single-writer pool vs MVCC multi-writer pool)
   - Integration examples for common Rust pool libraries (sqlx, r2d2, deadpool, bb8)

4. **PoolSimulator**
   - Test harness for pool configurations
   - Model concurrent connection behavior under various pool sizes
   - Find optimal pool size empirically for given workload
   - Uses benchmark infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.2

**Implementation:**
- Connection-level metrics in `fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs` (connect/disconnect tracking, idle time)
- Analysis utilities in fsqlite-observability (pool pattern analysis)
- PRAGMA fsqlite_connection_stats: pool_size_estimate, idle_connections, connection_age_max_ms
- Documentation in docs/connection-pooling.md

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs (connection lifecycle tracking)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (connection stats PRAGMA)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (pool pattern detection)
- docs/connection-pooling.md (comprehensive guide)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
Pool recommendations MUST emphasize that FrankenSQLite benefits from multiple writer connections (unlike C SQLite). Never suggest a single-writer pool as a "safe default" - that defeats the entire purpose of MVCC. Connection tracking MUST NOT introduce connection-level serialization.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: anti-pattern detection accuracy
  - Log: pattern_type (single_conn|over_pool|conn_leak|conn_thrash), confidence_score, evidence
  - Verify: single-connection-for-concurrent-use correctly detected
  - Verify: no false positives for healthy pool configurations
- Unit: pool size recommendation calculation
  - Log: workload_profile (read_heavy|write_heavy|mixed), recommended_pool_size, rationale
  - Verify: recommendation increases with write concurrency need
  - Verify: recommendation bounded by diminishing returns threshold
- Unit: connection lifecycle tracking
  - Log: conn_id, connect_ts, idle_since_ts, queries_executed, txn_count
  - Verify: lifecycle tracking accurate under concurrent connection use
- Integration: pool pattern detection under simulated workloads
  - Log: pool_size, concurrent_writers, conflicts_detected, recommendation
  - Scenario: single connection with 4 threads -> detect anti-pattern
  - Scenario: 100 connections with 4 threads -> detect over-pooling
  - Scenario: connections never closed -> detect leak pattern
- Integration: advisor recommendations improve throughput
  - Log: pool_size_before, throughput_before, pool_size_after, throughput_after, improvement_pct
  - Verify: following pool size recommendation improves throughput

title: Schema Design Advisor for Concurrency
description:
**Idea #11 - Phase 3**

Analyze schema design for concurrent write performance. Consumes conflict analytics from bd-t6sv2.1 and page cache data from bd-t6sv2.8 to provide data-driven schema recommendations.

**Components:**
1. **HotspotDetector**
   - Identify tables with single-row contention patterns (auto-increment rowid on last page)
   - Find auto-increment columns causing page contention (all INSERTs hit the rightmost leaf)
   - Detect wide rows that dominate pages (few rows per page = more conflicts per row)
   - Use conflict analytics from bd-t6sv2.1 to identify actual hotspot pages

2. **IndexAnalyzer**
   - Evaluate index selectivity for lock scope (more selective = fewer pages locked)
   - Identify missing indexes that cause table scans (scan locks all pages)
   - Find redundant indexes adding write overhead (each index is a separate B-tree)
   - Quantify write amplification contribution per index (using data from bd-t6sv2.9)

3. **SchemaAdvisor**
   - Suggest WITHOUT ROWID tables for UUID-keyed tables (spreads inserts across pages)
   - Recommend covering indexes for read-heavy queries (avoid table page access)
   - Propose column ordering to minimize page splits (fixed-width columns first)
   - Identify tables where page size adjustment would reduce conflicts

4. **SchemaSimulator**
   - Model lock contention for given schema + workload profile
   - Compare alternatives quantitatively (estimated conflicts/second)
   - Generate ALTER TABLE / CREATE INDEX migration statements
   - Uses page cache data from bd-t6sv2.8 for cache impact estimation

**Implementation:**
- Schema analysis utilities in `fsqlite-planner` (index selectivity, page density estimation)

title: Deterministic Replay Debugger
description:
**Idea #12 - Phase 3**

Enable reproducible debugging of concurrent write scenarios. Build on existing infrastructure: `repro_fcw_loss.rs` for FCW reproduction, `deterministic_rebase.rs` for rebase replay, `time_travel.rs` for time-travel queries, and asupersync's Lab reactor for deterministic scheduling.

**Components:**
1. **RecordMode**
   - Capture all inputs: queries, timing, page state, random seeds
   - Deterministic timestamp assignment (logical clock, not wall clock)
   - Compact binary format for recording (versioned for forward compatibility)
   - Record MVCC version chain state at conflict points
   - Leverage asupersync's Lab reactor for deterministic scheduling capture

2. **ReplayMode**
   - Reproduce exact same execution order using captured schedule
   - Step through conflicts frame-by-frame with inspector hooks
   - Verify behavior matches recording (state assertion checkpoints)
   - Support concurrent_mode=true replays (CRITICAL - never serialize for replay)
   - Use DPOR-based schedule replay from asupersync

3. **MinimalReproducer**
   - Automatically minimize failure case (delta debugging)
   - Extract relevant transactions only (dependency-based slicing)
   - Generate standalone test case (compilable Rust test or SQL script)
   - Output includes: minimal schema, minimal data, minimal operations

4. **DiffAnalyzer**
   - Compare two executions (expected vs actual)
   - Identify divergence point (first differing MVCC version chain state)
   - Explain behavioral differences at page-level detail
   - Highlight MVCC state divergence (version chain, lock table, SSI graph)

**Implementation:**
- Recording hooks in Connection/Transaction (extend `lifecycle.rs`)
- Replay runtime with controlled scheduling (integrate with asupersync Lab reactor)
- Integrate with conflict tracer from bd-t6sv2.1 for conflict-point recording

**Test Requirements:**

title: Version Chain Garbage Collection Tuner
description:
**Idea #15 - Phase 3**

Optimize GC behavior for different workload patterns. The GC implementation lives in `fsqlite-mvcc/src/gc.rs` (40KB). This bead depends on transaction lifecycle data (bd-t6sv2.5) for snapshot age tracking and benefits from page cache data (bd-t6sv2.8) for understanding memory pressure.

**Components:**
1. **GCMetrics**
   - Versions reclaimed per GC cycle (with breakdown by table/page)
   - GC latency distribution (P50/P99 per cycle)
   - Blocked GC due to old snapshots (snapshot age, blocking txn_id)
   - Version chain depth distribution (histogram)
   - Uses shared observability infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.1

2. **GCAnalyzer**
   - Version chain depth distribution over time (growing = GC falling behind)
   - Reclamation rate vs creation rate (steady-state analysis)
   - Memory pressure from old versions (bytes held by reclaimable versions)
   - Correlation with page cache pressure from bd-t6sv2.8
   - Identify: "GC is reclaiming N versions/sec but creation is N+M/sec - falling behind"

3. **GCTuner**
   - Adaptive GC scheduling (increase frequency when version chains grow)
   - Workload-aware horizon advancement (batch GC during low-write periods)
   - Memory-pressure-triggered GC (fire GC when cache eviction increases)
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_gc_interval_ms for manual tuning (default: 1000ms from README spec)
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_gc_batch_size for max versions reclaimed per cycle

4. **GCAdvisor**
   - Recommend GC parameters based on workload profile
   - Identify snapshot-holding culprits: "Transaction txn_id (age: Nms) is blocking GC"
   - Suggest transaction pattern changes: "Shorten transactions to allow GC to advance"
   - Alert: "Version chain depth > threshold - GC cannot keep up"
   - Uses transaction lifecycle data from bd-t6sv2.5 to identify long-running snapshots

**Implementation:**
- Extend GC in `gc.rs` with metrics collection (atomic counters)
- Add tuning parameters via PRAGMA in `fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs`
- Adaptive scheduling logic in `gc.rs` (feedback loop on chain depth)
- Virtual table: fsqlite_gc_stats (per-cycle statistics)

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/gc.rs (metrics, adaptive scheduling, tuning)
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/core_types.rs (version chain depth tracking)
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/lifecycle.rs (snapshot age feed to GC advisor)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (GC tuning PRAGMAs)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (shared infrastructure)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
GC tuning MUST NOT violate the fundamental MVCC invariant: a version is only reclaimable if no active transaction can see it. The GC tuner adjusts SCHEDULING (when/how often GC runs), never CORRECTNESS (which versions are safe to reclaim). Adaptive scheduling MUST NOT cause GC to reclaim versions still visible to active snapshots.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: GC metric accuracy
  - Log: gc_cycle_id, versions_scanned, versions_reclaimed, cycle_latency_us, chain_depth_max
  - Verify: reclaimed count matches actual versions freed
  - Verify: latency measurement accurate (within 1ms)
  - Verify: chain depth histogram matches actual chain traversal
- Unit: adaptive scheduling behavior
  - Log: chain_depth_avg, gc_interval_ms_before, gc_interval_ms_after, adjustment_reason
  - Verify: interval decreases when chain depth grows (more frequent GC)
  - Verify: interval increases when chain depth shrinks (less frequent GC)
  - Verify: interval bounded by configurable min/max
- Unit: GC safety under concurrent writes
  - Log: active_txns, gc_horizon, versions_retained, versions_that_would_violate_mvcc
  - Verify: GC never reclaims a version visible to any active transaction
  - Verify: GC horizon correctly computed as min(active_snapshot_ids)
  - Property: forall active snapshots S, forall pages P, visible_version(P, S) is never reclaimed
- Integration: GC keeps up with sustained write load
  - Log: write_rate_ops_per_sec, gc_rate_versions_per_sec, chain_depth_over_time, memory_usage_bytes
  - Scenario: sustained 10K writes/sec for 60 seconds -> verify chain depth bounded
  - Scenario: burst writes then idle -> verify GC catches up during idle
  - Verify: memory usage does not grow unbounded
- Integration: GC advisor identifies blocking transactions
  - Log: blocking_txn_id, snapshot_age_ms, versions_blocked, advisory_message
  - Scenario: start long-running read transaction, start writes -> verify advisor identifies blocker
  - Verify: advisory message includes actionable suggestion
- Integration: PRAGMA tuning parameters work correctly
  - Log: pragma_name, old_value, new_value, gc_behavior_change
  - Verify: fsqlite_gc_interval_ms changes GC frequency
  - Verify: fsqlite_gc_batch_size limits versions per cycle
- E2E: memory bounded under sustained writes
  - Log: duration_sec, total_writes, peak_memory_bytes, final_chain_depth, gc_cycles
  - Verify: peak memory < 2x steady-state for 300-second sustained workload
  - Verify: chain depth converges to stable value
- E2E: adaptive scheduling vs fixed scheduling comparison
  - Log: scheduling_mode (fixed|adaptive), avg_chain_depth, max_chain_depth, gc_cpu_pct, write_throughput
  - Verify: adaptive scheduling produces lower max chain depth
  - Verify: adaptive scheduling does not significantly increase GC CPU usage
- Proptest: GC correctness under arbitrary workloads
  - Log: seed, txn_count, write_ops, gc_cycles, mvcc_violations_found
  - Property: mvcc_violations_found == 0 (always)
  - Property: after all transactions close, all versions eventually reclaimed

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_gc_tuner.sh that:
1. Runs sustained write workload with GC metrics enabled
2. Verifies memory stays bounded (no unbounded growth)
3. Tests adaptive scheduling vs fixed scheduling
4. Verifies GC advisor correctly identifies blocking transactions
5. Validates PRAGMA tuning parameters
6. Outputs pass/fail with memory/performance charts as JSON

**Success Criteria:**
- GC never becomes a bottleneck under normal workloads
- Memory usage predictable and bounded
- Long-running queries detected and reported before they block GC indefinitely
- Adaptive scheduling demonstrably better than fixed for bursty workloads
- GC correctness proven: no MVCC violations under any workload

title: Concurrent Writer Benchmark Suite & Regression CI
description:
**Idea #2 - High Priority**

Establish performance benchmarks that prove concurrent writer superiority.

**Components:**
1. **MicroBenchmarks** (criterion, in existing `benches/` directory)
   - Page lock acquire/release latency (P50/P99)
   - Version chain traversal cost by depth
   - Checkpoint throughput under write load
   - GC overhead per reclaimed version
   - Conflict observer overhead (tracing on vs off)

2. **MacroBenchmarks** (custom harness, extends existing `fsqlite-e2e/src/benchmark.rs`)
   - TPC-C variant with concurrent transactions
   - OLTP read-heavy (95/5) vs write-heavy (50/50)
   - Single-table hotspot contention scenarios
   - Multi-table distributed writes
   - Correlated with conflict analytics from bd-t6sv2.1

3. **Baseline Tracking**
   - Store benchmark results in CI artifacts (JSON structured output)
   - Compare against baseline with statistical significance (Welch t-test)
   - Alert on P50 regression > 5%, P99 regression > 10%
   - Baseline stored in `.github/baselines/` as JSON

4. **Comparison Mode**
   - Run same workloads against C SQLite (via rusqlite)
   - Generate comparison reports showing concurrent writer wins
   - Highlight scenarios where serialized mode is faster (single-writer)
   - Pair benchmark results with conflict metrics from bd-t6sv2.1

**Implementation:**
- Use existing `benches/` directory for criterion benchmarks (NOT a new crate)
- Extend `crates/fsqlite-e2e/src/benchmark.rs` for macro benchmarks
- GitHub Actions workflow: bench-regression.yml
- Rust-based baseline comparison tool (Cargo binary in fsqlite-e2e)

**CI Integration:**
- Run on every PR to main (quick subset: microbenchmarks only)
- Full suite on merge to main (micro + macro)
- Weekly extended suite with larger datasets and longer durations

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
All benchmarks MUST run with concurrent_mode_default=true. The serialized mode comparison is ONLY for demonstrating the concurrent writer advantage, never as a default. Verify concurrent_mode_default=true at benchmark start.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: each microbenchmark has --verbose mode with detailed timing breakdown
  - Log: operation, iterations, P50/P99/max latency_ns, throughput_ops_per_sec
  - Verify: benchmark harness correctly detects concurrent_mode=true
- Unit: baseline comparison produces valid statistical analysis
  - Log: sample_count, mean, stddev, t_statistic, p_value, regression_detected
- Integration: benchmark harness logs all configuration parameters
  - Log: page_size, cache_size, writer_count, duration_ms, seed
  - Verify: results deterministic for same seed (within noise threshold)
- E2E: comparison reports include raw data for reproducibility
  - Log: fsqlite_throughput, sqlite_throughput, speedup_factor, conflict_rate
  - Verify: report includes hardware info (CPU, memory, disk type)
- E2E: full benchmark suite completes within CI time budget
  - Log: total_duration_ms, benchmark_count, failures

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_benchmarks.sh that:
1. Runs quick benchmark subset (< 60 seconds)
2. Verifies all benchmarks complete without error
3. Verifies JSON output is valid and complete
4. Compares against stored baseline (if available)
5. Reports regressions with statistical confidence

**Success Criteria:**
- Developers see immediate feedback on perf changes in PRs
- Concrete numbers demonstrate concurrent writer advantage
- Regressions caught before merge with statistical significance
- Results reproducible from logged parameters and seeds
- Benchmark results correlate with conflict analytics

All 808 MVCC tests pass, zero clippy warnings.

title: RaptorQ Self-Healing Observability & Verification
description:
**Idea #3 - High Priority**

Make RaptorQ's self-healing capabilities visible and verifiable. Build on existing infrastructure in `wal_fec.rs` (80KB) and `repair_symbols.rs`.

**Components:**
1. **RepairTracer**
   - Emit structured events when RaptorQ repair activates
   - Record: frame_id, symbols_lost, symbols_used, repair_success, latency_ns
   - Track repair budget utilization over time
   - Build on existing repair PRAGMA infrastructure in `fsqlite-core/src/repair_symbols.rs`

2. **RepairMetrics**
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_raptorq_stats: repairs_total, repairs_failed, symbols_reclaimed, budget_utilization_pct
   - Histogram of symbol loss severity (buckets: 1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+)
   - WAL health score (0-100 based on recent repair frequency and severity)
   - Uses shared observability infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.1

3. **VerificationSuite**
   - Inject controlled corruption, verify repair
   - Test boundary conditions (exactly R, R+1, R-1 lost symbols)
   - Continuous background verification option (integrity sampling)
   - Build on existing corruption test infrastructure in `fsqlite-e2e/src/corruption.rs` (116KB)

4. **WAL Health Dashboard**
   - Virtual table: fsqlite_raptorq_events (recent repair history)
   - Configurable thresholds for repair frequency alerts via PRAGMA
   - Early warning for degrading media (trend detection)

**Implementation:**
- Extend `crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal_fec.rs` with repair observer callbacks
- Extend `crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal.rs` with metrics aggregation
- Extend `crates/fsqlite-core/src/repair_symbols.rs` with new PRAGMAs
- Use shared observability crate from bd-t6sv2.1

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal_fec.rs (repair observer callbacks)
- crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal.rs (metrics aggregation)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/repair_symbols.rs (extend existing PRAGMA infrastructure)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (new PRAGMAs)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (shared metrics from bd-t6sv2.1)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
Repair observation is read-only diagnostic. It MUST NOT alter repair behavior or introduce additional I/O barriers. Observer callbacks must be non-blocking.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: verify metric accuracy under controlled corruption
  - Log: corruption_type (bitflip|zero|truncate), symbols_lost, symbols_available, repair_outcome (success|failure|partial)
  - Verify: metrics match actual repair events 1:1
  - Verify: zero overhead when no corruption (no false positives)
- Unit: WAL health score calculation
  - Log: input_events, score_before, score_after, threshold_exceeded
  - Verify: score=100 with no repairs, score degrades proportionally
- Integration: repair events match actual bitflip scenarios
  - Log: frame_id, checksums_before, checksums_after, repair_budget_used_pct
  - Scenario: inject 1 symbol loss -> repair succeeds, budget barely used
  - Scenario: inject R symbols -> repair succeeds, budget fully used
  - Scenario: inject R+1 symbols -> repair fails, error logged with detail
- E2E: stress test with continuous writes + corruption injection
  - Log: writes_per_sec, repairs_per_sec, success_rate_pct, mean_repair_latency_us
  - Build on existing corruption scenarios in `fsqlite-e2e/src/corruption.rs`
  - Verify: database integrity maintained throughout stress test
- Proptest: repair always succeeds when within symbol budget
  - Log: seed, symbols_lost, symbols_available, repair_success
  - Property: symbols_lost <= R implies repair_success == true
  - Property: repairs_total == sum(repairs over all frames)

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_raptorq_healing.sh that:
1. Creates database with known content (deterministic seed)
2. Injects controlled corruption (1, R/2, R, R+1 symbols per frame)
3. Reads data back and verifies correctness for repairable cases
4. Reports repair statistics in JSON format
5. Verifies failure for over-budget corruption
6. Outputs pass/fail with evidence artifacts

**Success Criteria:**
- Operators know when RaptorQ is saving them from data loss
- Degrading storage detected before catastrophic failure
- Repair budget utilization guides R parameter tuning
- Tests produce reproducible verification evidence
- Builds on existing infrastructure (no redundant code)

title: SQLite Conformance & Compatibility Dashboard
description:
**Idea #4 - Phase 2**

Track and display SQLite compatibility status with focus on MVCC-specific behavioral divergences. This bead COMPLEMENTS (not duplicates) the PARITY-100 program (bd-1dp9) which handles comprehensive conformance testing.

**Scope Boundary:** bd-1dp9 handles the conformance test corpus, differential harness, and gap closure. THIS bead focuses specifically on:
- Documenting INTENTIONAL divergences caused by MVCC concurrent writer mode
- Providing a user-facing compatibility scorecard for MVCC-aware behavior differences
- Generating migration guidance for users coming from single-writer C SQLite

**Components:**
1. **MVCC Divergence Catalog**
   - Document all intentional behavioral differences vs C SQLite
   - Categories: timing differences, error code differences, concurrency semantics
   - Each divergence: description, rationale, user impact, workaround

2. **CompatibilityScorecard**

   - Diff against previous version (track progress over time)

4. **Migration Guide**

   - MVCC-specific considerations (snapshot isolation, conflict handling)

title: Transaction Lifecycle Analyzer & Advisor
description:
**Idea #5 - Phase 2**

Provide deep visibility into transaction behavior with actionable guidance. Transaction lifecycle data feeds directly into GC tuning (bd-t6sv2.15) and checkpoint scheduling (bd-t6sv2.7).

**Components:**
1. **TxnTracer**
   - Track: begin_time, first_read, first_write, commit/rollback_time
   - Page access pattern (read set size, write set size, evolution over time)
   - Savepoint depth and rollback frequency
   - Snapshot age for MVCC pressure assessment
   - Build on existing transaction instrumentation in `lifecycle.rs` (159KB, 29 tracing spans)

2. **TxnMetrics**
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_txn_stats: active_count, avg_duration_ms, long_running_count, max_snapshot_age_ms
   - Per-transaction state via virtual table: SELECT txn_id, duration_ms, pages_read, pages_written, snapshot_age_ms FROM fsqlite_transactions
   - GC pressure indicator: oldest_active_snapshot vs current commit_seq (feeds bd-t6sv2.15)

3. **TxnAdvisor**
   - Warn: "Transaction held for >N seconds without activity" (configurable threshold via PRAGMA)
   - Suggest: "Consider batching these M small transactions" (detect rapid begin/commit cycles)
   - Alert: "Snapshot too old, blocking GC - consider shorter transaction scope"
   - Alert: "Transaction read set growing beyond N pages - consider narrower queries"

4. **TxnVisualizer**
   - Timeline data export as JSON (txn start/end, conflict points, page accesses)
   - Conflict points annotated with resolution outcome
   - Export format compatible with external timeline tools (Chrome DevTools trace format)
   - Uses shared observability infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.1

**Implementation:**
- Extend Transaction struct in `lifecycle.rs` with lightweight instrumentation
- New virtual table: fsqlite_transactions (read-only, reflects in-memory state)
- Advisory system with configurable PRAGMA thresholds
- Build on shared observability crate from bd-t6sv2.1

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/lifecycle.rs (transaction instrumentation)
- crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/core_types.rs (snapshot age tracking)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (advisory thresholds, stats PRAGMAs)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs (virtual table registration)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (shared infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.1)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
Transaction tracing MUST NOT alter transaction ordering or introduce synchronization. Instrumentation uses atomic counters and lock-free data structures. The virtual table provides a read-only snapshot of transaction state - it MUST NOT hold any locks while returning results.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: timing accuracy under controlled delays
  - Log: txn_id, begin_ts_ns, first_read_ts_ns, first_write_ts_ns, commit_ts_ns, duration_ms
  - Verify: timestamps monotonically increasing within transaction
  - Verify: duration = commit_ts - begin_ts within 1ms tolerance
- Unit: page access tracking correctness
  - Log: txn_id, pages_read, pages_written, read_set_pages, write_set_pages
  - Verify: read_set superset of write_set (every written page was also read)
  - Verify: page counts match actual B-tree operations
- Unit: advisor trigger thresholds
  - Log: advisor_type (long_txn|batch_suggest|gc_pressure|large_read_set), txn_id, threshold, actual_value
  - Verify: advisor fires at exactly the configured threshold
  - Verify: no advisories when all transactions are healthy
- Integration: multi-txn scenario with correct lifecycle tracking
  - Log: txn_count, concurrent_peak, avg_duration_ms, max_snapshot_age_ms
  - Scenario: 10 concurrent transactions, verify all lifecycles tracked independently
  - Scenario: nested savepoints, verify savepoint depth tracked correctly
- E2E: virtual table returns accurate data under concurrent load
  - Log: query_time_ms, rows_returned, active_txn_count, gc_pressure_score
  - Verify: virtual table query does not block concurrent transactions
  - Verify: data consistent (no torn reads of in-flight transaction state)
- E2E: advisor recommendations verified against actual performance
  - Log: advisory, action_taken, before_metric, after_metric, improvement_pct
  - Verify: following advisor recommendations actually improves the metric

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_txn_lifecycle.sh that:
1. Starts multiple concurrent transactions with known behavior patterns
2. Queries fsqlite_transactions virtual table
3. Verifies lifecycle timing matches expected patterns
4. Triggers each advisory type and verifies output
5. Outputs pass/fail with evidence JSON

**Success Criteria:**
- Developers understand transaction behavior at page-level detail
- Anti-patterns detected and explained with actionable guidance
- GC-blocking snapshots identified early (before memory pressure)
- Transaction data feeds downstream beads (bd-t6sv2.7, bd-t6sv2.15)

title: Query Plan Concurrency Hints
description:
**Idea #6 - Phase 2**

Extend EXPLAIN output to show concurrent writer implications, enabling developers to predict and prevent conflicts at query plan time.

**Components:**
1. **LockPrediction**
   - Static analysis: which tables/pages likely accessed by each query
   - Worst-case lock footprint estimation (based on table statistics)
   - Index vs table scan lock patterns (index scan = fewer page locks)
   - Annotate with page count estimates from planner statistics

2. **ConflictProbability**
   - Based on table statistics, access patterns, and conflict history from bd-t6sv2.1
   - "Low/Medium/High conflict risk" annotation per table access
   - Hotspot identification in plan output (pages with historical conflict density)

3. **ConcurrencyAdvisor**
   - Suggest index additions to reduce lock scope (fewer pages touched = fewer conflicts)
   - Recommend transaction batching strategies based on access patterns
   - Identify table scans that could cause broad page locking
   - Suggest covering indexes to avoid table page access entirely

4. **EXPLAIN CONCURRENT**
   - New EXPLAIN variant showing concurrency analysis alongside query plan
   - JSON output for tooling integration
   - Diff mode: compare two queries for potential conflict overlap
   - Show: estimated_pages_locked, conflict_risk_per_table, suggested_indexes

**Implementation:**
- Extend CodegenContext in `fsqlite-vdbe` with lock analysis metadata
- New EXPLAIN handler in `fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs`
- Query plan annotation framework in `fsqlite-planner`
- Consume conflict statistics from bd-t6sv2.1 for historical risk

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-planner/src/ (lock footprint estimation during planning)
- crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/ (EXPLAIN CONCURRENT output generation)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (EXPLAIN CONCURRENT handler)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (consume conflict stats from bd-t6sv2.1)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
Lock prediction is purely advisory and read-only. It MUST NOT alter query execution, introduce additional locks, or change transaction behavior. The EXPLAIN CONCURRENT output is informational only.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: lock prediction accuracy for known query patterns
  - Log: query_sql, predicted_pages, predicted_tables, conflict_risk_level
  - Verify: table scan predicts higher page count than index scan
  - Verify: covering index scan predicts zero table page accesses
  - Verify: same query produces deterministic predictions (plan stability)
- Unit: conflict probability calculation
  - Log: table_name, historical_conflicts, access_pattern, risk_level (low|medium|high), confidence
  - Verify: risk level correlates with actual conflict rates from test workloads
- Integration: EXPLAIN CONCURRENT output format correctness
  - Log: explain_rows, json_valid, fields_present, annotation_count
  - Verify: JSON output parseable and contains all required fields
  - Verify: text output human-readable and aligned
- Integration: advisor recommendations reduce actual conflicts
  - Log: query_before, suggestion, query_after, conflicts_before, conflicts_after
  - Scenario: table scan query -> advisor suggests index -> verify fewer page locks
  - Scenario: wide row table -> advisor suggests narrower access pattern
- E2E: full EXPLAIN CONCURRENT workflow with concurrent writers
  - Log: query_count, total_predictions, prediction_accuracy_pct
  - Verify: predictions correlate with actual runtime conflict behavior
  - Verify: diff mode correctly identifies overlapping page access between two queries
- E2E: EXPLAIN CONCURRENT does not affect query performance
  - Log: query_time_without_explain_ms, query_time_with_explain_ms, overhead_pct
  - Verify: overhead < 5% for EXPLAIN CONCURRENT vs regular EXPLAIN

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_explain_concurrent.sh that:
1. Runs EXPLAIN CONCURRENT on a set of known queries
2. Compares predictions against actual runtime conflict behavior
3. Verifies advisor suggestions produce measurable improvement
4. Validates JSON output format
5. Outputs pass/fail with accuracy statistics

**Success Criteria:**
- Developers predict conflicts before runtime with reasonable accuracy
- Query optimization considers concurrency impact
- Anti-patterns caught at plan time with actionable suggestions
- EXPLAIN CONCURRENT output integrates with external query analysis tools

## Acceptance Criteria
Canonical pass/fail contract is tracked in the issue's structured `acceptance_criteria` field. This section is kept in sync for template conformance and planning hygiene.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Implementation is complete and behaviorally correct against explicit invariants and edge-case requirements, including fault and recovery paths where applicable. 2. Comprehensive unit/property tests cover normal, boundary, and adversarial conditions with deterministic fixtures and regression seeds. 3. End-to-end scenario scripts validate integrated behavior in real execution flows and include deterministic replay instructions. 4. Structured logging/metrics (traceable IDs, timing, counters, error context) are emitted and validated so failures are diagnosable and auditable.

title: Checkpoint Scheduling Advisor
description:
**Idea #7 - Phase 2**

Intelligent checkpoint scheduling based on workload analysis. Checkpoint timing directly impacts write amplification (bd-t6sv2.9) and is informed by transaction lifecycle data (bd-t6sv2.5).

**Components:**
1. **WALMonitor**
   - Track WAL size over time (pages, bytes)
   - Write rate estimation (pages/second, rolling window)
   - Checkpoint duration history (with variance tracking)
   - Build on existing checkpoint infrastructure in `checkpoint_executor.rs` (22KB)

2. **CheckpointPredictor**
   - Estimate time until WAL threshold reached
   - Predict checkpoint impact on writers (based on active transaction count from bd-t6sv2.5)
   - Model write stall probability (based on WAL growth rate vs checkpoint throughput)

3. **SchedulingAdvisor**
   - Recommend checkpoint timing: "Checkpoint now: low write activity detected"
   - Warn: "WAL growth rate exceeds checkpoint throughput - consider TRUNCATE mode"
   - Suggest: "Optimal checkpoint window: low-activity period detected at [time range]"
   - Alert: "WAL size exceeds N pages - checkpoint urgently needed"

4. **AutoCheckpoint Enhancement**
   - Adaptive auto_checkpoint threshold based on workload patterns
   - Write-rate-aware scheduling (delay checkpoint during write bursts)
   - Low-activity window detection (checkpoint during quiet periods)
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_checkpoint_schedule for manual override

**Implementation:**
- Extend `crates/fsqlite-wal/src/checkpoint_executor.rs` with metrics collection
- Add workload analysis to `crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal.rs`
- New PRAGMAs for checkpoint scheduling in `fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs`
- Consume transaction lifecycle data from bd-t6sv2.5

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-wal/src/checkpoint_executor.rs (metrics, adaptive scheduling)
- crates/fsqlite-wal/src/checkpoint.rs (checkpoint mode analysis)
- crates/fsqlite-wal/src/wal.rs (WAL size tracking, write rate estimation)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (new PRAGMAs)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (shared infrastructure)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
Checkpoint scheduling MUST NOT block concurrent writers unnecessarily. Adaptive scheduling may DELAY checkpoints (not block writers). The auto_checkpoint threshold adjustment must preserve the property that writers are never blocked waiting for a checkpoint to start.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: WAL size tracking accuracy
  - Log: wal_pages, wal_bytes, writes_since_last_checkpoint, growth_rate_pages_per_sec
  - Verify: tracked size matches actual WAL file size
  - Verify: growth rate calculation stable over rolling window
- Unit: checkpoint duration prediction accuracy
  - Log: predicted_duration_ms, actual_duration_ms, prediction_error_pct, wal_pages
  - Verify: prediction within 20% of actual for steady-state workloads
- Unit: advisor threshold triggers
  - Log: advisor_type (checkpoint_now|wal_growth_warning|optimal_window|urgent), threshold, actual_value
  - Verify: each advisor type fires at exactly the configured threshold
  - Verify: no advisories when WAL growth is within normal bounds
- Integration: adaptive scheduling reduces write stalls
  - Log: stall_count_baseline, stall_count_adaptive, improvement_pct, checkpoint_count
  - Scenario: bursty write workload with baseline vs adaptive scheduling
  - Verify: adaptive scheduling produces fewer write stalls
- Integration: checkpoint scheduling respects active transactions
  - Log: active_txn_count, checkpoint_delayed, delay_reason, eventual_checkpoint_time_ms
  - Verify: checkpoint delayed when many active transactions
  - Verify: checkpoint eventually completes (no indefinite delay)
- E2E: full adaptive scheduling under realistic workload
  - Log: total_writes, total_checkpoints, avg_wal_size_pages, max_wal_size_pages, stall_rate_pct
  - Verify: WAL size bounded without manual tuning
  - Verify: checkpoint timing correlates with low-activity periods
- E2E: PRAGMA override correctly controls scheduling
  - Log: pragma_value, scheduled_checkpoint_time_ms, actual_checkpoint_time_ms
  - Verify: manual PRAGMA overrides adaptive scheduling

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_checkpoint_scheduling.sh that:
1. Runs a bursty write workload with default checkpoint settings
2. Runs the same workload with adaptive checkpoint scheduling
3. Compares stall counts and WAL growth patterns
4. Verifies advisor recommendations match workload characteristics
5. Outputs pass/fail with comparative statistics

**Success Criteria:**
- Checkpoint never surprises high-write workloads with unexpected stalls
- WAL growth bounded without manual tuning in common workloads
- Operators understand checkpoint behavior and can override when needed
- Write stall rate measurably reduced by adaptive scheduling

## Acceptance Criteria
Canonical pass/fail contract is tracked in the issue's structured `acceptance_criteria` field. This section is kept in sync for template conformance and planning hygiene.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Implementation is complete and behaviorally correct against explicit invariants and edge-case requirements, including fault and recovery paths where applicable. 2. Comprehensive unit/property tests cover normal, boundary, and adversarial conditions with deterministic fixtures and regression seeds. 3. End-to-end scenario scripts validate integrated behavior in real execution flows and include deterministic replay instructions. 4. Structured logging/metrics (traceable IDs, timing, counters, error context) are emitted and validated so failures are diagnosable and auditable.

title: Page Cache Efficiency Monitor
description:
**Idea #8 - Phase 2**

Expose page cache behavior for tuning and debugging. The ARC cache implementation lives in `fsqlite-pager/src/arc_cache.rs` (113KB) and is critical for MVCC performance since it keys on `(PageNumber, TxnId)` for version coexistence.

**Components:**
1. **CacheMetrics**
   - Hit rate (overall, per-table estimated via page-to-table mapping)
   - Eviction frequency and patterns (T1 vs T2 evictions)
   - Dirty page ratio over time
   - MVCC version coexistence overhead (pages with multiple versions cached)

2. **ARCAnalyzer**
   - ARC ghost list (B1/B2) effectiveness: ghost hit rate indicates ARC adaptation quality
   - T1/T2 balance: target parameter `p` tracking over time
   - Adaptation history: how `p` responds to workload changes
   - MVCC-specific: version chain depth per cached page

3. **CacheAdvisor**
   - Recommend cache size adjustments based on working set analysis
   - Identify tables with poor cache affinity (high eviction rate)
   - Suggest covering index strategies to reduce page cache pressure
   - Alert: "MVCC version chains consuming N% of cache capacity"

4. **CacheDiagnostics**
   - PRAGMA fsqlite_cache_stats: hit_rate_pct, eviction_count, dirty_ratio_pct, t1_size, t2_size, b1_size, b2_size, p_target
   - Virtual table: fsqlite_cache_pages (pgno, version_txn_id, in_t1_or_t2, dirty, ref_count, access_count)
   - Per-page access frequency for working set identification

**Implementation:**
- Extend ArcCache in `arc_cache.rs` with lightweight counters (atomic increments)
- Add PRAGMA handlers in `fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs`
- Virtual table for page-level inspection in `fsqlite-core`
- Use shared observability infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.1

**Files to Modify:**
- crates/fsqlite-pager/src/arc_cache.rs (counter instrumentation)
- crates/fsqlite-pager/src/pager.rs (aggregate metrics)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/pragma.rs (new PRAGMAs)
- crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs (virtual table registration)
- crates/fsqlite-observability/ (shared infrastructure from bd-t6sv2.1)

**CRITICAL: MVCC Preservation**
Cache monitoring MUST NOT change eviction decisions or cache behavior. All counters use atomic operations to avoid introducing synchronization. The virtual table MUST NOT pin pages or prevent eviction while returning results. Observer is purely read-only.

**Test Requirements:**
- Unit: hit rate calculation accuracy
  - Log: total_accesses, hits, misses, hit_rate_pct, measurement_window_ms
  - Verify: hit_rate = hits / total_accesses within floating point tolerance
  - Verify: counters reset correctly via PRAGMA fsqlite_cache_reset
- Unit: ARC parameter tracking
  - Log: p_target, t1_size, t2_size, b1_hits, b2_hits, adaptation_events
  - Verify: p increases on B1 ghost hit (recency signal)
  - Verify: p decreases on B2 ghost hit (frequency signal)
- Unit: MVCC version coexistence tracking
  - Log: pages_with_multiple_versions, max_version_chain_depth, cache_mvcc_overhead_pct
  - Verify: version count matches actual concurrent transaction count
- Integration: cache metrics under controlled workload
  - Log: workload_type (sequential|random|zipfian), hit_rate_pct, eviction_count, p_steady_state
  - Scenario: sequential scan -> verify low hit rate, T1 dominant
  - Scenario: zipfian access -> verify high hit rate, T2 dominant
  - Scenario: scan + point queries -> verify ARC adapts p correctly
- Integration: virtual table reflects actual cache state
  - Log: cached_pages, dirty_pages, pinned_pages, query_time_us
  - Verify: virtual table query does not alter cache state
  - Verify: returned data consistent with actual cache contents
- E2E: cache tuning recommendations verified
  - Log: cache_size_before, advisor_recommendation, cache_size_after, hit_rate_before, hit_rate_after
  - Verify: following advisor recommendations improves hit rate
  - Verify: MVCC version pressure advisory triggers when appropriate
- E2E: monitoring overhead measurement
  - Log: throughput_without_monitoring, throughput_with_monitoring, overhead_pct
  - Verify: monitoring overhead < 2% for typical workloads

**Verification Script:**
Create scripts/verify_cache_monitor.sh that:
1. Runs workloads with known cache behavior patterns
2. Verifies PRAGMA stats match expected hit rates
3. Queries virtual table and validates page-level data
4. Tests ARC adaptation under workload changes
5. Measures monitoring overhead
6. Outputs pass/fail with evidence JSON

**Success Criteria:**
- Cache behavior no longer a black box for operators
- Tuning decisions data-driven with clear metrics
- Memory pressure from MVCC versions detected early
- Monitoring overhead negligible (< 2%)

## Acceptance Criteria
Canonical pass/fail contract is tracked in the issue's structured `acceptance_criteria` field. This section is kept in sync for template conformance and planning hygiene.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Implementation is complete and behaviorally correct against explicit invariants and edge-case requirements, including fault and recovery paths where applicable. 2. Comprehensive unit/property tests cover normal, boundary, and adversarial conditions with deterministic fixtures and regression seeds. 3. End-to-end scenario scripts validate integrated behavior in real execution flows and include deterministic replay instructions. 4.
