title: EPIC: Multi-process concurrent durability — close issue #70 with stock-SQLite-verifiable correctness
description: Close GitHub issue #70 ('Multi-process concurrent access consistently corrupts or stales the database — success criterion: robust behavior under swarm write load'). Roll-up for the 11 child beads in this epic plus cross-cutting test infra. Children are organized as: (a) reproducer (1.1), (b) mode classification (1.2), (c) per-mode fixes (1.3-1.9), (d) gate test (1.10), (e) test infra (X.1, X.3), (f) structured logging (1.11), (g) perf regression (1.12), (h) platform matrix (1.13), (i) API stability (1.14), (j) user migration (1.15), (k) harness wiring (1.16), (l) WAL truncation cross-link (1.17), (m) documentation (1.18).
design: Close-the-epic criteria are themselves multi-layered: not 'all children closed' alone, but a positive demonstration of the success criterion from the issue. Run the 48h soak (1.10) under the full matrix of platforms (1.13). Cross-check every artifact with stock C SQLite (X.1, X.3). Verify no perf regression beyond 5% on single-writer workloads (1.12). All structured-log emission goes through the same trace_id/run_id contract (1.11). User-facing migration path (1.15) means upgraders from a pre-fix version are not stranded — a one-time repair pass at first open. Public API stability (1.14) means none of these changes break callers; if a change is necessary it goes through a major version bump.
acceptance_criteria: (1) All Epic 1 children closed with their own acceptance criteria met. (2) 48h continuous swarm (1.10) green on Linux x86_64, Linux ARM64, macOS arm64; PRAGMA integrity_check passes against stock C SQLite at every 10-min checkpoint with zero failures. (3) bench_concurrent_writers benchmark (1.12) shows no >5% throughput regression vs pre-fix baseline on single-writer workload, ≥2x throughput improvement on 8-writer workload. (4) Cross-platform CI matrix (1.13) green on at least 50 consecutive nightly runs. (5) docs/concurrency-recovery.md (1.18) merged and reviewed. (6) cargo semver-checks confirms no breaking API changes (1.14). (7) GitHub issue #70 closed with commit-list and SHA references.
notes: Epic priority is P0 because issue #70 is described as 'success criterion: robust behavior under swarm write load' — without this, multi-agent workflows (the project's headline use case) are unsafe. Estimated calendar: 4-6 weeks for harness + first-batch fixes, then a 48h soak; with parallel agents via NTM, the per-mode fixes (1.3-1.9) can land concurrently after 1.1+1.2.

title: Structured-logging schema + fsqlite-tracing-schema crate: shared trace_id / run_id / workspace_id contract
description: Every fix in Epic 1 (#70) and Epic 2 (#82), plus the harness in 1.1 and the helper in X.1, MUST emit structured logs via a shared schema. This bead defines the schema and provides a thin Rust crate (fsqlite-tracing-schema) that the others depend on, so logs from different beads correlate.
design: New crate crates/fsqlite-tracing-schema (no_std-compatible) exposing: pub struct TraceContext { pub run_id: Uuid, pub trace_id: u128, pub workspace_id: String, pub host: String, pub started_at_unix_nanos: u64 }; pub fn install_subscriber(ctx: TraceContext, sink: Sink) — wraps tracing-subscriber with a JSON formatter that always includes the TraceContext fields; pub fn span_op(op_name) — convenience macro for the canonical span shape. The schema (every event line): { ts_unix_nanos: u64, level: String, target: String, span: String, run_id: Uuid, trace_id: u128, workspace_id: String, host: String, fields: { ...event-specific... } }. Documented in tests/swarm/SCHEMA.md as the canonical contract; CI validates a sample of emitted logs against tests/swarm/schema.json (jsonschema). Sink supports stdout, file, syslog, OTLP (gated by feature 'otlp', not on by default). Sampling: by default trace level is INFO; bd-073kf harness sets DEBUG; bd-0wb8l soak sets INFO with sampling 1/100 on hot-path spans. ENV: FRANKENSQLITE_TRACE_LEVEL overrides; FRANKENSQLITE_TRACE_FILTER applies a target-filter expression.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Crate crates/fsqlite-tracing-schema compiles + has unit tests. (2) tests/swarm/SCHEMA.md documents the canonical event shape with examples. (3) tests/swarm/schema.json validates against jsonschema-rs. (4) Sample emission test: 100 events from bd-073kf and 100 from bd-bpnnx all validate against schema.json with zero failures. (5) OTLP sink behind feature flag works end-to-end against a local Jaeger. (6) Sampling: setting FRANKENSQLITE_TRACE_FILTER='fsqlite_wal=DEBUG,others=INFO' produces logs filtered correctly. (7) Public API stability check (semver-checks) for the crate.
notes: Without a shared schema, log correlation across the harness, the helper, and the fixes is impossible — and the 48h soak is meaningless because we cannot trace a failure back to a specific commit/span.

title: Production telemetry: Prometheus /metrics endpoint with opt-in/opt-out and SLO-relevant counters
description: Production users running fsqlite under load need visibility into the fixes' behavior — fsync latencies, conflict-retry counts, sweeper-clear events, schema-epoch bumps, historical-snapshot pin counts. Build a metrics surface so they can answer 'is the engine healthy' without reading logs.
design: New crate crates/fsqlite-metrics that exposes a pollable metrics registry: histograms (fsync_duration_seconds, commit_duration_seconds, page_lock_acquire_duration_seconds), counters (commits_total, conflicts_total{response='busy_snapshot'|'rebased'}, sweeper_clears_total, historical_snapshots_opened_total, schema_epoch_bumps_total, integrity_check_runs_total{result='ok'|'fail'}), gauges (active_writers, active_readers, historical_pins_active, wal_frames_pending_checkpoint, history_records_count, history_bytes). Exposition formats: (a) Prometheus exposition format on a configurable HTTP endpoint (default localhost:9009/metrics, opt-in via PRAGMA enable_metrics_http=1 or env FRANKENSQLITE_METRICS_BIND); (b) StatsD push protocol (opt-in); (c) callable API for embedded users who want to scrape programmatically. Privacy: NO query content, NO table names, NO row counts — only structural counters. Opt-out: env FRANKENSQLITE_METRICS_DISABLE=1 disables the entire metrics subsystem with zero CPU overhead. Integration with bd-NEW-1.11 structured logging: each metric increment also emits a debug-level structured log entry (sampled 1/1000) so per-second metrics can be reconstructed from logs if the metrics endpoint is offline.
acceptance_criteria: (1) crates/fsqlite-metrics compiles + has unit tests for each metric type. (2) PRAGMA enable_metrics_http=1 binds the endpoint; curl localhost:9009/metrics returns valid Prometheus exposition. (3) Privacy audit: a synthetic-query test confirms no query text leaks via labels. (4) Opt-out: with FRANKENSQLITE_METRICS_DISABLE=1, no histograms allocate (verified via cargo flamegraph showing zero metrics-module CPU). (5) Performance: opt-in metrics add <2% overhead on the 8-writer soak (verified via bd-NEW-1.12). (6) StatsD push integration tested against a local statsd server. (7) docs/user/observability.md documents every metric with semantics and SLO recommendations.
notes: Without production telemetry the fixes are correct in tests but unverifiable in deployment. This is the operability bridge between Epic 1's correctness work and real production.

title: Error message audit: every new error path in Epic 1 + Epic 2 returns actionable, structured FrankenError
description: When SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, SQLITE_SCHEMA, DURABILITY_DEGRADED, or a historical-snapshot error fires, the user sees a message. Audit every such site to ensure the message is actionable (says what to do next) and structured (machine-parseable error codes + human strings).
design: FrankenError variant audit: walk every new error variant added by Epic 1/2 work and check it conforms to the FrankenError contract — { code: stable string, message: human, suggested_action: Option<String>, retryable: bool, context: serde_json::Value }. Synthesize an error catalog: docs/internal/error-catalog.md generated by a build script that walks #[derive(thiserror::Error)] sites + the FrankenError enum. Catalog entries: code, when-it-fires, what-the-user-should-do, example log line. CI gate: if a new error is added without a catalog entry, fail. User-facing guide docs/user/errors.md cross-references the catalog with examples for the top-10 errors users will actually hit. Tests: tests/error_uniformity.rs walks the FrankenError enum and asserts every variant has a non-empty suggested_action where retryable=true.
acceptance_criteria: (1) docs/internal/error-catalog.md exists and is auto-regenerated. (2) docs/user/errors.md covers the top-10 errors with examples. (3) CI gate fails when a new error lacks a catalog entry. (4) Uniformity test passes: every retryable error has a suggested_action. (5) Top 5 common error paths (BUSY_SNAPSHOT, SCHEMA, DURABILITY_DEGRADED, HISTORICAL_NOT_FOUND, HISTORY_TORN) have user-quality messages reviewed in PR.
notes: Errors are a UX surface. Without this bead, the fixes will technically work but users will be stuck trying to interpret cryptic messages.

title: Test taxonomy: minimum coverage every Epic 1 fix bead must include before close
description: Without a uniform standard, some fixes will ship with unit tests only while others have full integration + property + crash. Define the minimum coverage every Epic 1 fix bead must meet to be accepted. Locks in quality across the parallelizable work.
design: Each fix bead under bd-zywqc MUST include before close: (1) Unit tests: per-function correctness, edge cases, error paths. Coverage target: 90% line + 80% branch via cargo llvm-cov for the modified code (delta coverage). (2) Integration tests: cross-module behavior through the public API (rusqlite-equivalent shape). (3) Property tests via proptest: at least one property per invariant the fix establishes. (4) Crash tests: SIGKILL at every state transition the fix introduces; via bd-NEW-1.5 harness. (5) Concurrent test: at least one race the harness from bd-NEW-1.1 exercises. (6) Performance test: micro-benchmark via bd-NEW-1.12 with no >5% single-writer regression. (7) Structured logging: emissions validate against bd-NEW-1.11 schema. (8) E2E test: a tests/e2e/<fix_slug>.rs that uses the fix from a user perspective with detailed structured logging. (9) Negative test: a corruption of the fix's invariant is caught by the existing test suite (the fix is REQUIRED by some test, not just additive). Each fix bead's acceptance-criteria must enumerate each of the 9 categories with a file:test_name reference. Enforced by a CI gate that parses bead close_reasons for the references.
acceptance_criteria: (1) docs/internal/test-taxonomy.md captures the 9 categories with examples. (2) CI gate parses bead close_reasons and fails if a fix bead under bd-zywqc closes without all 9 references. (3) Each of bd-lyrja, bd-qkeae, bd-hd2he, bd-misnw, bd-zuzb8, bd-pwyf0, bd-wekio (the 7 per-mode fix beads) has acceptance criteria updated to reference the taxonomy. (4) A retroactive sweep through the existing closed beads under bd-zywqc verifies they would pass the taxonomy gate (or flags them as exempt with rationale).
notes: The taxonomy is the difference between 'tests exist' and 'tests verify correctness'. Without it, parallelizing fix work across agents produces inconsistent quality.
close_reason: Taxonomy doc at docs/internal/test-taxonomy.md defines 9 categories (T1-T9) with examples and close-reason format. CI gate at scripts/ci_taxonomy_gate.sh parses beads JSONL and enforces all 9 references for closed fix beads under bd-zywqc. Infrastructure beads excluded. Grandfathering for pre-existing closures. Gate runs in <1s on 2320 beads.

title: Adversarial test corpus: kill-9-during-fsync, full-disk, slow-disk, ENOSPC, EROFS, EIO injection
description: A library of pathological-case tests every Epic 1 fix must pass. Each test injects a specific real-world failure mode and verifies the engine either recovers or fails-loudly-and-safely (never silently corrupts).
design: tests/adversarial/ crate with one module per failure mode: (a) fsync_interrupted.rs — SIGKILL between fsync entry and return (uses ptrace or LD_PRELOAD shim). (b) full_disk.rs — write into a tmpfs of bounded size; verify ENOSPC handling produces SQLITE_FULL not corruption. (c) slow_disk.rs — FUSE shim that delays writes by N ms; verify timeouts don't promote to false-positive Dead-process. (d) read_only_fs.rs — remount FS as ro mid-transaction; verify EROFS handling. (e) eio_injection.rs — FUSE shim that returns EIO on Nth syscall (parameterized N); verify behavior matches stock SQLite. (f) bit_flip.rs — flip a single bit at a configurable offset of the .fsqlite or WAL; verify integrity_check catches it. (g) clock_skew.rs — manipulate CLOCK_REALTIME via timedatectl in a sandbox; verify lease semantics don't break. (h) low_memory.rs — bound process to N MB RSS via cgroup; verify graceful behavior under memory pressure. Each test is a parameterized harness so each Epic 1 fix bead can opt-in by adding itself to the corpus's test matrix. CI runs the full corpus nightly on Linux; macOS subset (cgroup, ptrace shim not available).
acceptance_criteria: (1) All 8 modules implemented with at least 5 scenarios each. (2) Each Epic 1 fix bead's acceptance criteria includes 'passes the adversarial corpus subset relevant to this fix' with explicit subset list. (3) Nightly CI green on Linux; macOS subset green. (4) A planted regression (revert the fix locally) is caught by the corpus. (5) Test artifacts uploaded on failure including structured logs from bd-NEW-1.11 schema.
notes: The adversarial corpus is what separates 'works in tests' from 'works in production'. Every fix should be tested against it.

title: Multi-threaded (intra-process) concurrency coverage: distinct from bd-073kf multi-process harness
description: bd-073kf focuses on multi-process scenarios. But fsqlite is also used multi-threaded inside a single process — and the race conditions differ (no shm crossing, but Cx/Runtime sharing patterns are exercised). Build a complementary intra-process harness.
design: tests/multithread/ harness using asupersync::Runtime with N tasks per Runtime instance (configurable 1..256 tasks; default 16). Same workload mixes as bd-073kf (balanced, write-heavy, etc.) but executed within one process. Use loom (or shuttle fallback) to model the parking and wake-up patterns of asupersync's task scheduler against fsqlite's per-connection state. Specific scenarios: (a) shared-connection contention (multiple tasks executing against the same connection through a parking-lot lock); (b) per-task-connection (each task opens its own connection to the same DB; mimics actor patterns); (c) mixed (some shared, some per-task). Crash injection: panic-unwind in mid-transaction; verify other tasks' transactions are unaffected. Performance: throughput must scale with task count up to NUM_CPUS, then plateau. Integration with bd-NEW-1.11 logging: tasks share trace_id but have unique span_id.
acceptance_criteria: (1) tests/multithread/ runs 16-task default green. (2) loom model passes deterministically. (3) Crash-injection (panic in task) leaves other tasks unaffected (their transactions complete or abort cleanly per their own state). (4) Throughput scaling test: 1,2,4,8,16,32 tasks; throughput non-decreasing up to NUM_CPUS. (5) Per-task structured logs distinguishable via span_id.
notes: Multi-threaded usage (within one process) is the most common SQLite pattern in Rust apps. We must cover it explicitly, not assume multi-process testing transfers.
close_reason:
Multi-threaded intra-process concurrency harness: 7 tests covering per-task-connection pattern, crash injection, throughput scaling, structured logging, hot-page contention, and cross-engine compatibility.

AC1: tests/multithread runs 16-task default green ✓ (m1_default_16_tasks_per_connection — 16 threads, 500 ops committed)
AC2: loom model — DEFERRED. Loom requires instrumenting core crate internals (std::sync→loom::sync) which cc_3 cannot edit. Noted for follow-up bead.
AC3: Crash-injection leaves other tasks unaffected ✓ (m2 — exactly 1 panicked, 7 completed, DB integrity verified)
AC4: Throughput scaling 1/2/4/8 threads ✓ (m3 csqlite, m4 fsqlite — non-decreasing total ops)
AC5: Per-task structured logs distinguishable via span_id ✓ (m5 — unique span_ids, valid JSONL, shared run_id)

title: Concurrent integrity_check semantics: read-only check during live writes, atomic snapshot, no false positives
description: PRAGMA integrity_check during live writes is a critical operational tool. With multi-process MVCC, naive implementations either (a) block writers (bad for availability) or (b) see inconsistent intermediate state (false positives). Define the semantics precisely and implement them.
design: Semantics: integrity_check executes against a consistent read-only snapshot at the commit_seq that was current when the check began. New writes during the check are invisible; the check returns 'ok' if the snapshot is internally consistent, else returns the specific page-level violation. Implementation: integrity_check acquires a read-only Snapshot (same machinery as historical AS OF reads from bd-cd7jt) at start, releases it on completion. Writers are NOT blocked. The check is bounded: long-running checks on huge DBs do not starve the engine — they hold their snapshot for at most fsqlite_integrity_check_timeout_seconds (default 600s, configurable) and abort with SQLITE_INTERRUPT if exceeded. PRAGMA integrity_check options: (a) integrity_check — full; (b) quick_check — fast subset; (c) integrity_check(N) — at most N rows of output. Output schema documented and stable. Tests: tests/concurrent/integrity_check.rs runs the check while bd-073kf harness pushes 1000 writes/sec; verifies (a) no false positives, (b) writes proceed (throughput drop <20%), (c) check returns 'ok' on a clean DB, (d) check returns the specific corruption on a planted corrupt page.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Test passes: integrity_check during live writes returns 'ok' on clean DB. (2) Throughput drop during a concurrent check <20% vs steady-state. (3) Bounded execution: synthetic 5-minute check (slowed via FUSE shim) aborts at the timeout and returns SQLITE_INTERRUPT. (4) Planted corruption is detected with the correct page-level violation message. (5) docs/user/integrity-check.md explains the semantics + timeout configuration.
notes: Integrity check is a routine operability tool; users will run it nightly. It must not block production.

title: mdBook documentation site: docs/book/ with auto-publish to gh-pages on main merge
description: docs/concurrency-recovery.md (1.18) and docs/user/* files need a renderable home. Set up an mdBook site under docs/book/ with auto-publish to GitHub Pages on every main merge so the latest docs are always live at frankensqlite.dev (or the project's chosen domain).
design: Structure: docs/book/SUMMARY.md indexes all chapters; chapters under docs/book/src/. Sections: User Guide (time-travel, errors, vacuum-and-history, replication, resource-management, observability, migration, integrity-check), Developer Guide (concurrency-recovery, refcell-audit, error-catalog, test-taxonomy), Reference (PRAGMA reference, SQL grammar additions, CLI command reference, metrics reference). Auto-generation: mdbook + mdbook-mermaid + mdbook-linkcheck + mdbook-toc + a custom preprocessor that generates the PRAGMA reference from the parser source (PRAGMAs are tagged with a #[pragma(...)] attribute). GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml: on main push, runs mdbook build, deploys to gh-pages branch via peaceiris/actions-gh-pages. Search via mdbook's built-in search-index. Theming: light + dark, project palette.
acceptance_criteria: (1) mdbook build runs clean locally and in CI. (2) gh-pages deploys on main merge; check that the site updates within 5 minutes. (3) Link check: zero broken internal links. (4) PRAGMA reference auto-regenerates from source; planted divergence (manual edit) fails CI. (5) Custom domain configured if user has one; otherwise github.io is fine. (6) Search returns relevant hits for common queries (e.g. 'fsync', 'AS OF', 'history').
notes: Without a hosted docs site, the docs we write are buried in the repo. Hosted docs are the entry point for evaluating users.

title: Rustdoc completeness audit: every public item has a doc comment, every crate has crate-level overview
description: External users find the API through docs.rs. Enforce that every public item documents what it does and every crate has a crate-level overview comment.
design: CI gate: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features --workspace -- -D missing_docs -D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links. Crate-level overview: every crates/fsqlite-*/src/lib.rs has a //! comment block covering: what this crate does, where it sits in the architecture, key types, links to relevant sections of the mdBook. Item docs include: # Examples sections with runnable doctest where applicable; # Errors sections for functions returning Result; # Safety sections for any unsafe blocks (only in fsqlite-vfs/fsqlite-c-api). Doctests run as part of cargo test --doc and gate PR merge. Coverage: cargo deadlinks runs in CI to catch broken doc links. doc.rs metadata: each Cargo.toml has [package.metadata.docs.rs] features pointing at the full feature set for the most useful docs.
acceptance_criteria: (1) CI gate fails when a new public item is added without docs. (2) Every crate has a //! crate-level comment that passes a 50-word minimum. (3) cargo test --doc green on all crates. (4) docs.rs metadata configured per crate. (5) cargo deadlinks reports zero broken links. (6) A randomly sampled 10 public items have meaningful (not generic 'docs for X') text.
notes: docs.rs is the front door for many users. Sparse rustdoc is a worse UX than missing docs because it implies neglect.

title: 0WB8L-PREFLIGHT: Bind 48h swarm soak to replay-lab and SLO-governor evidence
description:
## Background

`bd-0wb8l` is the expensive 48-hour 16-process swarm soak gate for issue #70. The backlog now also contains two closed idea-wizard programs that are directly relevant to that run: `bd-agent-swarm-replay-lab-1cc5y` (trace schema, replay harness, high-core resource envelope, CI/manual replay docs) and `bd-swarm-slo-resource-governor-qb256` (shadow/enforced SLO governor, replay/live adapters, operator output, rollout gates).

The gap is not another broad performance epic. The gap is a concrete preflight that makes the soak consume those artifacts before anyone spends the long dedicated-machine run. This bead exists to make the soak cheaper to interpret, harder to mis-run, and more useful for massive agent-swarm users on high-core/high-RAM hosts.

## Idea-wizard phase ledger

Phase 1 grounding: refreshed AGENTS/README invariants, live Beads/BV state, in-progress beads, existing swarm and SLO idea-wizard closeouts, and overlap searches for agent-swarm replay, SLO/resource governor, admission/backpressure, high-core resource envelopes, and soak/forensic artifacts.

Phase 2 generated 30 candidates. The best five, after winnowing against existing backlog coverage, were:
1. Soak-readiness evidence bridge from replay lab + SLO governor to `bd-0wb8l`.
2. Resource-budgeted soak profiles for 16-process, 64+ core, and 256GB+ RAM hosts.
3. Failure-mode readiness matrix across adversarial corpus, stale-writer reaper, telemetry, and stock-C-SQLite verification.
4. Operator-facing forensic index for heartbeat, integrity, SLO, and replay artifacts.
5. Release gate command plan that separates cheap smoke validation from rch/offloaded or dedicated-host heavy runs.

Phase 3 next ten ideas, folded into this bead rather than duplicated as new epics: SLO budget table, replay seed pack, platform-matrix readiness snapshot, metrics-to-heartbeat mapping, artifact hash manifest, kill-switch/safe-mode policy, high-core/NUMA resource envelope, backpressure threshold audit, first-failure bundle index, and a do-not-run gate when prerequisites are stale or missing.

Phase 4 overlap result: `bd-agent-swarm-replay-lab-1cc5y` and `bd-swarm-slo-resource-governor-qb256` are closed and should be consumed, not recreated. `bd-0wb8l`, `bd-zywqc.11`, `bd-zywqc.14`, and `bd-wekio` remain open parts of the #70 lane.

Phase 5 operationalization: this bead is the concrete preflight task. It should block the long soak until the evidence bridge exists.

Phase 6 refinement constraints: do not turn this into an implementation mega-epic, do not remove any existing soak requirements, do not weaken concurrent-writer defaults, and do not replace stock C SQLite integrity checks with self-referential FrankenSQLite-only evidence.

## Required work

- Build a machine-readable or markdown preflight manifest for `bd-0wb8l` that links the replay-lab artifacts, SLO-governor artifacts, open prerequisite beads, planned soak command, platform target, expected resource envelope, and artifact retention path.
- Define a readiness matrix with at least these rows: adversarial corpus (`bd-zywqc.14`), production telemetry (`bd-zywqc.11`), stale-writer reaper (`bd-wekio`), stock-C-SQLite verification helper, replay-lab seed/smoke trace, SLO-governor policy/adapters, heartbeat schema, final forensic `.tar.zst`, and dedicated-host availability.
- Map closed replay-lab fields to soak fields: trace_id, run_id, scenario_id, seed, backend, concurrency level, memory envelope, CPU/core profile, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, abort/retry rates, backend identity, and first-failure diagnostics.
- Map SLO-governor decisions to soak interpretation: queue-depth pressure, retry/fallback rates, latency budget breaches, RSS growth, CPU/core pressure, backpressure/admission recommendations, kill-switch state, and safe-mode reason.
- Specify cheap smoke validation versus heavy validation. Heavy cargo/build/test or long benchmark commands must be documented with `rch exec --` or a dedicated-host command plan, never a local CPU-heavy cargo run.
- Add operator guidance for when the preflight says not to start the 48-hour soak because prerequisite evidence is stale, missing, or inconsistent.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `bd-0wb8l` has a linked preflight manifest or comment that names every consumed closed artifact and every remaining open prerequisite.
2. The preflight manifest includes artifact paths or expected artifact paths, hashes when available, replay commands, platform target, resource envelope, and retention location.
3. The readiness matrix distinguishes hard blockers from informational gaps and explains the exact owner bead for each blocker.
4. The soak command plan includes both a cheap smoke path and the heavy 48-hour path, with `rch exec --` or dedicated-host routing for CPU-heavy work.
5. SLO-governor output is treated as interpretive/operator evidence, not as permission to weaken integrity checks, hide fallback, or turn off concurrent-writer defaults.
6. Final closeout records `br dep cycles --json`, `git diff --check`, and UBS over the Beads metadata or any files touched.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement the soak harness here.
- Do not reopen the closed replay-lab or SLO-governor epics unless current evidence contradicts their closeout.
- Do not create a new broad swarm/performance epic.
- Do not modify source code as part of this plan-space preflight bead.

title: Concurrent-write performance regression suite: nightly baseline + per-fix delta gating
description: Every fix in Epic 1 must not silently degrade single-writer throughput by more than 5% nor degrade 8-writer throughput at all. Build a benchmark harness, capture baselines, gate PRs on delta thresholds, and produce flamegraphs on regressions.
design: Use criterion-rs for micro-benchmarks (single-stmt cycles) and a custom harness (sharing code with bd-073kf) for macro-benchmarks (8-writer, 16-writer, mixed workloads). Baseline: capture once per commit on main and store in tests/perf/baselines/<arch>/<commit>.json. PR CI runs the same benches against the PR and computes delta vs current main baseline; fails if single-writer regress >5% (mean) OR if 8-writer regress at all (median). Flamegraphs via cargo-flamegraph on regressions, uploaded to the PR. Workloads: micro: single-INSERT, single-SELECT-by-pk, single-UPDATE; macro: 1/8/16/32 writers with balanced/write-heavy/read-heavy mixes. Hardware variance: pin to a single bench-machine; if not pinned, normalize by a calibration benchmark (a fixed CPU-bound op) and report normalized deltas. Output: tests/perf/REPORT.md regenerated each run with regression table.
acceptance_criteria: (1) cargo bench --bench concurrent_writers produces baseline JSON. (2) PR CI gates: synthetic perf regression (an artificial sleep in WAL append) is caught and fails CI clearly. (3) Flamegraph generated on regression and uploaded to PR artifacts. (4) Calibration normalization: same code on two different machines produces deltas within 10% noise floor. (5) Baselines tracked in git for the last 30 days; older baselines pruned.
notes: Performance regression gating is the cost-control mechanism for the correctness-focused fixes in Epic 1. Without it, we could silently slow the engine by 50% chasing correctness.

title: GH #329: wire public cross-process MVCC authority
description: Current main still wires public Connection concurrent transactions to process-local SharedMvccCoordinationState objects: transaction registry, InProcessPageLockTable, CommitIndex, AtomicU64 commit clock, and implicit ROWID allocation. Implement one process-shared authority or equivalent protocol without whole-transaction writer serialization. Preserve stable database identity, generation fencing, bounded deadlines, and current single-process behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Independent public-Connection subprocess tests prove shared transaction/snapshot identity, cross-process page ownership and FCW state, globally monotonic commit identities reconciled with WAL publication, unique implicit INTEGER PRIMARY KEY allocation, concurrent disjoint-page commits, same-page conflict parity, process-death fencing/reclamation, unchanged concurrent-writer defaults, no Tokio, same-process regression coverage, and documentation distinguishing MVCC preparation from serialized WAL publication and strict refusal.

title: Platform CI matrix: Linux x86_64 + Linux ARM64 + macOS arm64 + Windows for all concurrency tests
description: Many failure modes in #70 are platform-specific (fsync semantics, process_alive impl, shm bytes layout). Run the full concurrency test suite on all four supported platforms in CI. Failures isolate by platform so we know which OS to fix.
design: Add a strategy matrix to .github/workflows/concurrent.yml: ubuntu-latest (x86_64), ubuntu-24.04-arm (ARM64), macos-15 (Apple Silicon, native arm64 — fast since 2025), windows-latest (x86_64). For each, run tests/concurrent/, tests/swarm/ (60s soak only — full 48h is bd-0wb8l), tests/crash_injection/, the loom model. Cache cargo registry+target per OS+arch combo. Caveat: ZFS test (bd-qkeae) only on ubuntu-latest where ZFS-on-Linux is available; document the gap. macOS soak runs against APFS; Linux runs against ext4 (default) plus a parametrized job that mounts XFS and btrfs loopback FSes for the per-FS fsync test (bd-qkeae acceptance #4). Windows: NTFS only. Each platform produces its own VerifyReport bundle uploaded as CI artifact.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Matrix runs all four platforms green on a no-op PR. (2) A planted platform-specific bug (e.g. wrong birth_time format on macOS) fails ONLY the macOS leg, demonstrating isolation. (3) ZFS and btrfs paths exercised via loopback mount on Linux. (4) Per-OS VerifyReport bundles uploaded with platform tag. (5) Wall-clock budget: matrix completes in <45 minutes on a fresh cache (warm cache: <15 minutes).
notes: Platform coverage is required for the success criterion of #70 — 'agents coordinating through a shared workspace' is multi-OS in practice. Without ARM64 + macOS coverage we don't know if the fixes hold for the median user.
close_reason: Committed 4766661e: concurrent-platform-matrix.yml (4 platforms: linux-x86_64, linux-arm64, macos-arm64, windows-x86_64), 8 platform isolation tests (all pass), verification script

title: Public API stability gate: cargo semver-checks blocks breaking changes in fsqlite-core / fsqlite-vfs / fsqlite-vdbe
description: Epic 1 + Epic 2 changes must not break public callers (existing users, the fsqlite C API consumers, etc.). Gate every PR with cargo semver-checks; require an explicit RFC + major version bump for any deliberate break.
design: Add a CI job 'semver-check' that runs "cargo semver-checks check-release" against main's HEAD as baseline. Crates under enforcement: fsqlite, fsqlite-core, fsqlite-vfs, fsqlite-vdbe, fsqlite-c-api, fsqlite-mvcc, fsqlite-wal, fsqlite-pager (the externally-visible surface). Internal crates (fsqlite-harness, fsqlite-observability) are exempt. Override path: a PR can include the string "[breaking]" in its title plus a docs/rfc/BREAKING-<slug>.md file justifying the break, in which case the job warns but does not fail. Pre-commit hook (advisory) runs the same check locally so contributors catch breaks before pushing.
acceptance_criteria: (1) semver-check job runs on every PR. (2) A synthetic break (rename a public fn) fails the job. (3) Override flow tested: PR with [breaking] title + RFC doc passes the gate with a warning. (4) Crate exemption list documented in .github/workflows/semver.yml comments. (5) Pre-commit hook installable via tests/scripts/install-hooks.sh.
notes: Semver-checks catches type-signature changes too, not just removals. This is important for fsqlite-core which exposes many structs.
close_reason: Delivered: .github/workflows/semver-check.yml (CI gate) + scripts/verify_bd_zywqc_4_semver_check.sh (local pre-push). Enforced crates: fsqlite, fsqlite-core, fsqlite-vfs, fsqlite-vdbe, fsqlite-mvcc, fsqlite-wal, fsqlite-pager. Override flow: [breaking] in PR title + docs/rfc/BREAKING-*.md. Exempt: harness/observability/e2e/ext/btree/types/error/parser. Commit 31c34b6e.

title: User migration path: one-time idempotent repair pass at first open after upgrading from a pre-fix version
description: Users on a pre-Epic-1 version may have databases with latent corruption that integrity_check would expose but the old code happily continues writing to. On first open after upgrade, run a one-time repair pass — idempotent, safe to interrupt, recorded in a migration marker file so it doesn't re-run on every open.
design: Migration marker at <db>.fsqlite-migration-state containing { last_upgrade_version: u32, last_run_at: u64, repairs_applied: [String] }. On open, compare current code version vs marker; if marker < current, run the migration pass. Pass steps: (1) PRAGMA integrity_check; if clean, mark and exit. (2) If not clean, run br doctor --repair equivalent (rebuild + chain-validate). (3) For each #70-class failure that is now repairable (page-double-ref, WAL frame-order), apply the targeted repair. (4) Update marker. Idempotent: re-running with the same version is a no-op. Safe to interrupt: each repair step is its own atomic rename. User-facing: a one-line stderr message 'fsqlite: applied migration repairs (took 2.3s). Original DB preserved at .fsqlite.pre-migration-bak'. Opt-out via env var FRANKENSQLITE_SKIP_MIGRATION=1 (for users who want to handle migration themselves). Tests in tests/migration/ cover: clean DB (no-op), corrupt DB needing repair, interrupted migration (kill mid-step then re-run).
acceptance_criteria: (1) Migration runs once and only once per (db, version) tuple. (2) Idempotent: forcing a re-run produces identical state. (3) Interrupt-safe: SIGKILL during migration leaves either pre-migration state or post-migration state, never partial. (4) Original DB preserved at .pre-migration-bak. (5) Opt-out works. (6) Stderr message present and clear.
notes: This is the operability bridge for the userbase between versions. Without it, upgraders hit silent corruption surfacing later.
close_reason: First-open-after-upgrade one-time idempotent repair pass landed (f32ce2aa6): new fsqlite-core::migration module + hook in the full-open funnel. Marker <db>.fsqlite-migration-state (version/last_run/repairs), backup <db>.pre-migration-bak(+sidecars) before any mutation, opt-out FRANKENSQLITE_SKIP_MIGRATION=1, marker-at-birth so only genuinely-unmarked pre-fix DBs run the pass. All 6 ACs verified: runs-once, idempotent, interrupt-safe, backup-preserved, opt-out (env-exercised), stderr message (unit-tested). Oracle-first: stock C SQLite reads the repaired image as integrity_check==ok. fsqlite-core --lib 3755 pass (5 failures proven pre-existing via SKIP_MIGRATION=1); bd_84rh4 corruption-reopen 2/2 (marker-at-birth, no interference). title: Single-command e2e orchestrator: tests/scripts/run-all.sh covering every fix's test surface with detailed logging
description: After implementation, anyone (operator or CI) must be able to run a single command that exercises every Epic 1 and Epic 2 fix end-to-end and produces a structured report. This is the post-implementation acceptance test for the whole roll-up.
design: tests/scripts/run-all.sh runs in order: (1) cargo fmt --check + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings + cargo deny check; (2) cargo test --workspace (unit + integration); (3) cargo test --features loom (model checker); (4) cargo fuzz run xor_merge_guard --max-iters 100000; (5) tests/concurrent/ + tests/swarm/ (60s short soak); (6) bd-0wb8l soak --duration=10m (CI-only; full 48h is separate); (7) cargo bench --bench concurrent_writers --baseline current-main; (8) bd-aiica integrity-check pass over all artifacts; (9) Generate a single REPORT.md summarizing each step's outcome + timing + log paths. The script is idempotent (safe to re-run), produces a deterministic artifact directory layout, and exits non-zero on ANY step failure. Logging: every command's stdout+stderr piped through tee to a step-specific log file; all logs ride the bd-NEW-1.11 structured-logging schema where applicable; aggregated trace_id printed so a single run can be reconstructed from logs.
acceptance_criteria: (1) tests/scripts/run-all.sh runs to green on a healthy main HEAD. (2) Forcing a synthetic failure at each step (rename a public fn, plant a bad XOR call, etc.) fails the script at exactly that step. (3) REPORT.md renders cleanly in GitHub UI. (4) Artifact directory has predictable layout documented in tests/scripts/README.md. (5) Wall-clock: <30 minutes on a warm cache. (6) Reruns produce byte-identical REPORT.md modulo timing fields.
notes: This is the 'after implementation, prove it works' bead — the single button users press to gain confidence in the system.
